- **Never:** A styled ::-webkit-scrollbar written per component. **Instead:** The scrollbar-quiet utility. Chromium ignores ::-webkit-scrollbar once scrollbar-width is set; the utility handles both engines.

## Details

### A scrolling panel

```tsx
// before
<div className="overflow-y-auto">
// after
<div className="overflow-y-auto scrollbar-quiet" ref={useScrollActivity()}>
```

No bar at rest; it appears while scrolling, hovered or focused, and fades a beat after. Content cut off at the edge is what says the region scrolls.

**Related:** `sable docs surfaces` · `sable docs accessibility` · `sable component Scroller`

---

# Accessibility

Sable's components ship accessible behavior from Base UI. These rules cover what an app composing them still has to get right.

**WCAG AA · 44px targets · visible focus · reduced motion · logical properties**

## Floors

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `Contrast` | 4.5:1 text · 3:1 UI and large text | Every semantic text/surface pair is checked per theme by contrast.test.ts. |
| `Hit area` | 44×44px | hit-target keeps a small control at the floor without moving layout. |
| `Focus` | ring-2 ring-ring, full opacity | Visible on every interactive element, in light, dark and forced-colors. |
| `Mobile input text` | ≥ 16px | iOS Safari zooms the page on focus below it. |
| `Reduced motion` | --motion-scale: 0 | Transitions resolve instantly; loaders hold their first frame. |

## Rules

1. **Use the component, not a div with a click handler.** Base UI supplies roles, keyboard handling and focus management. A clickable div has none of them.
2. **Every control has an accessible name.** Icon-only buttons take aria-label. Fields take a <Label> through <Field>, which also wires aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
3. **A live region exists before it has anything to say.** Render role="status" empty from the start and swap its text. A region inserted together with its content is announced inconsistently.
4. **On client-side navigation, update document.title and move focus to the new view's h1.** Route changes are silent to assistive technology unless the app announces them. AppShell supplies the skip link and landmarks; the app does the rest.
5. **Keep submit enabled; validate on submit and focus the first invalid field.** A disabled submit hides why it is disabled. Focus is the only way a screen-reader user finds the error.
6. **Use logical properties: ms-/me-/ps-/pe-/text-start/inset-inline-*.** Flex and grid mirror for free under dir="rtl"; hand-positioned elements do not. *Enforced by design-lint: physical-direction (ratchet).*
7. **Decorative layers over content take pointer-events-none and aria-hidden.** Scrims, glows and fades otherwise swallow clicks on the controls beneath.
8. **Check focus and disabled states under forced-colors: active.** Windows High Contrast overrides ring colors and erases opacity-based disabled styling.

## Never

- **Never:** Color as the only signal (a red border with no message). **Instead:** Color plus text or an icon. Roughly 1 in 12 men cannot tell red from green.
- **Never:** Opacity on the focus ring. **Instead:** ring-ring at full opacity; tune the token in the theme. A faded ring loses the contrast the theme tested. *Enforced by sable-lint: faded-focus-ring.*
- **Never:** Blocking paste, or type="number" for codes and card numbers. **Instead:** type="text" inputMode="numeric" with the right autocomplete. Blocking paste breaks password managers; number inputs scroll-change identifiers.
- **Never:** forced-color-adjust: none to 'fix' high-contrast mode. **Instead:** Let the system colors apply; verify the result. It removes the user's chosen colors exactly where they need them.
- **Never:** outline: none without a replacement. **Instead:** focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring. Keyboard users lose their place.

## Details

### An icon-only button

```tsx
// before
<Button size="icon"><Icon name="xmark" /></Button>
// after
<Button size="icon" aria-label="Close"><Icon name="xmark" /></Button>
```

Without a name, a screen reader announces only 'button'.

### A status that announces

```tsx
// before
{saved && <p role="status">Saved</p>}
// after
<p role="status">{saved ? "Saved" : ""}</p>
```

The region is in the accessibility tree before its text changes, so the change is announced.

**Related:** `sable docs typography` · `sable docs motion` · `sable component <Name> --a11y`

# AuthPage

Centered auth card: a form-width region vertically centered in the viewport, one Card holding the Form, an alternate-action divider, and a quiet switch-to-sign-up link beneath it.

**Intent:** Reach for this for sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, and any single-purpose one-column form route (invite accept, unsubscribe). Not for multi-section forms (use SettingsPage).

## Notes

- Region cap is `form` (480px) — the narrowest named cap; auth never needs more.
- The card is the only surface on the page: no app chrome, no sidebar — minimal exit paths.
- min-h-dvh + grid place-items-center centers the card without magic offsets.
- Field handles label/error wiring; the submit button is full-width — the primary (and only) action.
- Secondary actions (here, switch to sign-up; add forgot password the same way) are quiet `link-underline` links, never competing buttons.

## Accessibility

- The route renders inside <main> with the page h1 in the card header (an h1 inside CardTitle, which carries the type).
- Field auto-wires labels, describedby, and invalid state onto the inputs.
- Autocomplete attributes (email, current-password) keep password managers working.

## Source

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, Field, Form, Input, Region, Separator, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

export function AuthPage() {
	return (
		<main className="grid min-h-dvh place-items-center bg-background">
			<Region max="form" safeArea={["top", "bottom"]}>
				<Stack gap={3}>
					<Card>
						<CardHeader>
							{/* CardTitle carries the type; the h1 inside it is the page heading. */}
							<CardTitle>
								<h1>Sign in</h1>
							</CardTitle>
							<CardDescription>Welcome back — pick up where you left off.</CardDescription>
						</CardHeader>
						<CardContent>
							<Form onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
								<Field label="Email" required>
									<Input type="email" name="email" autoComplete="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
								</Field>
								<Field label="Password" required>
									<Input type="password" name="password" autoComplete="current-password" />
								</Field>
								<Button type="submit" className="w-full">
									Sign in
								</Button>
								<Separator label="or" />
								<Button variant="outline" className="w-full">
									Continue with wallet
								</Button>
							</Form>
						</CardContent>
					</Card>
					<p className="text-center text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">
						No account?{" "}
						<a href="/signup" className="link-underline motion-interactive text-foreground">
							Create one
						</a>
					</p>
				</Stack>
			</Region>
		</main>
	)
}
```

# BrandLandingPage

High-fidelity brand/product landing page: pill navigation, editorial hero type, a dark product scene, calm status tones, CTA pair, feature cards, metrics, and a complete branded footer.

**Intent:** Use this for a polished product marketing route that still needs to show a credible app surface. It is warmer and more tactile than the canonical LandingPage, but avoids trend-driven neon and generic hype cues.

## Notes

- One display headline owns the first viewport; supporting copy stays in body-lg at prose measure.
- The nav spends one compact pill surface, with a clear brand signal and two primary paths: sign in and request access.
- The product scene uses overlay tokens for a stable dark media surface, then semantic tones for status and chart signals.
- The footer closes the page with brand reassurance, a three-column sitemap, a digest signup, operational mini-metrics, and legal links.
- Every surface outside the product scene is a real Card (feature, metric and digest cards); status marks are StatusDot. The scene's nested panels take `rounded-concentric-xl/<inset>` from the shell's radius, so the corners stay parallel at any radius preset.
- Radius and shadow are theme-controlled. In Cove the same rounded-lg/xl classes read larger and softer; in other themes the structure still holds.
- Color is intentionally broad: porcelain/plum/lavender/blue/mint/saffron/coral through semantic roles, not a one-note purple gradient.

## Accessibility

- The brand nav is a labeled nav landmark with real links and visible text.
- The footer is a real footer landmark with a labeled footer nav, visible link text, and a labeled email field.
- TextReveal preserves the full headline as one accessible label and honors reduced-motion policy.
- Status dots are paired with visible text labels so color is never the only signal.

## Source

```tsx

	{ label: "Intake", state: "Open", tone: "info" as const },

	},

		title: "Resources",

			{ label: "Guides", href: "/guides" },

			{ label: "Changelog", href: "/changelog" },
			{ label: "Docs", href: "/docs" },
		],
	},
]

const footerSignals = [
	{ label: "Uptime", value: "99.98%" },
	{ label: "Regions", value: "12" },
	{ label: "Response", value: "42s" },
]

export function BrandLandingPage() {

								understandable flow.

									<Card key={feature.title} render={<article />} className="h-full">
										<CardContent>
											<span className="grid size-10 place-items-center rounded-md bg-highlight text-highlight-foreground">
												<Icon name={feature.icon} className="text-xl" />
											</span>
											<h3 className="mt-5 text-title-lg">{feature.title}</h3>
											<p className="mt-2 text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">{feature.body}</p>
										</CardContent>
									</Card>
								))}
							</div>
						</div>
					</Region>
				</section>

				<Region as="section" max="wide" className="py-14">
					<div className="grid gap-3 md:grid-cols-3">
						{metrics.map((metric) => (
							<Card key={metric.label}>
								<CardContent>
									<p className="text-label-md text-muted-foreground">{metric.label}</p>
									<p className="mt-3 text-display-lg">{metric.value}</p>
									<p className="mt-1 text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">{metric.detail}</p>
								</CardContent>
							</Card>
						))}
					</div>
				</Region>
			</main>

			<footer className="border-t border-border bg-muted/35">
				<Region max="wide" className="py-10 sm:py-12">
					<div className="grid gap-8 lg:grid-cols-[1fr_1.35fr_1fr]">
						<Stack gap={3} className="max-w-md">
							<a href="/" className="flex w-fit items-center gap-2 rounded-full motion-interactive motion-press">
								<span className="grid size-9 place-items-center rounded-full bg-primary text-primary-foreground">
									<Icon name="sparkles" className="text-sm" />
								</span>
								<span className="text-title-lg">Cove</span>
							</a>
							<p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">
								A calm operating surface for teams that need trust, speed, and
								context without the noise.
							</p>
							<Row gap={1} wrap>
								<Badge size="sm" icon={<Icon name="lock" />}>
									Private
								</Badge>
								<Badge tone="success" size="sm" icon={<Icon name="circle-check" />}>
									Live
								</Badge>
							</Row>
						</Stack>

						<nav aria-label="Footer" className="grid gap-6 sm:grid-cols-3">
							{footerGroups.map((group) => (
								<div key={group.title}>
									<h2 className="text-label-md text-muted-foreground">{group.title}</h2>
									<ul className="mt-3 space-y-1">
										{group.links.map((link) => (
											<li key={link.label}>
												<a
													href={link.href}
													className="flex min-h-9 items-center text-body-sm text-muted-foreground motion-interactive hover:text-foreground"
												>
													{link.label}
												</a>
											</li>
										))}
									</ul>
								</div>
							))}
						</nav>

						<Card>
							<CardHeader>
								{/* CardTitle carries the type; the h2 inside it keeps the outline. */}
								<CardTitle>
									<h2>Signal digest</h2>
								</CardTitle>
								<CardDescription>
									One weekly note on trusted workflows and product releases.
								</CardDescription>
								<CardAction>
									<span className="grid size-9 place-items-center rounded-full bg-highlight text-highlight-foreground">
										<Icon name="sparkles" className="text-sm" />
									</span>
								</CardAction>
							</CardHeader>
							<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-4">
								<form action="/newsletter" className="grid gap-2 sm:grid-cols-[1fr_auto]">
									<label htmlFor="brand-footer-email" className="sr-only">
										Work email
									</label>
									<Input
										id="brand-footer-email"
										name="email"
										type="email"
										autoComplete="email"
										placeholder="you@company.com"
									/>
									<Button type="submit" className="w-full sm:w-auto">
										Join
									</Button>
								</form>
								<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-2">
									{footerSignals.map((signal) => (
										<div key={signal.label} className="rounded-md bg-muted p-3">
											<p className="text-mono-sm">{signal.value}</p>
											<p className="mt-1 text-caption text-muted-foreground">{signal.label}</p>
										</div>
									))}
								</div>
							</CardContent>
						</Card>
					</div>

					<div className="mt-10 flex flex-col gap-3 border-t border-border pt-5 text-caption text-muted-foreground sm:flex-row sm:items-center sm:justify-between">
						<p>© 2026 Cove. All rights reserved.</p>
						<Row gap={3} wrap>
							<a
								href="/privacy"
								className="flex min-h-9 min-w-9 items-center motion-interactive hover:text-foreground"
							>
								Privacy
							</a>
							<a
								href="/terms"
								className="flex min-h-9 min-w-9 items-center motion-interactive hover:text-foreground"
							>
								Terms
							</a>
							<a
								href="/contact"
								className="flex min-h-9 min-w-9 items-center motion-interactive hover:text-foreground"
							>
								Contact
							</a>
						</Row>
					</div>
				</Region>
			</footer>
		</div>
	)
}
```

# ChatPanel

A full-height conversation surface: titled header, scrolling transcript, and a composer pinned to the bottom — the assembled shape of an AI assistant, a support thread, or a DM.

**Intent:** Reach for this for any conversation that owns its screen — an assistant, a support inbox thread, a DM. Not for a chat docked beside other work (compose the same three parts inside a Sheet or a PanelGroup instead), and not for a comment thread under an article, which is a FeedPage concern.

## Notes

- The panel is a fixed-height column, not a growing page. `h-[calc(100dvh_-_--spacing(12))]` on the Card (the viewport minus the Page's py-6, in spacing units so density moves both together — a fixed `3rem` drifts the moment density moves the padding) and `flex-1 min-h-0` on the MessageScroller are what make the transcript scroll instead of the document — the single most common thing to get wrong here, and it fails by pushing the composer off the bottom of the screen.
- The panel is a Card, not a hand-built bordered section: CardHeader (title, description, CardAction), the MessageScroller and a CardFooter all inset by the card's own `--card-p`, so the three regions share one edge at any card density.
- `dvh` rather than `vh`: on mobile the URL bar collapses, and a `vh`-sized panel puts the composer under it exactly when someone is trying to type.
- Region cap is `feed` (640px) — a conversation is a reading column, and the Bubble measure cap is tuned to the same assumption.
- The composer sits outside the scroll region, in a bordered CardFooter, so it stays put while the transcript moves.
- Grouping is derived from the data (`turns[i - 1].mine === turn.mine`) rather than hand-set, and the tail is dropped on continuations — that pairing is what makes a run read as one block.
- The assistant's long-form answer uses `variant="plain"`. A tinted box around a code block reads as a quote rather than as a turn.
- The answer in flight is a `StreamingText` in a `plain` Bubble, and ONE `pending` flag drives both it and the composer's `busy`. They are the same wait reported at the two ends of the panel; letting them drift gives you a composer still saying 'sending' under an answer that already finished.
- A spinner `Marker` (or `ThinkingOrb`) belongs BEFORE the first token and is replaced once tokens land, not kept alongside. Two indicators for one wait read as two things happening — which is also why `StreamingText` takes `caret={false}` when something adjacent already reports it.
- MessageScroller needs no configuring for this: it re-follows on "a message grew" (ResizeObserver) as well as "a message arrived", so the newest token stays pinned while a reader who has scrolled up is left alone.
- For a new thread, swap the transcript's children for an `<EmptyState>` inside the same MessageScroller — the panel, header and composer are unchanged, which is the point of keeping them separate.

## Accessibility

- The panel header's title is the page's <h1> (an h1 inside CardTitle, which carries the type); the transcript is a scroll region with native overflow, so keyboard scrolling works unchanged.
- The answer in flight carries `aria-busy` rather than sitting in a live region. That is deliberate: a live region around streamed text announces every token, which is unusable. Announce once when the turn settles, from whatever owns the turn — the incomplete state is still exposed, just not narrated.
- The composer is a real <form> whose Enter handling skips IME composition, and every icon-only control in the panel carries an accessible label.

## Source

```tsx
import { Attachment, Avatar, Bubble, BubbleReaction, BubbleReactions, Button, Card, CardAction, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, ChatComposer, CodeBlock, Icon, Marker, MenuRadioGroup, MenuRadioItem, Message, MessageScroller, Page, SettingsMenu, SettingsRow, StreamingText } from "@sableui/react"

/**
 * The request is in flight. In an app this is your send state — from `useChat`,
 * a fetch, whatever owns the turn — and it is deliberately ONE flag driving two
 * places: the composer's `busy` and the answer's `streaming`. They are the same
 * wait reported at both ends of the panel, and letting them drift is how you get
 * a composer that still says "sending" under an answer that already finished.
 */
const pending = true

/** The answer so far. Append tokens to this; `StreamingText` assumes it only grows. */
const streamed =
	"Anchor on the oldest rendered message and add back however far it moved. Appends"

const turns = [
	{
		id: "t_01",
		mine: true,
		body: "Our chat scroll jumps every time older messages load. What are we doing wrong?",
	},
	{
		id: "t_02",
		mine: false,
		body: "Almost always the anchor. If you preserve the scroll position by measuring the container, prepending history moves everything under the reader.",
	},
	{
		id: "t_03",
		mine: false,
		body: "Anchor on the oldest rendered message instead and add back however far it moved. Appends leave it alone, so the same rule covers both.",
	},
]

export function ChatPanel() {
	return (
		<Page as="main" max="feed" gap={0} className="py-6">
			{/* h-dvh minus the page's own padding (py-6 = 12 spacing units, in
			    spacing units so density moves both together): the panel owns the
			    viewport, and the transcript — not the page — is the thing that
			    scrolls. The panel is a Card; its parts inset by the card's own
			    --card-p, so header, transcript and composer share one edge. */}
			<Card
				render={<section aria-labelledby="chat-title" />}
				className="flex h-[calc(100dvh_-_--spacing(12))] flex-col overflow-hidden"
			>
				<CardHeader className="border-b border-border pb-(--card-p)">
					{/* CardTitle carries the type; the h1 inside it is the page heading. */}
					<CardTitle>
						<h1 id="chat-title">Scroll behaviour</h1>
					</CardTitle>
					<CardDescription>Assistant · answers from your team's docs</CardDescription>
					<CardAction>
						<Button variant="outline" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Start a new chat">
							<Icon name="plus" />
						</Button>
					</CardAction>
				</CardHeader>

				{/* flex-1 min-h-0 is the whole layout: it bounds the scroll region
				    against the panel instead of letting the transcript grow the page. */}
				<MessageScroller className="min-h-0 flex-1 p-(--card-p)">
					<Marker variant="separator">Today</Marker>

					{turns.map((turn, i) => (
						<Message
							key={turn.id}
							messageId={turn.id}
							align={turn.mine ? "end" : "start"}
							grouped={i > 0 && turns[i - 1].mine === turn.mine}
							avatar={turn.mine ? undefined : <Avatar size="sm" fallback="AI" />}
						>
							<Bubble
								variant={turn.mine ? "primary" : "muted"}
								align={turn.mine ? "end" : "start"}
								tail={i === 0 || turns[i - 1].mine !== turn.mine}
							>
								{turn.body}
							</Bubble>
						</Message>
					))}

					<Marker variant="note" icon="sparkles">
						Read message-scroller.md
					</Marker>

					{/* An assistant's long-form answer: no bubble, because a tinted box
					    around a code block reads as a quote rather than as a turn. */}
					<Message messageId="t_04" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="AI" />}>
						<Bubble variant="plain">
							<p className="text-body-md text-foreground">
								Here is the shape of it:
							</p>
							<CodeBlock
								code={
									"const shift = anchor.offsetTop - lastTop\nif (shift !== 0) viewport.scrollTop += shift"
								}
								filename="preserve.ts"
							/>
						</Bubble>
						<BubbleReactions>
							<BubbleReaction emoji="🎯" count={2} active />
						</BubbleReactions>
					</Message>

					<Message messageId="t_05" align="end">
						<Attachment name="scroller.tsx" meta="4.2 KB · TSX" />
					</Message>

					{/* The answer arriving. A `Marker` with a spinner — or ThinkingOrb —
					    is what sits here BEFORE the first token; once tokens land it is
					    replaced rather than kept, because two indicators for one wait
					    read as two things happening.

					    No bubble, same as the long-form answer above: a tinted box around
					    a growing paragraph makes the reflow look like the box breathing.

					    MessageScroller needs no help with this — it already re-follows on
					    "a message grew" (ResizeObserver), not just on "a message arrived",
					    so the newest token stays pinned while the reader can still scroll
					    up without being yanked back. */}
					<Message messageId="t_06" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="AI" />}>
						<Bubble variant="plain">
							<StreamingText text={streamed} streaming={pending} />
						</Bubble>
					</Message>
				</MessageScroller>

				<CardFooter className="border-t border-border pt-(--card-p)">
					<ChatComposer
						className="flex-1"
						placeholder="Ask a follow-up…"
						// Same flag as the answer's `streaming`, which is what turns Send
						// into Stop. A composer that stays sendable mid-answer invites a
						// second request on top of the one still running.
						busy={pending}
						onStop={() => undefined}
						onAttach={() => undefined}
						footer="Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line"
						// Model and effort sit in `actions`, at the send end of the row:
						// they qualify the message about to be sent, so they belong beside
						// the button that sends it rather than next to the attach control.
						actions={
							<SettingsMenu
								variant="subtle"
								size="xs"
								label="Change model and effort"
								summary={
									<>
										<span className="text-foreground">5.6 Sol</span>{" "}
										<span className="text-muted-foreground">High</span>
									</>
								}
							>
								<SettingsRow label="Model" value="5.6 Sol">
									<MenuRadioGroup defaultValue="sol">
										<MenuRadioItem value="sol">5.6 Sol</MenuRadioItem>
										<MenuRadioItem value="lite">5.6 Lite</MenuRadioItem>
									</MenuRadioGroup>
								</SettingsRow>
								<SettingsRow label="Effort" value="High">
									<MenuRadioGroup defaultValue="high">
										<MenuRadioItem value="low">Low</MenuRadioItem>
										<MenuRadioItem value="standard">Standard</MenuRadioItem>
										<MenuRadioItem value="high">High</MenuRadioItem>
									</MenuRadioGroup>
								</SettingsRow>
								<SettingsRow label="Speed" value="Standard">
									<MenuRadioGroup defaultValue="standard">
										<MenuRadioItem value="standard">Standard</MenuRadioItem>
										<MenuRadioItem value="priority">Priority</MenuRadioItem>
									</MenuRadioGroup>
								</SettingsRow>
							</SettingsMenu>
						}
					/>
				</CardFooter>
			</Card>
		</Page>
	)
}
```

---

# DashboardPage

App-shell dashboard: sidebar chrome (AppHeader + BottomNav below lg), a wide content region, a stat-card row that breathes, and a data table — the default shape for operator/analytics home routes.

**Intent:** Reach for this when a route's job is monitoring or managing many records (metrics, deployments, orders, posts). Not for reading-focused routes (use FeedPage) or single-record routes (use ListDetailPage's detail side).

## Notes

- Region cap is `wide` (1280px): dashboards hold tables and multi-column grids, never a reading column.
- Stat cards: CardHeader carries label (CardDescription) + value + trend badge (CardAction pins it top-right); KPI values are `text-mono-xl` — the metric mono tier, tabular figures — never a heading tier.
- Stat cards use an explicit cols map (1 → 2 → 4) — a 4-stat row must fold to 2×2, never strand an orphan the way auto-fit can.
- The table runs flush to the card edges with `<CardContent flush>`, which hands the card's padding to the table (`--table-edge-px`), so the first and last columns line up with the CardHeader at any card density — never hand-set pl-6/pr-6. Numeric columns align end in mono.
- The Activity list is Entity rows in CardList, inset to the card padding and divided by hairlines — the same list shape as ListDetailPage, never CardContent with hand-tuned px.
- Believable density is part of the pattern: 7 rows, commit hashes in mono-caption, RelativeTime muted — never 3 rows of filler.
- The page has exactly one heading-1 (PageHeader); card titles are Title tier, not headings.
- Chrome (Sidebar) is outside the content grid; the Page region caps only content.
- Sidebar hides below lg, so the shell's header carries an AppHeader and its footer a BottomNav with the same destinations — never strand mobile users without navigation.

## Accessibility

- AppShell provides the skip link and <main id="main-content"> landmark.
- The active SidebarItem and BottomNavItem carry aria-current via `active`.
- DataTable headers are real <th>; sortable columns are announced.

## Source

```tsx
import { AppHeader, AppShell, Avatar, Badge, BottomNav, BottomNavItem, Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardList, CardTitle, DataTable, Entity, Grid, Icon, Page, PageHeader, RelativeTime, Row, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarItem, SidebarNav } from "@sableui/react"

const MIN = 60 * 1000
const HOUR = 60 * MIN

const stats = [
	{ label: "Revenue", value: "$12,480", delta: "+8.2%", up: true, note: "vs. previous 30 days" },
	{ label: "Collects", value: "1,284", delta: "+3.1%", up: true, note: "182 from new collectors" },
	{ label: "New collectors", value: "312", delta: "+12.4%", up: true, note: "best month this year" },
	{ label: "Sell-through", value: "64%", delta: "−1.8%", up: false, note: "across 48 active editions" },
]

const deployments = [
	{ id: "dp_01", project: "storefront", commit: "a41f2c9", status: "ready" as const, duration: "42s", updated: 2 * MIN },
	{ id: "dp_02", project: "api", commit: "7c03bd1", status: "building" as const, duration: "1m 08s", updated: 9 * MIN },
	{ id: "dp_03", project: "docs", commit: "e992a70", status: "queued" as const, duration: "—", updated: 12 * MIN },
	{ id: "dp_04", project: "worker", commit: "51b8e04", status: "failed" as const, duration: "18s", updated: 1 * HOUR },
	{ id: "dp_05", project: "storefront", commit: "90cc41a", status: "ready" as const, duration: "39s", updated: 3 * HOUR },
	{ id: "dp_06", project: "renderer", commit: "b7714dd", status: "ready" as const, duration: "2m 31s", updated: 5 * HOUR },
	{ id: "dp_07", project: "api", commit: "f30a9e2", status: "ready" as const, duration: "1m 02s", updated: 8 * HOUR },
]

const activity = [
	{ id: "ac_01", who: "Nina Simone", initials: "NS", what: "collected Gold Rush #42", when: 2 * MIN },
	{ id: "ac_02", who: "Grace Hopper", initials: "GH", what: "minted a 100-run edition", when: 26 * MIN },
	{ id: "ac_03", who: "Ada Lovelace", initials: "AL", what: "followed you", when: 1 * HOUR },
	{ id: "ac_04", who: "Mary Shelley", initials: "MS", what: "collected Quiet Harbor", when: 3 * HOUR },
	{ id: "ac_05", who: "Frida Kahlo", initials: "FK", what: "tipped 0.2 SOL on Process", when: 6 * HOUR },
]

export function DashboardPage() {
	return (
		<AppShell
			// Sidebar hides below lg, so the same destinations ride in the shell's
			// mobile slots — without them the route has no navigation under 1024px.
			header={<AppHeader title={<span className="text-title-sm">Atelier</span>} />}
			bottomNav={
				<BottomNav aria-label="Primary">
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="grid" />} label="Overview" showLabel active render={<a href="/" />} />
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="image-stack" />} label="Editions" showLabel render={<a href="/editions" />} />
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="user" />} label="Collectors" showLabel render={<a href="/collectors" />} />
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Activity" showLabel render={<a href="/activity" />} />
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="gear" />} label="Settings" showLabel render={<a href="/settings" />} />
				</BottomNav>
			}
			sidebar={
				<Sidebar>
					<SidebarHeader>
						<span className="text-title-sm">Atelier</span>
					</SidebarHeader>
					<SidebarNav>
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="grid" />} label="Overview" active render={<a href="/" />} />
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="image-stack" />} label="Editions" render={<a href="/editions" />} />
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="user" />} label="Collectors" render={<a href="/collectors" />} />
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Activity" render={<a href="/activity" />} />
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="gear" />} label="Settings" render={<a href="/settings" />} />
					</SidebarNav>
				</Sidebar>
			}
		>
			<Page max="wide" gap={4} className="py-6">
				<PageHeader
					title="Overview"
					description="Sales, collects, and edition activity for the last 30 days."
					actions={
						<Row gap={2}>
							<Button variant="outline">Export</Button>
							<Button>New edition</Button>
						</Row>
					}
				/>
				<Grid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2, xl: 4 }} gap={3}>
					{stats.map((stat) => (
						<Card key={stat.label}>
							<CardHeader>
								<CardDescription>{stat.label}</CardDescription>
								<CardTitle className="text-mono-xl">{stat.value}</CardTitle>
								<CardAction>
									<Badge tone={stat.up ? "success" : "neutral"} size="sm">
										<Icon name={stat.up ? "chevron-up" : "chevron-down"} />
										{stat.delta}
									</Badge>
								</CardAction>
							</CardHeader>
							<CardContent>
								<p className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">{stat.note}</p>
							</CardContent>
						</Card>
					))}
				</Grid>
				<Grid cols={{ base: 1, xl: 3 }} gap={3}>
					<Card className="xl:col-span-2">
						<CardHeader>
							<CardTitle>Recent deployments</CardTitle>
							<CardDescription>Builds across every project, newest first.</CardDescription>
							<CardAction>
								<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" render={<a href="/deployments" />}>
									View all
								</Button>
							</CardAction>
						</CardHeader>
						<CardContent flush>
							<DataTable
								data={deployments}
								rowKey={(row) => row.id}
								columns={[
									{ key: "project", header: "Project", sortable: true, className: "text-label-md" },
									{ key: "commit", header: "Commit", cell: (row) => <span className="text-mono-caption text-muted-foreground">{row.commit}</span> },
									{ key: "status", header: "Status", cell: (row) => <Badge appearance="plain" tone={statusTone(row.status)} dot>{row.status}</Badge> },
									{ key: "duration", header: "Duration", align: "end", cell: (row) => <span className="text-mono-caption">{row.duration}</span> },
									{ key: "updated", header: "Updated", align: "end", cell: (row) => <RelativeTime date={Date.now() - row.updated} className="text-body-xs text-muted-foreground" /> },
								]}
							/>
						</CardContent>
					</Card>
					<Card>
						<CardHeader>
							<CardTitle>Activity</CardTitle>
							<CardDescription>Collects, mints, and follows.</CardDescription>
						</CardHeader>
						<CardList>
							{activity.map((item) => (
								<Entity
									key={item.id}
									density="compact"
									leading={<Avatar size="sm" fallback={item.initials} alt={item.who} />}
									title={
										<span className="text-body-sm">
											<span className="text-label-md">{item.who}</span>{" "}
											<span className="text-muted-foreground">{item.what}</span>
										</span>
									}
									action={<RelativeTime date={Date.now() - item.when} className="text-caption text-muted-foreground" />}
								/>
							))}
						</CardList>
					</Card>
				</Grid>
			</Page>
		</AppShell>
	)
}
```

# FeedPage

Single-column reading feed: a feed-width region, one Card per post (Entity byline, zero-shift media, body copy, quiet action row), and explicit load-more pagination.

**Intent:** Reach for this for timelines, activity streams, and any reverse-chronological reading surface. Not for record management (DashboardPage) or side-by-side browsing (ListDetailPage).

## Notes

- Region cap is `feed` (640px) — a single reading column; media and copy share one measure.
- Post media sits in an AspectBox so late-loading images never shift the column.
- The byline is Entity (Avatar + name + handle) in a CardList — the same row primitive as everywhere else, inset to the card padding by CardList rather than by zeroing paddings on CardHeader and Entity.
- Actions are ghost sm Buttons (icon + count) in a Row, pulled out by the button's own padding (`-ms-3`) so the first icon sits on the text edge: quiet chrome under content, not competing pills.
- Pagination is an explicit load-more Button (secondary; set `loading` while the next page fetches — `loadingLabel` names that state), not infinite scroll — predictable for keyboard and AT users.

## Accessibility

- Each post is an <article>, so AT users can jump between posts.
- Icon-only action buttons carry aria-labels.
- Media images get meaningful alt text from the post, empty alt only if decorative.

## Source

```tsx
import { AspectBox, Avatar, Button, Card, CardContent, CardList, Entity, Icon, Page, PageHeader, Row, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const posts = [
	{
		id: "p_01",
		author: "Ada Lovelace",
		handle: "@ada · 2h",
		initials: "AL",
		body: "New edition drops Friday — 100 signed prints, each with the on-chain original.",
		image: "/media/edition-cover.svg",
		alt: "Edition cover — Gold Rush series",
		likes: 128,
		comments: 24,
	},
	{
		id: "p_02",
		author: "Grace Hopper",
		handle: "@grace · 5h",
		initials: "GH",
		body: "Process shot from this week's series. Compilers and copper ink.",
		image: "/media/process-shot.svg",
		alt: "Work-in-progress plotter drawing in copper ink",
		likes: 86,
		comments: 9,
	},
]

export function FeedPage() {
	return (
		<Page as="main" max="feed" gap={4} className="py-6">
			<PageHeader title="Home" description="Latest posts from artists you follow." />
			<Stack gap={3}>
				{posts.map((post) => (
					<article key={post.id}>
						<Card className="overflow-hidden">
							{/* The byline is an Entity row in CardList, which insets it to the
							    card's own padding on every side — no hand-zeroed paddings. */}
							<CardList>
								<Entity
									leading={<Avatar fallback={post.initials} alt={post.author} />}
									title={post.author}
									subtitle={post.handle}
									action={
										<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Post options">
											<Icon name="ellipsis" />
										</Button>
									}
								/>
							</CardList>
							<AspectBox ratio={16 / 9}>
								<img src={post.image} alt={post.alt} className="size-full object-cover" />
							</AspectBox>
							<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-2">
								<p className="text-body-md text-foreground">{post.body}</p>
								{/* Pulled out by exactly a sm Button's own padding (px-3), so the
								    first icon lands on the text edge above it. Both are on the
								    spacing scale, so they stay aligned at every density. */}
								<Row gap={1} className="-ms-3">
									<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" aria-label={`Like — ${post.likes}`}>
										<Icon name="heart" />
										{post.likes}
									</Button>
									<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" aria-label={`Comments — ${post.comments}`}>
										<Icon name="comment" />
										{post.comments}
									</Button>
									<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" aria-label="Share">
										<Icon name="share" />
									</Button>
								</Row>
							</CardContent>
						</Card>
					</article>
				))}
			</Stack>
			<Button variant="secondary" loadingLabel="Loading…">Load more posts</Button>
		</Page>
	)
}
```

# LandingPage

Marketing hero + feature grid: display-tier headline as the page's single loud moment, an eyebrow kicker, a two-action CTA row, and a three-up feature grid that reveals on scroll.

**Intent:** Reach for this for the marketing/landing route of a product — the one page where Display type and scroll reveals belong. Not for product UI (display type and one-per-view rules forbid it inside the app).

## Notes

- Display type is the marketing voice: exactly one display headline per page, tight leading, weight 700+.
- The eyebrow is a small outline Badge (`size="sm"`) — the badge's own size, never a type class forced onto its label; hierarchy above the headline is eyebrow → display → lede.
- The lede is body-lg capped at the prose measure — the headline may be wide, reading text may not.
- Two CTAs max: one primary, one quiet outline. More actions dilute the hero.
- Reveal wraps below-the-fold sections only; it no-ops under reduced motion via the motion policy.
- Feature cards are Cards in a Grid with minItemWidth (three-up that reflows on its own width), each icon + title + body-sm copy.

## Accessibility

- The hero headline is the page h1; feature titles are h2s restyled with the Title tier.
- Reveal renders content immediately (no animation) when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
- CTA buttons are real links or buttons with visible text — no icon-only CTAs.

## Source

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, Card, CardContent, Grid, Icon, Region, Reveal, Row, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const features = [
	{
		icon: "sparkles" as const,
		title: "Own the surface",
		body: "Semantic tokens end-to-end — re-theme the whole product without touching a component.",
	},
	{
		icon: "component" as const,
		title: "Behavior included",
		body: "Focus, keyboard nav, and ARIA ride on Base UI primitives under every surface.",
	},
	{
		icon: "layout" as const,
		title: "Pages, not just parts",
		body: "Purpose-named regions, an 8px rhythm, and canonical page shells for the routes every product needs.",
	},
]

export function LandingPage() {
	return (
		<div className="min-h-dvh bg-background">
			<header>
				<Region as="nav" aria-label="Main" className="grid h-16 grid-cols-[1fr_auto_1fr] items-center">
					<span className="justify-self-start text-title-sm">Sable</span>
					<Row gap={1} className="justify-self-center max-sm:hidden">
						<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" render={<a href="/docs" />}>
							Docs
						</Button>
						<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" render={<a href="/patterns" />}>
							Patterns
						</Button>
						<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" render={<a href="/themes" />}>
							Themes
						</Button>
					</Row>
					<Button size="sm" className="justify-self-end" render={<a href="/signup" />}>
						Get started
					</Button>
				</Region>
			</header>
			<main>
				<Region as="section" max="wide" className="py-24">
					<Stack gap={4} align="center" className="text-center">
						<Badge appearance="outline" size="sm">
							Now in beta
						</Badge>
						<h1 className="max-w-4xl text-balance text-display-2xl">
							Ship product UI your agents can't get wrong
						</h1>
						<p className="max-w-(--measure-prose) text-body-lg text-muted-foreground">
							An owned, themeable component system with enforced tokens, typography,
							and motion — documented for machines as carefully as for people.
						</p>
						<Row gap={2} justify="center">
							<Button size="cta">Get started</Button>
							<Button size="cta" variant="outline">
								Read the docs
							</Button>
						</Row>
					</Stack>
				</Region>
				<Region as="section" max="wide" className="pb-24">
					<Reveal>
						{/* Three-up that reflows on its own width (minItemWidth), one Card
						    per feature — never a hand-drawn bordered grid. */}
						<Grid minItemWidth="calc(var(--spacing) * 64)">
							{features.map((feature) => (
								<Card key={feature.title}>
									<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-2">
										<Icon name={feature.icon} className="text-xl text-muted-foreground" />
										<h2 className="text-title-lg">{feature.title}</h2>
										<p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">{feature.body}</p>
									</CardContent>
								</Card>
							))}
						</Grid>
					</Reveal>
				</Region>
			</main>
			<footer className="border-t border-border">
				<Region className="flex h-16 items-center justify-between">
					<span className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">© 2026 Sable</span>
					<Row gap={3}>
						<a href="/github" className="text-caption text-muted-foreground motion-interactive hover:text-foreground">
							GitHub
						</a>
						<a href="/changelog" className="text-caption text-muted-foreground motion-interactive hover:text-foreground">
							Changelog
						</a>
					</Row>
				</Region>
			</footer>
		</div>
	)
}
```

# ListDetailPage

Two-column list-detail: a wide region split 8/4, the record list as Entity rows in the main column, and a sticky supporting rail (detail, filters, or summary) beside it.

**Intent:** Reach for this when a route lists records AND keeps one selected/summarized in view (members + member detail, inbox + message, orders + order). For pure browsing with no rail, a single-column FeedPage or DashboardPage table is simpler.

## Notes

- Region cap is `wide`; the split is Columns 12 → Col 8 + Col 4, collapsing to stacked full-width columns below lg via breakpoint maps.
- List rows are Entity inside one bordered Card, in CardList: it insets each row to the card padding and divides them with hairlines — on a dark canvas rows need an anchoring surface, not a flat float.
- Pending records live in the same list, muted (muted title + `Invited` badge), instead of a separate section.
- The rail card holds label/value pairs as a Description list — muted terms, mono (tabular) values — plus one quiet action. Never hand-built `justify-between` rows.
- The rail is sticky (top on the 4px scale) so the summary stays in view while the list scrolls.

## Accessibility

- Entity rows given `interactive` + `onSelect` (to open a member's detail) render as real buttons; keyboard focus follows list order. Rows here are presentational.
- The rail is an <aside> landmark; the list column is the main content.

## Source

```tsx
import { Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardList, CardTitle, Col, Columns, Description, DescriptionItem, Entity, Page, PageHeader, SearchInput, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

const members = [
	{ id: "u_01", name: "Ada Lovelace", handle: "@ada", role: "Owner", initials: "AL", pending: false },
	{ id: "u_02", name: "Grace Hopper", handle: "@grace", role: "Admin", initials: "GH", pending: false },
	{ id: "u_03", name: "Mary Shelley", handle: "@mary", role: "Member", initials: "MS", pending: false },
	{ id: "u_04", name: "Nina Simone", handle: "@nina", role: "Member", initials: "NS", pending: false },
	{ id: "u_05", name: "Frida Kahlo", handle: "@frida", role: "Member", initials: "FK", pending: false },
	{ id: "u_06", name: "hopper@navy.mil", handle: "invited 2 days ago", role: "Member", initials: "?", pending: true },
]

export function ListDetailPage() {
	return (
		<Page as="main" max="wide" gap={4} className="py-6">
			<PageHeader
				title="Members"
				description="Everyone with access to this workspace."
				actions={<Button>Invite member</Button>}
			/>
			<Columns count={{ base: 1, lg: 12 }}>
				<Col span={{ base: 1, lg: 8 }}>
					<Stack gap={3}>
						<SearchInput placeholder="Search members" aria-label="Search members" />
						<Card className="overflow-hidden">
							<CardList>
									{members.map((member) => (
										<Entity
											key={member.id}
											leading={
												<Avatar
													fallback={member.pending ? "•" : member.initials}
													alt={member.pending ? "" : member.name}
												/>
											}
											title={
												<span className={member.pending ? "text-muted-foreground" : undefined}>
													{member.name}
												</span>
											}
											subtitle={member.handle}
											action={
												member.pending ? (
													<Badge>Invited</Badge>
												) : (
													<Badge appearance="outline">{member.role}</Badge>
												)
											}
										/>
									))}
							</CardList>
						</Card>
					</Stack>
				</Col>
				<Col span={{ base: 1, lg: 4 }}>
					<aside className="sticky top-6">
						<Card>
							<CardHeader>
								<CardTitle>Workspace</CardTitle>
							</CardHeader>
							<CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-3">
								{/* Label/value pairs are a Description list, not hand-built rows. */}
								<Description>
									<DescriptionItem term="Members" detail={<span className="text-mono-md">5</span>} />
									<DescriptionItem term="Pending invites" detail={<span className="text-mono-md">1</span>} />
									<DescriptionItem term="Seats used" detail={<span className="text-mono-md">6 / 10</span>} />
								</Description>
								<Button variant="outline" size="sm" className="mt-1 self-start">
									Manage plan
								</Button>
							</CardContent>
						</Card>
					</aside>
				</Col>
			</Columns>
		</Page>
	)
}
```

# SettingsPage

Stacked settings sections inside the app shell: a content-width region, one Fieldset card per concern (each with its own save), auto-wired Form/Field rows, and a destructive zone last.

**Intent:** Reach for this for account/profile/workspace settings and any 'edit a handful of grouped preferences' route. Not for a single short form (use AuthPage's centered form shape) or bulk record editing (use DashboardPage + DataTable).

## Notes

- Region cap is `content` (896px): settings panes hold labeled rows and the occasional 2-up field, never a full grid.
- One Fieldset per concern, each with its own footer save — per-section saves beat one page-wide submit for settings.
- Field wires label/description/error a11y automatically; never hand-roll <label> + <input> pairs here.
- The destructive section is visually last, isolated in its own Fieldset with a destructive-variant action.
- Toggles use orientation="horizontal" Fields so the label sits beside the Switch.
- Lives in the same AppShell as DashboardPage: Sidebar from lg up, AppHeader + BottomNav below it, with Settings marked active in both.

## Accessibility

- AppShell provides the skip link and <main id="main-content"> landmark; the active SidebarItem and BottomNavItem carry aria-current.
- Each section is a real <fieldset> with a <legend> (FieldsetLegend).
- Field auto-wires htmlFor/id, aria-describedby (description + error), aria-invalid, and required.
- The danger action is a real button labeled by its visible text — no icon-only destructive controls.

## Source

```tsx
import { AppHeader, AppShell, BottomNav, BottomNavItem, Button, Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetDescription, FieldsetFooter, FieldsetLegend, Form, Icon, Input, Page, PageHeader, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarItem, SidebarNav, Switch, Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

export function SettingsPage() {
	return (
		<AppShell
			// Sidebar hides below lg, so the same destinations ride in the shell's
			// mobile slots — without them the route has no navigation under 1024px.
			header={<AppHeader title={<span className="text-title-sm">Atelier</span>} />}
			bottomNav={
				<BottomNav aria-label="Primary">
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="grid" />} label="Overview" showLabel render={<a href="/" />} />
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="image-stack" />} label="Editions" showLabel render={<a href="/editions" />} />
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="user" />} label="Collectors" showLabel render={<a href="/collectors" />} />
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Activity" showLabel render={<a href="/activity" />} />
					<BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="gear" />} label="Settings" showLabel active render={<a href="/settings" />} />
				</BottomNav>
			}
			sidebar={
				<Sidebar>
					<SidebarHeader>
						<span className="text-title-sm">Atelier</span>
					</SidebarHeader>
					<SidebarNav>
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="grid" />} label="Overview" render={<a href="/" />} />
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="image-stack" />} label="Editions" render={<a href="/editions" />} />
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="user" />} label="Collectors" render={<a href="/collectors" />} />
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Activity" render={<a href="/activity" />} />
						<SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="gear" />} label="Settings" active render={<a href="/settings" />} />
					</SidebarNav>
				</Sidebar>
			}
		>
			{/* No `as="main"`: AppShell already renders <main id="main-content">. */}
			<Page max="content" gap={4} className="py-6">
				<PageHeader
					title="Settings"
					description="Your profile, notifications, and account controls."
				/>
				<Form onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
					<Fieldset>
						<FieldsetLegend>Profile</FieldsetLegend>
						<FieldsetDescription>How you appear across the app.</FieldsetDescription>
						<FieldsetContent>
							<Field label="Display name" required>
								<Input name="displayName" defaultValue="ada" />
							</Field>
							<Field label="Bio" description="Shown on your public profile.">
								<Textarea name="bio" rows={3} placeholder="Tell collectors who you are" />
							</Field>
							<Field label="Timezone">
								<Select defaultValue="utc" name="timezone">
									<SelectTrigger />
									<SelectContent>
										<SelectItem value="utc">UTC</SelectItem>
										<SelectItem value="est">Eastern (UTC−5)</SelectItem>
										<SelectItem value="pst">Pacific (UTC−8)</SelectItem>
									</SelectContent>
								</Select>
							</Field>
						</FieldsetContent>
						<FieldsetFooter>
							<Button type="submit">Save profile</Button>
						</FieldsetFooter>
					</Fieldset>
				</Form>
				<Form onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
					<Fieldset>
						<FieldsetLegend>Notifications</FieldsetLegend>
						<FieldsetDescription>What we email you about.</FieldsetDescription>
						<FieldsetContent>
							<Field label="New collector alerts" orientation="horizontal">
								<Switch name="collectorAlerts" defaultChecked />
							</Field>
							<Field label="Weekly digest" orientation="horizontal">
								<Switch name="weeklyDigest" />
							</Field>
						</FieldsetContent>
						<FieldsetFooter>
							<Button type="submit">Save notifications</Button>
						</FieldsetFooter>
					</Fieldset>
				</Form>
				<Fieldset>
					<FieldsetLegend>Danger zone</FieldsetLegend>
					<FieldsetDescription>
						Deleting your account removes your posts and collections permanently.
					</FieldsetDescription>
					<FieldsetFooter>
						<Button variant="destructive">Delete account</Button>
					</FieldsetFooter>
				</Fieldset>
			</Page>
		</AppShell>
	)
}
```

---

# Region

**Status:** stable

The page region: fluid, edge-to-edge with the fluid page inset (--page-inset). Opt-in centered max cap picked by ROLE (prose/form/feed/content/wide/full), never a global page max-width. The root of nearly every route.

**Keywords:** region, page width, container, layout

## Usage

Use Region as the page-width primitive that applies fluid page inset and an optional purpose-named max width.

### Best practices

- Do: Choose the max value by content role, such as prose, form, feed, content, wide, or full.
- Do: Use Region near the route or section boundary so inner layout stays intentional.
- Don't: Do not use Region as a global wrapper that forces every page into the same max width.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| as | ElementType | "div" | Semantic element to render (e.g. "main", "section", "nav"). |
| inset | boolean | true | Apply the fluid horizontal page inset (--page-inset). |
| max | "prose" \| "form" \| "feed" \| "content" \| "wide" \| "full" \| CSS length | — | Opt-in centered max-width cap, purpose-named: prose 65ch (long-form reading) · form 480px (auth, narrow single-column forms) · feed 640px (single-column timeline) · content 896px (settings/admin panes) · wide 1280px (dashboards, tables, card grids) · full 1536px (full-bleed ceiling). Omit for fully fluid. |
| bleed | boolean | false | Full-bleed: edge to edge with no inset. Overrides inset. |
| safeArea | boolean \| ("top"\|"bottom"\|"left"\|"right")[] | false | env(safe-area-inset-*) padding for fixed or native-shell surfaces. true pads top+bottom; pass an edge array to target edges. |

## Related

- Components: Page, Grid, Columns

## Examples

### Settings pane

```tsx
import { PageHeader, Region } from "@sableui/react"

<Region as="main" max="content"><PageHeader title="Settings" /></Region>
```

### Fluid dashboard region

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, Grid, Region } from "@sableui/react"

<Region max="wide"><Grid minItemWidth="16rem"><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Revenue</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Collects</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card></Grid></Region>
```

---

# Page

**Status:** stable

A route shell: Region (inset + opt-in max cap) whose children flow as a vertically-rhythmic Stack. Use as the top-level wrapper of a route's content — distinct from AppShell (the frame around routes) and PageHeader (the heading block inside).

**Keywords:** page, route shell, region, stack

## Usage

Use Page as a route content shell that combines Region sizing with vertical rhythm.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it as the top-level wrapper for route content after application chrome.
- Do: Set max by the page's content role rather than by the current viewport.
- Don't: Do not confuse Page with AppShell; Page is content, AppShell is the frame around routes.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gap | number \| string | 4 | Vertical gap between stacked page sections. Number = rhythm units (×8px, so 4 = 32px); string = raw CSS. |
| align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" | "stretch" | Cross-axis alignment of the stacked sections. |
| …RegionProps | as, inset, max, bleed, safeArea | — | All Region props pass through (Page IS a Region). |

## Related

- Components: Region, Stack, PageHeader, AppShell

## Examples

### Feed route

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, Page, PageHeader } from "@sableui/react"

<Page as="main" max="feed"><PageHeader title="Home" description="Latest posts from artists you follow." /><Card><CardContent><p className="text-body-md">First post.</p></CardContent></Card></Page>
```

---

# Grid

**Status:** stable

CSS Grid within a region. Two modes: fixed/responsive cols count, or minItemWidth auto-fit so cells breathe with NO breakpoints (the default choice for card grids).

**Keywords:** grid, card grid, auto fit, layout

## Usage

Use Grid for uniform grid layouts inside a Region, especially card grids that can breathe responsively.

### Best practices

- Do: Prefer minItemWidth for responsive card grids that do not need breakpoint-specific spans.
- Do: Use explicit columns only when the design truly needs a fixed track count.
- Don't: Do not use Grid to set a page's reading width; use Region or Center.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cols | number \| { base?, sm?, md?, lg?, xl?, "2xl"? } | 12 | Fixed column count or a mobile-first breakpoint map ({ base: 2, md: 4 }). Ignored when minItemWidth is set. |
| minItemWidth | string | — | Auto-fit mode: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(minItemWidth, 1fr)) — the grid grows/wraps responsively without breakpoints. e.g. "16rem". |
| gap | number \| string | var(--grid-gutter) | Gap between cells. Number = rhythm units (×8px); string = raw CSS. |

## Related

- Components: Region, Columns, Card

## Examples

### Card grid that breathes (no breakpoints)

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, Grid } from "@sableui/react"

<Grid minItemWidth="16rem" gap={3}><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Alpha</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Beta</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Gamma</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card></Grid>
```

### Responsive fixed columns

```tsx
import { Badge, Grid } from "@sableui/react"

<Grid cols={{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }}><Badge appearance="plain" tone="standard" dot /><Badge appearance="plain" tone="warning" dot /><Badge appearance="plain" tone="neutral" dot /><Badge appearance="plain" tone="destructive" dot /></Grid>
```

---

# Columns

**Status:** stable

An explicit N-column track (default 12) for proportioned layouts — pair with Col spans (list-detail, asymmetric editorial layouts). For uniform card grids prefer Grid minItemWidth.

**Keywords:** columns, 12 column, span, layout

## Usage

Use Columns and Col for proportioned layouts that need explicit spans, such as list-detail or asymmetric panes.

### Best practices

- Do: Use breakpoint span maps when the same layout needs to collapse cleanly on smaller screens.
- Do: Use Columns for proportional composition, not for uniform card wrapping.
- Don't: Do not use column spans as a replacement for Region width or text measure.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Columns | yes | The explicit column track container. |
| Col | yes | A child cell with span and optional start placement. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Col | span?: number \| breakpoint map · start?: number \| breakpoint map | A cell in the track: columns to span (default 1) and optional 1-based start column. Both accept breakpoint maps ({ base: 12, lg: 8 }). |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| count | number \| breakpoint map | 12 | Columns in the track; a breakpoint map ({ base: 2, md: 6, lg: 12 }) thins the track on small screens. |
| gap | number \| string | var(--grid-gutter) | Gap between columns and rows. Number = rhythm units (×8px); string = raw CSS. The column gap is capped so all gaps together never take more than 75% of the track's width — a large gap can't push a narrow screen into horizontal scroll, and at normal desktop widths it renders exactly as given. The row gap is never capped. |

## Related

- Components: Grid, SplitPane, Region

## Examples

### List-detail (8/4)

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, Col, Columns } from "@sableui/react"

<Columns count={12}><Col span={{ base: 12, lg: 8 }}><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Posts</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card></Col><Col span={{ base: 12, lg: 4 }}><Card variant="flat"><CardHeader><CardTitle>Filters</CardTitle></CardHeader></Card></Col></Columns>
```

---

# Stack

**Status:** stable

Vertical flow on the 8px rhythm — the default container for stacked content. Gap by role: tight within a group (1.5–2), looser between groups (3–4), generous between sections (6+).

**Keywords:** stack, vertical rhythm, layout, spacing

## Usage

Use Stack for vertical flow where child spacing should follow the Sable rhythm scale.

### Best practices

- Do: Use smaller gaps within a group and larger gaps between sections.
- Do: Use Stack instead of ad hoc margins when siblings form a vertical composition.
- Don't: Do not use Stack to create page width or grid structure; pair it with Region, Grid, or Columns.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gap | number \| string | 2 | Vertical gap. Number = rhythm units (×8px, fractions ok — 2 = 16px); string = raw CSS. |
| align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" | "stretch" | Cross-axis alignment. |
| justify | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between" | "start" | Main-axis distribution. |

## Related

- Components: Row, Page, Fieldset

## Examples

### Form field group

```tsx
import { Field, Input, Stack, Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

<Stack gap={2}><Field label="Display name"><Input name="name" /></Field><Field label="Bio"><Textarea name="bio" /></Field></Stack>
```

---

# Row

**Status:** stable

Horizontal flex flow — inline rows of controls, toolbars, action clusters. Defaults to center-aligned, no wrap.

**Keywords:** row, toolbar, horizontal, layout

## Usage

Use Row for horizontal clusters such as action groups, toolbars, metadata, and inline controls.

### Best practices

- Do: Use wrap when controls may not fit on smaller screens.
- Do: Use justify and align intentionally so clusters scan as one unit.
- Don't: Do not use Row for navigation menus or dense tabular structure.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gap | number \| string | 2 | Horizontal gap. Number = rhythm units (×8px); string = raw CSS. |
| align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" | "center" | Cross-axis alignment. |
| justify | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between" | "start" | Main-axis distribution. |
| wrap | boolean | false | Allow items to wrap. |

## Related

- Components: Stack, Button, Spacer

## Examples

### Action cluster

```tsx
import { Button, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={2} justify="end"><Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button><Button>Save changes</Button></Row>
```

# Spacer

**Status:** stable

Explicit space on the rhythm, or a flexible grow pusher between siblings (e.g. pushing a footer item to the end of a Row).

**Keywords:** spacer, spacing, grow, layout

## Usage

Use Spacer for explicit rhythm space or a flex grow pusher between siblings.

### Best practices

- Do: Use grow inside Row when one side of a cluster should push to the far edge.
- Do: Use fixed size only when the space has semantic rhythm value.
- Don't: Do not use Spacer to patch broad layout problems that should be solved by Stack, Row, Grid, or Region.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size | number | 1 | Fixed size in rhythm units (×8px; fractions ok). Ignored when grow. |
| axis | "vertical" \| "horizontal" | "vertical" | Axis the fixed size applies to. |
| grow | boolean | — | Flex-grow to push siblings apart (fills available space). |

## Related

- Components: Row, Stack

## Examples

### Push actions to the end

```tsx
import { Button, Row, Spacer } from "@sableui/react"

<Row><span className="text-title-sm">Members</span><Spacer grow /><Button size="sm">Invite</Button></Row>
```

# Center

**Status:** stable

Horizontally center a block, optionally capping its width (commonly "prose" for a reading column inside a wider layout).

**Keywords:** center, measure, reading width, layout

## Usage

Use Center to center a block and optionally cap its width inside a wider layout.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for reading columns, forms, or compact content inside a broad Region.
- Do: Choose a named max when the content role matches Sable's measure tokens.
- Don't: Do not use Center for full page inset or app chrome; use Region or AppShell.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| max | "prose" \| "form" \| "feed" \| "content" \| "wide" \| CSS length | — | Cap width: a named region token or any raw CSS length. |

## Related

- Components: Region, Page, Stack

## Examples

### Reading column in a wide page

```tsx
import { Center } from "@sableui/react"

```

# AspectBox

**Status:** stable

Reserves space via aspect-ratio so async media loads with zero layout shift. Wrap images, video, embeds.

**Keywords:** aspect box, aspect ratio, media, layout shift

## Usage

Use AspectBox to reserve stable aspect-ratio space for async media, embeds, and responsive previews.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it around images, video, and embeds that should not shift layout while loading.
- Do: Match the ratio to the expected media or design slot.
- Don't: Do not use AspectBox for content whose height should grow with text or controls.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ratio | number | 16/9 | Width / height ratio (e.g. 1 for square, 4/5 for portrait). |

## Related

- Components: Video, Dialog, Browser

## Examples

### Cover image slot

```tsx
import { AspectBox } from "@sableui/react"
```

# Bleed

**Status:** stable

Escape a width-capped or inset ancestor to span the full CONTENT area (container-query units, so it stops at a fixed Sidebar instead of bleeding under it). Hero bands, profile covers, full-bleed media inside a capped Page.

**Keywords:** bleed, full bleed, media band, layout

## Usage

Use Bleed to let a band or media element escape an inset or width-capped ancestor while staying within the content area.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for hero bands, profile covers, or media that should align beyond a capped page column.
- Do: Keep surrounding content inside Region or Page so the bleed remains intentional.
- Don't: Do not use Bleed to place content under fixed app chrome or sidebars.

## Related

- Components: Page, Region, AspectBox

## Examples

### Full-bleed hero inside a capped page

```tsx
import { AspectBox, Bleed, Page, PageHeader } from "@sableui/react"

<Page max="feed"><Bleed><AspectBox ratio={3}><img src="/cover.jpg" alt="" className="size-full object-cover" /></AspectBox></Bleed><PageHeader title="Profile" /></Page>
```

# SplitPane

**Status:** stable

Responsive two-pane layout: side-by-side at/above a breakpoint, stacked (primary first) below. List-detail, media + metadata.

**Keywords:** split pane, two pane, list detail, responsive

## Usage

Use SplitPane for responsive two-pane layouts where a primary pane and supporting pane stay conceptually linked.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for media-detail, list-detail, or editor-preview workflows.
- Do: Pick a ratio that reflects the actual priority of the panes.
- Don't: Do not use SplitPane for unrelated columns or uniform grids.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| primary | ReactNode | — | The leading / larger pane (e.g. the media column). |
| secondary | ReactNode | — | The trailing / supporting pane (e.g. the detail column). |
| collapseBelow | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl" | "lg" | Breakpoint at/above which panes sit side by side. |
| ratio | string | "1/1" | Primary:secondary width ratio as "a/b" fr units (e.g. "2/1"). |
| gap | number \| string | var(--grid-gutter) | Gap between panes. |

## Related

- Components: Columns, Grid, Sheet

## Examples

### Media + detail

```tsx
import { AspectBox, Button, SplitPane, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

<SplitPane ratio="2/1" primary={<AspectBox ratio={1}><img src={post.imageUrl} alt={post.title} className="size-full object-cover" /></AspectBox>} secondary={<Stack gap={2}><h1 className="text-heading-1">{post.title}</h1><p className="text-body-md text-muted-foreground">{post.description}</p><Button>Collect</Button></Stack>} />
```

# SafeArea

Use SafeArea to pad fixed or native-shell surfaces away from device notches and home indicators.

- Do: Target only the edges that need device inset padding when possible.

Use GridOverlay only as a development or documentation visualizer for the column structure.
