# Accordion

**Status:** stable

Stacked, collapsible disclosure sections over Base UI Accordion — roving focus, arrow-key navigation, ARIA region/heading/button wiring, and an animated height transition. Each item pairs a full-width trigger (with a rotating chevron) and a panel.

**Keywords:** accordion, disclosure, collapse, faq

## Usage

Use Accordion to reveal a vertical set of related sections while keeping the surrounding page scannable.

### Best practices

- Do: Use concise trigger text that describes the content revealed below it.
- Do: Keep section content focused so expanding one item does not feel like navigating to a new page.
- Don't: Do not hide required fields, primary actions, or critical errors inside collapsed sections.
- Don't: Do not nest an Accordion inside an Accordion. Two layers of roving focus fight each other, and the arrow keys become ambiguous — flatten the hierarchy or use a Tree.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AccordionItem | yes | One expandable section in the group. |
| AccordionTrigger | yes | The button-like control that opens the section. |
| AccordionPanel | yes | The content revealed by the trigger. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AccordionItem | Base UI Accordion.Item props + className (value, disabled, onOpenChange) | Pairs a header with its panel. Give each a stable `value` to control or set initial open state. |
| AccordionTrigger | Base UI Accordion.Trigger props + className + indicator?: ReactNode | The header button (Header + Trigger composed). Renders children plus a chevron that rotates via data-[panel-open] by default; pass `indicator` to replace the icon and its open-state behavior entirely (e.g. a plus that becomes an × for a FAQ-style toggle). |
| AccordionPanel | Base UI Accordion.Panel props + className (keepMounted, hiddenUntilFound) | The collapsible body. Animates height using the --accordion-panel-height CSS var; fades on data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style]. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accordion (Root) | Base UI Accordion.Root props (value, defaultValue, multiple, disabled, onValueChange, orientation, loopFocus, keepMounted, hiddenUntilFound) | — | Groups all items and owns the open value(s). Uncontrolled via defaultValue, controlled via value. |
| defaultValue | Value[] | [] | Uncontrolled set of item values that start expanded (e.g. ['faq-1']). |
| value | Value[] | — | Controlled set of expanded item values; pair with onValueChange. |
| onValueChange | (value: Value[]) => void | — | Called with the new set of expanded item values when an item opens or closes. |
| multiple | boolean | false | Whether more than one item can be open at the same time. When false, opening one closes the others. |

## Tokens used

`border`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — An accordion is page furniture that is present from first paint. Animating it in would stage content the reader is already scanning past.
- **response** · AccordionTrigger · `motion-interactive` — The whole header row is the hit target, and it looks like a heading rather than a control. The hover shift is what tells the reader it can be clicked before they click it.
- **transition** · AccordionPanel · `motion-disclosure` — Panel height is the only cue that content came from THIS header rather than appearing at the bottom of the page. Snapping it open moves everything below by a screenful with nothing connecting cause to effect.
- **activity** · Root · _no motion_ — Nothing here is indeterminate — the panel content is already resident. A panel that loads on expand should put its own loader inside the panel.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders the trigger inside an <h3> heading and wires aria-expanded / aria-controls to the panel region.
- Arrow keys move roving focus between triggers; Home/End jump to the first/last; loopFocus wraps by default.
- Each trigger toggles its panel with Enter/Space; the panel is announced as a labelled region.
- A disabled AccordionItem dims and is skipped by keyboard focus while neighbouring items stay interactive.
- The chevron rotation is driven by data-[panel-open] and the focus ring by focus-visible — both honor reduced-motion via the consumer's transitions.

## Related

- Components: Collapsible, Tabs

## Examples

### Single (default)

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Accordion defaultValue={["a"]}><AccordionItem value="a"><AccordionTrigger>Is it permanent?</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>Yes — stored on Arweave.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem><AccordionItem value="b"><AccordionTrigger>How much?</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>A one-time mint fee.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem></Accordion>
```

### Multiple open

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Accordion multiple defaultValue={["a", "b"]}><AccordionItem value="a"><AccordionTrigger>First</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>One.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem><AccordionItem value="b"><AccordionTrigger>Second</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>Two.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem></Accordion>
```

### Custom indicator (plus-becomes-×)

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Accordion defaultValue={["a"]}><AccordionItem value="a"><AccordionTrigger indicator={<Icon name="plus" className="text-xs text-muted-foreground transition-transform [[data-panel-open]_&]:rotate-45" />}>Is it permanent?</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>Yes — stored on Arweave.</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem></Accordion>
```

---

# AppHeader

**Status:** stable

Mobile top bar (sticky, hidden at lg) with leading / title / actions slots on a 3-column grid that keeps the title optically centered. Grows into the top safe-area.

**Keywords:** app header, top bar, mobile header, chrome

## Usage

Use AppHeader for compact application chrome at the top of a screen, usually with navigation, identity, and a small action set. Pass it to AppShell's `header` slot so screen content clears it on mobile (it is sticky and hides itself at lg).

### Best practices

- Do: Keep the header actions narrow and predictable so the page title remains legible.
- Do: Use it once per app view as chrome, not as repeated content inside page sections.
- Don't: Do not overload it with filters, forms, or page-specific controls that belong in the content area.
- Don't: Do not render more than one per app, or put a second one inside a route. It is sticky chrome, so two of them stack and permanently eat the top of the viewport.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| leading | ReactNode | — | Leading slot — back button, create action, or menu trigger. |
| title | ReactNode | — | Center slot — brand wordmark or contextual page title. |
| actions | ReactNode | — | Trailing slot — wallet trigger, action buttons. |

## Tokens used

`background`, `border`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders a <header> landmark.
- Pair with a leading control that has an accessible label (e.g. a BackButton).

## Related

- Components: AppShell, PageHeader, BottomNav

## Examples

### Contextual header

```tsx
import { AppHeader, Button, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<AppHeader leading={<Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label="Back"><Icon name="chevron-left" /></Button>} title="Notifications" />
```

### Choosing between AppHeader and PageHeader

```tsx
import { AppHeader, AppShell, PageHeader, Region } from "@sableui/react"

// AppHeader is APP chrome — it persists across routes and holds global
// affordances (brand, search, account). One per app.
<AppShell header={<AppHeader title="Studio" />}>
  <Region max="content">Route content</Region>
</AppShell>

// PageHeader is CONTENT — it introduces the current route and scrolls away
// with it. One per page, INSIDE the region.
<Region max="content">
  <PageHeader title="Billing" description="Plans, invoices, payment methods." />
</Region>

// ✗ Putting route-specific actions in AppHeader. They then persist onto routes
//   where they mean nothing, and the header becomes a dumping ground.
```

---

# AppShell

**Status:** stable

The application frame: slots for status banners, a mobile header, a desktop sidebar, main content, a mobile bottom nav, and floating overlays — plus a built-in skip link and #main-content target.

**Keywords:** app shell, layout, frame, sidebar, header, bottom nav, mobile, banners, main

## Usage

Use AppShell as the outer product frame for authenticated or app-like experiences. It coordinates responsive chrome slots and guarantees a skip link plus main landmark; put route content inside the children and let AppHeader, Sidebar, BottomNav, and Banner own their own semantics.

### Best practices

- Do: Use AppShell once around the route tree or major app area so the skip link and main landmark stay stable.
- Do: Pass app-wide outage or status messages through banners so they remain above the frame.
- Do: Use Region inside the main content to choose each route's reading width.
- Do: Wrap EVERY return of a route in its own Page or Region — including early returns for loading, empty and error states. AppShell's <main> deliberately carries no padding (it is a frame, and padding belongs to the region that chose the width), so a route that returns a bare spinner or error renders flush against the chrome. This is the most common conversion bug: the happy path gets a Page, the three early returns do not.
- Don't: Nest AppShell inside route cards or panels. It is page chrome, not local content.
- Don't: Put desktop-only navigation in the mobile header slot or mobile-only controls in the sidebar slot.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Banners | no | Full-width app status messages rendered above the shell. |
| Header | no | Mobile top chrome, usually AppHeader. |
| Sidebar | no | Desktop navigation chrome, usually Sidebar. |
| Main | yes | The route content landmark with id main-content. |
| Bottom nav | no | Mobile fixed navigation with reserved bottom space. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| banners | ReactNode | — | Full-width status banners pinned in flow above the frame (offline / chain-down). |
| header | ReactNode | — | Mobile top header (e.g. AppHeader); expected to hide itself at lg. |
| sidebar | ReactNode | — | Desktop side navigation (e.g. Sidebar); expected to hide itself below lg. Leading column of the body row. |
| bottomNav | ReactNode | — | Mobile bottom navigation (e.g. BottomNav); fixed to the bottom edge. main reserves space for it. |
| overlays | ReactNode | — | Floating overlays — a message launcher, FAB, or modal mount points. |

## Tokens used

`background`, `foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders a skip link to #main-content as the first focusable element.
- Wraps content in a <main id="main-content"> landmark.
- Slot components own their own ARIA (nav landmarks, labels).

## Related

- Components: AppHeader, Sidebar, SideNav, BottomNav, Banner
- Patterns: DashboardPage, FeedPage, SettingsPage

## Examples

### Full frame

```tsx
import { AppHeader, AppShell, Banner, BottomNav, BottomNavItem, Icon, PageHeader, Region, Sidebar, SidebarItem, SidebarNav } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<AppShell
  banners={<Banner tone="warning">Network congested — mints may be slow.</Banner>}
  header={<AppHeader title="Studio" />}
  sidebar={
    <Sidebar>
      <SidebarNav>
        <SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="home" />} label="Home" active render={<Link to="/" />} />
        <SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Notifications" render={<Link to="/notifications" />} />
        <SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="gear" />} label="Settings" render={<Link to="/settings" />} />
      </SidebarNav>
    </Sidebar>
  }
  bottomNav={
    <BottomNav>
      <BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="home" />} label="Home" active render={<Link to="/" />} />
      <BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Alerts" render={<Link to="/notifications" />} />
    </BottomNav>
  }
>
  <Region max="feed">
    <PageHeader title="Home" description="Latest posts from artists you follow." />
  </Region>
</AppShell>
```

### Minimal (sidebar + content only)

```tsx
import { AppShell, Icon, PageHeader, Region, Sidebar, SidebarItem, SidebarNav } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<AppShell
  sidebar={
    <Sidebar>
      <SidebarNav>
        <SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="home" />} label="Dashboard" active render={<Link to="/" />} />
      </SidebarNav>
    </Sidebar>
  }
>
  <Region max="wide">
    <PageHeader title="Dashboard" />
  </Region>
</AppShell>
```

### Route content width

```tsx
import { AppShell, Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle, Field, Icon, Input, PageHeader, Region, Sidebar, SidebarItem, SidebarNav } from "@sableui/react"

<AppShell sidebar={<Sidebar><SidebarNav><SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="home" />} label="Home" active /></SidebarNav></Sidebar>}><Region max="content"><PageHeader title="Settings" description="Manage account and workspace preferences." /><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Profile</CardTitle></CardHeader><CardContent><Field label="Display name"><Input defaultValue="Nova" /></Field></CardContent></Card></Region></AppShell>
```

---

# Attachment

**Status:** stable

A file or image attached to a message: media or icon lead, name and metadata, upload and error states, an actions slot, and a full-card trigger that keeps those actions separately clickable.

**Keywords:** attachment, file, upload, image preview, chat file, document, drag and drop, file card

## Usage

The card a file takes in a conversation — in the composer while it uploads, and in the transcript once it has. It renders all four states an attachment actually moves through (queued, uploading, failed, delivered) rather than only the delivered one, because the other three are the states that are hard to get right and would otherwise fall back on every caller.

### Best practices

- Do: Use `variant="media"` for images and `variant="card"` for documents. A filename tells you nothing about a photo, and a thumbnail tells you nothing about a contract.
- Do: Pass `onOpen` rather than wrapping the card in your own button. It renders a stretched trigger underneath the actions, so the card is one tab stop, each action is its own, and clicking "remove" never opens the file.
- Do: Give `status="uploading"` a numeric `progress` when you have one and omit it when you do not — the bar goes indeterminate rather than lying about 0%.
- Do: Put the reason in `meta` when `status="error"`. The card re-colors but keeps its shape, so a failed upload stays recognisable as the file it was — the text is what says why.
- Don't: Do not nest interactive controls inside a card you have wrapped in a link or button yourself. That is invalid HTML and unreachable in the order it looks like; `onOpen` exists to avoid it.
- Don't: Do not use it as a generic file-list row. `Tree` is the file listing; this one is shaped for a conversation, where an attachment is a message payload.
- Don't: Do not rely on the error colour alone to signal failure. Colour is not a status for anyone who cannot see it — say what happened in `meta`.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Media | yes | Thumbnail crop or file glyph. Fills the tile in `media`, a lead square in `card`. |
| Label | yes | Name and metadata. A row beside the media in `card`; a scrim strip over the picture in `media`, shown only when there is something to say. |
| Actions | no | Remove / retry / download controls, stacked above the stretched trigger so they stay separately clickable. |
| Progress | no | A hairline bar along the bottom edge while `status="uploading"`; determinate with `progress`, indeterminate without. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | string | — | File name. Truncated rather than wrapped — the stem truncates and a short extension stays visible — and used as the default label for the stretched trigger and the media tile's alt text. |
| meta | ReactNode | — | Size, type, upload progress, or the failure reason — the quiet second line. |
| thumbnail | string | — | Image preview URL. Present means the card shows a crop of the file instead of a glyph. |
| icon | string | "file" | Semantic icon name for a non-image file (resolved through IconProvider). Defaults to "image-stack" when a thumbnail is set. |
| variant | "card" \| "media" | "card" | `card` is a name-led horizontal row for documents; `media` is a square tile that is mostly picture. |
| status | "idle" \| "uploading" \| "error" | "idle" | Transfer state. `uploading` adds a progress bar; `error` re-colors the card without changing its shape. |
| progress | number | — | Percentage 0–100 while uploading. Omit for an indeterminate bar. |
| actions | ReactNode | — | Remove / retry / download controls. Stay clickable when `onOpen` makes the card a trigger. On a `media` tile they float on the top-end corner over the picture, so pass `variant="floating"` buttons there. |
| onOpen | () => void | — | Makes the whole card activate, via a stretched button rendered beneath the actions rather than by wrapping the card. |
| openLabel | string | `Open ${name}` | Accessible label for that stretched trigger. |
| ...div props | Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<"div">, "onClick"> | — | Spread onto the card. Use `onOpen` rather than `onClick` — a click handler on a div is not a control. |

## Variants

- **variant**: card, media
- **status**: idle, uploading, error

## Tokens used

`card`, `border`, `border-strong`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `destructive`, `overlay`, `overlay-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- The full-card trigger is a real stretched `<button>` with an accessible label, not a click handler on a div — so it is one tab stop, keyboard-activatable, and focus-ringed.
- Actions sit above that trigger in the stacking order, which keeps them individually focusable and stops a click on `remove` from also opening the file. Text is only made click-through when a trigger is present, so a filename stays selectable otherwise.
- A thumbnail is described as the attachment in `media` (where the picture is the only label) and left decorative in `card` (where the filename is right beside it), so AT never reads the same name twice.
- The upload bar carries an accessible name via Progress; the error state is carried by text in `meta` as well as colour.
- Label text on a media tile sits on `overlay` / `overlay-foreground` — a fixed pairing that stays legible over arbitrary imagery, where a theme surface token would not.

## Related

- Components: Message, Bubble, MessageScroller, Progress

## Examples

### Document with a remove action

```tsx
import { Attachment, Button, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Attachment name="proposal.pdf" meta="2.4 MB · PDF" onOpen={() => open(file)} actions={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-xs" aria-label="Remove"><Icon name="xmark" /></Button>} />
```

### Image tile, uploading

```tsx
import { Attachment } from "@sableui/react"

<Attachment variant="media" name="cover.png" thumbnail={previewUrl} status="uploading" progress={62} meta="Uploading… 62%" />
```

### Failed upload with a retry

```tsx
import { Attachment, Button } from "@sableui/react"

<Attachment name="recording.mov" meta="Upload failed — file is over the 50 MB limit" status="error" icon="warning" actions={<Button variant="ghost" size="xs" onClick={retry}>Retry</Button>} />
```

### Attachments as a message payload

```tsx
import { Attachment, Message, RelativeTime } from "@sableui/react"

<Message messageId="m7" align="end" footer={<RelativeTime date={sentAt} />}>
	<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
		{files.map((f) => (<Attachment key={f.id} variant="media" name={f.name} thumbnail={f.url} onOpen={() => open(f)} />))}
	</div>
</Message>
```

# Avatar

**Status:** stable

Circular profile image over Base UI Avatar — automatic image-load tracking with an initials/glyph fallback. Ergonomic Avatar plus low-level AvatarRoot/AvatarImage/AvatarFallback parts, and AvatarGroup for an overlapping stack with a "+N" overflow count.

**Keywords:** avatar, profile, user, identity, initials, fallback, group, team, stack, overflow, collaborators, facepile

## Usage

Use Avatar to represent a person, team, or account with a compact visual identity. Wrap several in AvatarGroup for collaborators, assignees, or attendees — it overlaps them, rings each in the surface colour, and collapses the rest into a "+N" count; use the low-level parts only when you need custom image/fallback layout.

### Best practices

- Do: Provide meaningful alt text for profile images, or an empty alt when the adjacent text already names the person.
- Do: Use initials or a simple glyph fallback so missing images still communicate identity.
- Do: Use consistent sizes within a group; reserve lg for profile headers or major identity moments.
- Do: Use AvatarGroup for a stack of people, and give it an aria-label with the real count ("12 collaborators"). Set `surface` (or `--avatar-group-ring`) to whatever the group sits on, so the separating ring matches a card or popover, not the page. When it shares a row with actions, set `fit` so it gives up avatars to the "+N" count before the row has to wrap.
- Don't: Hand-build a stack with negative margins and per-avatar ring classes, or fake the overflow as an Avatar with "+4" initials — screen readers hear "plus 4" with no context. Use AvatarGroup's `max`/`total`, or AvatarGroupCount.
- Don't: Use avatars as decoration without nearby identity context. They should help users recognize a person or account.
- Don't: Overload a dense table with large avatars; use sm or omit images when scanning data is more important.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root | yes | The circular frame that clips the image, owns size, and contains image plus fallback. |
| Image | no | The loaded profile image, cropped to fill the root. |
| Fallback | yes | Initials, a glyph, or short text shown while loading, on error, or when no image exists. |
| Group | no | AvatarGroup: the overlapping stack. Sets one size for every avatar and rings each in the surface colour. |
| Count | no | AvatarGroupCount: the "+N" avatar ending a group, read as "and N more". Rendered automatically by `max`/`total`. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AvatarRoot | Base UI Avatar.Root props + size + className | Low-level circular frame for full composition control — clips the image and holds the `size` axis. Wraps AvatarImage and AvatarFallback. |
| AvatarImage | Base UI Avatar.Image props + className | The profile image. Fills and crops the frame; hidden by Base UI until it loads. |
| AvatarFallback | Base UI Avatar.Fallback props (delay) + className | Shown when no image is available — typically initials or a glyph. Accepts a delay prop. |
| AvatarGroup | { size?: "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"; surface?: "background" \| "card" \| "popover" \| "muted"; max?: number; fit?: boolean; total?: number; countLabel?: (count: number) => string; "aria-label"?: string; className?: string; children: ReactNode } | Overlapping stack (role=group) — name it with aria-label ("12 collaborators"). `size` applies to every avatar inside. `max` shows that many and collapses the rest into a "+N" count; `total` is the real head-count when you only pass some people. `fit` shows only as many avatars as fit the width the group is given (it fills the space left in a flex row) and folds the rest into the count, so a tight row reads "MO SR +5" instead of wrapping. The separating ring reads the inherited `--avatar-group-ring` (default: the page background); `surface` sets it to card, popover, or muted. |
| AvatarGroupCount | { count: number; label?: string; size?: "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"; className?: string } | The "+N" avatar. Shows "+4" and reads "and 4 more" (override with label). AvatarGroup renders it for you from max/total; use it directly only when composing the stack yourself. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| src | string | — | Image source. When omitted, still loading, or failed, the fallback shows. |
| alt | string | "" | Alt text for the image. Without an image it becomes the avatar's accessible name (role=img), so the initials are never read out as the name. |
| fallback | ReactNode | — | Initials or a glyph rendered when no image is displayed. |
| fallbackDelay | number | — | Delay before showing the fallback, in ms — avoids a flash on fast loads. |
| status | ReactNode | — | A presence indicator pinned to the bottom-end edge, usually <StatusDot tone="success" />. It sits outside the clipped circle and wears a ring in the surface colour (--avatar-group-ring, else the page background). Use this instead of absolutely positioning a dot over an Avatar. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Square footprint: 32px / 40px / 48px. |

## Variants

- **size**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`muted`, `muted-foreground`, `background`, `card`, `popover`

## Accessibility

- Base UI tracks the image loading status and swaps to the fallback on missing/loading/error — no manual onError wiring.
- Provide meaningful alt text via the alt prop; pass an empty alt for decorative avatars.
- The fallback (initials/glyph) gives a non-image identity cue for screen readers and slow connections.
- AvatarGroup renders role=group; give it an aria-label naming the whole set ("12 collaborators"), since the visible stack only shows some of them.
- The "+N" count is hidden from screen readers and replaced by "and N more" (AvatarGroupCount `label`, or AvatarGroup `countLabel`).

## Related

- Components: Entity, StatusDot, Badge, Row
- Patterns: DashboardPage, ListDetailPage

## Examples

### With image

```tsx
import { Avatar } from "@sableui/react"

<Avatar src="/pfp.png" alt="Alex Morgan" fallback="AM" />
```

### Fallback only

```tsx
import { Avatar } from "@sableui/react"

<Avatar fallback="AM" alt="Alex Morgan" />
```

### Sizes

```tsx
import { Avatar } from "@sableui/react"

<Avatar src="/pfp.png" alt="Alex Morgan" fallback="AM" size="sm" />
<Avatar src="/pfp.png" alt="Alex Morgan" fallback="AM" size="md" />
<Avatar src="/pfp.png" alt="Alex Morgan" fallback="AM" size="lg" />
```

### Low-level parts

```tsx
import { AvatarFallback, AvatarImage, AvatarRoot } from "@sableui/react"

<AvatarRoot size="lg"><AvatarImage src="/pfp.png" alt="Mara Okafor" /><AvatarFallback>MO</AvatarFallback></AvatarRoot>
```

### Group with overflow

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<AvatarGroup aria-label="6 collaborators" max={3} size="sm" surface="card"><Avatar src="/ana.png" alt="Ana Chen" fallback="AC" /><Avatar src="/mika.png" alt="Mika Lee" fallback="ML" /><Avatar fallback="JL" alt="Jo Lund" /><Avatar fallback="AK" alt="Ari Kim" /><Avatar fallback="SR" alt="Sam Reyes" /><Avatar fallback="MO" alt="Mo Ortiz" /></AvatarGroup>
```

### Group of a larger set

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<AvatarGroup aria-label="12 attendees" total={12} countLabel={(n) => `and ${n} more attendees`}><Avatar fallback="MO" alt="Mo Ortiz" /><Avatar fallback="SR" alt="Sam Reyes" /><Avatar fallback="JL" alt="Jo Lund" /></AvatarGroup>
```

### Composed count

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount } from "@sableui/react"

<AvatarGroup aria-label="7 reviewers"><Avatar fallback="AC" alt="Ana Chen" /><Avatar fallback="ML" alt="Mika Lee" /><AvatarGroupCount count={5} label="and 5 more reviewers" /></AvatarGroup>
```

### With status

```tsx
import { Avatar, Entity, StatusDot } from "@sableui/react"

<Entity leading={<Avatar src="/pfp.png" alt="Nova Reed" fallback="NR" status={<StatusDot tone="success" />} />} title="Nova Reed" subtitle="Online" />
```

# Badge

**Status:** stable

Compact static label, set on two axes: appearance (soft, outline, solid, overlay on media, plain text) and tone (neutral or a semantic tone). An optional leading icon, or a status dot (with pulse) for state.

**Keywords:** badge, tag, label, status, metadata, chip, pill, tone, category

## Usage

Use Badge for any short static label: metadata, categories, tone-coded labels, a label on artwork (appearance="overlay"), or a status line (appearance="plain" with dot). Use Pill for a chip someone clicks, NotificationBadge for an unread count on an icon, and Banner or Toast for messages that need attention.

### Best practices

- Do: Keep badge text short: one to three words or a compact count.
- Do: Use tone variants when the badge carries meaning, such as success, warning, destructive, edition, or collectible.
- Do: Pair icons with text; the icon reinforces meaning but should not be the only cue.
- Do: Choose appearance and tone separately: appearance is how loud it is (soft by default, solid for emphasis, overlay on images, plain for a status line); tone is what it means.
- Don't: Use a Badge as a button. If it triggers an action, use Button, Toggle, or a menu item.
- Don't: Stack many loud tone badges in one row; too many semantic colors compete with the actual content.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container | yes | The compact pill surface carrying the tone or neutral treatment. |
| Label | yes | Short visible text that names the category, state, role, or metadata value. |
| Icon | no | Optional leading Icon used to reinforce the label. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| appearance | "soft" \| "outline" \| "solid" \| "overlay" \| "plain" | "soft" | How it is drawn. soft: a tinted fill (neutral is the secondary surface). outline: a hairline. solid: the tone at full strength (neutral is the inverted chip). overlay: legible on images — a dark scrim, or the solid tone. plain: no fill or padding, a status line. |
| tone | "neutral" \| "standard" \| "collectible" \| "edition" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" | "neutral" | What it means. Every appearance takes every tone. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" | "md" | "sm" uses tighter padding + text-label-sm; "md" is the default look. |
| icon | ReactNode | — | Optional leading glyph (e.g. <Icon name="lock" />), rendered before the children with the base gap. Ignored when dot is set. |
| dot | boolean | false | A leading status dot in the badge's tone. With appearance="plain" it is a status line (● Ready). |
| pulse | boolean | false | Pulse the dot, for a state in progress. Needs dot. |

## Variants

- **appearance**: soft, outline, solid, overlay, plain
- **tone**: neutral, standard, collectible, edition, info, success, warning, destructive
- **size**: sm, md

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `border`, `foreground`, `background`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `tone-standard`, `tone-collectible`, `tone-edition`, `tone-info`, `success`, `tone-warning`, `destructive`, `overlay`, `overlay-foreground`, `tone-standard-foreground`, `tone-collectible-foreground`, `tone-edition-foreground`, `tone-info-foreground`, `success-foreground`, `tone-warning-foreground`, `destructive-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Badges are static text by default; do not rely on color alone for meaning.
- Use clear label text for semantic tones so assistive tech receives the same status information sighted users see.

## Related

- Components: Pill, StatusDot, NotificationBadge, Banner, Toast
- Patterns: DashboardPage, ListDetailPage

## Examples

### Tones

```tsx
import { Badge, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Badge tone="edition">Edition</Badge><Badge tone="collectible">Collectible</Badge><Badge tone="standard">Standard</Badge></Row>
```

### Solid

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@sableui/react"

<Badge appearance="solid" size="sm">Admin</Badge>
```

### Success

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@sableui/react"

<Badge tone="success">Resolved</Badge>
```

### With icon

```tsx
import { Badge, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Badge size="sm" icon={<Icon name="lock" />}>Locked</Badge>
```

### Small

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@sableui/react"

<Badge size="sm" tone="info">New</Badge>
```

### Metadata row

```tsx
import { Badge, Icon, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Badge>12 editions</Badge><Badge appearance="outline">Open edition</Badge><Badge tone="info" icon={<Icon name="info" />}>Curated</Badge></Row>
```

### Semantic state

```tsx
import { Badge, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Badge tone="success">Synced</Badge><Badge tone="warning">Review</Badge><Badge tone="destructive">Blocked</Badge></Row>
```

# Banner

**Status:** stable

Full-width, page-level announcement bar. A tone (neutral, info, success, warning, edition, destructive) × an appearance (soft tint or loud solid fill), and an optional leading scope label. Centers its message, or — with a trailing action — switches to a leading-text + trailing-button layout. Optionally sticky and dismissible.

**Keywords:** banner, announcement, alert, status, message, warning, success, offline, sticky

## Usage

Use Banner for page-level or app-level messages that affect the current experience: outages, maintenance, success confirmations, policy notices, or major warnings. Prefer Toast for transient feedback from a specific action, and prefer InlineStatus for local row or form state.

### Best practices

- Do: Use soft appearance for contextual notices and solid appearance for urgent, blocking, or system-wide states.
- Do: Set live='polite' or live='assertive' only when the banner appears or changes dynamically.
- Do: Include one clear action when the user can resolve or inspect the state.
- Don't: Use multiple stacked solid banners unless the page is genuinely blocked by multiple independent states.
- Don't: Use Banner for field-level validation, row status, or small local hints; use Field, InlineStatus, or Badge instead.
- Don't: Use Banner inside a dialog, a form, or a section to qualify the content around it — that is Note. Banner is a full-width announcement strip for page- or app-level state, so in a modal it reads as a slab heavier than the fields it warns about, and its soft appearance has no border and no tone-colored icon: the severity survives only as a faint wash.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Message | yes | The short announcement text. It should explain the state in plain language. |
| Action | no | Optional trailing action that changes the layout from centered copy to text plus action. |
| Dismiss | no | Optional close control for notices the user can safely hide. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tone | "neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "edition" \| "destructive" | "neutral" | Neutral surface or a tone that encodes the announcement's intent (info / success / warning / edition / destructive). |
| appearance | "soft" \| "solid" | "soft" | "soft" is a quiet tinted fill; "solid" is the full tone with its paired ink — for loud, can't-miss states (offline, chain-down, RPC errors). |
| label | ReactNode | — | A short scope label ("Preview", "Staging", a project name) in a leading chip — a Badge that reads on soft and solid fills. |
| action | ReactNode | — | A trailing action (e.g. a Button). Switches the bar to leading text + trailing action instead of centered text. |
| sticky | boolean | false | Stick the banner to the top of its scroll container (sticky top-0, z-30). |
| live | "off" \| "polite" \| "assertive" | "off" | ARIA live-region politeness for banners shown/updated at runtime (offline, RPC-down, "N new posts"). "polite" → role=status; "assertive" → role=alert. "off" keeps a static labelled region. |
| dismissible | boolean | false | Render a trailing close button that hides the banner when clicked. |
| onDismiss | () => void | — | Called after the banner is dismissed. |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, info, success, warning, edition, destructive
- **appearance**: soft, solid

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `foreground`, `background`, `tone-info`, `tone-info-foreground`, `success`, `success-foreground`, `tone-warning`, `tone-warning-foreground`, `tone-edition`, `tone-edition-foreground`, `destructive`, `destructive-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Static banners render as a labelled region (role=region); set `live` to announce dynamic status bars (role=status / role=alert) when they appear or change.
- The dismiss control is Button (on-color-ghost, icon-xs) with an aria-label; it takes the bar's own ink, so its glyph and focus ring stay legible on soft and solid fills alike.
- Solid fills pair each tone with its theme-adaptive ink token, so text stays legible in light and dark.

## Related

- Components: Note, AppShell, Toast, InlineStatus, EmptyState, Button
- Patterns: DashboardPage

## Examples

### Tones

```tsx
import { Banner } from "@sableui/react"

<Banner tone="info">Maintenance window tonight at 02:00 UTC.</Banner>
```

### Solid (loud)

```tsx
import { Banner } from "@sableui/react"

<Banner tone="destructive" appearance="solid" live="assertive">Blockchain unavailable. Collect and buy are temporarily disabled.</Banner>
```

### Success

```tsx
import { Banner } from "@sableui/react"

<Banner tone="success" live="polite">Credits authorized for Studio.</Banner>
```

### Action

```tsx
import { Banner, Button } from "@sableui/react"

<Banner sticky action={<Button variant="outline" size="sm">Refresh</Button>}>12 new posts</Banner>
```

### Dismissible

```tsx
import { Banner } from "@sableui/react"

<Banner tone="warning" dismissible>Your session expires soon.</Banner>
```

### Recoverable warning

```tsx
import { Banner, Button } from "@sableui/react"

<Banner tone="warning" action={<Button variant="outline" size="sm">Reconnect</Button>}>Wallet connection paused.</Banner>
```

### App-shell outage

```tsx
import { AppShell, Banner, EmptyState, Region } from "@sableui/react"

<AppShell banners={<Banner tone="destructive" appearance="solid" live="assertive">Uploads are temporarily unavailable.</Banner>}><Region max="feed"><EmptyState title="Uploads paused" description="Existing posts are still visible while the service recovers." /></Region></AppShell>
```

# BottomNav

**Status:** stable

Mobile bottom tab bar (fixed, hidden at lg), with home-indicator safe-area padding and evenly distributed BottomNavItem tabs. Items are router-agnostic via `render`.

**Keywords:** bottom nav, mobile nav, tabs, app navigation

## Usage

Use BottomNav for a small set of top-level mobile destinations that should remain reachable with one thumb. Mount it through `<AppShell bottomNav={…}>` so the content area reserves matching bottom space; it hides at lg, where the Sidebar takes over.

### Best practices

- Do: Limit the nav to the primary destinations users switch between often.
- Do: Give every item a clear label (it is the accessible name), and turn on showLabel when the icons alone are not obvious.
- Don't: Do not use BottomNav for desktop navigation, dense menus, or page-local actions.
- Don't: Do not omit the safe-area padding by overriding its padding-bottom. On a device with a home indicator the last row of targets ends up under the gesture area, where taps dismiss the app instead.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BottomNav | yes | The fixed or anchored navigation container. |
| BottomNavItem | yes | One destination with label, icon, and active state. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BottomNavItem | { label: string; icon?: ReactNode; active?: boolean; badge?: ReactNode; showLabel?: boolean; render?: useRender.RenderProp } + button props | A single tab, placed as a child of BottomNav. `label` is the accessible name (aria-label) and optional visible label; `icon` is the glyph node (consumer swaps fill weight for the active state); `active` marks the current route (active ink + aria-current); `badge` overlays a corner dot/count on the icon; `showLabel` shows the label text beneath the icon — defaults to false (icon-only); turn it on when the icons alone are not self-evident; `render` renders as another element, e.g. render={<Link to="/x" />}. |

## Tokens used

`background`, `border`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- BottomNav renders a <nav> landmark.
- Each tab is a 44px minimum touch target with an aria-label.
- Active tab carries aria-current="page".

## Related

- Components: Sidebar, SideNav, AppHeader

## Examples

### Tab bar

```tsx
import { BottomNav, BottomNavItem, Icon, NotificationBadge } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<BottomNav><BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="home" />} label="Home" active render={<Link to="/" />} /><BottomNavItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Notifications" badge={<NotificationBadge dot />} render={<Link to="/notifications" />} /></BottomNav>
```

### When NOT to use it

```tsx
import { AppShell, BottomNav, BottomNavItem, Icon, Region } from "@sableui/react"

// BottomNav is for 3–5 PEER destinations on a small viewport — the mobile
// counterpart to SideNav, not an action bar.

// ✗ Actions. A bottom bar of verbs (Save / Share / Delete) is a toolbar; it
//   competes with the OS gesture area and has no "current" state to show.
// ✗ More than five items. Past that, labels truncate and targets shrink below
//   the 44px floor — use a "More" destination that opens a Sheet.
// ✗ Nested navigation. BottomNav switches top-level sections only; drilling in
//   happens inside the section, with Breadcrumbs or a back affordance.

<AppShell bottomNav={<BottomNav>
  <BottomNavItem label="Home" icon={<Icon name="home" />} active />
  <BottomNavItem label="Search" icon={<Icon name="search" />} />
  <BottomNavItem label="Account" icon={<Icon name="user" />} />
</BottomNav>}>
  <Region max="feed">Route content</Region>
</AppShell>
```

---

# Breadcrumbs

**Status:** stable

Navigation trail showing the path to the current page. A labelled <nav> wraps an inline <ol> of crumbs — interactive ancestor links, separators, and a non-interactive current page. No Base UI.

**Keywords:** breadcrumbs, hierarchy, path, navigation

## Usage

Use Breadcrumbs to show the user's location inside a hierarchy and provide lightweight parent navigation.

### Best practices

- Do: Use breadcrumbs when users can arrive deep in a nested structure.
- Do: Keep the current page as text so it reads as location, not another link.
- Don't: Do not use breadcrumbs as a substitute for primary navigation or step progress.
- Don't: Do not make the last crumb a link. It points at the page you are already on, and screen readers announce it as a destination; render it as the current page with aria-current.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BreadcrumbItem | yes | A single step in the path. |
| BreadcrumbLink | no | A linked ancestor destination. |
| BreadcrumbPage | yes | The current non-linked page. |
| BreadcrumbSeparator | no | The visual separator between steps. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BreadcrumbItem | ComponentPropsWithRef<'li'> | A single crumb slot (<li>) holding a link or the current page. |
| BreadcrumbLink | ComponentPropsWithRef<'a'> | An interactive ancestor crumb (<a>). Muted by default, brightens to foreground on hover/focus. |
| BreadcrumbPage | ComponentPropsWithRef<'span'> | The current-page crumb (<span aria-current="page">). Non-interactive, full-contrast. |
| BreadcrumbSeparator | ComponentPropsWithRef<'li'> + { children? } | Decorative divider (<li aria-hidden>) between crumbs. Defaults to a chevron-right icon; pass children to swap the glyph. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Breadcrumbs | ComponentPropsWithRef<'nav'> | — | The trail root. Renders <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> around a flex <ol>. Pass the crumb parts as children. |

## Tokens used

`muted-foreground`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- The <nav> carries aria-label="Breadcrumb" so assistive tech announces the landmark.
- Crumbs sit in an ordered list (<ol>) to convey hierarchy and position.
- The current page uses aria-current="page" and is rendered as plain text, not a link.
- Separators are aria-hidden so the chevron glyph is not announced.

## Related

- Components: SideNav, PageHeader

## Examples

### Three-level trail

```tsx
import { BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbPage, Breadcrumbs, BreadcrumbSeparator } from "@sableui/react"

<Breadcrumbs><BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbSeparator /><BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/library">Library</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbSeparator /><BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Editions</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem></Breadcrumbs>
```

### Custom separator

```tsx
import { BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbPage, Breadcrumbs, BreadcrumbSeparator } from "@sableui/react"

<Breadcrumbs><BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbSeparator>/</BreadcrumbSeparator><BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Settings</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem></Breadcrumbs>
```

# Browser

**Status:** stable

A generic, current browser window: one compact toolbar (window controls, back/forward/reload, a centered address field) around page content.

**Keywords:** browser, mockup, preview, website

## Usage

Use Browser to frame a website or product surface preview when the browser chrome is part of the story.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for documentation, product examples, and visual previews where the page context matters.
- Do: Keep the framed content simple enough to remain legible at the rendered size.
- Don't: Do not use Browser for real navigation, real forms, or arbitrary card decoration.
- Don't: Do not put a real, working URL in the address pill. It reads as a link, is not one, and invites a click that does nothing.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| url | string | — | Address shown in the centered address pill. Omit for a blank pill. |
| children | ReactNode | — | Page content rendered inside the content region. |

## Tokens used

`card`, `background`, `border`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Purely presentational chrome; the framed content carries its own semantics.
- The toolbar is drawn, not interactive, and hidden from assistive technology; the address is decorative text.

## Related

- Components: Phone, Card

## Examples

### Framing a page

```tsx
import { Browser, PageHeader } from "@sableui/react"

<Browser url="studio.example/explore"><div className="p-8"><PageHeader title="Explore" description="Trending posts from every chain." /></div></Browser>
```

### Mockup, not chrome

```tsx
import { Browser, Region } from "@sableui/react"

// Browser is DECORATIVE framing for a screenshot or a demo — it belongs on a
// marketing page, never around your actual app.

<Region max="wide">
  <Browser url="studio.example">
    <img src="/screenshots/editor.png" alt="The editor" />
  </Browser>
</Region>

// ✗ Wrapping live UI in it. The frame implies "this is a picture of software";
//   putting real controls inside makes users hunt for a browser that isn't there.
// ✗ Using it to fake a URL bar for credibility. Show the real product.
```

# Bubble

**Status:** stable

The surface a message's content sits on: four treatments, an align-aware tail corner, a readable measure cap, and an optional row of reaction pills.

**Keywords:** chat bubble, message bubble, speech bubble, reactions, conversation, messaging, ai chat

## Usage

The tinted (or untinted) surface a turn's content sits on. Kept separate from Message because the row's layout and the content's surface change independently — an assistant's markdown answer wants no surface at all in exactly the same row a one-line reply wants a bubble.

### Best practices

- Do: Use `muted` for the other party and `primary` for the reader's own messages. Two treatments is the whole vocabulary a conversation needs to say who is speaking.
- Do: Reach for `variant="plain"` for long-form assistant output — rendered markdown, code blocks, tables. A tinted box around three paragraphs reads as a quote block rather than as a turn, and `plain` drops the measure cap with the surface.
- Do: Pass the same `align` you gave the enclosing Message, so the flattened corner lands on the speaker's side.
- Do: Set `tail={false}` on the continuation bubbles in a grouped run — the tail marks where a speaker starts, and repeating it on every line makes a block of one person's messages look like four separate turns.
- Do: Let the register size it. Inside `<Density value="compact">` a Bubble sets itself in the workspace prose tier automatically — a docked agent panel needs no per-call-site sizing, and hardcoding one defeats the mechanism.
- Don't: Do not remove the measure cap to fill a wide window. ~42rem is a reading measure; a bubble spanning a 1600px viewport is a paragraph at 140 characters per line.
- Don't: Do not put the timestamp or the author name inside the bubble. Those are Message's `header` / `footer`, which stay outside the surface and so still work under `variant="plain"`.
- Don't: Do not use a Bubble for a system note or a streaming status. Those are `Marker`, which is deliberately quieter than the message tier.
- Don't: Do not render reactions as static text. `BubbleReaction` is a toggle and reports `aria-pressed`, which is how a screen-reader user knows whether pressing it adds or removes their own reaction.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bubble | yes | The surface itself. Holds the variant, the side, and the flattened tail corner. |
| BubbleReactions | no | The row of reaction pills, just under the bubble at the message column's small gap, so it reads as belonging to that message rather than the next row. |
| BubbleReaction | no | One reaction pill — emoji, count (hidden at 1), and pressed state. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BubbleReactions | { align?: "start" \| "end" } & ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | Row container for reaction pills. Match `align` to the Bubble so the row hangs off the same edge. |
| BubbleReaction | { emoji: ReactNode; count?: number; active?: boolean } & ComponentPropsWithRef<"button"> | One reaction pill. A toggle, not a label: `active` drives `aria-pressed` as well as the styling, and `count` is hidden at 1 because the pill already says "one". |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | "muted" \| "primary" \| "outline" \| "plain" | "muted" | Surface treatment. `muted` for the other party, `primary` for the reader's own messages, `outline` for a quieter own-side, `plain` for long-form output that should not sit in a box (also drops the measure cap and padding). |
| align | "start" \| "end" | "start" | Which side of the conversation the bubble is on — flattens the corner nearest the speaker. Match it to the enclosing Message. |
| tail | boolean | true | Flatten the speaker-side corner. A flattened corner rather than a drawn arrow, so it holds up in every theme's radius language (flat through fully pilled) with no per-theme geometry. Turn it off for the continuation bubbles in a grouped run. |
| ...div props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | — | Spread onto the surface element. |

## Variants

- **variant**: muted, primary, outline, plain
- **align**: start, end
- **tail**: true, false

## Tokens used

`muted`, `foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `border`, `card`, `card-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- The surface is a plain container with no imposed role — a bubble is presentation, and announcing one as a region would put a landmark around every line of a conversation.
- Reaction pills are real buttons reporting `aria-pressed`, so the reader's own reaction is state rather than colour alone; the emoji is hidden from AT and the count is left readable.
- `whitespace-pre-wrap` and `break-words` keep pasted logs, long URLs, and hard-wrapped text inside the surface instead of overflowing the conversation.
- Every variant meets AA against its own surface, including `primary`, which pairs the primary fill with its paired foreground token rather than a hardcoded white.

## Related

- Components: Message, MessageScroller, Marker, Attachment

## Examples

### Two sides

```tsx
import { Bubble, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<>
	<Message messageId="m1"><Bubble>Did the deploy finish?</Bubble></Message>
	<Message messageId="m2" align="end"><Bubble variant="primary" align="end">Green across the board.</Bubble></Message>
</>
```

### Long-form assistant output

```tsx
import { Avatar, Bubble, CodeBlock, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<Message messageId="a1" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="AI" />}>
	<Bubble variant="plain" className="space-y-3">
		<p className="text-body-md text-foreground">Three things changed in this release:</p>
		<CodeBlock code={diff} filename="CHANGELOG.md" />
	</Bubble>
</Message>
```

### With reactions

```tsx
import { Bubble, BubbleReaction, BubbleReactions, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<Message messageId="m3">
	<Bubble>Shipped 0.45.0.</Bubble>
	<BubbleReactions>
		<BubbleReaction emoji="🎉" count={3} active onClick={() => toggle("🎉")} />
		<BubbleReaction emoji="👀" count={1} onClick={() => toggle("👀")} />
	</BubbleReactions>
</Message>
```

### A grouped run drops the repeated tail

```tsx
import { Bubble, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<>
	<Message messageId="m1" align="end"><Bubble variant="primary" align="end">One more thing.</Bubble></Message>
	<Message messageId="m2" align="end" grouped><Bubble variant="primary" align="end" tail={false}>The staging cert expires Friday.</Bubble></Message>
</>
```

# Button

**Status:** stable

Pill-shaped action primitive (theme-driven radius via --button-radius, defaults to full). Neutral tiers (primary/secondary/ghost/outline), plus destructive and link, and three on-color tiers (on-color/on-color-outline/on-color-ghost) that paint with the surrounding ink so a button reads on any tone or brand fill. Optional loading state shows a spinner and disables the button.

**Keywords:** button, action, cta, submit, save, cancel, destructive, loading, link, icon button, on color, inverse, band, brand fill, tone fill

## Usage

Use Button when the user commits an action, submits a form, opens UI, or confirms a decision. Use the visual tier to communicate priority: one primary action per local decision area, then secondary, ghost, outline, or link for lower-emphasis choices.

### Best practices

- Do: Use a single primary button in a view or dense panel so the action hierarchy stays obvious.
- Do: Write labels as actions, such as "Save changes" or "Delete draft", instead of vague labels like "OK".
- Do: Use loading with loadingLabel for async work so the action cannot double-fire and the state is announced.
- Do: Put icons in iconStart / iconEnd rather than as children, so the button applies its optical padding. Start icons say what the action is (plus, share); end icons say where it goes (chevron-right, external).
- Do: On a coloured fill — a solid Banner, a bg-tone-* or bg-primary band, an inverse (bg-foreground) section, a brand panel — use variant="on-color" for the main action and on-color-outline / on-color-ghost for the rest. They paint with the band's inherited ink (currentColor), so the surface must set its paired ink (text-tone-info-foreground, text-primary-foreground, text-background…), which it already should. Name the fill once on the surface, e.g. [--on-color-fill:var(--tone-info)], and the solid button's label takes the fill colour; unnamed, it falls back to black or white against the ink. Both clear 4.5:1 in every shipped theme and mode.
- Don't: Use destructive for reversible or low-risk actions; reserve it for operations with real loss or danger.
- Don't: Use a button for plain navigation. Compose with render={<a />} when the element should behave like a link.
- Don't: Use secondary on a tinted surface — inside a Note, a soft Banner, or any tone fill. `secondary` is a near-background surface token (in some themes within 2% of the page), so on a tint it reads as a hole punched in the fill rather than as a control sitting on it. On a soft tint use outline or ghost; on a full-strength fill use the on-color tiers.
- Don't: Use the on-color tiers on the page, a Card, a Note, or a soft tint — there the ink is the page foreground and the normal tiers already fit. And don't restyle a normal variant with bg-*/text-* classNames to make it read on a band; that hard-codes colours per theme and skips the contrast and focus handling on-color carries.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container | yes | The rounded hit target that carries the visual tier, focus ring, disabled state, and loading affordance. |
| Label | yes | Visible action text and the default accessible name. Icon-only buttons still need an aria-label. |
| Leading icon | no | An optional semantic Icon that reinforces the label without replacing it. |
| Spinner | no | Displayed during loading and paired with aria-busy plus disabled activation. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | "primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "outline" \| "destructive" \| "link" \| "floating" \| "on-color" \| "on-color-outline" \| "on-color-ghost" | "primary" | Visual emphasis tier. One primary per screen. The on-color tiers are for buttons ON a coloured fill: they paint with the inherited text colour (the fill's ink) — on-color is solid (ink background, fill-coloured label via the optional --on-color-fill var, else black/white), on-color-outline and on-color-ghost are transparent with an ink label. Never use them on page or card surfaces. floating is for a control that sits OVER content (carousel arrows, a marquee pause, a jump-to-latest over a conversation): its own edge, lift and translucent popover fill, so it reads on arbitrary content beneath. |
| size | "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "cta" \| "icon" \| "icon-sm" \| "icon-xs" | "md" | Reads the density ladder, so every value differs by register: page 28/32/40/44, workspace 24/28/32/36. xs and icon-xs were added in 0.31.0 for the workspace control floor and are the sizes tool chrome wants; md is the default everywhere. icon/icon-sm/icon-xs are square. |
| render | ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement | — | Compose with another element/component through the Base UI render prop. |
| loading | boolean | false | Disable the button and show a leading Spinner while an action is in flight. Sets aria-busy; a native button is disabled, a render element (e.g. an <a>) gets aria-disabled. |
| badge | ReactNode | — | A corner indicator (usually <NotificationBadge dot /> or a count) overlaid on the top-end corner of the glyph. For icon-only sizes; never hand-position a badge over a Button with absolute offsets. |
| loadingLabel | ReactNode | — | Optional text shown in place of children while loading. |
| iconStart | ReactNode | — | Icon before the label. The button takes one 2px step off its start padding so icon + label read as centred. Replaced by the spinner while loading. |
| iconEnd | ReactNode | — | Icon after the label (disclosure, external link, next). Same optical correction on the end side. |

## Variants

- **variant**: primary, secondary, ghost, outline, destructive, link, floating, on-color, on-color-outline, on-color-ghost
- **size**: xs, sm, md, cta, icon, icon-sm, icon-xs

## Tokens used

`primary`, `primary-foreground`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `input`, `destructive`, `destructive-foreground`, `ring`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — A button belongs to the layout it ships in. Whatever staged that region owns the entrance; a button that fades in on its own is a button that is briefly un-clickable for no stated reason.
- **response** · Root · `motion-interactive` — Hover, focus ring and disabled fade all ease on one declaration. This is the reference case for the whole recipe: it lists scale and translate alongside the colours specifically so motion-press can add a transform without a second, conflicting transition-property.
- **response** · Root · `motion-press` — The 0.97 settle on pointer-down is the only confirmation the press registered before the action's own result arrives — which on a slow network is the difference between waiting and clicking again. It skips disabled elements, so a dead button stays visibly dead.
- **transition** · Root · _no motion_ — A button has no state of its own to move between. A control that toggles is a Switch or a Toggle, and those carry the transition.
- **activity** · Root · _no motion_ — Pending work is passed in via `loading`, which renders a Spinner — the activity motion lives there rather than being duplicated here.

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <button> by default (keyboard + role free).
- Focus-visible ring uses the --ring token at 50% opacity.
- Use render={<a/>} for link semantics rather than onClick navigation.
- On-color tiers replace the --ring focus ring with one drawn in the band's ink past a transparent 2px gap, so focus stays visible on any fill (ink-on-fill is the theme's own tested pair).
- On-color contrast is measured in button.test.tsx for every shipped theme and mode on each tone, primary, destructive, success, highlight and inverse fill: solid label at rest and hover, and outline/ghost label on the hover wash, all at least 4.5:1.
- loading sets aria-busy and disables activation (disabled on a native button, aria-disabled on a render element) so the action can't double-fire.

## Related

- Components: Menu, DotsMenu, Icon, Banner
- Patterns: SettingsPage, AuthPage, DashboardPage

## Examples

### Primary

```tsx
import { Button } from "@sableui/react"

<Button>Collect</Button>
```

### Secondary + ghost

```tsx
import { Button, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button><Button variant="ghost">Skip</Button></Row>
```

### Loading

```tsx
import { Button } from "@sableui/react"

<Button loading loadingLabel="Saving…">Save</Button>
```

### Main action with options

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, Menu, MenuContent, MenuItem, MenuTrigger, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={2}><Button onClick={deploy}>Deploy</Button><Menu><MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" size="icon" aria-label="Deploy options"><Icon name="chevron-down" /></Button>} /><MenuContent align="end"><MenuItem>Deploy to preview</MenuItem><MenuItem>Deploy to production</MenuItem></MenuContent></Menu></Row>
```

### Copy to clipboard

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, useCopy } from "@sableui/react"

const { copy, copied } = useCopy(address)
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Copy address" onClick={copy}><Icon name={copied ? "check" : "copy"} /></Button>
```

### As link

```tsx
import { Button } from "@sableui/react"

<Button render={<a href="/explore" />}>Explore</Button>
```

### Primary + secondary decision row

```tsx
import { Button, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Button>Publish</Button><Button variant="secondary">Save draft</Button><Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button></Row>
```

### Destructive with confirmation copy

```tsx
import { Button, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button><Button variant="destructive">Delete edition</Button></Row>
```

### Leading icon

```tsx
import { Button, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Button iconStart={<Icon name="plus" />}>New project</Button>
```

### Trailing icon

```tsx
import { Button, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Button variant="secondary" iconEnd={<Icon name="chevron-right" />}>Continue</Button>
```

### Both icons

```tsx
import { Button, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Button variant="outline" iconStart={<Icon name="file" />} iconEnd={<Icon name="chevron-down" />}>Export</Button>
```

### Icon-only

```tsx
import { Button, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label="Share"><Icon name="share" /></Button>
```

### Icon button with an unread badge

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, NotificationBadge } from "@sableui/react"

<Button size="icon" variant="ghost" aria-label="Notifications" badge={<NotificationBadge dot />}><Icon name="bell" /></Button>
```

### On a coloured band

```tsx
import { Button } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="flex gap-3 bg-tone-info p-6 text-tone-info-foreground [--on-color-fill:var(--tone-info)]"><Button variant="on-color">Join the beta</Button><Button variant="on-color-outline">Read the notes</Button></div>
```

### Action in a solid Banner

```tsx
import { Banner, Button } from "@sableui/react"

<Banner tone="warning" appearance="solid" action={<Button variant="on-color" size="sm">Reconnect</Button>}>Wallet connection paused.</Banner>
```

# Calendar

**Status:** stable

Date picker grid wrapping react-day-picker v9, themed entirely with semantic tokens (no external stylesheet). Supports single, multiple, and range selection; nav chevrons render through the injected icon set.

**Keywords:** calendar, date grid, month, schedule

## Usage

Use Calendar to browse or choose dates in a month grid, especially when relative date position matters.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it when users need to compare weekdays, ranges, or nearby dates.
- Do: Provide selected, disabled, and today states when date choice is interactive.
- Don't: Do not use Calendar when a compact DatePicker (with granularity="minute" for a time) would be faster.
- Don't: Do not use it as the only way to enter a date. A grid is slow for a date far from today and unusable for someone who knows the value — always pair it with a text input.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode | "single" \| "multiple" \| "range" | — | Selection behavior. Pair with the matching selected/onSelect shape (Date, Date[], or DateRange). |
| selected | Date \| Date[] \| DateRange \| undefined | — | The controlled selection. Shape follows mode. |
| onSelect | (value, triggerDate, modifiers, event) => void | — | Fires when a day is chosen. The first argument's type follows mode. |
| defaultMonth | Date | — | The month shown on first render (uncontrolled navigation). |
| month | Date | — | Controlled displayed month; pair with onMonthChange. |
| numberOfMonths | number | 1 | How many month grids to render side by side. |
| disabled | Matcher \| Matcher[] | — | Days matching this are dimmed and non-selectable (e.g. { before: new Date() }). |
| showOutsideDays | boolean | true | Render leading/trailing days from adjacent months, dimmed. |
| bare | boolean | false | Drop the card frame (border, fill, padding) so the grid sits flush inside a surface that already has one, such as a Popover. DatePicker renders its Calendar this way. |
| className | string | — | Merged onto the bordered card container that wraps the grid. |
| classNames | Partial<ClassNames> | — | Per-part class overrides merged over the themed defaults. Themed slots: months, month, nav, button_previous, button_next, month_caption, caption_label, month_grid, weekdays, weekday, week, day, day_button, range_start, range_middle, range_end, selected, today, outside, disabled, hidden. Selection/state slots (selected/today/range_*/outside/disabled) style the day CELL; the inner day button is targeted via the [&>button] descendant. |
| components | Partial<CustomComponents> | — | Render overrides for RDP parts. Chevron is supplied by default and merged with yours. |

## Variants

- **mode**: single, multiple, range

## Tokens used

`card`, `card-foreground`, `border`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- react-day-picker manages the roving-tabindex grid, arrow-key navigation, and ARIA roles/labels for the calendar.
- Selected days use bg-primary/text-primary-foreground for AA contrast; today is marked with a dot under the number (not a ring, which is reserved for keyboard focus) rather than color alone.
- Disabled and outside days are dimmed and removed from the tab order.
- Nav chevrons resolve through the injected IconProvider; ensure chevron-left and chevron-right are registered in the icon set.

## Related

- Components: DatePicker

## Examples

### Single date

```tsx
import { Calendar } from "@sableui/react"

const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>()
<Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />
```

### Range

```tsx
import { Calendar } from "@sableui/react"
import type { DateRange } from "react-day-picker"

const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange>()
<Calendar mode="range" selected={range} onSelect={setRange} numberOfMonths={2} />
```

# Card

**Status:** stable

Raised surface container (rounded-lg) with optional Header/Title/Description/Action/Content/Footer parts. A density knob trades the part padding (comfortable vs compact) for denser section panels. `render` makes the whole card one link or button, with a hover, a full-card focus ring and motion.

**Keywords:** card, surface, panel, container, tile, section, header, footer, settings, link card, clickable card, nav card

## Usage

Use Card for a discrete thing with its own boundary, such as one product, one notification, one metric, or one setting cluster. Do not use Card as the default way to group every page section; whitespace, headings, Stack, Section, and dividers often create cleaner hierarchy.

### Best practices

- Do: Use Card when the item could be reordered, removed, selected, or compared independently.
- Do: Keep sibling cards on the same density and padding rhythm so lists and grids scan cleanly.
- Do: Use CardHeader, CardContent, and CardFooter when the card has a stable title/body/action structure.
- Do: Make the whole card one link (`render={<a href="…" />}`) when the card IS a single destination — a nav tile, a gallery item, a news teaser — and nothing inside it is interactive. All of the card text becomes the accessible name of the link, so keep it short: a title and a line.
- Don't: Make a card a link when it holds its own buttons, menus, switches or links. Interactive content nested in a link is invalid HTML and announces twice; keep the card a plain surface and put the link on its title or in CardFooter instead.
- Don't: Wrap every settings section or form group in a card; use headings, Stack, or the SettingsPage pattern instead.
- Don't: Nest cards inside cards. Flatten the hierarchy or use dividers and spacing inside one card.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container | yes | The raised or flat surface that creates the item boundary. |
| Header | no | Optional title, description, and aligned action area for the card's identity. |
| Content | yes | The body region. It should contain the information or controls that belong to this one item. |
| Footer | no | Optional action or metadata row, usually lower-emphasis than the header. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CardHeader | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | Top section holding CardTitle/CardDescription (and optionally CardAction). Padding follows the density knob. |
| CardTitle | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | The card's name (text-title-lg). |
| CardDescription | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | Muted supporting line under the title. |
| CardAction | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | Header-aligned top-right action slot (e.g. a dots menu, switch, or close button). Place inside CardHeader, which becomes a 2-column grid when present and collapses to a single column otherwise. |
| CardContent | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> & { flush?: boolean } | The body region. Padding follows the density knob on all sides — does not assume a preceding CardHeader, so it is safe to use standalone (e.g. no CardHeader in the card). When paired with CardHeader, the seam stays tight because CardHeader zeroes its own bottom padding. `flush` runs it edge to edge for a table: the Table insets its first and last columns by exactly the card padding, so it lines up with the header — never hand-set pl-6/pr-6 on columns. |
| CardList | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | Rows that run edge to edge in the card (Entity rows, most often), divided by hairlines. Insets each row to the card's own padding, so a list card lines up with every other card at any density — no hand-tuned px-* on the rows. Under a CardHeader it opens with a hairline and a gap; alone it fills the card. |
| CardFooter | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | Bottom row for actions/meta. Padding follows the density knob. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | "default" \| "flat" | "default" | "default" raises with bg-card + border + soft shadow; "flat" is transparent. |
| density | "comfortable" \| "compact" | "comfortable" | Padding of the Header/Content/Footer parts: comfortable = p-6 (default), compact = p-4 for denser section panels (pair compact with the flat variant for a settings / form section panel). Threaded to the parts via the inherited --card-p custom property. Card sets --card-p via inline style, which beats a plain (non-!important) stylesheet override of the same property on the same element — use this prop rather than a className override; if an external override is unavoidable, it needs !important. |
| render | useRender.RenderProp | — | Replace the rendered element through the Base UI render prop — most often `render={<a href="/x" />}` (or a router Link) to make the whole card one link. When the rendered element is a link (a[href]) or a button, the card gains a hover state (stronger border and shadow; a muted fill when flat), a full-card focus-visible ring and motion-interactive easing. Any other element (article, li) stays a static surface. Children can answer the hover with `group-hover/card:`. |

## Variants

- **variant**: default, flat
- **density**: comfortable, compact

## Tokens used

`card`, `card-foreground`, `border`, `border-strong`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Container · _no motion_ — A card is part of the layout it ships in; whatever stages that region owns the entrance. A card that fades in on its own delays reading the thing it holds.
- **response** · Container · `motion-interactive` — Only when the card is rendered as a link or button. The border, shadow and ring ease in so the pointer reads as landing on one target, not as the grid flickering. No motion-press: a 0.97 settle on a surface this large reads as the layout lurching. A static card has no response, so it gets no transition.
- **transition** · Container · _no motion_ — A card has no states of its own to move between. Selection is CheckboxCard or RadioCard; disclosure is Collapsible or Accordion.
- **activity** · Container · _no motion_ — A card does not work on anything. Loading content inside it is a Skeleton's job.

## Accessibility

- Purely presentational by default; add headings/landmarks in content as needed.
- Rendered as a link or button, the whole card is one target: its full text is the accessible name, and the focus ring wraps the whole card. Nothing interactive may sit inside it — nested links or buttons inside a link are invalid and unreachable for keyboard users in some browsers.
- A Card is a container, not a landmark and not a heading. If its title is the only heading in the region, render it as a real heading element with a title tier — a visually-styled div gives screen-reader heading navigation nothing to find.

## Related

- Components: Region, Stack, Separator, Button, Badge
- Patterns: DashboardPage, SettingsPage, ListDetailPage

## Examples

### With parts

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@sableui/react"

<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Edition</CardTitle><CardDescription>Limited run of 100.</CardDescription></CardHeader><CardContent><p className="text-body-md">Each collector receives a signed print and the on-chain edition.</p></CardContent></Card>
```

### With a header action

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Edition</CardTitle><CardAction><Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="More"><Icon name="ellipsis" /></Button></CardAction></CardHeader><CardContent><p className="text-body-md text-muted-foreground">24 of 100 collected.</p></CardContent></Card>
```

### Compact section panel

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@sableui/react"

<Card variant="flat" density="compact"><CardHeader><CardTitle>Notifications</CardTitle></CardHeader><CardContent><p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">Push and email are enabled.</p></CardContent></Card>
```

### Product card with actions

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@sableui/react"

<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Midnight Archive</CardTitle><CardDescription>Edition #24 of 100</CardDescription><CardAction><Badge tone="edition">Edition</Badge></CardAction></CardHeader><CardContent><p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">A signed print and token-gated download for collectors.</p></CardContent><CardFooter><Button size="sm">Collect</Button><Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Preview</Button></CardFooter></Card>
```

### Whole card as a link

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardTitle, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Card render={<a href="/components" />}><CardContent className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4"><div className="min-w-0"><CardTitle>Components</CardTitle><CardDescription>Every building block, with live examples.</CardDescription></div><Icon name="chevron-right" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground motion-interactive group-hover/card:translate-x-0.5 group-hover/card:text-foreground" /></CardContent></Card>
```

### Metric card

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@sableui/react"

<Card density="compact"><CardHeader><CardTitle>Revenue</CardTitle><CardDescription>Last 30 days</CardDescription></CardHeader><CardContent><p className="text-heading-3">128.4 SOL</p><p className="text-body-sm text-success">+12.8% from previous period</p></CardContent></Card>
```

### List card

```tsx
import { Avatar, Card, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardList, CardTitle, Entity } from "@sableui/react"

<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Members</CardTitle><CardDescription>3 people can edit this space.</CardDescription></CardHeader><CardList>{people.map((p) => <Entity key={p.id} interactive onSelect={() => open(p)} leading={<Avatar fallback={p.initials} alt={p.name} />} title={p.name} subtitle={p.role} />)}</CardList></Card>
```
