# Carousel

**Status:** stable

Generic, accessible, zero-dependency slide carousel. Transform track with measured slide pitch — multiple slides per view, infinite loop (cloned ends), pointer drag-to-swipe with snap, autoplay (with a pause control + hover/focus/reduced-motion pausing), arrows, dots, counter, and keyboard. Motion is token-driven.

**Keywords:** carousel, gallery, slides, horizontal

## Usage

Use Carousel for a curated, finite sequence of media or cards that benefits from horizontal browsing.

### Best practices

- Do: Use obvious previous and next controls and make the current position understandable.
- Do: Keep slide content independent so users do not need every slide to complete a task.
- Don't: Do not hide critical information or primary conversion actions only inside later slides.
- Don't: Do not autoplay without a visible pause control. Motion that cannot be stopped fails WCAG 2.2.2 and makes the surrounding text hard to read.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | — | Each top-level child becomes one slide. |
| slidesToShow | number \| { base?: number; sm?: number; md?: number; lg?: number; xl?: number } | 1 | Slides visible per view. A number, or a mobile-first breakpoint set keyed to Tailwind's default min-widths (sm 640, md 768, lg 1024, xl 1280px); a missing key inherits from the next smaller defined one, and base (default 1) is also the server-render value. Resolved with matchMedia, so no hand-rolled resize hook is needed. |
| gap | string | "0px" | Gap between slides (any CSS length). Use the spacing scale — e.g. "calc(var(--spacing) * 4)" — so density moves it. |
| loop | boolean | false | Infinite loop via cloned ends (needs count > slidesToShow). |
| autoplay | number | 0 | Auto-advance interval in ms (0 = off). Pauses on hover/focus/reduced-motion and exposes a play/pause control. |
| arrows | boolean | true | Prev/next arrow buttons. |
| dots | boolean | true | Pagination dots. |
| counter | boolean | false | An N / M slide counter. |
| draggable | boolean | true | Pointer drag-to-swipe. |
| index | number | — | Controlled active index. |
| defaultIndex | number | 0 | Initial index (uncontrolled). |
| onIndexChange | (index: number) => void | — | Notified when the active index changes. |
| label | string | — | Accessible label for the carousel region. |
| slideClassName | string | — | Class for each slide wrapper (e.g. an aspect ratio). |
| arrowClassName | string | — | Class for both prev/next arrow buttons. Merged through cn(), so a radius or shadow utility replaces the default rounded-full shadow-md rather than stacking with it. |

## Tokens used

`border`, `ring`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Region carries aria-roledescription='carousel'; each slide is a group with aria-roledescription='slide' and an 'N of M' label; clones are aria-hidden.
- Arrows and dots are real buttons (dots set aria-current); Left/Right arrow keys navigate when the viewport is focused.
- A polite live region announces the active slide; it goes silent while auto-rotating (APG).
- Autoplay exposes a pause/play control and pauses on hover, focus, and under prefers-reduced-motion (which also makes transitions instant).

## Related

- Components: Scroller, Dialog

## Examples

### Looping media

```tsx
import { Carousel } from "@sableui/react"

<Carousel loop dots slideClassName="aspect-video">{images.map((s) => <img key={s.id} src={s.url} alt={s.alt} className="size-full object-cover" />)}</Carousel>
```

### Multiple per view

```tsx
import { Carousel } from "@sableui/react"

<Carousel slidesToShow={3} gap="calc(var(--spacing) * 4)">{cards}</Carousel>
```

### Responsive per view

```tsx
import { Carousel } from "@sableui/react"

<Carousel slidesToShow={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }} gap="calc(var(--spacing) * 6)" label="Templates">{cards}</Carousel>
```

### Autoplay

```tsx
import { Carousel } from "@sableui/react"

<Carousel loop autoplay={4000} counter>{slides}</Carousel>
```

# ChatComposer

**Status:** stable

The input half of a conversation: one surface holding attachments, an auto-growing field, and its controls. Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line, and send becomes stop while a reply streams.

**Keywords:** chat input, composer, message input, prompt input, send message, ai chat, support chat, textarea

## Usage

Pairs with MessageScroller to make a working chat. A single surface rather than an input with buttons parked beside it: attachments above, text in the middle, affordances along the bottom. Works controlled or uncontrolled — uncontrolled is the default because it is what the common case wants, and what lets a hook-free page shell ship a composer that actually types.

### Best practices

- Do: Pass `busy` while a reply streams, and `onStop` alongside it. Interrupting a long generation is the most common thing a reader wants during one, and the control belongs where their cursor already is.
- Do: Leave it uncontrolled unless you need the text elsewhere — a slash-command menu, a draft you persist. Uncontrolled clears itself on send; controlled does not.
- Do: Render pending uploads as `<Attachment>` chips in `attachments`, so the file and the message it belongs to stay in one box.
- Do: Put model pickers and tool toggles in `leading`, beside the attach button — they are composer state, not message content, and belong on the chrome row rather than in the field.
- Do: Building a docked agent panel inside a tool? Wrap the whole conversation — scroller, messages and composer — in `<Density value="compact">`. The entire set follows the workspace register from there: prose drops a tier, the rhythm tightens, and the controls come off the compact ladder. Do not hand-size it at the call site.
- Don't: Do not clear a controlled composer for the user on send. Only the caller knows whether the send succeeded, and clearing on their behalf loses the message when it did not.
- Don't: Do not add your own Enter-to-send handler on top. The built-in one already guards against firing mid-IME-composition, which is the line hand-rolled chat inputs miss.
- Don't: Do not use it as a general multi-line input. That is `Textarea` — this one submits on Enter, which is wrong for any field inside a larger form.
- Don't: Do not override the field's type utility to make it match your transcript. The field and `Bubble` both read the same tier already, which is what stops a message changing size the moment it is sent — overriding one breaks that pairing.
- Don't: Do not remove the height cap to let the field grow without limit. A pasted essay would push the conversation off the screen; past the cap it scrolls.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attachments | no | Pending files as chips, above the field, inside the same surface. |
| Field | yes | An auto-growing Textarea, stripped of its own border and ring — the surface carries both — capped before it eats the transcript. |
| Controls | yes | Attach and any `leading` controls on the left; `actions` and the send/stop button on the right. |
| Footer | no | Helper text or a character counter below the controls. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | string | — | Controlled value. Omit for an uncontrolled composer that owns its own text. |
| defaultValue | string | "" | Initial value when uncontrolled. |
| onValueChange | (value: string) => void | — | Notified on every keystroke. Required when `value` is supplied. |
| onSend | (value: string) => void | — | Called with the trimmed message. An uncontrolled composer clears itself afterwards; a controlled one is the caller's to clear. |
| placeholder | string | "Send a message…" | Placeholder for the field. |
| busy | boolean | false | A reply is streaming. Disables send, and swaps it for a stop control when `onStop` is supplied. |
| onStop | () => void | — | Interrupt the in-flight reply. Supplying it turns send into stop while busy. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Block sending entirely — over a limit, disconnected, read-only thread. Distinct from `busy`, which is temporary and offers a way out (stop). |
| invalid | boolean | false | Mark the current text invalid. Colours the surface border and sets `aria-invalid` on the field. |
| attachments | ReactNode | — | Attachment chips, shown above the field. |
| leading | ReactNode | — | Controls on the left of the footer row — model picker, tool toggles. |
| actions | ReactNode | — | Extra controls left of the send button. |
| onAttach | () => void | — | Attach handler. Supplying it renders the built-in attach button. |
| label | string | "Message" | Accessible label for the field. |
| sendLabel | string | "Send message" | Accessible label for the send button. |
| stopLabel | string | "Stop generating" | Accessible label for the stop button. |
| footer | ReactNode | — | Helper text or counter below the controls. |
| fieldRef | Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement> | — | Ref to the underlying textarea — for focusing after a send, or on mount. |
| ...form props | Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<"form">, "onSubmit" \| "defaultValue"> | — | Spread onto the form element. Use `onSend` rather than `onSubmit`. |

## Variants

- **invalid**: true, false

## Tokens used

`card`, `input`, `ring`, `destructive`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`

## Accessibility

- A real `<form>`, so the send button is a submit button and the whole thing behaves as one control to assistive tech and to password managers alike.
- Enter never submits while an IME composition is open (`isComposing`), so a CJK reader confirming a candidate word does not mail a fragment of their first sentence.
- The focus ring is drawn on the surface via `focus-within`, not on the textarea, so the visible focus indicator matches the box a sighted user perceives as the input.
- Send is disabled — not merely styled down — until there is non-whitespace to send, so the affordance and the behaviour agree for keyboard users.
- Icon-only attach, send and stop buttons all carry accessible labels, each overridable for localisation.

## Related

- Components: MessageScroller, Message, Bubble, Attachment, Textarea
- Patterns: ChatPanel

## Examples

### Uncontrolled — the common case

```tsx
import { ChatComposer } from "@sableui/react"

<ChatComposer onSend={(text) => send(text)} onAttach={pickFile} />
```

### Streaming, with a stop control

```tsx
import { ChatComposer } from "@sableui/react"

<ChatComposer onSend={send} busy={isStreaming} onStop={stop} placeholder="Ask a follow-up…" />
```

### Controlled, with pending attachments

```tsx
import { Attachment, Button, ChatComposer, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<ChatComposer
	value={draft}
	onValueChange={setDraft}
	onSend={(text) => { post(text, files); setDraft("") }}
	onAttach={pickFile}
	attachments={files.map((f) => (<Attachment key={f.id} variant="media" name={f.name} thumbnail={f.url} actions={<Button variant="floating" size="icon-xs" aria-label="Remove" onClick={() => drop(f.id)}><Icon name="xmark" /></Button>} />))}
	footer={`${draft.length} / 4000`}
	invalid={draft.length > 4000}
/>
```

### A working chat, end to end

```tsx
import { Bubble, ChatComposer, Marker, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="flex h-128 flex-col gap-3">
	<MessageScroller className="flex-1 min-h-0">
		{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id} align={m.mine ? "end" : "start"}><Bubble variant={m.mine ? "primary" : "muted"} align={m.mine ? "end" : "start"}>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}
		{streaming ? <Marker icon="spinner" spin shimmer>Thinking…</Marker> : null}
	</MessageScroller>
	<ChatComposer onSend={send} busy={streaming} onStop={stop} />
</div>
```

# Checkbox

**Status:** stable

Square toggle (18px at rest, on the spacing scale) over Base UI's Checkbox. Checked/indeterminate/disabled states; controlled or uncontrolled; form-ready via the hidden native input.

**Keywords:** checkbox, boolean, multi select, form control

## Usage

Use Checkbox for independent boolean choices or for selecting multiple options in a set.

### Best practices

- Do: Use Checkbox when each option can be toggled independently.
- Do: Attach a visible label that explains the consequence of checking the control.
- Don't: Do not use Checkbox for mutually exclusive choices; use Radio or Select instead.
- Don't: Do not use it without a label or an aria-label. An 18px square with no accessible name is announced as just "checkbox", which tells a screen-reader user nothing about what they are agreeing to.
- Don't: Do not phrase the label as a negative, such as "Don't send read receipts". Paired with an unchecked box it becomes a double negative the reader has to solve before they can answer. Label the state being turned on.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| checked | boolean | — | Controlled checked state. Pair with onCheckedChange. Omit for uncontrolled. |
| defaultChecked | boolean | false | Initial checked state for an uncontrolled checkbox. |
| onCheckedChange | (checked: boolean, eventDetails) => void | — | Fires when the checkbox is ticked or unticked. Note: Base UI passes a second eventDetails arg — not the common (checked) => void, so a single-arg handler must widen its signature. |
| indeterminate | boolean | false | Mixed state (neither checked nor unchecked). Renders a dash instead of the check. For a "select all" box inside a CheckboxGroup, use `parent` instead and the group sets this for you. |
| parent | boolean | false | Makes this the "select all" box of a CheckboxGroup that has `allValues`. It checks or clears every child, and shows the dash when only some are checked. Only works inside a CheckboxGroup. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Ignores user interaction and dims the control. |
| name | string | — | Field name for the hidden input on form submit. |
| value | string | — | Value submitted with the form when checked. Inside a group-owned CheckboxGroup, it is the name the group's value array uses for this checkbox. |
| render | ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement | — | Compose the root with another element through the Base UI render prop. |

## Tokens used

`card`, `input`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders a hidden native <input type=checkbox> for keyboard, focus, and form semantics.
- Space toggles; focus-visible draws a 2px ring in the --ring token.
- indeterminate sets aria-checked=mixed automatically; a `parent` checkbox in a CheckboxGroup gets aria-checked=mixed and aria-controls for its children from the group.
- Label it with Field orientation="horizontal": it wires the label's htmlFor to the checkbox, so the label text joins the click target, and adds the description and error plumbing.

## Related

- Components: CheckboxCard, Switch, Radio

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@sableui/react"

<Checkbox defaultChecked />
```

### Controlled

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@sableui/react"

<Checkbox checked={value} onCheckedChange={setValue} />
```

### Indeterminate

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@sableui/react"

<Checkbox indeterminate />
```

### Select all in a group

```tsx
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, Field } from "@sableui/react"

<CheckboxGroup allValues={["email", "sms"]} defaultValue={["email"]} className="gap-3"><Field label="All channels" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox parent /></Field><Field label="Email" orientation="horizontal" className="ps-7"><Checkbox value="email" /></Field><Field label="SMS" orientation="horizontal" className="ps-7"><Checkbox value="sms" /></Field></CheckboxGroup>
```

### With label

```tsx
import { Checkbox, Field } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Remember me" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox /></Field>
```

# CheckboxCard

**Status:** stable

A multi-select selection card — a card-sized Base UI Checkbox with a checkbox box, title, and optional description. The checkbox twin of RadioCard (same tone table). CheckboxGroup lays a column out and can own the selection: give each card a `value` and the group holds the checked values as an array, with an optional parent "select all" Checkbox.

**Keywords:** checkbox card, select card, multi select, option card

## Usage

Use CheckboxCard when an option needs more visual weight, supporting text, or iconography than a plain checkbox row.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for a small number of options where details help users compare choices.
- Do: Keep the checked state visible across the full card, not only inside the indicator.
- Do: Let CheckboxGroup own the selection when the cards answer one question: give each card a `value` and read one array from `onValueChange` instead of wiring a toggle per card.
- Do: Use a plain Checkbox with `parent` for "select all", and list every child value in the group's `allValues`. The group works out its checked and mixed states.
- Don't: Do not use CheckboxCard for long lists; use Checkbox rows or a Combobox with `multiple` instead.
- Don't: Do not put a link or a button inside the card. The whole card is the checkbox's label, so a nested interactive element is either unreachable or steals the click that should toggle it.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CheckboxCard | yes | One card-shaped checkbox option. |
| CheckboxGroup | no | A grouped set of related checkbox cards. Optionally owns the selected values and a parent "select all" checkbox. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CheckboxGroup | { className?: string; children: ReactNode; value?: string[]; defaultValue?: string[]; onValueChange?: (value: string[]) => void; allValues?: string[]; disabled?: boolean } | Column wrapper (role=group) over Base UI's CheckboxGroup. With no group props it is layout only and each card stays independent. Pass value/defaultValue/onValueChange (string[]) and give each child a `value` to let the group own the selection — works for CheckboxCard and plain Checkbox children alike. Add allValues plus a `<Checkbox parent />` for a select-all box that turns mixed when only some are checked. `disabled` disables every child. onValueChange gets (value, eventDetails). Override the grid via className for multi-column layouts. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onCheckedChange | (checked: boolean, eventDetails) => void | — | Fires with the next checked state (Base UI passes eventDetails second). Pair with `checked` for a controlled card; omit both to let it manage its own state. |
| title | ReactNode | — | The card's primary label (text-title-sm). |
| description | ReactNode | — | Optional supporting copy beneath the title (text-body-sm, muted). |
| icon | ReactNode | — | Optional leading glyph (a solid <Icon>); takes the tone colour. |
| tone | "neutral" \| "standard" \| "collectible" \| "edition" \| "info" \| "warning" | "neutral" | Semantic colour the checked state carries across the border, checkbox box, and icon. |
| value | string | — | Names the card inside a group-owned CheckboxGroup: the card is checked when the group's value array includes it. Also the value submitted with a form. Inside a CheckboxGroup, `name` stands in for `value` when `value` is omitted. |
| checked / onCheckedChange / defaultChecked / disabled | Base UI Checkbox.Root props | — | Standard checkbox state. Without a group-owned value, each card is independent — drive checked/onCheckedChange per item for multi-select. |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, standard, collectible, edition, info, warning

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `ring`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `accent`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `tone-standard`, `tone-standard-foreground`, `tone-collectible`, `tone-collectible-foreground`, `tone-edition`, `tone-edition-foreground`, `tone-info`, `tone-info-foreground`, `tone-warning`, `tone-warning-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides the checkbox role, aria-checked, hidden native input, keyboard toggle, and data-[checked]/data-disabled state.
- The whole card is the hit target; focus draws a 2px outline outside the card (not a ring, so the checked tone ring survives focus); Space toggles the focused card.
- Selection never relies on colour alone — the filled checkbox box + check mark and the card border all shift.
- A parent select-all Checkbox gets aria-checked=mixed and aria-controls pointing at its children from Base UI; give it a visible label.

## Related

- Components: Checkbox, RadioCard

## Examples

### Group-owned selection

```tsx
import { CheckboxCard, CheckboxGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<CheckboxGroup value={selected} onValueChange={setSelected}>{REASONS.map((r) => (<CheckboxCard key={r} value={r} title={r} />))}</CheckboxGroup>
```

### Select all

```tsx
import { Checkbox, CheckboxCard, CheckboxGroup, Field } from "@sableui/react"

<CheckboxGroup allValues={REASONS} value={selected} onValueChange={setSelected}><Field label="All reasons" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox parent /></Field>{REASONS.map((r) => (<CheckboxCard key={r} value={r} title={r} />))}</CheckboxGroup>
```

### A single independent card

```tsx
import { CheckboxCard } from "@sableui/react"

<CheckboxCard title="Email me a receipt" description="Sent when the mint settles" checked={receipt} onCheckedChange={setReceipt} />
```

### Toned with description

```tsx
import { CheckboxCard } from "@sableui/react"

<CheckboxCard tone="edition" title="Editions" description="Sell as numbered NFT editions" defaultChecked />
```

---

# Code

**Status:** stable

Inline code. A styled `<code>` for code spans, keys, and identifiers inside running text — soft muted fill, monospace.

**Keywords:** code, inline code, token, monospace

## Usage

Use Code for short inline identifiers, commands, tokens, props, and file names inside prose.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for brief technical literals that need to stand apart from body copy.
- Do: Keep inline code short enough that it does not dominate the paragraph.
- Don't: Do not use Code for multiline snippets; use CodeBlock instead.
- Don't: Do not put a value the reader needs to copy inside it. Code has no copy affordance, so they will select it by hand and catch the surrounding punctuation; use CodeBlock with a prompt.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ...props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"code"> | — | All native `<code>` attributes (children, className, ref, …) pass through. |

## Tokens used

`muted`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders a semantic `<code>` element so assistive tech announces it as code.
- A `<code>` element is not announced distinctly by most screen readers — a code span in running prose is read as ordinary text. Where the exactness matters (a command to type verbatim, a case-sensitive identifier), say so in the sentence rather than relying on the styling to carry it.

## Related

- Components: CodeBlock, Kbd

## Examples

### Inline

```tsx
import { Code } from "@sableui/react"

Run <Code>pnpm dev</Code> to start the server.
```

### Code vs CodeBlock

```tsx
import { Code, CodeBlock } from "@sableui/react"

// Picking the wrong one is the usual mistake:
//
//   Code                   inline, inside a sentence       → `useState`
//   CodeBlock              multi-line, read-only           → an example to study
//   CodeBlock prompt="$"   one line, meant to be COPIED    → an install command

Install with <Code>pnpm add @sableui/react</Code>          {/* ✗ they will want to copy it */}
<CodeBlock prompt="$" code="pnpm add @sableui/react" />   {/* ✓ one line, with a copy button */}
```

---

# CodeBlock

**Status:** stable

Multi-line code surface. Optional header bar carries a filename and a copy affordance; the body is a horizontally scrollable monospace pre. Syntax highlighting is opt-in: pass a highlighter per block or once via CodeHighlightProvider (the package ships none).

**Keywords:** code block, snippet, pre, example

## Usage

Use CodeBlock for multiline code samples that users may read, inspect, or copy.

### Best practices

- Do: Give the snippet a filename, or a sentence of surrounding copy, when it helps readers and agents place it.
- Do: Keep examples complete enough to teach the intended pattern.
- Do: Wire highlighting once with CodeHighlightProvider and map token colors to semantic tone tokens (keywords → tone-edition, strings → success, comments → muted-foreground), so code follows the theme instead of a fixed palette.
- Don't: Do not put short inline identifiers in a CodeBlock; use Code for those.
- Don't: Do not paste code with the indentation the surrounding file had. A block indented to sit inside your JSX shows the reader leading whitespace that is not part of the example.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CodeBlock | yes | The surface: optional filename header, copy affordance, scrollable pre. |
| CodeHighlightProvider | no | Optional app-level wrapper that supplies one highlighter to every CodeBlock inside it. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CodeHighlightProvider | { highlight: (code: string) => ReactNode; children: ReactNode } | Supplies one highlighter to every CodeBlock beneath it, so an app wires highlighting once. Map the highlighter's token colors to Sable tone tokens so code follows the theme. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| code | string | — | The code to display. Always what the copy button copies, whatever the highlighter renders. |
| filename | string | — | Optional filename shown in the header bar. |
| showCopy | boolean | true | Show the copy affordance — in the header bar with a filename, floating in the corner without one. |
| highlight | ((code: string) => ReactNode) \| false | — | Highlighter for this block; overrides CodeHighlightProvider. false renders plain text inside a provider. |
| prompt | string | — | A shell prompt ("$", ">"). Makes it a one-line command: the prompt is dimmed and unselectable, the line truncates, and copy takes only code. |

## Tokens used

`border`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- Code renders inside a <pre><code> for correct semantics and screen-reader handling.
- Copy is the ghost icon Button with `useCopy`, which guards clipboard access for SSR safety.

## Related

- Components: Code

## Examples

### With filename + copy

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@sableui/react"

<CodeBlock filename="cn.ts" code={"import { clsx } from \"clsx\"\nexport const cn = clsx"} />
```

### With a highlighter for the whole app

```tsx
import { CodeBlock, CodeHighlightProvider } from "@sableui/react"

<CodeHighlightProvider highlight={(code) => <span dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: highlightToHtml(code) }} />}><CodeBlock code={"const a = 1"} /></CodeHighlightProvider>
```

### No header

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@sableui/react"

<CodeBlock showCopy={false} code={"type Size = \"sm\" | \"md\"\nconst size: Size = \"md\""} />
```

---

# Collapsible

**Status:** stable

Show/hide a panel of content over Base UI Collapsible — open/close state, ARIA expanded wiring, and the animated height transition. The minimal primitive behind Accordion: a trigger that toggles an overflow-clipped panel.

**Keywords:** collapsible, disclosure, expand, collapse

## Usage

Use Collapsible for a single piece of optional content that can expand in place.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for local detail, advanced settings, or secondary context.
- Do: Make the trigger label describe the hidden content, not the mechanism.
- Don't: Do not use Collapsible for multi-section navigation; use Accordion or Tabs instead.
- Don't: Do not animate it by transitioning height from auto. Use the motion-disclosure recipe, which transitions to the measured panel height — `auto` does not animate and the panel will snap.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CollapsibleTrigger | yes | The control that toggles the panel. |
| CollapsiblePanel | yes | The content that expands or collapses. |
| CollapsibleIndicator | no | A visual affordance for open or closed state. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CollapsibleTrigger | Base UI Collapsible.Trigger props + render | The button that toggles the panel. Compose with render={<Button variant="ghost" … />}. |
| CollapsiblePanel | Base UI Collapsible.Panel props + className (keepMounted, hiddenUntilFound) | The collapsible contents. Overflow-hidden; animates height via the --collapsible-panel-height var Base UI sets. |
| CollapsibleIndicator | { className? } | Auto-rotating disclosure chevron. Place it inside the trigger content and add the `group/collapsible` class to the trigger so it flips 180° on open. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Collapsible (Root) | Base UI Collapsible.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, disabled) | — | Groups the trigger and panel and owns open state. Uncontrolled by default; pass `open` + `onOpenChange` to control it. |
| defaultOpen | boolean | false | Whether the panel starts open in the uncontrolled case. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Disables the trigger and prevents toggling. |

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI wires aria-expanded on the trigger and aria-controls/id between trigger and panel.
- Trigger is a real <button>; toggles on click and Enter/Space.
- Animate open/close via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style]; data-[panel-open] marks the open state.
- Set hiddenUntilFound on the panel to let in-page browser search expand it.

## Related

- Components: Accordion, ShowMore

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Button, Collapsible, CollapsiblePanel, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Collapsible><CollapsibleTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost">Details</Button>} /><CollapsiblePanel><p className="pt-3">Hidden content revealed on toggle.</p></CollapsiblePanel></Collapsible>
```

### Open by default

```tsx
import { Button, Collapsible, CollapsiblePanel, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Collapsible defaultOpen><CollapsibleTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost">Summary</Button>} /><CollapsiblePanel><p className="pt-3">Visible on first render.</p></CollapsiblePanel></Collapsible>
```

### With rotating chevron

```tsx
import { Button, Collapsible, CollapsibleIndicator, CollapsiblePanel, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Collapsible><CollapsibleTrigger className="group/collapsible" render={<Button variant="ghost">Details <CollapsibleIndicator /></Button>} /><CollapsiblePanel><p className="pt-3">Revealed on toggle.</p></CollapsiblePanel></Collapsible>
```

# ColorField

**Status:** stable

A colour swatch that opens a themed picker — saturation/value area, hue and alpha sliders, hex entry, presets, and transparent as a value rather than a separate toggle.

**Keywords:** color, colour, color picker, swatch, hex, alpha, transparency, eyedropper, property, workspace

## Usage

Use ColorField wherever a colour is a property: a canvas background, an effect parameter, a stroke or fill. It is sized to the control ladder so it lines up inside a PropertyRow or PropertyPair. Deliberately not <input type="color">, which opens the OS dialog — that ignores the theme entirely, cannot show a transparency checkerboard, has no alpha channel, hosts no eyedropper or presets, and renders at whatever size the platform picks, so it never aligns in a property grid.

### Best practices

- Do: Use allowTransparent when "no colour" is a real value. It appears inside the picker as a value; a transparent switch sitting beside a colour control reads as two properties when it is one.
- Do: Pass swatches when a surface has a house palette. Presets are how most colour choices actually get made, and they cost one row.
- Do: Decide whether your persistence layer accepts 8-digit hex before enabling allowAlpha. The value format is the contract — see the tokens note.
- Don't: Put a separate opacity slider next to a ColorField that already has allowAlpha. Two controls writing one channel is how they drift out of sync.
- Don't: Re-derive hue from the committed value on every render. Grey has no hue, so dragging saturation to zero would snap the hue slider to red with no way back — ColorField keeps hue in its own state for exactly this reason.
- Don't: Hand-roll a transparency checkerboard. Use the `checkerboard` utility with `--checkerboard-size` (~16px for an artboard, ~8px for a 24px swatch); two hand-rolled copies had already drifted before it existed. Its colours come from --panel / --panel-raised, so it is correct in both modes. It is deliberately not named bg-checkerboard: a custom bg-* utility lands in tailwind-merge's background group and silently evicts, or is evicted by, a real bg-* colour class.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trigger | yes | A swatch at --control-xs with a hairline ring, on a checkerboard so a translucent or transparent value reads as such. |
| Picker | yes | Saturation/value area over the current hue, a hue slider, an alpha slider when allowAlpha, and a hex field. |
| Presets | no | An optional swatch row, and the Transparent entry when allowTransparent. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | string | — | The current value: "transparent", "#rrggbb", or "#rrggbbaa". |
| onValueChange | (value: string) => void | — | Called with the new value on every commit, including mid-drag. |
| allowTransparent | boolean | false | Offers "transparent" as a value inside the picker. Colour → transparent → colour restores the colour you had. |
| allowAlpha | boolean | false | Enables the alpha slider, and therefore 8-digit hex output. Off by default because it widens the value format. |
| swatches | string[] | — | Optional preset row. |
| label | string | "Colour" | Accessible name for the trigger; the current value is appended to it. |

## Tokens used

`panel`, `panel-raised`, `hairline`, `hairline-strong`, `ring`, `popover`

## Accessibility

- The trigger's accessible name includes the current value, so a screen reader announces the colour rather than just "button" — the swatch itself conveys nothing without sight.
- The Transparent entry is a toggle with aria-pressed, because it is a state of the value and not a navigation action.
- The hex field is the keyboard path to any colour. The saturation/value area and the sliders are pointer-driven and are NOT keyboard operable — a known gap, and the reason the hex field is never hidden.
- The eyedropper is only rendered where the EyeDropper API exists (Chromium), rather than shown and broken elsewhere.

## Related

- Components: PropertyRow, PropertyPair, ScrubField, Input, Popover

## Examples

### Canvas background

```tsx
import { ColorField, PropertyRow } from "@sableui/react"

<PropertyRow label="Background">
  <ColorField value={background} onValueChange={setBackground} allowTransparent />
</PropertyRow>
```

### With alpha and a palette

```tsx
import { ColorField } from "@sableui/react"

<ColorField
  value={tint}
  onValueChange={setTint}
  allowAlpha
  swatches={["#f43f5e", "#facc15", "#22c55e", "#3b82f6", "#a855f7"]}
  label="Tint"
/>
```

### The value format is the contract

```tsx
import { isTransparent, parseHex } from "@sableui/react"

// ColorField only ever EMITS these three shapes:
//   "transparent" | "#rrggbb" | "#rrggbbaa"
// It accepts #rgb and #rgba on paste but never produces them, so a consumer's
// parser has three cases to handle rather than five.
//
// Alpha is omitted when fully opaque — "#3b82f6", never "#3b82f6ff" — so a
// parser written before alpha support keeps reading opaque colours correctly.
// Only enable allowAlpha once your parser and your persisted format accept the
// 8-digit form, or a document saved by a newer build degrades on an older one.

import { parseHex, isTransparent } from "@sableui/react"

const parsed = isTransparent(value) ? null : parseHex(value) // null = not a colour
```

---

# Combobox

**Status:** stable

Autocomplete over Base UI Combobox — type-to-filter, roving focus, ARIA combobox/listbox wiring, collision-aware positioning, Esc/outside dismissal. A search input (with chevron trigger) plus a portal-rendered popup of filterable items.

**Keywords:** combobox, autocomplete, typeahead, search select, filter, suggestions, picker

## Usage

Use Combobox when users choose from a list that benefits from typing, filtering, or autocomplete — one value, or several with `multiple` and ComboboxChips (tags, collaborators, categories). Use Select for short finite sets, a Checkbox group when every choice should stay visible, and CommandMenu for global actions.

### Best practices

- Do: Pass items so internal filtering, empty state, and accessibility wiring have the full option set.
- Do: Use ComboboxEmpty with helpful copy for zero matches.
- Do: Wrap in Field when the combobox is part of a form.
- Do: Reach for ComboboxVirtualList past roughly a thousand rows, and leave filtering to the root. It reads the filtered list through useFilteredItems(), so the rendered rows and the rows Base UI navigates cannot drift apart.
- Do: Use `multiple` with ComboboxChips for several values from a filterable set, and keep chip labels short so the field does not turn into a paragraph.
- Don't: Use Combobox for tiny option sets where Select or Radio would be easier to scan.
- Don't: Use Combobox as a command launcher. Use CommandMenu for actions and navigation.
- Don't: Take filtering over with filteredItems in order to virtualize. Base UI ignores filteredItems while the untouched field still holds the selected item's label, so the list you render and the list it indexes diverge — and the symptom is clicking one row and getting another.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root | yes | Owns selected value, input value, filtering, and open state. |
| Input | yes | The searchable text field and trigger. |
| Chips | no | The field for `multiple`, used in place of Input: one removable chip per selected item plus the text input, in one wrapping shell. |
| Content | yes | The positioned popup surface. |
| List | yes | The listbox inside the popup. Takes a render function that receives each filtered item. |
| Item | yes | A selectable suggestion row. |
| Empty | no | Fallback shown when filtering returns no items. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ComboboxInput | Base UI Combobox.Input props (minus the native `size` attribute) + size?: "md" \| "xs" + className | The search field, styled like Input, wrapped with an InputGroup + chevron Trigger that toggles the popup. The chevron flips while the popup is open (data-[popup-open] on the toggle). `size="xs"` is the property-grid rung and mirrors SelectTrigger's `xs` exactly — same height, radius and inset surface — so a combobox and a select in one panel are the same shape holding different content (a font-family picker directly above a font-weight select is the case it exists for). Note the type: the native numeric `size` attribute is omitted rather than shadowed, because intersecting a string union onto it resolves to `never` and breaks every call site. |
| ComboboxChips | Base UI Combobox.Input props (minus the native `size` attribute) + size?: "md" \| "xs" + chipLabel?: (item) => string + className | The field for a `multiple` combobox, used in place of ComboboxInput. Each selected item renders as a soft `sm` Badge with a ghost `icon-xs` Button that removes it (labelled "Remove {label}"), followed by the text input; the shell wraps and grows as chips are added. `chipLabel` turns an item into its chip text — defaults to the item for strings/numbers and its `label` field for objects. Keyboard is Base UI's: Backspace in an empty field removes the last chip, ←/→ move between chips, Backspace/Delete removes the highlighted one. `size="xs"` mirrors ComboboxInput's property-grid rung. |
| ComboboxContent | Base UI Popup props + { side?: Side; align?: Align; sideOffset?: number; scroll?: boolean; className?: string } | Portal + Positioner + Popup — it does not render a list, so put a ComboboxList (or ComboboxVirtualList) inside it. Width matches the input via --anchor-width. side is which side of the input the popup renders against (auto-flips on collision), align its alignment along that side, sideOffset the gap in px. Defaults to side='bottom', align='start', sideOffset=6, scroll=true. Pass scroll={false} when a ComboboxVirtualList inside owns the scrolling. |
| ComboboxList | Base UI Combobox.List props (children: ReactNode \| (item, index) => ReactNode) | The listbox. Required inside ComboboxContent: pass a render function and it is called once per filtered item (or per group when `items` is grouped), so the rendered rows always match Base UI's filtering. |
| ComboboxVirtualList | { itemHeight: number; groupLabelHeight?: number; overscan?: number; children: (item, { index }) => ReactNode; renderGroupLabel?; className?; itemClassName? } | A windowed list: only the rows on screen exist. Fixed row heights (nothing is measured, so late-arriving content changes how a row looks and never where the rows are). Filtering stays Base UI's — the component reads the filtered list through useFilteredItems() — and groups keep their role=group wrapper and label association. Needs virtualized on the root and scroll={false} on ComboboxContent. |
| ComboboxItem | Base UI Combobox.Item props + className (value, disabled, index, onClick) | A suggestion row. Highlights via data-[highlighted]; shows a trailing check (ItemIndicator) when it matches the selected value. |
| ComboboxEmpty | Base UI Combobox.Empty props + className | Fallback shown when the filtered list is empty. Requires the `items` prop on the root. |
| ComboboxGroup | Base UI Combobox.Group props + className | Groups related items under an accessible label auto-associated with the group. |
| ComboboxGroupLabel | Base UI Combobox.GroupLabel props + className | The label for a ComboboxGroup. Auto-associated with the group it sits in. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Combobox (Root) | Base UI Combobox.Root props (items, value, defaultValue, onValueChange, inputValue, onInputValueChange, open, onOpenChange, multiple, autoHighlight, filter, disabled) | — | Groups all parts and owns selection + filter state. Pass `items` (flat array or groups) to enable internal filtering and ComboboxEmpty. |
| items | readonly any[] \| readonly ComboboxItemGroup[] | — | The pool of options, flat or grouped ({ value, items }). Drives type-to-filter and is required for ComboboxEmpty to render its fallback. |
| multiple | boolean | false | Select several items instead of one. `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` become arrays, choosing an item toggles its membership, and the popup stays open between picks. Pair it with ComboboxChips in place of ComboboxInput; every other part is unchanged. |
| virtualized | boolean | false | Tells Base UI the DOM holds only part of the list. Required when using ComboboxVirtualList. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`, `destructive`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `primary`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides role=combobox/listbox/option, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and type-to-filter.
- Esc and outside-press dismiss; focus returns to the input on close.
- The chevron Trigger carries an aria-label and toggles the suggestions popup.
- ComboboxEmpty announces filter results politely; keep it mounted (do not conditionally render it).
- Animate open/close via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes.
- With `multiple`, the listbox is multi-selectable and each chip's remove button is labelled `Remove {label}`; Backspace in an empty field removes the last chip and ←/→ move between chips, so every chip is reachable without a pointer.
- ComboboxVirtualList gives every rendered row aria-setsize (the full filtered count) and aria-posinset, so a screen reader is told the size of the list rather than the size of the window.
- A highlight that lands on a row the window has not rendered is scrolled into view by the root, which forwards it to the list; Base UI's own scrollIntoView only reaches rows that exist.

## Related

- Components: Select, Checkbox, CommandMenu, Field, SearchInput, Badge
- Patterns: SettingsPage, ListDetailPage

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Combobox, ComboboxContent, ComboboxEmpty, ComboboxInput, ComboboxItem, ComboboxList } from "@sableui/react"

<Combobox items={fruits}><ComboboxInput placeholder="Search fruit…" /><ComboboxContent><ComboboxEmpty>No matches.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxList>{(item) => (<ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>)}</ComboboxList></ComboboxContent></Combobox>
```

### Controlled value

```tsx
import { Combobox, ComboboxContent, ComboboxInput, ComboboxItem, ComboboxList } from "@sableui/react"

<Combobox items={fruits} value={value} onValueChange={setValue}><ComboboxInput /><ComboboxContent><ComboboxList>{(item) => (<ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>)}</ComboboxList></ComboboxContent></Combobox>
```

### Multiple selection

```tsx
import { Combobox, ComboboxChips, ComboboxContent, ComboboxEmpty, ComboboxItem, ComboboxList } from "@sableui/react"

<Combobox multiple items={tags} value={value} onValueChange={setValue}><ComboboxChips placeholder="Add tags…" /><ComboboxContent><ComboboxEmpty>No matching tags.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxList>{(item) => (<ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>)}</ComboboxList></ComboboxContent></Combobox>
```

### Virtualized (long list)

```tsx
import { Combobox, ComboboxContent, ComboboxEmpty, ComboboxInput, ComboboxVirtualList } from "@sableui/react"

<Combobox virtualized items={districts} value={district} onValueChange={setDistrict}><ComboboxInput placeholder="Search districts…" /><ComboboxContent scroll={false}><ComboboxEmpty>No district matches.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxVirtualList itemHeight={32}>{(item) => item.label}</ComboboxVirtualList></ComboboxContent></Combobox>
```

### Inside Field

```tsx
import { Combobox, ComboboxContent, ComboboxEmpty, ComboboxInput, ComboboxItem, ComboboxList, Field } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Creator" description="Search by display name."><Combobox items={creators} value={creator} onValueChange={setCreator}><ComboboxInput placeholder="Search creators" /><ComboboxContent><ComboboxEmpty>No creators found.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxList>{(item) => (<ComboboxItem key={item.id} value={item}>{item.name}</ComboboxItem>)}</ComboboxList></ComboboxContent></Combobox></Field>
```

---

# CommandMenu

**Status:** stable

A command palette (Cmd+K) built on our Dialog: a top-aligned wide surface with a search input and a scrollable, JS-filtered list of grouped commands. CommandMenuPanel renders the same palette in place, on a card in the page.

**Keywords:** command, command menu, palette, launcher, cmd k, search, quick action, spotlight, navigation, search trigger, header search, keyboard shortcut, inline command menu, embedded palette, settings search

## Usage

Use CommandMenu for global or contextual keyboard-driven actions: navigation, creation, quick settings, or searchable commands. It should feel curated and fast; use Select, Menu, or Combobox for ordinary inline choices.

### Best practices

- Do: Open the palette from a header search with CommandMenuTrigger: a button wearing SearchInput's field shell, with the ⌘K / Ctrl K hint and the page-wide shortcut built in. A palette with no visible trigger still takes useCommandMenuShortcut rather than a hand-written keydown listener.
- Do: Group items by task area, such as Navigation, Create, or Settings, so users can scan before typing.
- Do: Keep command labels action-oriented and unique enough to search.
- Do: Provide useful bootstrap items so the menu is valuable before the user types.
- Do: Pass a filter when the palette searches more than one source. Ranking (exact prefix over substring over subsequence) is the caller's to own, and the returned order is kept verbatim — including group order, which follows each group's first surviving row.
- Do: List a command the user cannot currently run as disabled with the reason in hint, rather than filtering it away. A palette that hides what you cannot do teaches you nothing about why.
- Do: Resize the list with listClassName rather than reaching past className into the palette's DOM. className is the dialog surface; listClassName is the Scroller that actually scrolls.
- Do: Use CommandMenuPanel when the palette lives in the page: a sidebar launcher, a settings search, a demo. It takes the same items, filter, query and children, and keeps the same keyboard model; it is a static card, so it does not trap focus or take it on mount, and Esc clears the query instead of closing anything.
- Don't: Hand-style a <button> to look like a search field, or put a SearchInput in the header that opens a dialog when focused. The first drifts from the field it imitates; the second is a text box you cannot type in. A header search that opens the palette is CommandMenuTrigger.
- Don't: Use CommandMenu as a replacement for every dropdown. Simple choices belong in Select, Menu, or Tabs.
- Don't: Hand-build a palette mock from a search glyph, a row of buttons and a highlight. That is CommandMenuPanel, and the hand-built one has no combobox, no filtering and no keyboard model.
- Don't: Dump every app route and action into one uncurated list. Keep the palette opinionated.
- Don't: Rebuild the combobox over Dialog to get consumer-owned ranking. query/onQueryChange and filter are that seam; the keyboard model, activedescendant wiring, and result-count live region come with them.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trigger | no | CommandMenuTrigger — the search-field-shaped button in a header that opens the palette on click or on ⌘K / Ctrl+K. It sits outside CommandMenu; wire its onOpen to the palette's open state. |
| Dialog surface | yes | The modal shell that traps focus and positions the launcher. CommandMenuPanel replaces it with a static card in the page (border, card fill, no shadow). |
| Search input | yes | The combobox input that filters commands while focus remains in the field. |
| Groups | no | Labelled command sections that keep results scannable. |
| Items | yes | Keyboard-selectable command rows that run onSelect and close the palette. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CommandMenuTrigger | { onOpen?: () => void; placeholder?: string; shortcut?: string \| false; size?: "sm" \| "md"; disabled?: boolean } | The search field in a header that is really a button. Wears SearchInput's shell (border-input, card surface, leading magnifier, muted placeholder) on the control ladder, with a trailing Kbd: ⌘K on macOS, Ctrl K elsewhere. onOpen runs on click and on the shortcut, which it listens for page-wide (useCommandMenuShortcut). shortcut is the key (default "k"); false drops both the hint and the listener. size is sm in a header beside small buttons, md (default) beside Input and SearchInput. It sits outside CommandMenu, so the Dialog returns focus to it on close. |
| useCommandMenuShortcut | (onShortcut: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void, key?: string \| false) => void | The page-wide ⌘K / Ctrl+K listener CommandMenuTrigger installs, for a palette with no visible trigger. Ignored while focus is in a text field, textarea, select or contenteditable (Ctrl+K belongs to the field there) except the palette's own input, so the callback may toggle. It calls preventDefault() on a match and skips an event already prevented, so two listeners on one page fire once. key defaults to "k"; false turns it off. Removed on unmount. |
| CommandMenuPanel | { items?: CommandItem[]; query?: string; onQueryChange?: (query: string) => void; filter?: CommandFilter; listClassName?: string; placeholder?: string; emptyMessage?: string; title?: string; scope?: ReactNode; inputProps?: ComponentProps<'input'>; className?: string; children?: ReactNode } | The palette rendered in place: the same search header, filtered and grouped listbox, keyboard model and result-count live region, on a static card (border-border, bg-card, no shadow) instead of in a Dialog. Takes every CommandMenu prop except open, onOpenChange, finalFocus and description; className lands on the card, title names the listbox. Focus is not trapped and the input does not take focus on mount (inputProps.autoFocus opts in). Esc clears the query, and passes through once it is empty, so a Popover around the panel still closes. A chosen row runs its onSelect and the panel stays as it was. The page-wide shortcut does not fire from its input. |
| CommandMenuGroup | { label: string; children } | A labelled group of command rows. |
| CommandMenuItem | { onSelect?: () => void; icon?: string; detail?: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; id?: string; children } | A selectable row. Self-filters by its text (unless the root was given a filter), runs onSelect, then closes the palette. detail is secondary text after the label; hint is the end-aligned trailing slot — a shortcut, a count, or a disabled row's reason. A disabled row stays listed, stays announced, and stays reachable by arrow key so its reason can be read, but is inert to Enter and to a click. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| scope | ReactNode | — | A scope chip in the header, between the search glyph and the input — "In: Backdrop". A scope belongs beside the field rather than in its value: put it in the value and the user deletes prose to widen their search, and your filter parses it back out. Pair with inputProps.onKeyDown handling Backspace on an empty query, or the only way out of a scope is the mouse. |
| inputProps | Omit<ComponentProps<'input'>, 'role' \| 'value' \| 'onChange' \| aria-*> | — | Extra props for the search input. `onKeyDown` runs BEFORE the palette's own handling and opts out of a key by calling preventDefault() — which is what makes a scope chip Backspace-dismissable. Running first is deliberate: Backspace happens not to be a key the palette claims today, so a plain passthrough would work until the palette grows a 'Backspace clears the query' affordance, at which point the consumer's behaviour breaks silently. The combobox wiring (role, aria relationships, controlled value) is not overridable; aria-label and className compose. |
| open | boolean | — | Controlled open state of the palette. |
| onOpenChange | (open: boolean) => void | — | Called on open/close (select, Esc, outside click). |
| items | CommandItem[] | — | Data-driven commands ({ group, label, onSelect, id?, icon?, detail?, hint?, disabled? }). Ignored when children are provided. id is optional identity: filter is handed these same objects, so it is how a caller that ranks over its own richer model maps the array back onto it — and it becomes the row's DOM id (namespaced to the palette) and React key, so two rows may share a label. |
| query | string | — | Controlled query. Leave undefined to let the palette own it; either way it resets on close (a controlled caller gets onQueryChange('')). |
| onQueryChange | (query: string) => void | — | Called on every query change. Required to control query, optional otherwise. |
| filter | ((items: CommandItem[], query: string) => CommandItem[]) \| null | case-insensitive substring match on label | Replaces or disables the built-in match. A function ranks and filters items itself and its order is kept verbatim; null renders items exactly as given. Either also stops declarative CommandMenuItem children self-filtering. The query arrives raw — trimming and case are policy, and this is the prop that hands policy over. |
| listClassName | string | — | Classes for the scrolling list. className lands on the dialog surface, so this is the seam for the list's own height cap — listClassName="max-h-[60vh]". The list is a Scroller, so the cap lands on the element that scrolls and the edge fades come free. |
| placeholder | string | "Type a command or search…" | Placeholder for the search input. |
| emptyMessage | string | "No results found." | Copy shown when the query matches nothing. |
| title | string | "Command menu" | Accessible name for the palette dialog (visually hidden). |
| description | string | "Search for a command and press Enter to run it." | Accessible description for the palette dialog (visually hidden). |
| finalFocus | RefObject<HTMLElement> \| ((closeType) => HTMLElement \| false) \| false | — | Where focus goes when the palette closes. The Dialog default returns it to the trigger — the CommandMenuTrigger, when there is one. A palette opened by the keystroke alone has none, so pass a resolver to restore whatever had focus, or false to restore nothing. |
| children | ReactNode | — | Declarative commands via CommandMenuGroup / CommandMenuItem. Takes precedence over items. |

## Tokens used

`card`, `card-foreground`, `border`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`

## Accessibility

- CommandMenuTrigger is a real <button> named by its visible placeholder, with aria-haspopup=dialog and aria-keyshortcuts (Meta+K on macOS, Control+K elsewhere). Its Kbd hint is aria-hidden, so the shortcut is announced once rather than read as part of the name.
- The shortcut never fires from inside a text field, textarea, select or contenteditable (Ctrl+K is delete-to-end-of-line in macOS text views), except the palette's own input.
- CommandMenuPanel is the same combobox and listbox in the page, with no dialog: it does not trap or steal focus, and Esc clears a non-empty query (stopping there) instead of dismissing. With an empty query Esc is left alone for whatever contains the panel.
- Built on Base UI Dialog, so focus trap, scroll lock, and Esc/outside dismissal come for free; the dialog carries a visually-hidden title + description so it is announced.
- Follows the ARIA combobox pattern: the search input is role=combobox (aria-autocomplete=list) that owns the role=listbox popup via aria-controls.
- ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End and PageUp/PageDown move a virtual aria-activedescendant highlight while focus stays in the input; Enter runs the highlighted command. Arrow keys wrap; page jumps clamp.
- Groups expose role=group labelled by their heading; items are role=option and never enter the tab order.
- A polite role=status live region announces the result count as the query narrows, so the size of the list is available without reading it.
- A disabled row carries aria-disabled and is skipped when seeding the highlight, but stays in the arrow-key walk so its reason can be reached and read.
- The component keeps ownership of aria-activedescendant even when a caller claims a key through inputProps.onKeyDown. Skipping a move is coherent (they took responsibility for that key), but nothing may leave the active id naming a row that is not painted as active — so the opt-out returns before any highlight change rather than after it.
- Exactly one row is ever painted as active: the pointer takes the highlight over (moving onto a row makes it the aria-activedescendant) rather than adding a hover fill of its own, so what looks highlighted is always what Enter will run.

## Related

- Components: Dialog, SearchInput, Kbd, Menu, Select, Combobox
- Patterns: DashboardPage, ListDetailPage

## Examples

### Data-driven

```tsx
import { CommandMenu } from "@sableui/react"

<CommandMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} items={[{ group: 'Navigation', label: 'Go to feed', icon: 'home', onSelect: () => {} }, { group: 'Actions', label: 'New post', onSelect: () => {} }]} />
```

### Declarative

```tsx
import { CommandMenu, CommandMenuGroup, CommandMenuItem } from "@sableui/react"

<CommandMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}><CommandMenuGroup label='Navigation'><CommandMenuItem icon='home' onSelect={() => {}}>Go to feed</CommandMenuItem></CommandMenuGroup></CommandMenu>
```

### Grouped launcher

```tsx
import { CommandMenu, CommandMenuGroup, CommandMenuItem } from "@sableui/react"

<CommandMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}><CommandMenuGroup label="Create"><CommandMenuItem icon="plus" onSelect={() => createPost()}>New post</CommandMenuItem><CommandMenuItem icon="sparkles" onSelect={() => createEdition()}>New edition</CommandMenuItem></CommandMenuGroup><CommandMenuGroup label="Navigation"><CommandMenuItem icon="home" onSelect={() => navigate("/")}>Home</CommandMenuItem><CommandMenuItem icon="gear" onSelect={() => navigate("/settings")}>Settings</CommandMenuItem></CommandMenuGroup></CommandMenu>
```

### Consumer-owned ranking

```tsx
import { CommandMenu } from "@sableui/react"

<CommandMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} query={query} onQueryChange={setQuery} filter={(items, q) => rank(items, q)} items={items} />
```

### Listed but unavailable

```tsx
import { CommandMenu } from "@sableui/react"

<CommandMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} items={[{ group: 'Layers', label: 'Align left', disabled: true, hint: 'Select another layer to align to', onSelect: () => {} }]} />
```

### Inline panel

```tsx
import { CommandMenuPanel, Kbd } from "@sableui/react"

<CommandMenuPanel className="w-80" items={[{ group: 'Create', label: 'New project', icon: 'plus', hint: <Kbd>N</Kbd>, onSelect: () => {} }, { group: 'Settings', label: 'Open settings', icon: 'gear', onSelect: () => {} }]} />
```

### Header search trigger

```tsx
import { CommandMenu, CommandMenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<CommandMenuTrigger size="sm" placeholder="Search docs" onOpen={() => setOpen(true)} className="w-56" />
<CommandMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} items={items} />
```

### Keyboard shortcut with no visible trigger

```tsx
import { CommandMenu, useCommandMenuShortcut } from "@sableui/react"

useCommandMenuShortcut(() => setOpen((value) => !value))
<CommandMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} items={items} />
```

# ContextCard

**Status:** stable

Hover/focus-triggered rich preview card over Base UI PreviewCard. Reveals contextual content (a profile, an edition summary) from an inline anchor; 20rem-wide surface with delayed open and collision-aware positioning.

**Keywords:** context card, rich tooltip, hover card, preview

## Usage

Use ContextCard to show richer contextual content near a trigger without taking users out of flow.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for previews, summaries, or supporting context tied to a specific element.
- Do: Keep the card read-only and make the trigger the action: it is a real link to the full profile or item. Keyboard users cannot reach a button inside the card, because moving focus off the trigger closes it. If the preview needs an action (Follow, Add), use a Popover instead.
- Don't: Do not put critical decisions, long forms, or required workflow steps inside ContextCard.
- Don't: Do not open it on click. It is a hover/focus preview; making it click-triggered gives you a Popover with no dismiss affordance and no way to reach the content it previews.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ContextCardTrigger | yes | The element that anchors the card. |
| ContextCardContent | yes | The contextual surface shown near the trigger. |
| ContextCardArrow | no | An optional arrow connecting card and trigger. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ContextCardTrigger | Base UI Trigger props + render + delay \| closeDelay | The inline anchor (renders an <a>). Use render={<a href='…'/>} to compose with a link. delay defaults to 600ms, closeDelay to 300ms. |
| ContextCardContent | Base UI Popup props + side \| align \| sideOffset + className | Portals + positions + paints the popup; surface is a fixed 20rem-wide card. side is which side of the trigger to render against (auto-flips on collision), align the alignment along it, sideOffset the gap in px. Defaults to side="bottom", align="center", sideOffset=8. |
| ContextCardArrow | Base UI Arrow props + className | Optional pointer connecting the popup to its trigger. Place inside ContextCardContent. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ContextCard (Root) | Base UI PreviewCard.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange) | — | Groups the trigger and content. Uncontrolled by default; opens on hover/focus of the trigger. |

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`

## Accessibility

- Opens on hover and on keyboard focus of the trigger, after a short delay; dismisses on Esc, outside press, and blur.
- The trigger renders an <a> by default — compose render={<a href='…'/>} so it stays a real, navigable link.
- Base UI wires the popup's ARIA association with the trigger; the card holds non-interactive context, not focusable controls.
- Animate via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] opacity attributes on the popup.

## Related

- Components: Popover, Tooltip

## Examples

### Profile preview

```tsx
import { Avatar, ContextCard, ContextCardContent, ContextCardTrigger, Entity } from "@sableui/react"

<ContextCard><ContextCardTrigger render={<a href='/u/ada' className='text-title-sm underline-offset-2 hover:underline'>@ada</a>} /><ContextCardContent><Entity className='[--entity-px:0] [--entity-py:0]' leading={<Avatar fallback='AL' size='lg' />} title='Ada Lovelace' subtitle='@ada' /><p className='mt-3 text-body-sm text-muted-foreground'>Minting generative editions on Solana. Permanently on Arweave.</p></ContextCardContent></ContextCard>
```

### With stat row

```tsx
import { Avatar, ContextCard, ContextCardContent, ContextCardTrigger, Description, DescriptionItem, Entity } from "@sableui/react"

<ContextCard><ContextCardTrigger render={<a href='/u/nyx' className='text-title-sm underline-offset-2 hover:underline'>@nyx</a>} /><ContextCardContent><Entity className='[--entity-px:0] [--entity-py:0]' leading={<Avatar fallback='NY' size='lg' />} title='Nyx' subtitle='@nyx' /><Description cols='2' className='mt-4 border-t border-border pt-3'><DescriptionItem term='Posts' detail='128' /><DescriptionItem term='Followers' detail='4.2k' /></Description></ContextCardContent></ContextCard>
```

# ContextMenu

**Status:** stable

Right-click menu over Base UI ContextMenu — opens on the native contextmenu event or long press and positions at the pointer. Shares Menu's roving focus, typeahead, ARIA menu/menuitem wiring, collision-aware positioning, and Esc/outside dismissal.

**Keywords:** context menu, right click, overflow, menu

## Usage

Use ContextMenu for actions that are specific to the object or area the user invoked.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for secondary object actions such as rename, duplicate, move, or delete.
- Do: Group destructive or uncommon actions away from frequent safe actions.
- Don't: Do not make ContextMenu the only way to access a primary or required action.
- Don't: Do not rely on it for touch. There is no right-click on a touchscreen — the long-press fallback is discoverable by nobody, so anything in here needs a visible route too.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ContextMenuTrigger | yes | The target area or element that opens the menu. |
| ContextMenuContent | yes | The menu surface. |
| ContextMenuItem | yes | One actionable command. |
| ContextMenuSeparator | no | A divider between command groups. |
| ContextMenuGroup | no | A semantic group of related commands. |
| ContextMenuGroupLabel | no | An optional label for a command group. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ContextMenuTrigger | Base UI ContextMenu.Trigger props + className + render | The right-clickable area that opens the menu on contextmenu (right click) or long press. Renders a <div>. |
| ContextMenuContent | Base UI Popup props + { side, align, sideOffset, className } | Portal + Positioner + Popup. Positions at the pointer. side is which side of the anchor the popup renders against (auto-flips on collision), align its alignment along that side, sideOffset the gap in px. Defaults to side='bottom', align='start', sideOffset=6. |
| ContextMenuItem | Base UI ContextMenu.Item props + variant?: "default" \| "destructive" + className (disabled, closeOnClick, onClick) | An interactive row. Lays out as a flex row, so a leading Icon sits inline before the label. Highlights via data-[highlighted]; dims via data-[disabled], and disabled items are skipped by keyboard focus. variant="destructive" marks a destructive command (Delete, Remove) and keeps its destructive ink while highlighted; never fake it with a text-destructive class, which the highlight repaints. |
| ContextMenuSeparator | Base UI Separator props + className | Hairline rule between item runs. |
| ContextMenuGroup | Base UI ContextMenu.Group props + className | Groups related items under an accessible label auto-associated with the group. |
| ContextMenuGroupLabel | Base UI ContextMenu.GroupLabel props + className | The label for a ContextMenuGroup. Auto-associated with the group it sits in. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ContextMenu (Root) | Base UI ContextMenu.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, orientation, loopFocus) | — | Groups all parts and controls open state. Renders no element. Uncontrolled by default. |

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides role=menu/menuitem, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and typeahead.
- Opens on right click (contextmenu) or long press; Esc and outside-press dismiss and restore focus.
- Animate open/close via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes.
- ContextMenuGroupLabel is auto-associated with its ContextMenuGroup for screen readers.

## Related

- Components: Menu, DotsMenu

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<ContextMenu><ContextMenuTrigger className="rounded-md border border-dashed border-border p-8 text-center text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">Right-click here</ContextMenuTrigger><ContextMenuContent><ContextMenuItem>Cut</ContextMenuItem><ContextMenuItem>Copy</ContextMenuItem><ContextMenuItem>Paste</ContextMenuItem><ContextMenuSeparator /><ContextMenuItem variant="destructive">Delete</ContextMenuItem></ContextMenuContent></ContextMenu>
```

### Grouped

```tsx
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuGroupLabel, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<ContextMenu><ContextMenuTrigger className="rounded-md border border-dashed border-border p-8">Right-click here</ContextMenuTrigger><ContextMenuContent><ContextMenuGroup><ContextMenuGroupLabel>Layout</ContextMenuGroupLabel><ContextMenuItem>Move up</ContextMenuItem><ContextMenuItem>Move down</ContextMenuItem></ContextMenuGroup><ContextMenuSeparator /><ContextMenuItem>Duplicate</ContextMenuItem></ContextMenuContent></ContextMenu>
```

# DataTable

**Status:** stable

A data-driven table over the Table primitives — a columns def + data array with built-in client-side sorting (click a sortable header to cycle asc → desc → none), optional row click / selection, and an empty state. For server data or paging, sort/page the data and pair with Pagination.

**Keywords:** data table, table, sortable, columns, rows, empty state, pagination, list

## Usage

Use DataTable when a data array and column definition should render a sortable, semantic table with optional row actions and an empty state. Use the lower-level Table parts for hand-authored markup or highly custom row layouts.

### Best practices

- Do: Put a table that fills a card in <CardContent flush>. The table runs edge to edge and its first and last columns inset to the card padding on their own; do not hand-set pl-6 / pr-6 on columns.
- Do: Provide stable rowKey values for dynamic data so selection and sorting do not jump.
- Do: Use sortable only on columns where ordering is obvious and useful.
- Do: Pair server-side datasets with Pagination and pass already-sorted/paged rows.
- Don't: Make every row clickable and also fill it with competing buttons. Choose a clear row interaction model.
- Don't: Use DataTable for heterogeneous cards or timeline content. A list or card layout will scan better.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Columns | yes | Definitions for headers, cell renderers, sorting, alignment, and classes. |
| Rows | yes | The data array rendered through the column definitions. |
| Empty state | no | Content spanning all columns when the row array is empty. |
| Caption | no | Accessible table caption rendered by the underlying Table. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| columns | DataTableColumn<Row>[] | — | Column defs: { key, header, cell?, sortValue?, sortable?, align?, className? }. cell defaults to row[key]; sortValue defaults to row[key]. When cell renders a formatted string (e.g. a date), pass sortValue returning the underlying value (e.g. date.getTime()) so the column sorts by the real value, not the rendered text. |
| data | Row[] | — | The rows to render. |
| rowKey | (row, index) => string \| number | index | Stable React key per row. |
| onRowClick | (row) => void | — | Row click handler — makes rows pointer-interactive. |
| isRowSelected | (row) => boolean | — | Mark a row visually selected (data-selected). Derive it from a stable id (row.id === selectedId), not the row index, so selection survives re-sorts. |
| defaultSort | { key: string; direction: "asc" \| "desc" } | — | Initial sort column + direction. |
| empty | ReactNode | "No results." | Rendered spanning all columns when data is empty. Pass an EmptyState for the full treatment (icon, title, next step). |
| caption | ReactNode | — | Bottom table caption. |

## Tokens used

`muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Sorted columns set aria-sort=ascending/descending on the header cell.
- Sortable headers are real <button>s with a focus-visible ring, keyboard-operable.
- Inherits the Table's scrollable frame and semantic <table>/<th>/<td> structure.

## Related

- Components: Table, Pagination, EmptyState, Badge
- Patterns: DashboardPage, ListDetailPage

## Examples

### Sortable columns

```tsx
import { DataTable } from "@sableui/react"

<DataTable data={users} columns={[{ key: "name", header: "Name", sortable: true }, { key: "role", header: "Role" }, { key: "joined", header: "Joined", sortable: true, sortValue: (u) => u.joinedAt, cell: (u) => formatDate(u.joinedAt) }]} />
```

### Clickable rows

```tsx
import { DataTable } from "@sableui/react"

<DataTable data={posts} columns={cols} onRowClick={(p) => navigate(`/post/${p.id}`)} rowKey={(p) => p.id} />
```

### Rich status column

```tsx
import { Avatar, Badge, DataTable, Entity } from "@sableui/react"

<DataTable data={deployments} rowKey={(row) => row.id} columns={[{ key: "name", header: "Name", sortable: true }, { key: "status", header: "Status", cell: (row) => <Badge appearance="plain" tone={row.status === "failed" ? "destructive" : row.status === "building" ? "warning" : "success"} dot>{row.statusLabel}</Badge> }, { key: "owner", header: "Owner", cell: (row) => <Entity className="[--entity-px:0] [--entity-py:0]" leading={<Avatar src={row.owner.avatar} alt={row.owner.name} fallback={row.owner.initials} size="sm" />} title={row.owner.name} /> }]} />
```

### In a card, edge to edge

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle, DataTable } from "@sableui/react"

<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Deployments</CardTitle></CardHeader><CardContent flush><DataTable data={deployments} rowKey={(row) => row.id} columns={[{ key: "project", header: "Project", sortable: true }, { key: "duration", header: "Duration", align: "end" }]} /></CardContent></Card>
```

### Empty state

```tsx
import { Button, DataTable, EmptyState, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<DataTable data={[]} columns={[{ key: "name", header: "Name" }, { key: "status", header: "Status" }]} empty={<EmptyState icon={<Icon name="search" />} title="No deployments" description="Try a different filter or create a deployment." action={<Button>Create deployment</Button>} />} />
```
