# DatePicker

**Status:** stable

Date (and optionally time) picker: a field-shaped trigger (the Input / SelectTrigger shell) opens a Popover holding Sable's Calendar. With granularity="day" selecting a day fires onValueChange and closes; granularity="minute" adds an hour + minute row of Selects and keeps the time-of-day when the day changes.

**Keywords:** date picker, calendar, date input, date time picker, time, schedule, form

## Usage

Use DatePicker when users need to choose one date — or, with granularity="minute", one date and time — from a compact control.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it in forms where a typed date alone would be error-prone.
- Do: Show clear selected and disabled states when date rules apply.
- Do: Set granularity="minute" when a time matters, with a minuteStep that matches the real precision (15 for meetings, 5 for scheduled posts).
- Don't: Do not show a time without saying which zone it is in. A meeting time with no zone is wrong for everyone not in yours — wrap the picker in a Field whose description names the zone.
- Don't: Do not leave the format ambiguous. `03/04` is two different dates depending on the reader's locale — the trigger shows a formatted date precisely so the interpretation is not guessed.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | Date | — | The selected date (controlled). When absent, the trigger shows a muted placeholder. |
| defaultValue | Date | — | Initial value when uncontrolled (no `value` prop). |
| onValueChange | (date: Date \| undefined) => void | — | Fired when the day is chosen or cleared, and under granularity="minute" when the hour or minute changes. With granularity="day" it also closes the popover. |
| onChange | (date: Date \| undefined) => void | — | Deprecated alias for onValueChange, kept for backwards compatibility. Both fire when set; prefer onValueChange. |
| granularity | "day" \| "minute" | "day" | What the picker chooses. "minute" adds an hour + minute row and keeps the popover open so day and time can be set in any order. |
| minuteStep | number | 5 | Minute increment for the time row (granularity="minute" only). |
| defaultTime | string | "00:00" | Time-of-day shown and applied while nothing is selected yet, as 24h "HH:mm" — the first day pick lands on this time instead of midnight (granularity="minute" only). |
| placeholder | string | "Pick a date" ("Pick date & time" with granularity="minute") | Trigger label shown when no date is selected. |
| disabled | boolean | — | Disable the trigger and block selection. |
| minDate | Date | — | Earliest selectable day (inclusive). Earlier days are disabled and navigation is bounded. |
| maxDate | Date | — | Latest selectable day (inclusive). Later days are disabled and navigation is bounded. |
| className | string | — | Extra classes merged onto the trigger. |
| id / aria-label / aria-labelledby / aria-describedby / aria-invalid / aria-required | button attributes | — | Forwarded to the trigger, so a wrapping Field ties its label to the picker and announces its description and error. Pass them yourself only when labelling the picker without a Field. |

## Tokens used

`primary`, `primary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `input`, `card`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Trigger opens on click/Enter/Space; the popover traps focus and restores it to the trigger on close (Base UI Popover).
- The calendar grid (react-day-picker) provides a roving tabindex, arrow-key day navigation, and aria-selected on the chosen day.
- Navigation chevrons render through the Icon adapter and inherit the calendar's button labels.
- Esc and outside press dismiss the popover.
- With granularity="minute" the hour and minute Selects are full Base UI listboxes (typeahead, ARIA) labelled "Hour" and "Minute"; selecting a day keeps the chosen time-of-day, so day and time can be set in any order.

## Related

- Components: Calendar, Field

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from "@sableui/react"

const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>()
<DatePicker value={date} onValueChange={setDate} />
```

### Custom placeholder

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from "@sableui/react"

<DatePicker placeholder="Schedule for…" value={date} onValueChange={setDate} />
```

### Date and time

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from "@sableui/react"

const [start, setStart] = useState<Date>()
<DatePicker granularity="minute" value={start} onValueChange={setStart} minDate={new Date()} defaultTime="09:00" minuteStep={15} />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from "@sableui/react"

<DatePicker disabled />
```

### Bounded (no past dates)

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from "@sableui/react"

<DatePicker value={date} onValueChange={setDate} minDate={new Date()} />
```

# Description

**Status:** stable

A labeled key/value list (definition list). Compose with DescriptionTerm + DescriptionDetail, or the ergonomic DescriptionItem shorthand. Aligns terms and details into a grid; cols="2" packs pairs two-wide.

**Keywords:** description list, metadata, details, key value

## Usage

Use Description to present label-value details where each term needs a clear corresponding value.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for object metadata, settings summaries, and read-only record details.
- Do: Keep terms brief and values scannable so the list works as reference material.
- Don't: Do not use Description for editable forms; pair Label and form controls instead.
- Don't: Do not use it for a single key/value. A definition list of one is a labelled value — use a Label and the value, and keep the list semantics for actual lists.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DescriptionItem | yes | One term and detail pair. |
| DescriptionTerm | yes | The label for the value. |
| DescriptionDetail | yes | The value or explanatory detail. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DescriptionTerm | <dt> props + className | The key. Muted label tier; sits in the first grid column. |
| DescriptionDetail | <dd> props + tone?: "default" \| "muted" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" + className | The value. Body tier on the foreground; sits in the second grid column. tone colors the value to encode a status (e.g. Ended → muted, Active → success), replacing inline conditional color classes; defaults to "default". |
| DescriptionItem | { term: ReactNode; detail?: ReactNode; tone?: "default" \| "muted" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive"; children? } | Ergonomic shorthand for one term/detail pair — renders a DescriptionTerm followed by a DescriptionDetail. Pass the value via detail or children; tone (defaults to "default") colors the detail value the same way it does on DescriptionDetail. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cols | "1" \| "2" | "1" | Column density. One term/detail column, or two pairs per row once the list's container is at least @md (28rem) wide; narrower, it stays one column. A container query, not a viewport breakpoint, so a narrow card on a wide screen stays one column. With cols="2" the <dl> is wrapped in an @container div. |

## Variants

- **cols**: 1, 2
- **tone**: default, muted, success, warning, destructive

## Tokens used

`muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `success`, `tone-warning`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Renders semantic <dl>/<dt>/<dd> elements so assistive tech announces the term/detail relationship.
- tone is a visual emphasis only — keep the value text itself meaningful (e.g. "Ended"), never color alone.

## Related

- Components: Fieldset, Entity

## Examples

### Metadata list

```tsx
import { Description, DescriptionItem } from "@sableui/react"

<Description>
	<DescriptionItem term="Network" detail="Solana" />
	<DescriptionItem term="Supply" detail="100" />
	<DescriptionItem term="Royalty" detail="5%" />
</Description>
```

### Composed term/detail

```tsx
import { Description, DescriptionDetail, DescriptionTerm } from "@sableui/react"

<Description>
	<DescriptionTerm>Network</DescriptionTerm>
	<DescriptionDetail>Solana</DescriptionDetail>
	<DescriptionTerm>Contract</DescriptionTerm>
	<DescriptionDetail className="text-mono-sm">7xKXtg2CW87d97TXJSDpbD5jBkheTqA83TZRuJosgAsU</DescriptionDetail>
</Description>
```

### Toned status value

```tsx
import { Description, DescriptionItem } from "@sableui/react"

<Description>
	<DescriptionItem term="Edition" detail="Midnight Archive" />
	<DescriptionItem term="Status" detail={isEnded ? "Ended" : "Active"} tone={isEnded ? "muted" : "success"} />
</Description>
```

# DestructiveActionModal

**Status:** stable

Confirmation modal for irreversible actions, built on AlertDialog (role=alertdialog; a backdrop click does not dismiss). Pairs a secondary Cancel with a destructive confirm; awaits an async onConfirm (spinner + stays open on failure) or takes an external pending flag; optional body slot and type-to-confirm guard for high-stakes deletions.

**Keywords:** destructive, modal, confirmation, danger

## Usage

Use DestructiveActionModal to confirm irreversible or high-risk actions before they run.

### Best practices

- Do: Name the affected object and the consequence of the action in plain language.
- Do: Make the destructive action visually distinct from the cancel path.
- Don't: Do not use it for routine low-risk actions where undo or inline confirmation would be faster.
- Don't: Do not put the destructive action where Cancel usually sits, or make it the default focus. A confirmation dialog exists to add friction; autofocusing Delete removes the friction it was added for.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | boolean | — | Controlled open state. |
| onOpenChange | (open: boolean) => void | — | Called when the open state should change (Esc, Cancel, or confirm). A backdrop click does not dismiss. |
| title | ReactNode | — | Modal heading — names the irreversible action. |
| description | ReactNode | — | Optional supporting copy explaining the consequence. |
| confirmLabel | string | "Delete" | Label for the destructive confirm button. |
| cancelLabel | string | "Cancel" | Label for the dismissing secondary button. |
| onConfirm | () => void \| Promise<void> | — | Called when the user confirms. If it returns a Promise the modal shows an in-flight spinner, closes on resolve, and stays open on reject; if void it closes immediately (unless pending is controlled). |
| pending | boolean | — | Externally-driven in-flight state. Overrides the internal await tracking; the parent owns closing (the modal stays open on a synchronous confirm). |
| confirmingLabel | string | confirmLabel | Confirm-button label shown while the action is in flight. |
| children | ReactNode | — | Body content rendered between the description and the type-to-confirm Input / footer — e.g. a warning <Note>. |
| confirmText | string | — | When set, renders an Input the user must type matching to enable the destructive confirm button. |

## Tokens used

`card`, `card-foreground`, `border`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `input`, `destructive`, `destructive-foreground`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Built on AlertDialog (Base UI): role="alertdialog", focus trapping, scroll lock, and aria-modal. Esc dismisses; a click on the backdrop does not, so a stray click can't throw away the decision.
- Focus opens on Cancel — the safe action — even when a type-to-confirm Input comes first, so a reflexive Enter never fires the destructive action.
- The title labels the modal; the description describes it.
- The type-to-confirm Input is wired to its label via htmlFor; the destructive Button is disabled (not just hidden) until the text matches.
- While a confirm is in flight (awaited onConfirm or pending), both buttons disable, the confirm Button sets aria-busy, and Esc dismissal is blocked so the action can't be interrupted or double-fired.

## Related

- Components: Dialog, Button, Banner

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { DestructiveActionModal } from "@sableui/react"

<DestructiveActionModal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title='Delete post?' description='This permanently removes the post. This cannot be undone.' onConfirm={handleDelete} />
```

### Async confirm (awaited spinner)

```tsx
import { DestructiveActionModal } from "@sableui/react"

<DestructiveActionModal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title='Block user?' description='They can no longer interact with you.' confirmLabel='Block' confirmingLabel='Blocking…' onConfirm={() => blockUser(id)} />
```

### Body slot + type-to-confirm

```tsx
import { DestructiveActionModal, Note } from "@sableui/react"

<DestructiveActionModal open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title='Delete this post?' confirmText='gold rush' confirmLabel='Delete forever' onConfirm={handleDelete}><Note tone='warning'>Collectors who minted this edition keep their copies.</Note></DestructiveActionModal>
```

---

# Dialog

**Status:** stable

Modal surface over Base UI Dialog (focus trap, scroll lock, Esc/outside dismissal). Centered on desktop; max-width 500px. size="fullscreen" is the full-bleed media viewer (image, video, Carousel) over a near-opaque scrim.

**Keywords:** dialog, modal, overlay, confirmation, alert, form, focus trap, sheet, lightbox, fullscreen, image viewer, media overlay, gallery

## Usage

Use Dialog for focused decisions, short modal forms, confirmations, and content that temporarily blocks the underlying page. Prefer Sheet for side-panel workflows, Popover for lightweight anchored content, and inline sections for content that should remain part of the page.

### Best practices

- Do: Always include DialogTitle and usually DialogDescription so the modal has an accessible name and context.
- Do: Keep the footer actions explicit: a safe escape path plus the primary or destructive action.
- Do: Use showCloseButton for dismissible informational dialogs; keep destructive confirmations action-led.
- Do: In a destructive confirmation, state the consequence in DialogDescription ("This is permanent.") and reserve the destructive button variant for actions that cannot be undone.
- Do: Use size="fullscreen" when an image, video, or gallery needs a larger view than the layout can give it. Give the popup an accessible name (aria-label on DialogContent, or a visually hidden DialogTitle) and alt text on the media.
- Do: Use the AlertDialog family for a confirmation that must be answered (discard changes, leave without saving). It looks identical but is role="alertdialog" and a backdrop click does not dismiss it — only Cancel, Esc, or the action. For irreversible deletes, use DestructiveActionModal, which is built on it.
- Don't: Put large multipage workflows in a centered dialog. Use Sheet or a page route when the task needs space.
- Don't: Use size="fullscreen" for forms, confirmations, or anything that isn't media. A dialog that happens to need room is a Sheet or a page; the fullscreen affordances (dark scrim, corner close, centred content) all assume something to look at.
- Don't: Hide the close button at size="fullscreen" without another visible way out. A full-bleed viewer that only Esc dismisses is a dead end for anyone who doesn't know the key.
- Don't: Open a dialog for passive status updates. Use Toast, Banner, or InlineStatus instead.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trigger | no | The element that opens the dialog when using the composed trigger pattern. |
| Overlay | yes | The dimming backdrop behind the modal content. |
| Content | yes | The modal surface that receives focus trap, labelled-by, and described-by wiring. |
| Header | yes | Title and optional description that explain the decision or task. |
| Footer | no | Action row for cancel, confirm, submit, or destructive choices. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DialogContent | Base UI Popup props + size?: "default" \| "fullscreen" + showCloseButton?: boolean + scroll?: boolean + className | Backdrop + popup; portals to <body>. Composes DialogOverlay by default. size="fullscreen" is the media viewer: a near-opaque scrim (bg-overlay/95), an edge-to-edge popup that centres its children with no card chrome, motion-fade instead of motion-pop, and a safe-area-aware floating close button (Button variant="floating"); at that size showCloseButton defaults to true and scroll to false, and the media fits itself with max-h-full max-w-full object-contain. At the default size, showCloseButton (defaults to false) renders a built-in close (X) button in the top-end corner, and the header leaves room for it (Icon name="xmark"). The popup caps at the viewport height less a 1rem margin and wraps its children in a scrolling region, so a tall dialog scrolls instead of overflowing a viewport whose own scroll is locked; pass scroll={false} when the dialog owns its internal layout (a pinned header over a scrolling body) and supplies its own min-h-0 scroll region. |
| DialogOverlay | Base UI Backdrop props + size?: "default" \| "fullscreen" + className | The styleable scrim/backdrop — bg-overlay/50 by default, near-opaque bg-overlay/95 at size="fullscreen". Composed into DialogContent (at the matching size) by default; exported for manual styling. |
| DialogTrigger | Base UI Dialog.Trigger props (render) | Element that opens the dialog. Compose via render prop. |
| DialogClose | Base UI Dialog.Close props (render) | Element that dismisses the dialog. Compose via render prop. |
| DialogHeader | ComponentProps<"div"> | Top section holding DialogTitle/DialogDescription. |
| DialogTitle | Base UI Dialog.Title props + className | The dialog's accessible name — wires aria-labelledby on the popup. |
| DialogDescription | Base UI Dialog.Description props + className | Muted supporting line; wires aria-describedby. |
| DialogFooter | ComponentProps<"div"> | Bottom action row (right-aligned buttons). |
| AlertDialog (Root) | Base UI AlertDialog.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange) | Root for a confirmation that needs an answer. Always modal; the popup is role="alertdialog" and a click outside does not dismiss — only an AlertDialogClose, an action that sets open to false, or Esc. |
| AlertDialogTrigger | Base UI AlertDialog.Trigger props (render) | Opens the alert dialog. |
| AlertDialogContent / AlertDialogOverlay / AlertDialogTitle / AlertDialogDescription / AlertDialogHeader / AlertDialogFooter / AlertDialogClose | Same props as the matching Dialog part | The Dialog parts under AlertDialog names — Base UI shares the popup, backdrop, title, description and close parts between the two, so the surface is identical. Pass initialFocus to AlertDialogContent (a ref to the Cancel button) to open focus on the safe action. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dialog (Root) | Base UI Dialog.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, modal) | — | Controls open state. Uncontrolled by default. |

## Variants

- **size**: default, fullscreen

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `muted-foreground`, `overlay`, `overlay-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `ring`

## Motion

- **arrival** · DialogOverlay · `motion-fade` — The scrim is what tells the reader the page behind is no longer live. Appearing at full opacity in one frame reads as a page navigation — the surrounding context vanishes instead of receding.
- **arrival** · DialogContent · `motion-pop` — The panel scales up as the scrim darkens, so the two read as one event. Overlay and panel arriving on separate timings is the most common way a modal feels cheap.
- **response** · DialogClose · `motion-interactive` — The close affordance is a small icon in a corner and is often the only control a reader looks for. Its hover state has to be findable, not just present.
- **transition** · DialogContent · `motion-pop` — Exit runs the same recipe in reverse so dismissal is legibly the inverse of opening. A modal that fades out having scaled in leaves the reader unsure whether it closed or navigated away.
- **activity** · DialogContent · _no motion_ — The dialog is a container. Work happening inside it is the content's to report — a dialog-level indicator would claim the whole surface is busy when usually one field is.

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides focus trapping, scroll lock, aria-modal, and labelled-by wiring (DialogTitle).
- Content taller than the viewport scrolls inside the dialog (thin scrollbar, contained overscroll) rather than overflowing off screen — the page behind is scroll-locked, so anything past the edge would be unreachable.
- Esc and click-outside dismiss by default. AlertDialog keeps Esc but ignores click-outside, and its popup is role="alertdialog".
- Animate via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes.
- size="fullscreen" has no title chrome, so name the popup yourself: aria-label on DialogContent (or a visually hidden DialogTitle), plus alt text on the media — the zoomed image is a separate image to assistive technology. Its built-in close button carries aria-label="Close" and clears the safe-area insets (notch, home indicator).

## Related

- Components: Sheet, Popover, Toast, Button, Form, Note, Carousel, Video
- Patterns: SettingsPage, AuthPage

## Examples

### Fullscreen media

```tsx
import { Button, Dialog, DialogContent, DialogTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Dialog><DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">View full size</Button>} /><DialogContent size="fullscreen" aria-label="Studio, 2026"><img src={url} alt="Studio, 2026" className="max-h-full max-w-full object-contain p-8" /></DialogContent></Dialog>
```

### Fullscreen gallery

```tsx
import { Button, Carousel, Dialog, DialogContent, DialogTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Dialog><DialogTrigger render={<Button>Open gallery</Button>} /><DialogContent size="fullscreen" aria-label="Gallery"><Carousel loop dots counter label="Gallery" className="w-full max-w-4xl px-8">{images.map((src) => <img key={src} src={src} alt="" className="size-full object-contain" />)}</Carousel></DialogContent></Dialog>
```

### Basic

```tsx
import { Button, Dialog, DialogClose, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Dialog><DialogTrigger render={<Button>Open</Button>} /><DialogContent><DialogHeader><DialogTitle>Edition details</DialogTitle><DialogDescription>A limited run of 100, stored permanently on Arweave.</DialogDescription></DialogHeader><DialogFooter><DialogClose render={<Button variant="secondary">Close</Button>} /><DialogClose render={<Button>Collect</Button>} /></DialogFooter></DialogContent></Dialog>
```

### Settings form

```tsx
import { Button, Dialog, DialogClose, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger, Field, Form, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Dialog><DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Rename collection</Button>} /><DialogContent showCloseButton><DialogHeader><DialogTitle>Rename collection</DialogTitle><DialogDescription>Update the display name shown to collectors.</DialogDescription></DialogHeader><Form><Field label="Collection name"><Input defaultValue="Midnight Archive" /></Field><DialogFooter><DialogClose render={<Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>} /><Button type="submit">Save changes</Button></DialogFooter></Form></DialogContent></Dialog>
```

### Destructive confirmation

```tsx
import { AlertDialog, AlertDialogClose, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogTrigger, Button } from "@sableui/react"

<AlertDialog><AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="destructive">Delete edition</Button>} /><AlertDialogContent><AlertDialogHeader><AlertDialogTitle>Delete edition?</AlertDialogTitle><AlertDialogDescription>This removes the edition and cannot be undone.</AlertDialogDescription></AlertDialogHeader><AlertDialogFooter><AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>} /><Button variant="destructive" onClick={deleteEdition}>Delete edition</Button></AlertDialogFooter></AlertDialogContent></AlertDialog>
```

# DotsMenu

**Status:** stable

An overflow ellipsis icon button that opens a Menu. Composes our Menu + Button + Icon — pass MenuItems as children and it wires the ghost icon trigger, accessible label, and portal-rendered content. All keyboard, focus, and dismissal behavior comes through Menu.

**Keywords:** dots menu, more actions, overflow, kebab

## Usage

Use DotsMenu for compact overflow actions when the primary action is already visible elsewhere.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for secondary commands that belong to a row, card, or toolbar item.
- Do: Keep labels explicit so the icon-only trigger does not obscure the command meaning.
- Don't: Do not hide the most important or most frequent action inside DotsMenu.
- Don't: Do not use it as the only affordance on a touch surface. It is revealed on hover in most layouts, and hover does not exist on touch — pair it with a visible action or make it always-visible there.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | — | The menu rows — MenuItem / MenuSeparator / MenuGroup, etc. Rendered inside MenuContent. |
| align | 'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' | end | Alignment of the popup along its side. Overflow menus typically right-align under the trigger; 'start' anchors the popup's left edge to the trigger instead. |
| label | string | More actions | Accessible label (aria-label) for the icon-only trigger button. |
| icon | string | ellipsis | Semantic icon name rendered in the trigger. |
| size | 'icon' \| 'icon-sm' \| 'icon-xs' | icon | The trigger's rung on the icon-button ladder. 'icon' for a card or page header; 'icon-sm' or 'icon-xs' in a list row or dense toolbar, so the trigger does not set the row height. |

## Variants

- **size**: icon, icon-sm, icon-xs

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- The icon-only trigger is labeled via aria-label (label prop, default 'More actions').
- Menu provides role=menu/menuitem, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and typeahead via Base UI.
- Esc and outside-press dismiss; focus returns to the trigger on close.

## Related

- Components: Menu, ContextMenu

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { DotsMenu, MenuItem, MenuSeparator } from "@sableui/react"

<DotsMenu label="Post actions"><MenuItem>Edit</MenuItem><MenuItem>Share</MenuItem><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem variant="destructive">Delete</MenuItem></DotsMenu>
```

### With leading icons

```tsx
import { DotsMenu, Icon, MenuItem, MenuSeparator } from "@sableui/react"

<DotsMenu><MenuItem><Icon name="check" className="text-sm" />Mark as read</MenuItem><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem variant="destructive"><Icon name="xmark" className="text-sm" />Delete</MenuItem></DotsMenu>
```

# EmptyState

**Status:** stable

The centered empty / error block: optional icon disc or error code, title, description and an action. tone="destructive" makes it an announced error, size="lg" a page-level state, surface="card" a self-contained card.

**Keywords:** empty, zero state, blank slate, no results, placeholder, onboarding, no data

## Usage

Use EmptyState when a content area has no items, no search results, or no first-time setup yet. The title should name the empty condition and the description/action should give the user a next step.

### Best practices

- Do: Explain what is empty in plain language, such as "No posts yet" or "No matching collectors".
- Do: Offer one next step when the user can recover, create, clear filters, or start setup.
- Do: Keep the icon decorative and make the title carry the meaning.
- Do: For a search or filter result, name the query back to the user and offer the way out, such as "No results for 'quarterly'" with a Clear filters action. An empty result that does not say what was searched leaves the user unsure whether the query or the data was wrong.
- Don't: Use generic copy like "No data"; it gives users and agents no useful path forward.
- Don't: Park anything the user needs permanently here, such as setup instructions, billing notices, or keyboard shortcuts. An empty state is the one surface guaranteed to disappear the moment content exists, so information that matters after the first item is lost exactly when the user has learned enough to want it.
- Don't: Use it for a field's validation error — that is Field error messaging. Reserve tone="destructive" for a view or block that failed to load.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Icon | no | A decorative cue that reinforces the empty condition. |
| Title | yes | The short message naming what is empty. |
| Description | no | Supporting copy that explains why the state exists or what to try next. |
| Action | no | One clear button or link that moves the user forward. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| icon | ReactNode | — | Optional leading glyph — pass an `<Icon />`. Rendered in a soft muted disc. |
| title | ReactNode | — | The headline. Short and direct. |
| description | ReactNode | — | Optional supporting line beneath the title. |
| action | ReactNode | — | Optional action below the copy — typically a `<Button />`. |
| code | ReactNode | — | A large figure above the title, such as an error code (404). |
| tone | "neutral" \| "destructive" | "neutral" | destructive is an error state: a destructive icon disc (a warning by default) and role="alert" so it is announced. |
| size | "md" \| "lg" | "md" | lg is page-level: the title is an h2 and the block takes more room. md sits in a panel, list or card. |
| surface | "none" \| "card" | "none" | card draws it as a Card, for an error or empty block standing on its own in a page. |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, destructive
- **size**: md, lg
- **surface**: none, card

## Tokens used

`muted`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Decorative icon discs should not carry meaning the title doesn't already convey.
- Pair with an actionable next step so the zero-state is a path forward, not a dead end.

## Related

- Components: Button, Icon, Card, Banner, DataTable
- Patterns: FeedPage, ListDetailPage, DashboardPage

## Examples

### With icon and action

```tsx
import { Button, EmptyState, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<EmptyState icon={<Icon name="info" />} title="No posts yet" description="Create your first." action={<Button>New post</Button>} />
```

### No search results

```tsx
import { Button, EmptyState, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<EmptyState icon={<Icon name="search" />} title="No matching posts" description="Try a different keyword or clear your filters." action={<Button variant="secondary">Clear filters</Button>} />
```

### First-run setup

```tsx
import { Button, EmptyState, Icon, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<EmptyState surface="card" icon={<Icon name="sparkles" />} title="Start your collection" description="Create a first edition, import an existing drop, or invite collaborators." action={<Row gap={1}><Button>Create edition</Button><Button variant="ghost">Import</Button></Row>} />
```

### Page-level error

```tsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from "@sableui/react"

<EmptyState tone="destructive" size="lg" code="404" title="Page not found" description="The page you are looking for has moved or never existed." action={<Button>Go home</Button>} />
```

### Error card

```tsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from "@sableui/react"

<EmptyState tone="destructive" surface="card" title="Could not load this edition" description="Check your connection and try again." action={<Button variant="secondary">Retry</Button>} />
```

### Empty table body

```tsx
import { DataTable, EmptyState } from "@sableui/react"

<DataTable data={[]} columns={[{ key: "name", header: "Collector" }, { key: "status", header: "Status" }]} empty={<EmptyState title="No collectors yet" description="Collectors appear here after the first mint." />} />
```

# Entity

**Status:** stable

A list-row record: leading visual + title/subtitle column + trailing action, with truncating text. Presentational by default (no hover); `interactive` rows gain the hover highlight, focus ring, and keyboard activation. Compact/comfortable density.

**Keywords:** entity, identity, object, avatar row

## Usage

Use Entity to show a compact identity block for a person, organization, file, project, or other object.

### Best practices

- Do: Use a clear title and one or two useful metadata lines.
- Do: Pair with Avatar or Badge (dot for a status) when identity needs state or type.
- Do: For a list, stack Entity rows directly in a column; each row owns its padding. For a list in a card, put the rows in CardList, which insets them to the card's own padding and divides them, so the rows line up with the card's header instead of being tuned by hand with px-* classes.
- Don't: Do not use Entity for long descriptions, editable fields, or full card content.
- Don't: Do not make the whole row a link when it also carries a trailing action. Nesting an interactive element inside a link is invalid, and the action becomes unreachable by keyboard.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| leading | ReactNode | — | Leading visual — typically an Avatar or an Icon. |
| title | ReactNode | — | Primary line (text-title-sm, truncated). Required. |
| subtitle | ReactNode | — | Secondary line (text-body-sm muted, truncated). |
| action | ReactNode | — | Trailing slot — typically a ghost icon Button or a StatusDot. |
| interactive | boolean | false | Make the whole row a target: the leading visual and text become a native <button> whose hit area stretches over the row (focus ring, Enter/Space). The action stays outside it. Requires onSelect. |
| onSelect | () => void | — | Activation handler for an interactive row (fired on click and Enter/Space). Required when interactive. |
| density | "compact" \| "comfortable" | "compact" | Row padding: compact (12px × 10px, the default) or comfortable (16px × 12px), on the spacing scale. The insets read --entity-px / --entity-py first, which CardList sets from the card's own padding so rows in a card line up with its header. |

## Variants

- **density**: compact, comfortable

## Tokens used

`muted`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Default rows are presentational layout; semantics come from the content you place in title/subtitle/action.
- interactive rows render a real <button> around the leading visual and text, with its ::after stretched over the whole row — native focus, a focus-visible ring, and Enter/Space. The action slot sits outside that button and above the overlay, so a Button there stays valid HTML and keeps its own clicks.
- Give any interactive action an accessible label (e.g. aria-label on a ghost icon Button).

## Related

- Components: Avatar, Badge, Description

## Examples

### Person row

```tsx
import { Avatar, Button, Entity, Icon } from "@sableui/react"

<Entity leading={<Avatar fallback="AM" />} title="Alex Morgan" subtitle="@alex" action={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="More"><Icon name="ellipsis" /></Button>} />
```

### Interactive (selectable) row

```tsx
import { Avatar, Entity } from "@sableui/react"

<Entity interactive onSelect={() => selectUser(user)} leading={<Avatar fallback="AM" />} title="Alex Morgan" subtitle="@alex" />
```

# Feedback

**Status:** stable

A compact feedback popover. Composes Popover + Textarea + Button + Toggle into a rating row plus a message field; submitting reports the rating + message and closes the popover.

**Keywords:** feedback, sentiment, rating, prompt

## Usage

Use Feedback to collect lightweight sentiment, usefulness, or quality signals from users.

### Best practices

- Do: Ask for feedback at a moment when the user has enough context to answer.
- Do: Keep the prompt short and optional unless feedback is required by the workflow.
- Don't: Do not use Feedback for errors, alerts, or required support forms.
- Don't: Do not require the message field. Most feedback is a rating with no comment, and forcing prose is how a feedback control stops being used.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string | "Feedback" | Trigger button text. |
| heading | string | "Send feedback" | Heading shown above the rating row. |
| placeholder | string | "What can we improve?" | Placeholder for the message field. |
| submitLabel | string | "Send" | Submit button text. |
| ratings | FeedbackRating[] | 🙁 / 😐 / 🙂 | The rating options shown as a row of toggles. Each is { value, label }. |
| onSubmit | (data: { rating?: string; message: string }) => void | — | Called with the selected rating + message when the form is submitted. |

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Trigger opens the popover on press; Base UI manages focus into the form and restores it to the trigger on close.
- The rating row is a Base UI ToggleGroup with arrow-key roving focus; each toggle carries an aria-label.
- The form is named by its heading (aria-labelledby), so it is announced as "Send feedback" rather than an unnamed form.
- The message field carries an aria-label matching its placeholder.
- Submit is disabled until there is a rating or a non-whitespace message. Either alone is a complete answer.

## Related

- Components: Toast, Banner, Form

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Feedback } from "@sableui/react"

<Feedback onSubmit={({ rating, message }) => console.log(rating, message)} />
```

### Custom labels

```tsx
import { Feedback } from "@sableui/react"

<Feedback label="Tell us" submitLabel="Send it" placeholder="Describe the issue…" />
```

# Fieldset

**Status:** stable

Form section panel (Card-like bordered surface) over Base UI Fieldset, with Legend/Description/Content/Footer parts.

**Keywords:** fieldset, form group, legend, fields

## Usage

Use Fieldset to group related controls under a shared label or explanation.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for grouped form sections such as contact details, preferences, or permissions.
- Do: Keep the legend meaningful so assistive tech and agents understand the group purpose.
- Don't: Do not use Fieldset as a generic spacing wrapper outside forms.
- Don't: Do not use a Legend that is really a heading. A legend names the group's question for assistive technology; using it as a section title puts a question mark where the outline should be.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fieldset | yes | The bordered group: a native <fieldset> whose disabled state reaches every control inside it. |
| Legend | yes | FieldsetLegend: the question the group's controls answer, announced before each of them. |
| Description | no | FieldsetDescription: muted copy under the legend. |
| Content | yes | FieldsetContent: the stacked body, one Field per control. |
| Footer | no | FieldsetFooter: the group's actions on a muted wash. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FieldsetLegend | ComponentPropsWithRef<typeof Fieldset.Legend> | The group's name — the question its controls answer. Base UI renders it as a <div> wired to the <fieldset> through aria-labelledby, so a screen reader announces it before each control in the group. This is the whole reason to reach for Fieldset. |
| FieldsetDescription | ComponentPropsWithRef<"p"> | Muted supporting copy under the legend. |
| FieldsetContent | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | The stacked body holding one Field per control. |
| FieldsetFooter | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | Optional right-aligned action bar on a muted wash. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| disabled | boolean | — | Disables the whole group. Renders <fieldset disabled> (native control disabling) and surfaces data-[disabled] for dimming. |
| render | ReactElement \| function | — | Base UI render prop to replace or compose the underlying element. |
| className | string | — | Merged onto each part via cn() for one-off overrides. |

## Tokens used

`card`, `card-foreground`, `border`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `muted`

## Accessibility

- Base.Root renders a native <fieldset>; Base.Legend renders an auto-associated label, so screen readers announce the group name.
- disabled propagates as native <fieldset disabled>, disabling all contained controls.
- Wrap each control inside FieldsetContent in a Field, which wires its own label, description and error to the control.

## Related

- Components: Form, Label, Description

## Examples

### A grouped question

```tsx
import { Button, Checkbox, Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetDescription, FieldsetFooter, FieldsetLegend } from "@sableui/react"

<Fieldset>
	<FieldsetLegend>Notify me about</FieldsetLegend>
	<FieldsetDescription>Pick what reaches your inbox.</FieldsetDescription>
	<FieldsetContent>
		<Field label="Mentions" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox defaultChecked /></Field>
		<Field label="Replies" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox /></Field>
		<Field label="Direct messages" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox /></Field>
	</FieldsetContent>
	<FieldsetFooter>
		<Button>Save preferences</Button>
	</FieldsetFooter>
</Fieldset>
```

### Why a fieldset, and when it is wrong

```tsx
import { Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetLegend, Radio, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

// Fieldset groups inputs that are ONE question with multiple parts, and gives
// the group a single accessible name — which is the part you cannot do with a
// div and a heading.

<Fieldset>
  <FieldsetLegend>Digest frequency</FieldsetLegend>
  <FieldsetContent>
    <RadioGroup defaultValue="weekly">
      <Field label="Daily" orientation="horizontal"><Radio value="daily" /></Field>
      <Field label="Weekly" orientation="horizontal"><Radio value="weekly" /></Field>
    </RadioGroup>
  </FieldsetContent>
</Fieldset>

// ✓ Required for radio groups: without a fieldset the options have no shared
//   name, so a screen reader announces "Weekly, radio" with no question.
// ✗ Not for visual grouping of unrelated fields. Use PanelSection on a panel or
//   a Card section on a page; a legend that is really a heading lies to
//   assistive technology about the form's structure.
```

# FileDropzone

**Status:** stable

Drag-and-drop target and file picker in one keyboard-operable button. Checks accept, maxSize and maxFiles on every selection, announces each rejection with how to fix it, and hands accepted files to you to list as Attachments.

**Keywords:** file upload, dropzone, drag and drop, file picker, upload, attach file, file input, import

## Usage

Use FileDropzone where adding files is the main job of a section — an upload step, an import screen, a document request. It gives the drag gesture a visible target and the same action a button for everyone who does not drag. It holds no list: render accepted files as Attachments beneath it, where progress, retry and remove belong.

### Best practices

- Do: State the constraints in `description` ("PNG or PDF, up to 10 MB") and give `acceptLabel` the same words, so a rejection repeats the rule the user already read.
- Do: Pair it with a list of Attachment rows that you own. Once files are added, switch to `size="sm"` so the target stays available without pushing the list below the fold.
- Do: Cap the total by passing `maxFiles={limit - files.length}`; the dropzone only sees one selection at a time. When none remain, set `disabled` and say why in `description` ("Remove one to add another").
- Don't: Do not use it for an incidental attach action inside a composer or a toolbar. A paperclip Button that opens the picker is the right weight there; ChatComposer already has one.
- Don't: Do not rely on `accept` alone to protect the server. The dropzone's checks are for the user's benefit; validate type and size again where the file is received.
- Don't: Do not silently drop rejected files. The zone announces each one, but if you also discard files later (a server-side limit), say so on the Attachment with `status="error"` and a fix.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zone | yes | A full-width button with a dashed border. Click, Enter or Space opens the picker; it is also the drop target. |
| Icon | no | A decorative mark that lifts while a file is dragged over the zone. |
| Label and description | yes | The call to action and the constraints. Together they form the button's accessible name. |
| Status | yes | A role=status region, present from the first render, that lists each rejected file and how to fix it. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| accept | string | — | Native accept syntax — `.pdf`, `application/pdf`, `image/*`, comma-separated. Enforced on drop and on pick. |
| maxSize | number | — | Largest accepted file, in bytes. |
| multiple | boolean | false | Accept more than one file per selection. |
| maxFiles | number | — | Most files accepted from one selection when `multiple`. Pass the remaining capacity to cap a total. |
| onFilesAccepted | (files: File[]) => void | — | Files that passed every check, in selection order. |
| onFilesRejected | (rejections: FileRejection[]) => void | — | Files that failed, each with `code` (file-invalid-type, file-too-large, too-many-files) and the announced `message`. |
| label | ReactNode | "Drop a file here or browse" | The visible call to action. Pluralised automatically when `multiple`. |
| description | ReactNode | — | The constraints in words, shown under the label. |
| acceptLabel | string | — | How the accepted types complete "Use … instead" in an error ("PNG or PDF", "an image or PDF"). Without it a type error can only say "Choose a different file". |
| formatError | (rejection) => string | — | Replace the rejection copy, e.g. to localize it. |
| icon | string | "arrow-up" | Semantic icon name. |
| size | "md" \| "sm" | "md" | `md` is the empty-section target; `sm` is a single-row strip above an existing list. |
| disabled / required / id / aria-invalid | — | — | Standard form-control props. `id` lands on the button, so `<Field>` labels it; `aria-invalid` draws the destructive border. |

## Variants

- **size**: md, sm

## Tokens used

`card`, `foreground`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `border-strong`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `ring`, `destructive`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Zone · _no motion_ — The zone is the section's content, present from the start. An entrance would only delay the drop target someone is already dragging toward.
- **response** · Zone · `motion-interactive` — Hover strengthens the border to primary, which confirms the whole dashed area — not just the word "browse" — is the click target.
- **transition** · Icon · `motion-interactive` — When a file crosses into the zone the icon fills and lifts and the surface tints. That is the only signal that releasing here will work; without it users drop on the page and the browser opens the file instead.
- **activity** · Zone · _no motion_ — The zone hands files off immediately and never uploads. Transfer progress belongs on each Attachment, where it can be per-file and retryable.

## Accessibility

- The zone is a native button: Enter or Space opens the system picker, so dragging is never the only way in.
- Rejections render into a role=status region that exists from the first render, and the button's aria-describedby points at it while it has content, so the reason is still read when focus returns.
- Every error names the file and says how to fix it ("Choose a smaller file"), rather than only what failed.
- The underlying file input is visually hidden and removed from the tab order; the button is the single focus stop.

## Related

- Components: Attachment, Input, Button, Progress

## Examples

### Images and PDFs

```tsx
import { FileDropzone } from "@sableui/react"

<FileDropzone accept="image/*,.pdf" acceptLabel="an image or PDF" maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024} multiple description="Images or PDFs, up to 10 MB each" onFilesAccepted={(files) => console.log(files)} />
```

### With an Attachment list

```tsx
import { Attachment, FileDropzone } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
	<FileDropzone size="sm" multiple description="Up to 5 files" onFilesAccepted={(files) => console.log(files)} />
	<Attachment name="contract.pdf" meta="2.4 MB · PDF" />
	<Attachment name="site-photo.jpg" meta="Uploading…" status="uploading" progress={42} />
</div>
```

### In a field

```tsx
import { Field, FileDropzone } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Proof of address" description="A bill or statement from the last 3 months."><FileDropzone accept=".pdf" acceptLabel="a PDF" maxSize={5 * 1024 * 1024} description="PDF, up to 5 MB" /></Field>
```

# Form

**Status:** stable

A styled <form> plus Field — the form orchestration layer, built on Base UI Form and Field. Field wires a label, control, helper text, and error message together with correct a11y (htmlFor, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, required) automatically, around any Sable control. Validation-library-agnostic: pass each Field an error string, or let Form check native constraints and Field validate functions on submit.

**Keywords:** form, field, label, validation, error, required, settings, input

## Usage

Use Form and Field as the default wrapper for Sable form controls. Field owns the label, description, required state, and error wiring so agents do not hand-roll inconsistent label/input relationships.

### Best practices

- Do: Wrap each control in Field unless a specialized component already owns its label and error semantics.
- Do: Use Field error for validation messages so aria-invalid and aria-describedby are wired together.
- Do: For built-in checks, put required / type="email" / minLength on the control (or a validate function on Field) inside a Form: on submit the message appears under the field and the first invalid control is focused. Pass server errors to Form errors, keyed by Field name.
- Do: Use horizontal Field orientation only for one-line boolean controls like Checkbox, Switch, or Radio.
- Don't: Use placeholder text as the only label. A visible label should identify the field.
- Don't: Wrap multiple controls in one Field. Field expects a single child control and wires that one control (an Input or Textarea nested in a wrapper is still found through context).

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Form | yes | The native form element (Base UI Form) with vertical field spacing; validates its Fields on submit. |
| Field | yes | The label/control/helper/error wrapper for one control. |
| Control | yes | The single Sable control. Base UI-backed controls register with Field through context; the child is also cloned with the same wiring. |
| Error | no | Validation copy associated with the control: the error prop when set, otherwise the Base UI validation message (native constraint, validate function, or Form errors). |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field | { label?: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; error?: ReactNode; required?: boolean; disabled?: boolean; name?: string; validate?: (value, formValues) => string \| string[] \| null \| Promise<…>; validationMode?: "onSubmit" \| "onBlur" \| "onChange"; validationDebounceTime?: number; orientation?: "vertical" \| "horizontal"; className?: string; children: ReactElement } | Wraps a single control element (e.g. <Input />) on Base UI Field and wires label (htmlFor + aria-labelledby), helper text and error (aria-describedby), aria-invalid, and required onto it automatically. Base UI-backed controls (Input, Textarea, Select, Combobox, NumberField, Checkbox, Switch, Slider, OtpField…) register through context; the child is also cloned so plain elements keep the same wiring. error renders a destructive message and takes precedence; without it the slot shows Base UI's validation message when the field fails (native constraint, validate, or Form errors). required adds the native attribute plus a visual asterisk (defaults to false). disabled disables the control and dims the label. name keys the field in Form errors / onFormSubmit. validationMode overrides the Form's. orientation defaults to "vertical" (label → control); "horizontal" places control then label inline for a single checkbox / switch / radio — the control centres on the label's first line (it stays there when the label wraps) and description/error sit in the label's column. The root, label, description, error and control carry data-invalid / data-valid, data-touched, data-dirty, data-filled, data-focused and data-disabled for state styling. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Form | { validationMode?: "onSubmit" \| "onBlur" \| "onChange"; errors?: Record<string, string \| string[]>; onFormSubmit?: (values, details) => void; actionsRef?: RefObject<Form.Actions> } + ComponentPropsWithRef<"form"> | — | A <form> laid out as a vertical column with comfortable field spacing (override with className, e.g. gap-4). On submit it validates every Field (native constraints plus Field validate), shows each message under its field, focuses the first invalid control, and only then calls onSubmit. validationMode defaults to "onSubmit" (then live re-validation on change). errors shows external (e.g. server) messages keyed by Field name and clears one when its field is edited. onFormSubmit receives the named Field values and prevents the native submit. A control outside any Field is still checked by the browser before onSubmit runs; pass noValidate to skip that. |
| validationMode | "onSubmit" \| "onBlur" \| "onChange" | "onSubmit" | When Fields validate. After the first submit, fields re-check as the user edits. A Field's own validationMode wins. |
| errors | Record<string, string \| string[]> | — | External (e.g. server) messages keyed by Field name, shown under that field. Each clears when its field is edited. |
| onFormSubmit | (values: Record<string, unknown>, details) => void | — | Called with the named Field values after validation passes; prevents the native submit. |
| actionsRef | RefObject<{ validate(name?: string): void }> | — | Imperative handle to validate every field, or one by name. |

## Tokens used

`muted-foreground`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Field auto-wires label htmlFor ↔ control id, aria-describedby (description + error), and aria-invalid — so the label, helper, and error are all announced for the control.
- required adds the native `required` attribute (not just a visual asterisk); the asterisk is aria-hidden.
- Error text is associated via aria-describedby and reinforced by the destructive color, not color alone.
- Inside Form, a failed submit focuses the first invalid control and shows its message inline instead of a browser bubble.

## Related

- Components: Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Switch, Button
- Patterns: SettingsPage, AuthPage

## Examples

### Text field

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Email" description="We'll never share it." required><Input type="email" /></Field>
```

### Field with an error

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Password" error="Must be at least 8 characters."><Input type="password" /></Field>
```

### Validated on submit

```tsx
import { Button, Field, Form, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Form onSubmit={handleSubmit}><Field label="Handle" required validate={(value) => String(value).length < 3 ? "At least 3 characters." : null}><Input name="handle" /></Field><Button type="submit">Claim</Button></Form>
```

### Server errors

```tsx
import { Field, Form, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Form errors={serverErrors}><Field label="Email" name="email"><Input type="email" /></Field></Form>
```

### Form

```tsx
import { Button, Checkbox, Field, Form, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Form onSubmit={handleSubmit}><Field label="Name"><Input /></Field><Field label="Subscribe" orientation="horizontal"><Checkbox /></Field><Button type="submit">Save</Button></Form>
```

### Settings form

```tsx
import { Button, Field, Form, Input, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Form onSubmit={handleSubmit}><Field label="Display name" description="Shown on your profile."><Input defaultValue="Nova Reed" /></Field><Field label="Visibility"><Select defaultValue="public"><SelectTrigger /><SelectContent><SelectItem value="public">Public</SelectItem><SelectItem value="private">Private</SelectItem></SelectContent></Select></Field><Button type="submit">Save changes</Button></Form>
```

# GlidingHighlight

**Status:** stable

One highlight that travels to the active item, instead of each item toggling its own background. Measured, not assumed, so rows of unequal height stay exact.

**Keywords:** highlight, active, selection, indicator, menu, list, glide, slide, thumb, hover

## Usage

Use GlidingHighlight for a set of items where one is active at a time and the pointer or arrow keys move between them — a menu, an option list, a command palette, a segmented control. It replaces per-item `hover:bg-*` with a single element that moves.

### Best practices

- Do: Pass `hovered ?? selected`. The fallback is what makes the pointer leaving a menu return the highlight to the current choice instead of dropping it, so the reader's place is never lost.
- Do: Reach for it wherever a list is keyboard-navigable. The gain is largest for arrow keys: a background that teleports between rows makes the eye re-find the highlight at every step, where one that moves can be tracked while it travels — which is what keeps a long list readable in motion rather than only at rest.
- Do: Keep selection semantics on the items — `aria-selected`, `aria-current`, `data-selected`. The highlight is `aria-hidden` decoration over whatever the children already announce.
- Don't: Do not use it for items that are not mutually exclusive. A travelling highlight says 'one of these, and it is this one'; over a multi-select list it contradicts the checkboxes beside it, and only one of the two can be right.
- Don't: Do not put non-item chrome among the direct children — a group heading, a separator, a footer hint. Every direct child is a measurable row, so `active` counts them, and the highlight lands one row off from the index the caller is reasoning about. Wrap the items in their own GlidingHighlight, or move the chrome outside.
- Don't: Do not drive it from a scroll position or a timer. It is an affordance for a set with a discrete active member; a highlight that moves without an item becoming active reads as the interface selecting things on its own.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container | yes | Positioning context for the highlight. Each direct child is measured as one item. |
| Highlight | yes | The travelling element. `aria-hidden`, absolutely positioned, invisible until something is active. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| active | number \| null | — | Index of the item the highlight sits behind, or `null` for none. Pass `hovered ?? selected`. |
| orientation | "vertical" \| "horizontal" | — | Deprecated and ignored: the highlight measures both axes, so a horizontal row needs no flag. |
| onPointerLeave | PointerEventHandler (and every other div prop) | — | The container is a plain div, so its props pass through. For a hover-following list, reset the hovered index here so the highlight returns to the selected row when the pointer leaves. |
| highlightClassName | string | — | Class for the travelling highlight itself, for changing its fill or radius. The radius defaults to `sable-frame-inner`, so inside a `sable-frame` container it nests concentrically; in any other rounded, inset container pass `rounded-concentric-<outer>/<inset>` here and on the rows. The container's own `className` styles the list. |

## Tokens used

`accent`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Highlight · _no motion_ — It deliberately does not animate in. Fading it up at rest position — usually row 0 — makes a menu look like it opened with the first item pre-selected, which is a claim about state that is not true. It stays invisible until something is genuinely active.
- **response** · Container · _no motion_ — The container is not the control; the items are, and they own their own pointer states. This draws the result.
- **transition** · Highlight · `motion-interactive` — The travel IS the component — a highlight that jumps is just a background toggle with extra machinery. Position, size and opacity ride one declaration so a tall row's height cannot catch up after its position has, which would read as the highlight stretching into place rather than moving.
- **activity** · Highlight · _no motion_ — Nothing here is indeterminate. A list still loading its options shows a Skeleton in place of the rows.

## Accessibility

- The highlight is `aria-hidden` and carries no semantics — it renders selection, it does not declare it. Keep `aria-selected` / `aria-current` on the items themselves.
- Pointer-free by construction (`pointer-events-none`), so it can never intercept a click meant for the item beneath it.
- Works with roving-tabindex and `aria-activedescendant` lists alike: it reads an index the caller already owns, and does not manage focus.
- Under reduced motion or with MotionProvider off, the highlight moves instantly rather than gliding — the active item is still shown, which is the part that carries meaning.

## Related

- Components: Menu, Select, Combobox, CommandMenu, SideNav

## Examples

### A hoverable menu, returning home on leave

```tsx
import { GlidingHighlight } from "@sableui/react"

<GlidingHighlight active={hovered ?? selected} className="sable-frame sable-surface sable-surface-popover sable-frame-popover" onPointerLeave={() => setHovered(null)}>{items.map((item, i) => (<button key={item.id} type="button" className="sable-frame-inner px-2 py-1.5 text-start" onPointerEnter={() => setHovered(i)} onClick={() => setSelected(i)}>{item.label}</button>))}</GlidingHighlight>
```

### Horizontal, as a segmented control

```tsx
import { GlidingHighlight } from "@sableui/react"

<GlidingHighlight active={tab} className="sable-well flex gap-1 rounded-md p-1" highlightClassName="rounded-concentric-md/1">{tabs.map((t, i) => (<button key={t} type="button" className="rounded-concentric-md/1 px-3 py-1" onClick={() => setTab(i)}>{t}</button>))}</GlidingHighlight>
```

### Keyboard navigation — the case it exists for

```tsx
import { GlidingHighlight } from "@sableui/react"

<GlidingHighlight active={cursor} onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === "ArrowDown") setCursor((c) => (c + 1) % rows.length) }}>{rows.map((r) => (<div key={r.id} role="option" aria-selected={false}>{r.label}</div>))}</GlidingHighlight>
```

---

# InlineStatus

**Status:** stable

A borderless single-line status message — a leading semantic icon + one line of text over the canonical tone scale (neutral/info/success/warning/destructive). The non-boxed sibling of Note for inline affirmations, errors, and progress; pass a custom icon (e.g. a Spinner) for a pending row.

**Keywords:** inline status, state, message, availability

## Usage

Use InlineStatus for short state messages placed near the thing they describe.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it beside inputs, rows, actions, or settings that need local status.
- Do: Keep the message brief and pair color with text.
- Don't: Do not use InlineStatus for global announcements or page-level alerts.
- Don't: Do not use tone as the only signal. Colour alone fails for colour-blind users — the leading icon is what carries the meaning, so never hide it.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tone | "neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" | "neutral" | Severity tone — drives the leading icon (name + color) and the text color. The shared status-tone vocabulary (STATUS_TONES). |
| size | "sm" \| "md" | "sm" | Text size: sm (text-body-sm) or md (text-body-md). sm is the default for inline placement under a control; md matches surrounding body copy. |
| icon | ReactNode | — | Override the leading glyph (e.g. a <Spinner />); otherwise the tone selects it. |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, info, success, warning, destructive
- **size**: sm, md

## Tokens used

`tone-info`, `success`, `tone-warning`, `destructive`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Color reinforces, never replaces, meaning — the leading icon and the message text carry the status.
- For a live status (e.g. a form submit result), render it in an aria-live region or pair it with the field's error wiring so the change is announced.

## Related

- Components: StatusDot, Badge, Banner, Note

## Examples

### Tones

```tsx
import { InlineStatus, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

<Stack gap={1}><InlineStatus tone="success">Top-up confirmed.</InlineStatus><InlineStatus tone="destructive">Insufficient balance.</InlineStatus></Stack>
```

### Pending (custom icon)

```tsx
import { InlineStatus, Spinner } from "@sableui/react"

<InlineStatus tone="neutral" icon={<Spinner size="sm" />}>Preparing transaction…</InlineStatus>
```

---

# Input

**Status:** stable

Styled native text input. Soft-square (rounded-sm), card surface, 2px focus ring; aria-invalid raises the destructive error treatment.

**Keywords:** input, text input, field, form, email, search, file, invalid, validation

## Usage

Use Input for short freeform text, search, email, password, file, and native input types. In forms, wrap Input in Field so label, description, required state, and validation messaging stay accessible and consistent.

### Best practices

- Do: Pair every Input with a visible label through Field or an explicit label/htmlFor connection.
- Do: Use type, inputMode, autoComplete, and placeholder as progressive hints, not as the only label.
- Do: Set aria-invalid or use Field error copy when validation fails.
- Do: Keep a focusable field at 16px or larger on mobile. iOS Safari zooms the whole page when a focused input computes under 16px and never zooms back out. Input handles this itself — below the sm breakpoint it renders text-body-lg (17px) and returns to text-body-md at sm and up. Build a custom field the same way: a second paired tier under a max-sm: variant, never a hand-set font-size.
- Don't: Override an Input's type with a page tier below 16px (text-body-md, text-body-sm, text-label-*) without a >=16px mobile arm — that reintroduces the iOS focus zoom.
- Don't: Use placeholder text as the label; it disappears once the user types and is not enough context.
- Don't: Use Input for long body copy. Use Textarea for multi-line content.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | yes | The native input element with Sable surface, disabled, focus, and invalid styling. |
| Label | yes | Usually provided by Field or a separate Label. It gives the input its visible purpose. |
| Description | no | Optional helper copy connected through aria-describedby when using Field. |
| Error | no | Validation message paired with aria-invalid and destructive styling. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size | "md" \| "xs" | "md" | md is the form field. xs is the dense inset field of a tool panel (an inset canvas fill, no outline, tight padding) — the same ladder as Select and Combobox. Use it instead of overriding the height with className. |
| type | string | "text" | Native input type (text, email, password, search, number, file, …). type="file" themes the native selector button via file: token utilities. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Dims the control and blocks pointer interaction. |
| aria-invalid | boolean | — | Surfaces the destructive border + ring. Base UI form fields set this automatically. |
| ...props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"input"> | — | All native input attributes (placeholder, value, onChange, ref, …) pass through. |

## Variants

- **size**: md, xs

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <input> — labels, keyboard, and form semantics come for free.
- Renders through Base UI's Input (Field.Control): inside a Field it picks up the label, description, error and validity wiring from context, even when nested in a wrapper.
- Always associate a <label htmlFor> (or wrap) — placeholder text is not a label.
- Focus-visible ring uses the --ring token at 40% opacity.
- Set aria-invalid='true' on error so the destructive treatment is conveyed, not color-only.

## Related

- Components: Field, Form, Textarea, SearchInput, NumberField
- Patterns: SettingsPage, AuthPage

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Input placeholder="Search posts" />
```

### With a label

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Email"><Input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" /></Field>
```

### Field with helper text

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Display name" description="Shown on your public profile."><Input placeholder="Nova Reed" /></Field>
```

### Field error

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Email" error="Enter a valid email address."><Input type="email" defaultValue="not-an-email" /></Field>
```

### Search input

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Search posts"><Input type="search" placeholder="Search by title, creator, or tag" /></Field>
```

### Invalid

```tsx
import { Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Input aria-invalid defaultValue="not-an-email" />
```

### File

```tsx
import { Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Input type="file" accept="image/*" />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
import { Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Input disabled placeholder="Disabled" />
```
