# Kbd

**Status:** stable

A keyboard key indicator. Renders a styled <kbd> key cap in monospace; compose several with a + between to show a shortcut combo. `mod` renders the platform modifier (⌘ or Ctrl).

**Keywords:** keyboard, shortcut, key, kbd

## Usage

Use Kbd to display keyboard keys or shortcuts in help text, menus, and docs.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it only for literal keyboard input such as Cmd, Enter, or Esc.
- Do: Keep multi-key shortcuts readable by separating individual keys.
- Don't: Do not use Kbd as a decorative badge or button replacement.
- Don't: Do not hardcode ⌘ or Ctrl. The modifier differs by platform; use `<Kbd mod />`, which renders ⌘ on macOS/iOS and Ctrl elsewhere, or Windows users read Mac keys.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mod | boolean | false | Render the platform's shortcut modifier in place of children: ⌘ on macOS and iOS, Ctrl everywhere else. Server-rendered as Ctrl and corrected on hydration. |
| className | string | — | Merge additional classes onto the key cap. |
| ...props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"kbd"> | — | All native <kbd> attributes (children, ref, etc.). |

## Tokens used

`border`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Uses the semantic <kbd> element so assistive tech announces keyboard input.
- Monospace key text keeps single keys and symbols legible at small sizes.

## Related

- Components: Code, Menu, CommandMenu

## Examples

### Single keys

```tsx
import { Kbd } from "@sableui/react"

<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
```

### Combo

```tsx
import { Kbd, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Kbd mod /><span>+</span><Kbd>K</Kbd></Row>
```

---

# Label

**Status:** stable

Styled native <label>. Paired label typography via a size step (xs / sm / md / lg, all sentence case) or an uppercase eyebrow (eyebrow), non-selectable, dims when its peer control is disabled. Optional hint adds a dotted-underline tooltip affordance.

**Keywords:** label, form label, control, accessibility

## Usage

Use Label to name a form control and create a clear accessible relationship with that control.

### Best practices

- Do: Use explicit, persistent labels for inputs, selects, textareas, and grouped controls.
- Do: Place helper text separately so the label stays short and direct.
- Don't: Do not rely on placeholder text as the only label for a control.
- Don't: Do not use it as a bare styled span. A Label without htmlFor or a wrapped control looks like a label and does nothing — clicking it will not focus the field, which is the entire point.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| htmlFor | string | — | Associates the label with a control by its id (native <label for>). |
| size | "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "lg" | Paired label typography step, all sentence case. xs is simply the smallest; for an uppercase eyebrow use eyebrow. |
| eyebrow | boolean | false | Set the label as an eyebrow: the uppercase, letter-spaced text-overline tier (themeable to sentence case). Replaces size. For a kicker above a group, not an ordinary field label. |
| hint | ReactNode | — | When set, the label gets a dotted-underline affordance and reveals this content in a tooltip on hover/focus. |
| className | string | — | Merge or override classes via cn(). |

## Variants

- **size**: xs, sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <label> — clicking it focuses/activates the associated control.
- Associate with a control via htmlFor (matching the control's id) or by wrapping the control.
- In a form, use Field: it renders this Label, wires htmlFor/id, and dims the label when the field is disabled. Hand-wired outside a Field, the label only dims via peer-disabled when the control carries `peer` AND precedes the Label in the DOM (Tailwind peer-* only matches a later sibling).
- With `hint`, the label becomes focusable and the help text is announced via the tooltip's aria-describedby — so the affordance works for keyboard and screen-reader users, not just hover.

## Related

- Components: Input, Textarea, Fieldset, Form, Field

## Examples

### With control

```tsx
import { Input, Label, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

<Stack gap={1}><Label htmlFor="name">Display name</Label><Input id="name" /></Stack>
```

### In a form

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Display name" disabled><Input /></Field>
```

### With hint

```tsx
import { Label } from "@sableui/react"

<Label htmlFor="royalty" hint="A percentage of every resale, paid to you.">Royalty</Label>
```

---

# Marker

**Status:** stable

A non-message row in a conversation: streaming status, system note, bordered notice, or a labelled rule for date breaks. Quieter than the message tier by design.

**Keywords:** chat status, typing indicator, thinking, streaming, tool call, system message, date separator, date break, conversation divider

## Usage

Everything in a conversation that is not a message. Date breaks, "Carla joined", "Thinking…", "Ran search — 3 results", "Message failed to send". One component because they share one job: annotate the stream without competing with it.

### Best practices

- Do: Use `status` with `icon="spinner" spin` for work in flight, and add `shimmer` while text is actually streaming. The shimmer is scale-aware, so it freezes with the rest of the system under reduced motion.
- Do: Use `variant="separator"` for date breaks. The label sits between two rules, which reads as a division of the transcript rather than as another thing someone said.
- Do: Replace a status marker's text as the work progresses — "Thinking…" → "Searching the docs" → "Writing the answer". It is a live region, so each change is announced.
- Do: Reach for `bordered` only when a note needs containing — an error, an escalation, a retention notice. Boxing routine system events makes a transcript look like a list of alerts.
- Don't: Do not style a Marker up to message weight. Its whole value is being below that tier; a marker as loud as a message competes with the conversation it is annotating.
- Don't: Do not leave a status marker mounted after the work finishes. A permanent "Thinking…" is a live region that never resolves, which is worse than no status at all.
- Don't: Do not use it for a message from a person or an assistant. That is `Message` + `Bubble` — a marker has no author and no side.
- Don't: Do not set `live` on a `separator` or on a run of `note` markers. Announcing every date break and join event turns the live region into noise and buries the status that mattered.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | "status" \| "note" \| "bordered" \| "separator" | "status" | `status` for live activity, `note` for a system event, `bordered` for a note that needs containing, `separator` for a labelled rule. |
| icon | string | — | Semantic icon name shown before the label, resolved through IconProvider. |
| spin | boolean | false | Spin the icon — pair with `icon="spinner"` for work in flight. |
| shimmer | boolean | false | Sweep the label while something is streaming, via the scale-aware `motion-text-shimmer` recipe (freezes under reduced motion). |
| live | boolean | true for `status`, false otherwise | Announce the label to assistive tech as it changes. On for `status`, because a screen-reader user otherwise gets silence for the whole generation and no way to tell a slow answer from a dead one. |
| ...div props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | — | Spread onto the row. |

## Variants

- **variant**: status, note, bordered, separator

## Tokens used

`muted-foreground`, `muted`, `border`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- `status` markers render as `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so a change of activity is announced without interrupting whatever is being read.
- The other variants are silent by default and can opt in with `live` — announcing every date break and join event would bury the status that mattered.
- The separator's rules are `aria-hidden`, leaving only the label in the accessibility tree; the shimmer is decoration over readable text, not a replacement for it.
- `motion-text-shimmer` keeps the label opaque through every frame — the gradient runs muted-foreground → foreground rather than fading to transparent, so the text never becomes unreadable mid-animation, and `--motion-scale` freezes it entirely under reduced motion.

## Related

- Components: Message, Bubble, MessageScroller, InlineStatus, Separator

## Examples

### Streaming status

```tsx
import { Marker } from "@sableui/react"

<Marker icon="spinner" spin shimmer>Thinking…</Marker>
```

### Date break

```tsx
import { Marker } from "@sableui/react"

<Marker variant="separator">Yesterday</Marker>
```

### System note

```tsx
import { Marker } from "@sableui/react"

<Marker variant="note" icon="user">Carla joined the conversation</Marker>
```

### A notice that needs containing

```tsx
import { Marker } from "@sableui/react"

<Marker variant="bordered" icon="warning">This conversation will be archived in 7 days.</Marker>
```

### In a transcript

```tsx
import { Bubble, Marker, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<MessageScroller className="h-96">
	<Marker variant="separator">Today</Marker>
	<Message messageId="m1"><Bubble>Can you summarise the release?</Bubble></Message>
	<Marker variant="note" icon="sparkles">Ran changelog — 12 entries</Marker>
	<Marker icon="spinner" spin shimmer>Writing the answer</Marker>
</MessageScroller>
```

# Marquee

**Status:** stable

Seamless, constant-speed infinite loop (logos, tags, testimonials). Zero-dependency: duplicates children to fill the track and advances exactly one group + gap per iteration so it never seams. Pauses on hover/focus; freezes to a scroll region when motion is off/reduced.

**Keywords:** marquee, ticker, scrolling, ambient

## Usage

Use Marquee for decorative or ambient continuous content where motion supports the surface.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for low-priority repeated content such as logos, tags, or lightweight highlights.
- Do: Respect reduced motion and keep the content understandable without relying on animation.
- Don't: Do not put critical messages, controls, or required reading inside Marquee.
- Don't: Do not put content that must be read in a Marquee. It moves continuously, so anything longer than a logo or a short label cannot be read reliably — and it must stop for prefers-reduced-motion.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direction | "left" \| "right" \| "up" \| "down" | "left" | Scroll direction; up/down switch to a vertical loop, which needs a bounded height (e.g. className="h-56"). |
| speed | number | 40 | Constant speed in px/s — independent of content length. |
| gap | string | "calc(var(--spacing) * 8)" | Gap between items (any CSS length). Use a spacing-scale value (calc(var(--spacing) * n)) so it moves with density. |
| pauseOnHover | boolean | true | Pause while hovered or keyboard-focused (WCAG 2.2.2). |
| controls | boolean | false | Render a visible pause/play control — recommended for WCAG 2.2.2 when content auto-scrolls. |
| fade | boolean | false | Fade the leading/trailing edges with a mask. |
| label | string | — | Accessible label for the scrolling region. |

## Accessibility

- Duplicate groups are aria-hidden, so screen readers read the content once.
- Pauses on hover and focus-within; under prefers-reduced-motion / MotionProvider off it stops and becomes a normal scroll region.
- Decorative by default — pass a label only when the row conveys meaning.

## Related

- Components: Scroller, Carousel, Badge

## Examples

### Logo row

```tsx
import { Marquee } from "@sableui/react"

<Marquee>{logos.map((l) => <img key={l.id} src={l.src} alt={l.name} className="h-8" />)}</Marquee>
```

### Reverse, faster

```tsx
import { Badge, Marquee } from "@sableui/react"

<Marquee direction="right" speed={70}>{tags.map((t) => <Badge key={t} appearance="outline">{t}</Badge>)}</Marquee>
```

### Vertical

```tsx
import { Marquee } from "@sableui/react"

<Marquee direction="up" className="h-64">{items}</Marquee>
```

---

# Menu

**Status:** stable

Dropdown menu over Base UI Menu — roving focus, typeahead, ARIA menu/menuitem wiring, collision-aware positioning, Esc/outside dismissal. Trigger + portal-rendered popup with items, groups, and separators.

**Keywords:** menu, dropdown, actions, commands

## Usage

Use Menu for a compact list of actions opened from a visible trigger.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for secondary or grouped commands that do not need to be visible all the time.
- Do: Keep item labels action-oriented and easy to scan.
- Do: Inside a <Workspace> a Menu adapts automatically — its popup re-applies the compact density across the portal, so items render on the chrome type tier and the control ladder resolves to workspace sizes. Do NOT override the size per call site; that was necessary before v0.41 and is now drift.
- Don't: Do not use Menu for complex forms, persistent navigation, or arbitrary rich content.
- Don't: Do not build a Select out of it. A menu fires actions and has no value; a Select holds one and reports changes. Swapping them loses form semantics and keyboard type-ahead.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MenuTrigger | yes | The control that opens the menu. |
| MenuContent | yes | The floating command surface. |
| MenuItem | yes | One selectable command. |
| MenuSeparator | no | A divider between groups. |
| MenuGroup | no | A grouped set of menu items. |
| MenuGroupLabel | no | A label for a group of items. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MenuTrigger | Base UI Menu.Trigger props + render | The button that opens the menu. Compose with render={<Button … />}. |
| MenuContent | Base UI Popup props + side: 'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' + align: 'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' + sideOffset: number + className | Portal + Positioner + Popup. side picks which side of the trigger the popup renders against (auto-flips on collision; defaults to 'bottom'); align sets alignment along that side (defaults to 'start'); sideOffset is the gap in px between trigger and popup (defaults to 6). |
| MenuItem | Base UI Menu.Item props + className (disabled, closeOnClick, onClick) + variant?: "default" \| "destructive" | An interactive row. Highlights via data-[highlighted]; dims via data-[disabled]. variant="destructive" for a delete or irreversible action: it keeps the destructive ink when highlighted (never className="text-destructive", which the highlight repaints). |
| MenuSeparator | Base UI Separator props + className | Hairline rule between item runs. |
| MenuSubmenu | Base UI Menu.SubmenuRoot props | A nested menu. Wraps a MenuSubmenuTrigger and its own MenuContent — pass side="inline-end" to that content so the submenu opens away from its parent in RTL as well as LTR. |
| MenuSubmenuTrigger | Base UI Menu.SubmenuTrigger props + value: ReactNode + className | The row that opens a submenu: item styling, a trailing chevron, and an optional `value` showing the current choice so the row reads "Effort  High ›" rather than making the reader open it to find out. |
| MenuRadioGroup | Base UI Menu.RadioGroup props (value, defaultValue, onValueChange) | A single-choice group inside a menu. Controlled via value/onValueChange, uncontrolled via defaultValue. |
| MenuRadioItem | Base UI Menu.RadioItem props + className (value, disabled) | One option in a MenuRadioGroup, rendered as menuitemradio with a real checked state. The check sits in a reserved leading column so labels never shift sideways as the highlight moves. |
| MenuCheckboxItem | Base UI Menu.CheckboxItem props + className + { checked?: boolean; defaultChecked?: boolean; onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void; disabled?: boolean } | A toggling row, with the same reserved leading column as MenuRadioItem so a menu mixing the two keeps one text margin. |
| MenuGroup | Base UI Menu.Group props + className | Groups related items; pair with MenuGroupLabel for an accessible group name. |
| MenuGroupLabel | Base UI Menu.GroupLabel props + className | The label for a MenuGroup — auto-associated with the group for screen readers. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Menu (Root) | Base UI Menu.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, modal, orientation, loopFocus) | — | Groups all parts and controls open state. Uncontrolled by default. |

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides role=menu/menuitem, roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and typeahead.
- Esc and outside-press dismiss; focus returns to the trigger on close.
- Animate open/close via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes.
- MenuGroupLabel is auto-associated with its MenuGroup for screen readers.
- A disabled MenuItem stays in the arrow-key order — Base UI keeps it focusable with aria-disabled so screen-reader users learn the command exists — but it cannot be activated, and it ignores the pointer.

## Related

- Components: ContextMenu, DotsMenu

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuContent, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, MenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Menu><MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Options</Button>} /><MenuContent><MenuItem>Edit</MenuItem><MenuItem>Duplicate</MenuItem><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem variant="destructive">Delete</MenuItem></MenuContent></Menu>
```

### Grouped

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuContent, MenuGroup, MenuGroupLabel, MenuItem, MenuSeparator, MenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Menu><MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Account</Button>} /><MenuContent><MenuGroup><MenuGroupLabel>Signed in</MenuGroupLabel><MenuItem>Profile</MenuItem><MenuItem>Settings</MenuItem></MenuGroup><MenuSeparator /><MenuItem>Sign out</MenuItem></MenuContent></Menu>
```

### Nested, with a single-choice submenu

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuContent, MenuItem, MenuRadioGroup, MenuRadioItem, MenuSubmenu, MenuSubmenuTrigger, MenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Menu>
	<MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">View</Button>} />
	<MenuContent>
		<MenuItem>Reload</MenuItem>
		<MenuSubmenu>
			<MenuSubmenuTrigger value={density}>Density</MenuSubmenuTrigger>
			<MenuContent side="inline-end" align="start" sideOffset={4}>
				<MenuRadioGroup value={density} onValueChange={setDensity}>
					<MenuRadioItem value="Comfortable">Comfortable</MenuRadioItem>
					<MenuRadioItem value="Compact">Compact</MenuRadioItem>
				</MenuRadioGroup>
			</MenuContent>
		</MenuSubmenu>
	</MenuContent>
</Menu>
```

### Toggling rows

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuCheckboxItem, MenuContent, MenuTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Menu>
	<MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Columns</Button>} />
	<MenuContent>
		<MenuCheckboxItem checked={cols.status} onCheckedChange={(v) => setCol("status", v)}>Status</MenuCheckboxItem>
		<MenuCheckboxItem checked={cols.updated} onCheckedChange={(v) => setCol("updated", v)}>Updated</MenuCheckboxItem>
	</MenuContent>
</Menu>
```

# Message

**Status:** stable

One row in a conversation: avatar gutter, side, and stacked header / content / footer. Layout only — the surface is Bubble, passed as children.

**Keywords:** chat, message, conversation row, turn, thread, messaging, grouped messages, ai chat

## Usage

The row a single turn occupies. It owns the geometry — which side, the avatar gutter, where the name and timestamp go, where reactions and receipts go — and nothing about how the content looks. That separation is the point: an assistant's markdown answer, a one-line reply, an attachment, and a tool-call card are all the same row with different children.

### Best practices

- Do: Set `messageId`. It is what MessageScroller reads for `scrollToMessage`, `initialScroll`, and visibility tracking — a message without one cannot be jumped to or marked as read.
- Do: Pass the same `align` to Message and to the Bubble inside it, so the flattened tail corner lands on the speaker's side.
- Do: Use `grouped` for consecutive messages from one author. It tightens the spacing and hides the avatar while keeping its column reserved, so the run reads as one block instead of stepping left. Pass `tail={false}` to the Bubble in each continuation too, so only the first message in the run carries a tail.
- Do: Match `avatarSize` to the `size` of the Avatar you pass (sm/md/lg line up 1:1). The gutter is declared, not measured, because it has to hold its width when `grouped` hides the avatar.
- Don't: Do not justify the content to move a message to the right. `align="end"` already mirrors the whole row, gutter included; adding your own justification fights it.
- Don't: Do not put the timestamp inside the Bubble. It belongs in `header` or `footer`, which stay outside the surface so `variant="plain"` content still has one.
- Don't: Do not reach for Message to lay out a system note or a date break. That is `Marker`, which is deliberately quieter than the message tier.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Avatar gutter | no | Fixed-width column for the author's Avatar. Kept (but emptied) when `grouped`, which is what keeps a run aligned. |
| Header | no | Author name and timestamp, above the content. |
| Content | yes | The children — usually a Bubble, but equally an Attachment, a tool card, or plain rendered markdown. |
| Footer | no | Reactions, delivery receipts, retry actions. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| messageId | string | — | Stable id, published as `data-message-id`. The handle MessageScroller uses for scroll commands and visibility tracking. |
| align | "start" \| "end" | "start" | Which side of the conversation. "start" is the other party or the assistant; "end" is the person reading. Mirrors the whole row, gutter included. |
| avatar | ReactNode | — | Avatar node for the gutter. Omit for a message with no author identity. |
| avatarSize | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "sm" | Gutter width, matching Avatar's own size scale 1:1 (32 / 40 / 48px). Declared rather than measured so it survives `grouped`. |
| header | ReactNode | — | Author name, timestamp — anything above the content. |
| footer | ReactNode | — | Reactions, receipts, retry actions — anything below the content. |
| grouped | boolean | false | This message continues a run from the same author: tightens the spacing (via `--message-gap`) and drops the avatar while reserving its column. |
| ...div props | Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<"div">, "id"> | — | Spread onto the row. Use `messageId` rather than `id` — the scroller matches on `data-message-id`. |

## Variants

- **align**: start, end
- **avatarSize**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- A plain container with no imposed role — the conversation's semantics belong to the list or log element you wrap it in, not to each row.
- `align` reverses the visual row without reordering the DOM, so reading order in assistive tech stays chronological regardless of which side a message is on.
- The header and footer render at the secondary type step in muted ink, keeping both below the message tier in the visual hierarchy without dropping either below the AA contrast floor.

## Related

- Components: Bubble, MessageScroller, Marker, Attachment, Avatar

## Examples

### Incoming and outgoing

```tsx
import { Avatar, Bubble, Message, RelativeTime } from "@sableui/react"

<>
	<Message messageId="m1" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="CA" />} header={<><strong className="text-foreground">Carla</strong><RelativeTime date={sentAt} /></>}>
		<Bubble>Did the deploy finish?</Bubble>
	</Message>
	<Message messageId="m2" align="end">
		<Bubble variant="primary" align="end">Green across the board.</Bubble>
	</Message>
</>
```

### A grouped run

```tsx
import { Avatar, Bubble, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<>
	<Message messageId="m1" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="CA" />} header={<strong className="text-foreground">Carla</strong>}>
		<Bubble>One more thing.</Bubble>
	</Message>
	<Message messageId="m2" grouped>
		<Bubble tail={false}>The staging cert expires Friday.</Bubble>
	</Message>
</>
```

### With reactions in the footer

```tsx
import { Avatar, Bubble, BubbleReaction, BubbleReactions, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<Message messageId="m3" avatar={<Avatar size="sm" fallback="JR" />} footer={<BubbleReactions><BubbleReaction emoji="🎉" count={3} active /><BubbleReaction emoji="👀" /></BubbleReactions>}>
	<Bubble>Shipped 0.45.0.</Bubble>
</Message>
```

### An attachment as the content

```tsx
import { Attachment, Message } from "@sableui/react"

<Message messageId="m4" align="end">
	<Attachment name="proposal.pdf" meta="2.4 MB · PDF" />
</Message>
```

# MessageScroller

**Status:** stable

Scroll container for a conversation. Auto-follows new messages until the reader scrolls away, holds position when older history is prepended, and exposes scroll commands and visibility tracking through its ref.

**Keywords:** chat, conversation, messages, thread, transcript, stick to bottom, auto scroll, streaming, infinite scroll, inbox, ai chat, support chat

## Usage

The scroll region a conversation lives in. It owns the scrolling and nothing else — not your messages, not your AI state, not your transport or persistence — so you bring the content renderer and it handles the behaviors that make streaming chat feel right: pinning to the newest message, releasing when the reader scrolls up, keeping the view still when older history loads above, jumping to a specific message, restoring a saved read position, and reporting what is actually on screen.

### Best practices

- Do: Bound it the way you would bound any scroll box — `flex-1 min-h-0` inside a flex column, or `max-h-96`. `className` lands on the element that actually scrolls, so the obvious bound is the correct one (same contract as Scroller).
- Do: Give every Message a `messageId`. It is the handle for `scrollToMessage`, `initialScroll`, and `onVisibleMessagesChange` — a message without one is invisible to all three.
- Do: Prepend older history directly into `children` when the reader reaches the top. The scroller anchors on the first rendered message and re-adds the height that appeared above it, so the view does not jump.
- Do: Set the rhythm between messages with the `gap` prop, not with a flex class on `className` — the messages are laid out in a column inside the scroll region, not directly on it.
- Do: Restore a reopened thread with `initialScroll={{ messageId: lastRead }}` instead of dropping the reader at the bottom of a conversation they have not finished.
- Do: Wrap a docked agent panel in `<Density value="compact">`. The scroller tightens its rhythm and every message inside it drops to the workspace type tier — one attribute for the whole conversation, no per-component sizing.
- Don't: Do not call `scrollToBottom` on every incoming token. Auto-follow already does it, and doing it yourself fights the reader who scrolled up to read something.
- Don't: Do not expect `ref` to be the DOM node — it is a command handle (`scrollToBottom`, `scrollToMessage`, `isFollowing`). Reach for `ref.current.element` when you genuinely need the element.
- Don't: Do not wrap it in a positioned div to place a jump-to-latest button. It ships one, stuck to the bottom edge from inside the scroll region, which is why `className` gets to stay on the scrolling element.
- Don't: Do not use it for an ordinary long list. That is `Scroller` — this one's follow-the-bottom behavior is wrong for content the reader is browsing rather than receiving.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scroll region | yes | The element that scrolls. Carries `className`: sizing, padding, and background. |
| Message column | yes | The flex column holding the children, spaced by `gap`. Publishes `--message-gap` so `<Message grouped>` can close it. |
| Jump to latest | no | A control stuck to the bottom edge, shown only while the reader is scrolled away from the newest message. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ref | Ref<MessageScrollerHandle> | — | Imperative commands, not the DOM node: `scrollToBottom(opts)`, `scrollToTop(opts)`, `scrollToMessage(id, opts)` (returns false when the message is not rendered), `isFollowing()`, and `element` for the scrolling node itself. |
| autoFollow | boolean | true | Keep the newest message in view as content arrives, until the reader scrolls away from the bottom. Set false for a transcript that must never move under the reader. |
| followThreshold | number | 64 | Distance from the bottom, in px, that still counts as following. A band rather than a pixel, so a token arriving mid-frame does not flicker the state. |
| onFollowChange | (following: boolean) => void | — | Notified when the viewport pins to, or releases from, the newest message. |
| initialScroll | "bottom" \| "top" \| { messageId: string } | "bottom" | Where a freshly mounted thread lands. Pass a messageId to restore a saved read position. Applied once, on mount — changing it later will not yank a reader mid-conversation. |
| jumpToLatest | boolean | true | Show the jump-to-latest control while the reader is scrolled away from the newest message. |
| jumpToLatestLabel | string | "Jump to latest" | Accessible label and tooltip for that control. |
| gap | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Vertical rhythm between messages. Also published as `--message-gap`, which `<Message grouped>` reads to collapse the gap within a run. |
| onVisibleMessagesChange | (ids: string[]) => void | — | Ids of the messages currently intersecting the viewport, in DOM order. The hook for read receipts, mark-as-seen, and unread counters. |
| ...div props | Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<"div">, "ref"> | — | Spread onto the scrolling element. `className` bounds and pads the scroll region; `onScroll` composes with the component's own. |

## Variants

- **gap**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`border`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Native overflow, so keyboard scrolling (arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End) and the OS scrollbar work unchanged; the scrollbar is styled thin, not replaced.
- Overscroll is contained, so a wheel gesture that runs out of conversation does not start scrolling the page behind it.
- The jump-to-latest control is a real button with an accessible label, reachable by keyboard, and only present when there is somewhere to jump to.
- Smooth scrolling is used only when motion is enabled — `prefers-reduced-motion` and <MotionProvider> off both collapse every scroll command to an instant jump.

## Related

- Components: Message, Bubble, Marker, Attachment, Scroller

## Examples

### Streaming conversation

```tsx
import { Bubble, Marker, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<MessageScroller className="flex-1 min-h-0 px-4 py-6">{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id} align={m.mine ? "end" : "start"}><Bubble variant={m.mine ? "primary" : "muted"} align={m.mine ? "end" : "start"}>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}{pending ? <Marker icon="spinner" spin shimmer>Thinking…</Marker> : null}</MessageScroller>
```

### Scroll to a message on demand

```tsx
import { Bubble, Button, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

function Thread({ messages, replyTo }) {
	const thread = useRef(null)
	return (
		<>
			<Button onClick={() => thread.current?.scrollToMessage(replyTo)}>Show original</Button>
			<MessageScroller ref={thread} className="max-h-96">
				{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id}><Bubble>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}
			</MessageScroller>
		</>
	)
}
```

### Restore a saved read position and track receipts

```tsx
import { Bubble, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<MessageScroller className="h-96" initialScroll={{ messageId: lastRead }} onVisibleMessagesChange={(ids) => markSeen(ids)}>{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id}><Bubble>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}</MessageScroller>
```

### Prepend older history without moving the view

```tsx
import { Bubble, Button, Message, MessageScroller } from "@sableui/react"

<MessageScroller className="h-96" gap="sm">{hasMore ? <Button variant="secondary" loadingLabel="Loading…" onClick={loadOlder}>Load earlier messages</Button> : null}{messages.map((m) => (<Message key={m.id} messageId={m.id}><Bubble>{m.body}</Bubble></Message>))}</MessageScroller>
```

# Meter

**Status:** stable

A role=meter reading over Base UI Meter, drawn as a bar or a ring — how full something is within a known range (storage, quota, strength), with a tone for good/caution/bad. Not task progress.

**Keywords:** meter, usage bar, storage, quota, capacity, limit, password strength, level

## Usage

Use Meter to show a static measurement against a known maximum — storage used, seats taken, API quota, password strength. It is announced as a meter, not a progress bar, so a screen-reader user hears a level rather than a task underway.

### Best practices

- Do: Label it and show the reading in units people use ("7.2 of 10 GB"), with MeterLabel and MeterValue. The bar shows proportion; the number is what gets acted on.
- Do: Pick `tone` from thresholds you own and apply them consistently across the page — warning near the limit, destructive at or over it. The component does not guess where good becomes bad.
- Do: Use shape="ring" when the reading is a score that belongs in a small, glanceable spot on a card. It is the same measurement drawn as a circular gauge, not a different component.
- Don't: Do not use Meter for a task in flight — an upload, an install, a step count. That is Progress; Meter tells assistive tech nothing is happening.
- Don't: Do not use it for a value without a meaningful maximum (followers, total spend). A bar implies a full scale; an unbounded count is a stat.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MeterTrack | yes | The rail that represents the full range. |
| MeterIndicator | yes | The fill, sized from value and coloured by tone. |
| MeterLabel | no | The visible name; also names the meter for assistive tech. |
| MeterValue | no | The formatted reading. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MeterTrack | Base UI Track props + className + size | The rail. Rendered automatically when Meter has no children; renders a MeterIndicator by default. |
| MeterIndicator | Base UI Indicator props + className + tone | The fill. Inherits the Meter's tone unless given its own. |
| MeterLabel | Base UI Label props + className | Visible label; wires aria-labelledby on the root. |
| MeterValue | Base UI Value props + className | Formatted reading. Accepts a `(formatted, value) => ReactNode` child. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number | — | The current reading, between min and max. Required. |
| min | number | 0 | The bottom of the range. |
| max | number | 100 | The top of the range. |
| tone | "primary" \| "standard" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" | "primary" | Fill colour, mapped to a semantic token. Choose it from your own thresholds. |
| shape | "bar" \| "ring" | "bar" | bar is a horizontal track; ring is a circular gauge for a small, glanceable reading — the same value, min, max and tones. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Ring diameter (40 / 64 / 96px at the default spacing; the centre value steps with it), or bar thickness on the same sm / md / lg rails as Progress. |
| showValue | boolean | — | Print the value in the ring's centre (formatted like MeterValue). |
| strokeWidth | number | 6 | Ring stroke width, in viewBox units of 100. |
| format | Intl.NumberFormatOptions | — | Formatting for MeterValue and aria-valuetext (percent, unit, currency). |
| getAriaValueText | (formatted: string, value: number) => string | — | Human-readable reading for assistive tech ("7.2 of 10 gigabytes used"). |
| locale | Intl.LocalesArgument | — | Locale for formatting. Defaults to the runtime locale. |

## Variants

- **tone**: primary, standard, success, warning, destructive
- **shape**: bar, ring
- **size**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `primary`, `success`, `tone-warning`, `destructive`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Meter · _no motion_ — A meter is a reading, present with the page that reports it. Animating the fill up from zero on load would act out a change that did not happen.
- **response** · Meter · _no motion_ — It reports and accepts no input. A bar that reacted to the pointer would read as a Slider the user could drag.
- **transition** · MeterIndicator · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Width and colour ease on the motion tokens (no recipe animates width) when the reading changes — freeing space after a delete visibly shrinks the bar, so the user sees the cause and effect rather than a different bar.
- **activity** · Meter · _no motion_ — A meter has no indeterminate state; a reading is either known or not shown. Unknown-but-working is Progress with no value.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders role=meter with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext — distinct from Progress's role=progressbar.
- Name it with MeterLabel or aria-label; an unnamed meter is announced as a bare number.
- Tone is colour only. Say the state in text too ("Almost full") when it matters, and use getAriaValueText to give units.

## Related

- Components: Progress, Badge

## Examples

### Ring

```tsx
import { Meter } from "@sableui/react"

<Meter shape="ring" value={72} showValue aria-label="Storage used" />
```

### Bare

```tsx
import { Meter } from "@sableui/react"

<Meter value={64} aria-label="Storage used" />
```

### Storage with label and reading

```tsx
import { Meter, MeterLabel, MeterTrack, MeterValue } from "@sableui/react"

<Meter value={7.2} max={10} tone="warning" getAriaValueText={(_, v) => `${v} of 10 gigabytes used`}>
	<div className="mb-2 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-x-3 gap-y-1">
		<MeterLabel>Storage</MeterLabel>
		<MeterValue>{(_, value) => `${value} of 10 GB`}</MeterValue>
	</div>
	<MeterTrack />
</Meter>
```

### Tones

```tsx
import { Meter } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
	<Meter value={30} tone="success" aria-label="Seats used" />
	<Meter value={82} tone="warning" aria-label="API quota used" />
	<Meter value={100} tone="destructive" aria-label="Storage used" />
</div>
```

# MiddleTruncate

**Status:** stable

Middle-truncates a long string (hash, address, signature) to `5J7s…8xQp`, keeping the start and end legible while preserving the full value on hover.

**Keywords:** truncate, middle truncate, hash, identifier

## Usage

Use MiddleTruncate when both the beginning and end of a long identifier must remain visible.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for hashes, addresses, long filenames, URLs, or generated IDs.
- Do: Provide the full value through title text, copy action, or surrounding detail when needed.
- Don't: Do not use MiddleTruncate for human prose where the middle words carry meaning.
- Don't: Do not middle-truncate a value with no way to obtain it in full. Truncation removes characters from the page, so the value needs a copy affordance beside it: an icon Button with useCopy, as in the Copyable value example.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | string | — | The full string to render. When it is truncated, the full value is also set as the title attribute (a pointer tooltip). |
| startChars | number | 6 | How many leading characters to keep before the ellipsis. |
| endChars | number | 6 | How many trailing characters to keep after the ellipsis. |

## Accessibility

- When truncated, the visible abbreviation is aria-hidden and a visually hidden copy carries the full value, so screen readers announce the whole string. The title attribute holds it too, for a pointer tooltip only.
- Renders the string verbatim when it is too short to benefit from truncation, so no value is hidden needlessly.

## Related

- Components: Code, Button

## Examples

### Solana address

```tsx
import { MiddleTruncate } from "@sableui/react"

<MiddleTruncate text="5J7sX2QpHt9vK4mNbR8wYcZ3dF6gH1jL0pA8xQpVnTu" />
```

### Custom start/end counts

```tsx
import { MiddleTruncate } from "@sableui/react"

<MiddleTruncate text="0xAbC1234567890dEf1234567890aBcDeF12345678" startChars={4} endChars={4} />
```

### Copyable value

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, MiddleTruncate, Row, useCopy } from "@sableui/react"

const { copy, copied } = useCopy(address)
<Row gap={1}><MiddleTruncate text={address} /><Button variant="ghost" size="icon-xs" aria-label="Copy address" onClick={copy}><Icon name={copied ? "check" : "copy"} /></Button></Row>
```

# Note

**Status:** stable

Callout / admonition box. Its tone follows the shared status-tone vocabulary (neutral/info/success/warning/destructive), pairing a soft tone fill with a matching leading icon. Optional title.

**Keywords:** note, callout, admonition, warning, caveat, hint, context

## Usage

Use Note for helpful supporting information that should sit near the relevant content — including a caveat or warning attached to a form, a dialog, or a section. It is the in-context callout; Banner is the page-level strip.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for tips, caveats, or secondary context that improves understanding.
- Do: Reach for Note rather than Banner when the message qualifies something on the page — a warning inside a dialog, a caveat above a submit button. Banner is a full-width announcement strip for page- or app-level state; inside a form it reads as a slab, and its soft fill carries no border or tone-colored icon, so the severity stops being visible.
- Do: Keep tone calm and concise so the note does not compete with primary content.
- Do: When the reader can resolve the state, pass `action` rather than putting a Button in children. The prop is data — label plus handler — so the callout owns the placement and weight; a Button dropped into children inherits neither, floats in the box's padding, and (in `secondary`) punches a near-background hole in the tone fill.
- Don't: Do not use Note for state the whole page or app is in (an outage, an offline session, a blocked account) — that is Banner — or for a message tied to one field, which is the field's own error text.
- Don't: Do not give a Note two actions. One remedy reads as the sentence's next move; two make it a decision point, which is a Dialog's job.
- Don't: Do not stack several in a row. Three notes together are a wall of asides; if everything is called out, nothing is.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| action | { label: string; onClick?: () => void; href?: string } | — | A single remedy, rendered below the body and aligned to the text column. Deliberately data, not a slot: Note owns the placement, weight, ink and motion, so the action cannot be styled into a button that outweighs the sentence explaining it. Use onClick for an in-place action (renders a button, no glyph) or href for a link (renders an anchor with a trailing chevron) — the chevron means navigate, so it appears only when the action genuinely goes somewhere. |
| tone | "neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" | "info" | Severity tone — drives the border, fill, and leading icon color/name. The shared status-tone vocabulary (STATUS_TONES). |
| title | string | — | Optional bold lead-in rendered above the body (text-title-sm). |
| icon | string \| ReactNode \| null | — | Override the variant glyph: a string swaps the icon name (keeping the tone color), a ReactNode replaces it, null removes it; omit for the variant default. |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, info, success, warning, destructive

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `border`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `tone-info`, `tone-warning`, `success`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Rendered with role="note" so assistive tech can announce it as an aside.
- Color is never the sole signal — the leading icon and optional title reinforce severity.

## Related

- Components: Banner, InlineStatus, EmptyState

## Examples

### Info

```tsx
import { Note } from "@sableui/react"

<Note tone="info">Editions mint on Solana mainnet.</Note>
```

### With title

```tsx
import { Note } from "@sableui/react"

<Note tone="warning" title="Low balance">Top up SOL before minting.</Note>
```

### Warning with a remedy, inside a dialog

```tsx
import { Note } from "@sableui/react"

<Note tone="warning" action={{ label: "Unload chat model", onClick: unloadChatModel }}>gemma-4 is holding VRAM — generating now may be slow or fail.</Note>
```

### Custom icon

```tsx
import { Note } from "@sableui/react"

<Note tone="neutral" icon="lock">Pricing and supply cannot be changed after an edition is purchased.</Note>
```

# NotificationBadge

**Status:** stable

An unread indicator. Renders a bare dot or a count pill (capped as "{max}+"), or nothing when there's nothing to show. overlay pins it to the corner of a relative host; it is aria-hidden, so the host's name carries the count.

**Keywords:** notification, badge, count, unread

## Usage

Use NotificationBadge to show a compact unread count, alert count, or attention marker.

### Best practices

- Do: Place it on or near the item that owns the notifications.
- Do: Use compact counts and cap large numbers when exact precision is not useful.
- Don't: Do not use NotificationBadge as a standalone status label or category marker.
- Don't: Do not show a bare dot when the count is meaningful. A dot says "something"; if the user can act on "how many", show the number.
- Don't: Do not put a neutral badge on a secondary host. Both are the secondary surface, so the badge disappears; use primary or destructive there.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dot | boolean | false | Render a bare dot indicator with no number. Takes precedence over count. |
| count | number | — | Unread count. Renders nothing when <= 0 and dot is unset. |
| max | number | 99 | Cap before showing "{max}+". |
| tone | "destructive" \| "primary" \| "neutral" | "destructive" | Fill color. destructive for alarming counts; primary/neutral for non-alarming ones. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Scales the dot/pill on the spacing scale (count pill: sm 16px, md 18px, lg 20px at the default density). |
| overlay | boolean | false | Pin to the top-end corner of the nearest relative host (an icon button) — one placement for every caller instead of hand-tuned absolute offsets. |

## Variants

- **tone**: destructive, primary, neutral
- **size**: sm, md, lg
- **overlay**: true, false

## Tokens used

`destructive`, `destructive-foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`

## Accessibility

- The badge is aria-hidden: a count rendered on a control is not associated with it, so the host needs an accessible name that includes the count — "Notifications, 3 unread" — or a screen-reader user hears "Notifications, button" and never learns there is anything new. Pass aria-hidden={false} only for a standalone badge whose number is the information.
- A dot carries no number and no words: on its own it tells a sighted user only that something changed, and tells everyone else nothing. Pair it with a label that says what is new, and never make its colour the only difference between two states.

## Related

- Components: Badge, StatusDot

## Examples

### Dot + counts

```tsx
import { NotificationBadge, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={3}><NotificationBadge dot /><NotificationBadge count={3} /><NotificationBadge count={128} /></Row>
```

### Overlay on an icon button

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, NotificationBadge } from "@sableui/react"

<Button variant="secondary" size="icon" aria-label="Notifications, 5 unread" className="relative"><Icon name="bell" /><NotificationBadge count={5} overlay /></Button>
```

# NumberField

**Status:** stable

Numeric input with decrement/increment steppers over Base UI NumberField — keyboard arrows, scroll, scrub-to-change, min/max clamping, locale formatting, and form integration. Styled like Input; drops straight into a Field.

**Keywords:** number field, numeric input, stepper, form

## Usage

Use NumberField for numeric values that benefit from validation, min/max bounds, or step controls.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for quantities, thresholds, percentages, and other real numeric values.
- Do: Set sensible min, max, and step behavior when the domain has bounds.
- Don't: Do not use NumberField for identifiers such as phone numbers, ZIP codes, or credit card numbers.
- Don't: Do not use it in a property grid with steppers left on. Its two 32px stepper buttons (36px each with their inset) put a ~110px floor on a control that needs ~44px there — pass steppers={false}, or use ScrubField.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| min | number | — | Lower bound. Clamps typing, arrows, scroll and scrub alike, so the value cannot leave the range by any route. |
| max | number | — | Upper bound, clamped on every input route the same way as `min`. |
| value / defaultValue | number | — | Controlled / uncontrolled numeric value. |
| onValueChange | (value: number \| null, event) => void | — | Fired when the value changes (null when cleared). |
| step / smallStep / largeStep | number | — | Increment amount; smallStep applies with the meta key, largeStep with shift. |
| format | Intl.NumberFormatOptions | — | Locale formatting (currency, percent, units, …). |
| steppers | boolean | true | Show the decrement / increment buttons. Turn off in a dense property grid — the two 32px stepper buttons (36px with their inset) put a ~110px floor on the control; without them the value left-aligns. |
| disabled / readOnly / required / name / id | — | — | Standard form-control props. Base UI applies id + required to the input, so it labels and validates correctly. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Decrement / Increment are labelled buttons (Decrease / Increase); the input is a spinbutton with aria-valuenow/min/max from Base UI.
- Routes aria-describedby / aria-invalid onto the input, so a Field's helper + error are announced for it.

## Related

- Components: Input, Slider

## Examples

### Bounded

```tsx
import { NumberField } from "@sableui/react"

<NumberField defaultValue={1} min={0} max={99} />
```

### In a field

```tsx
import { Field, NumberField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Quantity"><NumberField min={1} defaultValue={1} /></Field>
```

### Currency

```tsx
import { NumberField } from "@sableui/react"

<NumberField defaultValue={9.99} format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }} />
```

---

# OtpField

**Status:** stable

One-time-code entry over Base UI's OTP Field — one slot per character, SMS autofill on the first slot, paste fills every slot, and only one tab stop for the whole code.

**Keywords:** otp, one-time code, one-time password, verification code, 2fa, two-factor, mfa, pin, passcode, input otp

## Usage

Use OtpField for a short, fixed-length code the user copies from somewhere else — an SMS or email verification code, an authenticator app, a device pairing PIN. The slots show how long the code is and where the user is in it, which a plain Input cannot.

### Best practices

- Do: Set `length` to the exact length the server sends, and verify in `onValueComplete` (or with `autoSubmit` inside a form). Most users paste or autofill the whole code at once, so the moment of completion is the natural submit.
- Do: Label it through a `Field` ("Verification code") and say where the code was sent in the description. The first slot takes the field's name; the rest are announced by position.
- Do: Use `groupSize` for codes of 6 or more so the user can check the code in chunks against the message they are reading from.
- Don't: Do not use OtpField for a password, an arbitrary-length PIN, or anything the user types from memory. Slots promise a fixed length; use Input with `type="password"` and `autocomplete="current-password"` instead.
- Don't: Do not intercept paste or clear the field on a wrong code before the user has seen the error. Blocking paste breaks SMS autofill and password managers, and wiping the slots erases the evidence of which digit was wrong.
- Don't: Do not swap it for NumberField because the code is digits. A code is an identifier, not a quantity: NumberField strips leading zeros and offers steppers that make no sense here.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root | yes | A role=group that holds the value, carries the field label and description, and reports completion. |
| Slot | yes | One input per character. The first carries autocomplete="one-time-code" and accepts the whole code. |
| Group gap | no | A decorative dash inserted every `groupSize` slots; hidden from assistive tech. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| length | number | 6 | Number of character slots. Completion fires when every slot is filled. |
| groupSize | number | — | Insert a visual gap every N slots (3 renders 123 – 456). The value stays one contiguous string. |
| value / defaultValue | string | — | Controlled / uncontrolled code. |
| onValueChange | (value: string, details) => void | — | Fires on every edit. `details.reason` is input-change, input-clear, input-paste or keyboard. |
| onValueComplete | (value: string, details) => void | — | Fires once every slot is filled — the place to verify the code. Also fires when a complete code is pasted over a complete value. |
| onValueInvalid | (attempted: string, details) => void | — | Fires when typed or pasted text contains characters `validationType` rejects, so you can explain the rejection rather than letting it vanish. |
| validationType | "numeric" \| "alpha" \| "alphanumeric" \| "none" | "numeric" | Which characters a slot accepts. Also picks the virtual keyboard (numeric → number pad). |
| autoSubmit | boolean | false | Submit the owning form when the code becomes complete. |
| mask | boolean | false | Render slots as password inputs. Only for codes that are secret on screen, such as a card PIN. |
| getSlotLabel | (index: number, length: number) => string | Character N of L | Accessible name for slots after the first. Override to localize. |
| aria-invalid | boolean | — | Marks every slot invalid (destructive border). `<Field error>` sets it for you. |
| disabled / readOnly / required / name / id / form | — | — | Standard form-control props. `id` lands on the first slot, so `<Field>` and `<label htmlFor>` name the field. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `border-strong`, `primary`, `ring`, `destructive`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — A code field is part of the form it sits in and appears with it. Animating it in would delay the one thing the user arrived to do — paste the code they just copied.
- **response** · Slot · `motion-interactive` — Focus moves between slots on every keystroke. The eased ring and border are what let the eye follow the cursor across six identical boxes instead of hunting for it after each digit.
- **transition** · Slot · `motion-interactive` — A filled slot strengthens its border, so a pasted code visibly lands in every slot at once. Easing it reads as the code arriving rather than the field flickering.
- **activity** · Root · _no motion_ — Verifying the code is the form's work, not the field's. Show it on the submit Button's `loading` state, where the user expects the answer to appear.

## Accessibility

- The root is a role=group named by the field label; the first slot shares the label through `id`/`htmlFor`, and later slots are announced by position ("Character 2 of 6").
- Only one slot is in the tab order. Arrow keys, Home/End and Backspace move between slots; Tab leaves the whole field.
- The first slot carries autocomplete="one-time-code" and the numeric virtual keyboard, so iOS and Android offer the SMS code above the keyboard.
- Slots render at 20px (`text-mono-lg`), above the 16px floor that stops iOS Safari zooming on focus.

## Related

- Components: Input, Form, NumberField

## Examples

### Six digits

```tsx
import { Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Verification code"><OtpField length={6} onValueComplete={verify} /></Field>
```

### In a field, grouped

```tsx
import { Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Verification code" description="Enter the 6-digit code we sent to your phone."><OtpField length={6} groupSize={3} /></Field>
```

### With an error

```tsx
import { Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Verification code" error="That code has expired. Request a new code and try again."><OtpField length={6} groupSize={3} defaultValue="482913" /></Field>
```

### Alphanumeric

```tsx
import { Field, OtpField } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Pairing code"><OtpField length={8} groupSize={4} validationType="alphanumeric" /></Field>
```

---

# PageHeader

**Status:** stable

In-flow page heading block: a title row (optional back control + actions) over an optional description, with room for children (filters, tabs) below.

**Keywords:** page header, title, lede, page actions

## Usage

Use PageHeader to establish a page's title, supporting description, and primary page actions.

### Best practices

- Do: Use one PageHeader per major page or route.
- Do: Keep the title literal and put explanation in the lede or nearby content.
- Don't: Do not use PageHeader inside repeated cards, dialogs, or compact panels.
- Don't: Do not put it outside the Region that holds the page content. It then sits at a different measure from what it introduces, and the page reads as two documents.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | ReactNode | — | The page title (renders an <h1>). |
| description | ReactNode | — | Supporting copy beneath the title. |
| back | ReactNode | — | Leading element before the title — typically a back control on drill-in routes. Keep it a ghost icon Button (size="icon", variant="ghost", aria-label="Back") so it stays quieter than the title. |
| actions | ReactNode | — | Trailing actions aligned to the title row's end. They drop under the title when the row runs out of room, and the title wraps rather than truncating. |
| titleAs | "h1" \| "h2" | "h1" | The title's heading element. Keep h1 — the route's one h1. Use h2 only when something above already owns the h1: a shell that renders the route title, or a page showing a PageHeader as an example. |

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders the title as an <h1>; use one PageHeader per page.
- Its title renders the route's `h1`. Do not render another `h1` elsewhere on the page: heading navigation would report two documents, and the outline a screen-reader user builds from it stops matching the page.

## Related

- Components: AppHeader, Breadcrumbs, Button

## Examples

### With actions

```tsx
import { Button, PageHeader } from "@sableui/react"

<PageHeader title="Storage credits" description="Fund permanent storage." actions={<Button>Top up</Button>} />
```

### One per page, inside the region

```tsx
import { Button, PageHeader, Region } from "@sableui/react"

// PageHeader introduces the current route: title, optional description, and the
// actions that act on THIS page.

<Region max="content">
  <PageHeader
    title="Invoices"
    description="Every charge on this account."
    actions={<Button>Export</Button>}
  />
  <p className="text-body-md text-muted-foreground">Page content.</p>
</Region>

// ✗ Outside the Region. The header then sits at a different measure from the
//   content it introduces, and the page reads as two documents.
// ✗ Two on one page. A second one is a section heading — an h2 in a
//   smaller step (text-heading-3 or below), not another PageHeader.
// ✗ Global actions in it (account, search). Those persist across routes and
//   belong in AppHeader.
```

# PageLoader

**Status:** stable

Full-screen branded loading splash: the screen fades in, the mark breathes, and an indeterminate Progress bar pulses beneath it. All motion is token-driven, so it freezes to a calm static screen when motion is off/reduced.

**Keywords:** page loader, loading, route, pending

## Usage

Use PageLoader for full-route or full-page pending states where the entire view is not ready yet.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it during route transitions, auth checks, or initial data loading.
- Do: Prefer a clear page-level message when the wait may take noticeable time.
- Don't: Do not use PageLoader for small inline waits; use Spinner, an indeterminate Progress, or Skeleton.
- Don't: Do not leave it mounted if the route's data can fail. It covers the whole viewport, so a PageLoader that never resolves is indistinguishable from a hung application — always give it a failure path.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | — | Brand mark / logo shown at center. Falls back to a neutral pulsing mark. |
| label | string | "Loading" | Caption beneath the mark; also the accessible label on the role=status region. |
| fullscreen | boolean | true | Cover the viewport (fixed) vs fill the nearest positioned parent (absolute). |
| hideBar | boolean | false | Hide the indeterminate Progress bar under the mark. |

## Tokens used

`background`, `foreground`, `secondary`, `primary`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- role=status with an aria-label (the label prop) announces the loading state politely.
- Decorative mark and bar are aria-hidden.
- Motion respects the policy: under off/reduced the pulses hold their first frame (static).

## Related

- Components: Spinner, Skeleton, Progress

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { PageLoader } from "@sableui/react"

<PageLoader label="Loading Studio" />
```

### With a logo

```tsx
import { PageLoader } from "@sableui/react"

<PageLoader label="Loading"><img src="/logo.svg" alt="" className="h-10 w-auto" /></PageLoader>
```

### Contained (fills parent)

```tsx
import { PageLoader } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="relative h-80"><PageLoader fullscreen={false} hideBar /></div>
```

# Pagination

**Status:** stable

Page navigation built from our own Button + Icon (no Base UI). A <nav aria-label='Pagination'> with prev/next icon buttons that disable at the bounds and numbered page buttons; the current page is a secondary button marked aria-current. Collapses to first/last/current plus a sibling window, bridging skipped runs with an ellipsis.

**Keywords:** pagination, pager, pages, table, results, navigation, next, previous

## Usage

Use Pagination when a result set is split into discrete pages and the user needs predictable movement through them. Pair it with DataTable, list results, or server-paged views; use a load-more Button or infinite scroll when page numbers are not meaningful.

### Best practices

- Do: Keep page state controlled by the parent route or data layer so URL, filters, and result fetches stay in sync.
- Do: Use a specific label when multiple pagers appear on a page, such as "Collector pages".
- Do: Reset to page 1 when filters or search terms materially change the result set.
- Don't: Use Pagination for tiny lists where all items fit comfortably on one page.
- Don't: Hide disabled previous/next buttons at the bounds; disabled controls make the current position clearer.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nav | yes | The labelled pagination landmark. |
| Previous/next | yes | Icon buttons for adjacent page movement, disabled at the bounds. |
| Page buttons | yes | Numbered buttons with aria-current on the active page. |
| Ellipsis | no | Non-interactive marker for skipped page ranges. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| page | number | — | The active page (1-based). Clamped into the valid range. |
| total | number | — | Total number of pages. |
| onPageChange | (page: number) => void | — | Called with the next page when a control is activated. No-op for out-of-range or unchanged values. |
| siblingCount | number | 1 | Page buttons shown on each side of the current page before the list collapses into ellipses. First and last pages are always shown. |
| label | string | Pagination | Accessible label applied to the surrounding nav element. |
| className | string | — | Extra classes merged onto the nav. |

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Renders a landmark <nav> with aria-label so assistive tech can jump to the pager.
- The current page button carries aria-current='page'.
- Prev/next buttons are real <button>s with aria-label and become disabled at the bounds.
- Ellipsis slots are aria-hidden — they convey no navigable target.

## Related

- Components: DataTable, Table, Button
- Patterns: ListDetailPage, DashboardPage

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@sableui/react"

const [page, setPage] = useState(1)
<Pagination page={page} total={10} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Many pages (ellipsis)

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@sableui/react"

const [page, setPage] = useState(8)
<Pagination page={page} total={20} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Table results footer

```tsx
import { DataTable, Pagination, Stack } from "@sableui/react"

<Stack gap={2}><DataTable data={rows} columns={columns} rowKey={(row) => row.id} /><Pagination label="Collector pages" page={page} total={12} onPageChange={setPage} /></Stack>
```

### Server query state

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@sableui/react"

const [page, setPage] = useState(searchParams.page ?? 1)
<Pagination page={page} total={pageCount} onPageChange={(next) => { setPage(next); loadPage(next) }} />
```

# PanelGroup

**Status:** stable

A row of docked chrome panels around a flexible centre, with draggable and keyboard-resizable edges and optional persisted widths.

**Keywords:** panel, panels, resize, resizable, splitter, docked, workspace, tool, chrome, inspector, layout

## Usage

Use PanelGroup for the body of a tool workspace: fixed-width Panels docked left and/or right, a flexible Panel in the middle for the canvas, and a PanelResizer between them. Panels scroll internally and the group never scrolls. This is the workspace-register counterpart to SplitPane, which only switches between side-by-side and stacked at a breakpoint and cannot be resized.

### Best practices

- Do: Give every docked Panel a fixed width and leave the centre Panel width-less so it absorbs the remaining space.
- Do: Drive the width with usePanelWidth and pass a storageKey, so a user's layout survives a reload. Spread its bounds onto the PanelResizer rather than repeating min and max by hand.
- Do: Label every Panel — they are landmarks, and 'Layers' or 'Properties' is what a screen-reader user navigates by.
- Don't: Let the group scroll. Only panels and the canvas scroll; a scrolling group means the shell lost its height constraint.
- Don't: Use it for page content columns — that's Grid or Columns. PanelGroup is chrome, and it sits outside the content grid.
- Don't: Omit PanelResizer to save effort and then let users live with a fixed panel. If a panel holds a tree or a property grid, its width is a preference.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PanelGroup | yes | The flex row. Sets min-h-0/min-w-0 so children can actually shrink and scroll. |
| Panel | yes | One column. Fixed-width when `width` is set, flexible otherwise. Scrolls internally. |
| PanelResizer | no | The draggable edge between two panels: a 1px hairline with a wider hit area, operable by pointer and keyboard. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Panel | { label: string; width?: number; scroll?: boolean } | A docked or flexible column. `label` names the landmark; omit `width` for the flexible centre. `scroll` defaults to true — set it false for a header + scrolling body + pinned footer, so the footer doesn't scroll away with the list. When you own the layout, give the header and footer shrink-0 and the middle min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto. overflow-y-auto only activates if every flex ancestor can shrink: a single missing min-h-0 anywhere up the chain makes the panel grow instead of scroll, and nothing reports it. |
| PanelResizer | { side: 'left' \| 'right'; width: number; onWidthChange: (n: number) => void; label: string; min?: number; max?: number; step?: number } | The draggable edge. `side` says which side the resized panel is on, so the drag delta's sign is right. |
| usePanelWidth | (defaultWidth: number, options?: { storageKey?: string; min?: number; max?: number }) => readonly [number, (n: number) => void, { min: number; max: number }] | Controlled width for a Panel, clamped and optionally persisted to localStorage (only when `storageKey` is passed). Read through useSyncExternalStore, so there is no server/client hydration mismatch and no setState in an effect; do not hand-roll a localStorage read during render or a write from an effect. Without `storageKey` the width is kept in memory per hook instance. The third element is the `{ min, max }` it clamps to: spread it onto the paired PanelResizer so the separator's aria-valuemin/max and Home/End match the real clamp. |

## Tokens used

`primary`, `panel`, `hairline`, `hairline-strong`

## Accessibility

- PanelResizer is a role=separator with aria-orientation, aria-valuenow/min/max, and is focusable — a pointer-only resizer is a keyboard trap.
- Arrow keys resize by `step`; Home and End jump to the minimum and maximum.
- Each Panel renders an <aside> with an accessible name from `label`, so panels are navigable landmarks.

## Related

- Components: PanelSection, ScrubField, SplitPane, Sidebar, AppShell

## Examples

### Tool body with a resizable left panel

```tsx
import { Panel, PanelGroup, PanelResizer, PanelSection, PropertyRow, Switch, usePanelWidth } from "@sableui/react"

function Body() {
  const [leftWidth, setLeftWidth, leftBounds] = usePanelWidth(240, { storageKey: "app:panel:left", min: 180, max: 360 })
  return (
    <PanelGroup>
      <Panel label="Layers" width={leftWidth}>
        <PanelSection title="Layers">
          <PropertyRow label="Background">
            <Switch checked />
          </PropertyRow>
        </PanelSection>
      </Panel>
      <PanelResizer side="left" width={leftWidth} onWidthChange={setLeftWidth} label="Resize layers panel" {...leftBounds} />
      <Panel label="Canvas">
        <div className="grid h-full place-items-center bg-canvas text-ui-body text-muted-foreground">Canvas</div>
      </Panel>
    </PanelGroup>
  )
}
```

### Both edges resizable

```tsx
import { Panel, PanelGroup, PanelResizer, PanelSection, PropertyPair, ScrubField, usePanelWidth } from "@sableui/react"

function Body() {
  const [left, setLeft, leftBounds] = usePanelWidth(240, { storageKey: "app:left" })
  const [right, setRight, rightBounds] = usePanelWidth(256, { storageKey: "app:right" })
  return (
    <PanelGroup>
      <Panel label="Layers" width={left} />
      <PanelResizer side="left" width={left} onWidthChange={setLeft} label="Resize layers panel" {...leftBounds} />
      <Panel label="Canvas" />
      <PanelResizer side="right" width={right} onWidthChange={setRight} label="Resize properties panel" {...rightBounds} />
      <Panel label="Properties" width={right}>
        <PanelSection title="Blending">
          <PropertyPair>
            <ScrubField label="Opacity" icon="grid" suffix="%" value={100} min={0} max={100} />
            <ScrubField label="Blur" value={0} min={0} max={64} suffix="px" />
          </PropertyPair>
        </PanelSection>
      </Panel>
    </PanelGroup>
  )
}
```

### Fixed panel, no resizer

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, Panel, PanelGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<PanelGroup>
  <Panel label="Tools" width={56}>
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-1 p-1">
      <Button size="icon-xs" variant="ghost" aria-label="Toggle grid"><Icon name="grid" /></Button>
      <Button size="icon-xs" variant="ghost" aria-label="Hide"><Icon name="eye" /></Button>
    </div>
  </Panel>
  <Panel label="Canvas" />
</PanelGroup>
```

# PanelSection

**Status:** stable

A flush group of property rows inside a docked panel — eyebrow header, hairline separator, rows beneath. The workspace register's answer to Card, which does not belong in a panel.

**Keywords:** panel, section, inspector, properties, property grid, workspace, tool, chrome, sidebar

## Usage

Use PanelSection to group properties inside an inspector or docked panel, with PropertyRow for one label-plus-control line and PropertyPair for two controls side by side. This is the workspace register's grouping primitive: it separates with a hairline and nothing else, because a Card inside a 240px panel spends its border and inset on nothing and pushes every row inward.

### Best practices

- Do: Group related properties under a short functional title — Blending, Layout, Fill — the way a tool inspector names its sections.
- Do: Reach for PropertyPair before giving each property its own full-width row; pairing halves the vertical cost in a narrow panel.
- Do: Put a section-scoped control (a visibility toggle, an add action) in the action slot rather than inventing a second header row.
- Don't: Wrap panel content in Card. Cards are page-register furniture; in a panel they read as a page pasted into chrome.
- Don't: Repeat the panel's own title as the section title. If the header above already names the selection, title the section by what it controls (Parameters, Blending).
- Don't: Hand-roll a property line (`<div className="flex justify-between"><span>Opacity</span><Slider /></div>`). Use PropertyRow for every label-plus-control line: when each property type invents its own arrangement, a panel of fifteen properties ends up with fifteen layouts.
- Don't: Use PropertyRow for page forms — use Field, which carries label/description/error semantics. PropertyRow is a dense chrome row, not a form control.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Header | yes | The section title in the UI section tier, with an optional trailing action. |
| PropertyRow | no | One property: label left, control right. `stacked` moves the control to its own line for full-width controls. |
| PropertyPair | no | Two controls side by side, with optional captions above each. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PropertyRow | { label: ReactNode; htmlFor?: string; hint?: string; stacked?: boolean; scrub?: { value, onValueChange, step?, min?, max?, onGestureStart?, onGestureEnd?, disabled? } } | One property line. `hint` becomes the label's hover explanation; `stacked` puts the control on its own line. `scrub` makes the property NAME a drag handle for its value — the Figma/Framer/Paper convention, and the answer for a numeric row with no honest glyph to put in a ScrubField (a schema-generated `levels` or `seed`, where a `#` would be noise pretending to be meaning). Opt-in and additive: a row without it is unchanged. The label stays a real `<label htmlFor>` — a 2px jitter threshold keeps a click a click, and the click synthesised after a real drag is swallowed so a scrub does not also select the field's text. |
| PropertyPair | { labels?: [ReactNode, ReactNode] } | Two controls side by side in a 2-up grid, with optional captions above each. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | ReactNode | — | Section name, rendered as the header in the UI section tier. |
| action | ReactNode | — | Optional trailing control in the header — a visibility toggle, an add action. |

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `hairline`

## Accessibility

- PropertyRow renders a real <label>; pass htmlFor with the control's id so clicking the label focuses it.
- The section title is an h3, so panels contribute a real heading outline rather than styled divs.
- `hint` is exposed as the label's title attribute — keep the essential meaning in the label itself, since title text is not reliably announced.
- A `scrub` label does not replace keyboard editing and must not be the only way to set the value: the drag is a pointer affordance, so the control it names still has to accept typing and arrow keys. It also keeps its `htmlFor` behaviour, which is the reason the gesture arms on a 2px threshold rather than on pointerdown.

## Related

- Components: Workspace, PanelGroup, ScrubField, StatusBar, Field, Card

## Examples

### Blending section, 2-up

```tsx
import { PanelSection, PropertyPair, ScrubField, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<PanelSection title="Blending">
  <PropertyPair>
    <ScrubField label="Opacity" value={100} min={0} max={100} suffix="%" />
    <Select value="normal">
      <SelectTrigger size="xs" />
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectItem value="normal">Normal</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="multiply">Multiply</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  </PropertyPair>
</PanelSection>
```

### Rows with a stacked slider

```tsx
import { PanelSection, PropertyRow, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, Slider, Switch } from "@sableui/react"

<PanelSection title="Parameters">
  <PropertyRow label="Block size" hint="Block edge length in reference pixels." stacked>
    <Slider value={32} min={4} max={256} />
  </PropertyRow>
  <PropertyRow label="Direction">
    <Select value="both">
      <SelectTrigger size="xs" />
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectItem value="both">Both</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="horizontal">Horizontal</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  </PropertyRow>
  <PropertyRow label="Reverse">
    <Switch checked={false} />
  </PropertyRow>
</PanelSection>
```

### Section with a header action

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, PanelSection, PropertyRow, ScrubField } from "@sableui/react"

<PanelSection
  title="Blending"
  action={
    <Button size="icon-xs" variant="ghost" aria-label="Hide layer">
      <Icon name="eye" />
    </Button>
  }
>
  <PropertyRow label="Opacity">
    <ScrubField label="Opacity" value={60} min={0} max={100} suffix="%" />
  </PropertyRow>
</PanelSection>
```
