# Phone

**Status:** stable

A current smartphone frame at iPhone proportions: a dark body with a titanium band, thin bezels, an island, an optional status bar and a scrollable screen.

**Keywords:** phone, device mockup, mobile preview, frame

## Usage

Use Phone to frame a mobile product preview when the device context is useful.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for mobile UI demos, screenshots, and responsive previews.
- Do: Keep the framed content legible and avoid stuffing full desktop layouts into the phone frame.
- Don't: Do not use Phone as a generic panel, card, or production app shell.
- Don't: Do not use it to test responsive behaviour. The frame is a fixed aspect box, not a viewport, so media queries inside key off the real window.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | — | Content rendered inside the scrollable screen region. |
| statusBar | boolean | true | Draw a status bar (time, signal, battery) across the top of the screen. Turn it off to frame a screenshot that already has one. |
| systemChrome | boolean | true | Draw the camera pill and home indicator. Turn it off when the content draws its own system chrome, such as an iOS prototype framed by PhoneFrame from @sableui/react/ios/preview. |
| className | string | — | Additional classes merged onto the outer wrapper (set the width here; the screen keeps its proportions). |

## Tokens used

`background`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- Purely presentational frame; the screen region scrolls when content overflows. Add headings/landmarks in the content as needed.
- The frame's chrome (status bar, camera, buttons) is aria-hidden, so the content inside carries the entire accessible meaning. A screenshot with no alt text makes the whole mockup announce as nothing at all.

## Related

- Components: Browser

## Examples

### Framing a mobile layout

```tsx
import { Phone } from "@sableui/react"

<Phone><div className="p-4"><h2 className="text-title-lg">Activity</h2><p className="text-body-sm text-muted-foreground">3 new collects today.</p></div></Phone>
```

### Mockup, not a responsive preview

```tsx
import { Phone } from "@sableui/react"

// Phone is DECORATIVE framing for a mobile screenshot on a marketing surface.

<Phone>
  <img src="/screenshots/mobile.png" alt="The mobile app" />
</Phone>

// ✗ Using it to test responsive layout. The frame is a fixed aspect box, not a
//   viewport — media queries inside it key off the real window, so what you see
//   is not what a phone renders. Resize the browser, or use device emulation.
// ✗ Wrapping live, interactive app UI (forms, buttons that act). Same as Browser: the frame says "picture of
//   software", so real controls inside it read as a screenshot that moves. Static composed content is fine.
//   The exception is a clickable iOS prototype: PhoneFrame (@sableui/react/ios/preview)
//   frames a whole phone-sized document in an iframe, where the frame is the device.
```

# Pill

**Status:** stable

A chip someone clicks: a filter, a tag choice, an option in a row. Always a button with aria-pressed. appearance="solid" (filters; selected lifts onto the primary surface) or "outline" (quiet chips that annotate content, like reactions); size md or sm. A static label is a Badge.

**Keywords:** pill, chip, filter, tag, toggle chip, category

## Usage

Use Pill for a row of filters or choices a person clicks to narrow or toggle what they see. For a label that only describes something, use Badge.

### Best practices

- Do: Use short text that names the filter or choice.
- Do: Reflect the current choice with selected, so the active filter reads at a glance.
- Don't: Do not use Pill as a static label. A pressable-looking chip that does nothing is the most common cause of dead clicks in a filter row — that is a Badge.
- Don't: Do not use Pill for primary actions or important system status.
- Don't: Do not restyle a Pill with border or background classes to get a quieter chip. That is appearance="outline" (and size="sm" for a small one); an override is a look that exists nowhere else in the system.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| selected | boolean | false | Marks the pill as chosen. Solid lifts onto the primary surface; outline takes a primary tint and soft primary edge. Sets aria-pressed. |
| appearance | "solid" \| "outline" | "solid" | solid for a filter row; outline for quiet chips that annotate other content (a reaction under a message, a tag on a card), where a filled chip would compete with what it annotates. |
| size | "md" \| "sm" | "md" | sm sits on the density ladder's xs control height, for chips under or inside other content. |
| icon | ReactNode | — | Optional leading glyph (e.g. <Icon name="lock" />), rendered before the children with the base gap. |

## Variants

- **appearance**: solid, outline
- **size**: md, sm
- **selected**: true, false

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `card`, `border`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <button type="button"> for focus and keyboard activation.
- Selected state is exposed via aria-pressed.

## Related

- Components: Badge, ToggleGroup

## Examples

### Filter row

```tsx
import { Pill, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Pill selected onClick={() => {}}>All</Pill><Pill onClick={() => {}}>Editions</Pill><Pill onClick={() => {}}>Collectibles</Pill></Row>
```

### Outline, small (reactions)

```tsx
import { Pill, Row } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={1}><Pill appearance="outline" size="sm" selected onClick={() => {}}>🎉 3</Pill><Pill appearance="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => {}}>👀</Pill></Row>
```

### With icon

```tsx
import { Icon, Pill } from "@sableui/react"

<Pill icon={<Icon name="lock" />} onClick={() => {}}>Locked</Pill>
```

# Popover

**Status:** stable

Click-triggered overlay over Base UI Popover (focus management, collision-aware positioning, Esc/outside dismissal). Holds interactive content; 18rem-wide surface.

**Keywords:** popover, floating panel, anchored, disclosure

## Usage

Use Popover for anchored secondary content that needs more room than a tooltip but less commitment than a dialog.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for small pickers, summaries, or contextual controls tied to a trigger.
- Do: Keep focus behavior and dismissal predictable.
- Don't: Do not use Popover for blocking confirmations, long forms, or critical information.
- Don't: Do not put a form that can fail validation inside one. A popover dismisses on outside click, which discards what the user typed with no warning — that is a Dialog.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PopoverTrigger | yes | The element that anchors and opens the popover. |
| PopoverContent | yes | The floating content surface. |
| PopoverTitle | no | An optional heading for the content. |
| PopoverDescription | no | Optional supporting copy. |
| PopoverClose | no | An explicit close control when helpful. |
| PopoverArrow | no | An optional arrow pointing to the trigger. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PopoverTrigger | Base UI Trigger props + render | The anchor element. Use render={<Button/>} to compose with another component. |
| PopoverContent | Base UI Popup props + side: "top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-*" + align: "start" \| "center" \| "end" + sideOffset: number + anchor: Element \| Ref \| (() => Element) \| VirtualElement + className | Portals + positions + paints the popup. side picks which side of the trigger to render against (auto-flips on collision; defaults to "bottom"); align sets alignment along that side (defaults to "center"); sideOffset is the gap in px (defaults to 8). anchor positions against a different element/ref/getter than the trigger — Base UI 1.5 has no separate Anchor part, so pass it here to decouple the open-location from the trigger. |
| PopoverTitle | Base UI Title props + className | Accessible heading; Base UI wires aria-labelledby to the popup. |
| PopoverDescription | Base UI Description props + className | Supplementary copy; Base UI wires aria-describedby to the popup. |
| PopoverClose | Base UI Close props + render | A button that closes the popover. Use render={<Button/>} to compose. |
| PopoverArrow | Base UI Arrow props + className | Optional pointer connecting the popup to its trigger. Place inside PopoverContent. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Popover (Root) | Base UI Popover.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, modal) | — | Groups the trigger and content. Uncontrolled by default. |

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border-floating`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI manages focus into and out of the popup, traps focus when modal, and restores focus to the trigger on close.
- Opens on trigger press (click/Enter/Space); dismisses on Esc and outside press.
- PopoverTitle/PopoverDescription wire aria-labelledby/aria-describedby on the popup.
- Enters and exits on the motion-pop recipe (Base UI starting/ending-style attributes), so it follows the motion policy.

## Related

- Components: Tooltip, ContextCard, Dialog

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Button, Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverDescription, PopoverTitle, PopoverTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Popover><PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Details</Button>} /><PopoverContent><PopoverTitle>Edition details</PopoverTitle><PopoverDescription>A limited run of 100, stored permanently on Arweave.</PopoverDescription></PopoverContent></Popover>
```

### With close

```tsx
import { Button, Popover, PopoverClose, PopoverContent, PopoverDescription, PopoverTitle, PopoverTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Popover><PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Open</Button>} /><PopoverContent><PopoverTitle>Heads up</PopoverTitle><PopoverDescription>Collecting mints a compressed NFT to your wallet.</PopoverDescription><PopoverClose render={<Button size="sm">Got it</Button>} /></PopoverContent></Popover>
```

# Progress

**Status:** stable

Linear progress bar over Base UI Progress — value 0–100 drives the fill; omit value (or pass null) for an indeterminate, pulsing bar.

**Keywords:** progress, task progress, meter, loading

## Usage

Use Progress to communicate determinate or indeterminate completion for a task or process.

### Best practices

- Do: Use determinate values when progress can be measured.
- Do: Pair the visual indicator with text when users need context or exact values.
- Don't: Do not use Progress as a decorative divider or status color bar.
- Don't: Do not use a determinate Progress for an unknown duration. A bar that sits at 90% is worse than a Spinner, because it makes a promise about time that you cannot keep.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ProgressTrack | yes | The background track that defines the range. |
| ProgressIndicator | yes | The filled or animated progress indicator. |
| ProgressLabel | no | A text label for the progress task. |
| ProgressValue | no | A readable value such as 45 percent. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ProgressTrack | Base UI Track props + className | The rail. Rendered automatically when Progress has no children; renders a ProgressIndicator child by default. Takes `size` (inherited from Progress) for its thickness — use that rather than a className height. |
| ProgressIndicator | Base UI Indicator props + className | The fill. Width is set by Base UI from the value; spans full width and pulses while indeterminate. |
| ProgressLabel | Base UI Label props + className | Accessible label; wires aria-labelledby on the Root. |
| ProgressValue | Base UI Value props + className | Formatted value readout. Accepts a render-function child for custom formatting. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number \| null | null | Current value between min and max. null (or omitted) renders the indeterminate state. |
| min | number | 0 | The minimum value of the range. |
| max | number | 100 | The maximum value of the range. |
| format | Intl.NumberFormatOptions | — | Formatting options for ProgressValue (e.g. style: 'percent', or a currency). |
| getAriaValueText | (formatted, value) => string | — | Returns a human-readable text alternative for aria-valuenow. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Bar thickness, on the same three rails as Meter so the two match on one page. ProgressTrack inherits it. |

## Variants

- **size**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `primary`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — A progress bar appears because work started. Staging its entrance delays the one piece of information the reader is waiting for.
- **response** · Root · _no motion_ — It reports; it does not accept input. A bar that reacted to the pointer would read as a Slider, which is a control the reader can drag.
- **transition** · ProgressIndicator · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — Fill width eases between values on the motion tokens (no recipe animates width), so the bar reads as filling rather than as a series of unrelated widths. It matters most where progress arrives in coarse jumps — four chunked upload callbacks look like a glitching bar without it.
- **activity** · ProgressIndicator · `motion-pulse` — Indeterminate (value null) has no width to animate, so the pulse carries the whole signal that work is still happening. Without it the indeterminate state is a static bar — indistinguishable from a stalled determinate one.

## Accessibility

- Base UI sets role=progressbar with aria-valuenow / aria-valuemin / aria-valuemax and reports status to screen readers.
- Indeterminate state (value null) omits aria-valuenow per the ARIA spec.
- Pair ProgressLabel with the bar for a visible, associated name; ProgressValue exposes the formatted value.

## Related

- Components: Spinner, Skeleton

## Examples

### Determinate

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@sableui/react"

<Progress value={64} aria-label="Upload" />
```

### Indeterminate

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@sableui/react"

<Progress aria-label="Preparing export" />
```

### With label and value

```tsx
import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressTrack, ProgressValue } from "@sableui/react"

<Progress value={40}><div className="mb-2 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-x-3 gap-y-1"><ProgressLabel>Uploading</ProgressLabel><ProgressValue /></div><ProgressTrack /></Progress>
```

# Radio

**Status:** stable

Single-select control over Base UI RadioGroup + Radio (roving focus, arrow-key nav, ARIA radiogroup wiring, form integration). RadioGroup + Radio.

**Keywords:** radio, radio group, single choice, form control

## Usage

Use Radio when a user must choose exactly one option from a visible set.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it when all options should be visible for comparison.
- Do: Keep option labels mutually exclusive and easy to understand.
- Don't: Do not use Radio for independent toggles or multiple selection; use Checkbox or Switch.
- Don't: Do not use a radio group with only one option, and do not omit the Fieldset. Without the fieldset the options share no accessible name, so a screen reader reads the choices with no question attached.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RadioGroup | yes | The grouped set that manages one selected value. |
| Radio | yes | One selectable option in the group. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RadioGroup | Base UI RadioGroup props (value, defaultValue, onValueChange, name, disabled, readOnly, required) + className | The group container that wraps Radio items and shares selection state across them. Controlled via value + onValueChange; uncontrolled via defaultValue. Lays its Radio items out in a vertical stack. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Radio | Base UI Radio.Root props (value, disabled, readOnly, required) + className | — | A single radio button. value pairs it with the group's selected value. Renders a native button with radio semantics, the ring and an inner Indicator dot. A custom non-button render must also set nativeButton={false}. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `primary`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides the radiogroup/radio roles, aria-checked, hidden native inputs, and roving tabindex.
- Arrow keys move and select between items; Space selects the focused item; Tab enters/leaves the group.
- Checked state styling reads from the data-[checked] attribute; disabled items from the disabled state.
- Focus-visible draws a 2px ring on the focused item. Wrap each Radio in <Field label orientation="horizontal"> so the label names it, is part of the hit target, sits on the first line, and dims with it when disabled — do not hand-build a <label> row.

## Related

- Components: Checkbox, RadioCard, Field, Fieldset, Select

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetLegend, Radio, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<Fieldset>
	<FieldsetLegend>Post type</FieldsetLegend>
	<FieldsetContent>
		<RadioGroup defaultValue="standard">
			<Field label="Standard" orientation="horizontal"><Radio value="standard" /></Field>
			<Field label="Edition" orientation="horizontal"><Radio value="edition" /></Field>
		</RadioGroup>
	</FieldsetContent>
</Fieldset>
```

### With a disabled option

```tsx
import { Field, Fieldset, FieldsetContent, FieldsetLegend, Radio, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<Fieldset>
	<FieldsetLegend>Post type</FieldsetLegend>
	<FieldsetContent>
		<RadioGroup defaultValue="standard">
			<Field label="Standard" orientation="horizontal"><Radio value="standard" /></Field>
			<Field label="Edition" orientation="horizontal" disabled><Radio value="edition" /></Field>
		</RadioGroup>
	</FieldsetContent>
</Fieldset>
```

# RadioCard

**Status:** stable

A selectable card option (radio-card) over Base UI RadioGroup + Radio. RadioGroup shares selection state; each RadioCard is a card with a radio indicator, title, and description. Add an icon to switch to the richer two-dimensional card, and a tone to give the selected state a semantic colour identity.

**Keywords:** radio-card, choice card, selection, option card

## Usage

Use RadioCard for visual choice cards when users compare a small set of named options.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it when labels, descriptions, or icons make options easier to understand.
- Do: Make the selected state explicit and preserve keyboard access through the group.
- Don't: Do not use RadioCard for dense menus, long lists, or simple yes/no settings.
- Don't: Do not use a single RadioCard on its own. It is a radio, so one option cannot be deselected — a lone one is a switch, and should be a Switch.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RadioCard | yes | One selectable option card. |
| RadioGroup | no | A grouped set of related choice cards. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RadioGroup | Base UI RadioGroup props (value, defaultValue, onValueChange, name, disabled, readOnly, required) + className | The group container that wraps the RadioCard cards and shares their selection state. Controlled via value + onValueChange; uncontrolled via defaultValue. Lays its cards out in a single column by default; override with className (e.g. 'grid sm:grid-cols-3') for a grid — the group is a flex column, so a grid-cols-* class alone does nothing. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | string | — | The unique value that pairs this card with the group's selected value. |
| title | ReactNode | — | The card's primary label (rendered as text-title-sm). |
| description | ReactNode | — | Optional supporting copy beneath the title (text-body-sm, muted). |
| icon | ReactNode | — | Leading icon (e.g. a solid <Icon>). Its presence switches to the two-dimensional card — icon top-left, indicator top-right, copy below — and the glyph is rendered as a solid-fill icon in the tone colour. |
| tone | "neutral" \| "standard" \| "collectible" \| "edition" \| "info" \| "warning" | "neutral" | Semantic colour the selected state carries across the border, radio, and icon glyph. Neutral uses the primary ring with a muted wash. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Dims the card and blocks selection. The group skips it during keyboard navigation. |
| titleClassName | string | — | Merged onto the title span (default text-title-sm) — e.g. to tighten copy in a two-column layout. |
| descriptionClassName | string | — | Merged onto the description span (default text-body-sm text-muted-foreground). |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, standard, collectible, edition, info, warning

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `primary`, `muted`, `ring`, `muted-foreground`, `tone-standard`, `tone-collectible`, `tone-edition`, `tone-info`, `tone-warning`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides the radiogroup/radio roles, aria-checked, hidden native inputs, and roving tabindex.
- Arrow keys move and select between cards; Space selects the focused card; Tab enters/leaves the group.
- Checked state styling reads from the data-[checked] attribute; disabled cards from data-disabled.
- focus-within draws a 2px ring on the focused card; the whole card is the hit target.
- The icon is decorative — the title labels the card — so selection meaning never relies on colour alone (the border ring and the filled radio both shift; the neutral tone adds a muted fill).

## Related

- Components: Radio, CheckboxCard, Select

## Examples

### Post type (tone + icon)

```tsx
import { Icon, RadioCard, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<RadioGroup defaultValue="post" className="grid sm:grid-cols-3"><RadioCard value="post" tone="standard" icon={<Icon name="plus" />} title="Standard" description="Share without minting" /><RadioCard value="collectible" tone="collectible" icon={<Icon name="gem" />} title="Collectible" description="Free to collect as NFT" /><RadioCard value="edition" tone="edition" icon={<Icon name="image-stack" />} title="Edition" description="Sell as NFT editions" /></RadioGroup>
```

### Plan picker (plain)

```tsx
import { RadioCard, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<RadioGroup defaultValue="pro"><RadioCard value="free" title="Free" description="For trying things out." /><RadioCard value="pro" title="Pro" description="For growing teams." /><RadioCard value="enterprise" title="Enterprise" description="Custom limits and support." /></RadioGroup>
```

### With a disabled option

```tsx
import { RadioCard, RadioGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<RadioGroup defaultValue="free"><RadioCard value="free" title="Free" description="For trying things out." /><RadioCard value="enterprise" title="Enterprise" description="Contact sales to enable." disabled /></RadioGroup>
```

# RelativeTime

**Status:** stable

A human relative timestamp (e.g. "3 minutes ago") that reveals the full absolute date/time on hover or focus. Renders a native <time> element wrapped in our Tooltip; the absolute time is formatted with date-fns format(date, 'PPpp') (e.g. "Apr 29, 2025, 4:05:12 PM").

**Keywords:** relative time, timestamp, time ago, date

## Usage

Use RelativeTime to show recent activity or timestamps in conversational relative language.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for feeds, audit summaries, comments, and activity streams.
- Do: Expose the exact timestamp when precision matters.
- Don't: Do not use RelativeTime as the only date format for legal, billing, or audit-critical records.
- Don't: Do not render it during SSR without a stable absolute fallback. "2 minutes ago" computed on the server differs from the client's value, which is a hydration mismatch — and it silently drifts as the page sits open.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| date | Date \| string \| number | — | The instant to render. Accepts a Date, an ISO/parseable string, or an epoch number (ms). Coerced to a Date for date-fns. |
| className | string | — | Merged onto the <time> trigger element (the visible relative label). |
| ...time props | Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<"time">, "dateTime" \| "children"> | — | Remaining native <time> attributes pass through to the trigger. dateTime is set automatically from the parsed ISO value. |

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Renders a semantic <time> element with a machine-readable dateTime (ISO) attribute.
- The <time> carries tabIndex=0 (it is not focusable natively), so the absolute time — exposed via Base UI's Tooltip, which opens on keyboard focus as well as hover and wires aria-describedby — is reachable from the keyboard.
- It inherits the type size of the surrounding text rather than setting its own, so it sits inside a meta row or message header without changing tier.
- Wrap the page or a group in <TooltipProvider> to share open/close delays.
- Relative phrasing is supplementary; the dateTime attribute remains the canonical machine value.

## Related

- Components: InlineStatus, Table

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { RelativeTime, TooltipProvider } from "@sableui/react"

<TooltipProvider><RelativeTime date={new Date()} /></TooltipProvider>
```

### From an ISO string

```tsx
import { RelativeTime, TooltipProvider } from "@sableui/react"

<TooltipProvider><RelativeTime date="2025-04-29T16:05:12Z" /></TooltipProvider>
```

---

# Scroller

**Status:** stable

Scroll container that fades its leading/trailing edges when content overflows. Tracks scroll position to toggle the fades.

**Keywords:** scroller, overflow, horizontal scroll, carousel

## Usage

Use Scroller to create a contained overflow region for content that naturally extends beyond the viewport.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for chip rows, media strips, or comparison sets where horizontal browsing is expected.
- Do: Keep scroll affordances visible enough that overflow is discoverable.
- Do: Put everything on `className` — sizing (`max-h-80`, `h-64`, `flex-1 min-h-0`) and chrome (`rounded-lg border`, `bg-card`) alike. It styles the Scroller's outer box, and the scrolling element inside it is `flex-1 min-h-0`, so a cap on the Scroller is still a cap on what scrolls.
- Do: Pass `label` on any Scroller with real content. It is a focusable region, and an unnamed one announces as a bare group — "Tags" or "Recent covers" costs a word and is the difference between navigable and not.
- Don't: Do not use Scroller to hide primary page layout or required controls.
- Don't: Do not add your own wheel handler to make a horizontal strip mouse-scrollable — it already is. A second handler double-scrolls and usually loses the end-release, which traps the page.
- Don't: Do not reach past it with a child selector (`[&>div]:snap-x`). The scrolling element is addressable by name: `viewportClassName`.
- Don't: Do not use it to hide overflow you should have laid out. It exists to make an intentionally scrolling strip legible, not to contain content that overflowed by accident.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| orientation | "vertical" \| "horizontal" | "vertical" | "vertical" scrolls and fades top/bottom; "horizontal" scrolls and fades left/right. |
| wheelScroll | boolean | true | On a horizontal Scroller, let a vertical mouse wheel scroll it sideways. Ignored when vertical. Turn it off only if the region is inside something that owns the wheel itself (a map, a canvas). |
| label | string | — | Accessible name for the scroll region. The region takes focus, so it should say what it contains; without one a screen reader announces an unnamed group. |
| viewportClassName | string | — | Classes for the inner element that actually scrolls. Narrow on purpose — `className` is what you want almost always. This is for the few utilities that only mean something on the scrolling box: `snap-x`, `scroll-smooth`, `scroll-p-*`. |
| ...div props | ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'> | — | Everything except `className`/`style` spreads onto the SCROLLING element — `role`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*` and event handlers all describe the thing that scrolls, and CommandMenu relies on it to make this component its listbox. `ref` and `onScroll` likewise address the scroller, and compose with the component's own. |

## Variants

- **orientation**: vertical, horizontal
- **wheelScroll**: true, false

## Tokens used

`ring`

## Accessibility

- The edge fades are a CSS mask-image on the scrolling element, not overlay elements — there is nothing in the DOM to intercept a pointer or be read by assistive tech, and the content under a fade stays fully interactive.
- Two boxes: a chrome box carrying `className` (border, background, radius, sizing) and, inside it, the element that actually scrolls and carries the fade mask. They are split because a `mask-image` applies to its element's own border — so with both on one box, a bordered Scroller watched its frame dissolve at the scrolling edge. The axis is published as `data-orientation`, not `aria-orientation`, which is invalid on `role="group"`.
- The scroll region uses native overflow and contains overscroll, so a gesture that runs out of content does not scroll the page behind it.
- It is focusable (`tabIndex=0`, `role="group"`) and handles arrows, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown along its own axis. Chrome 128+ and Firefox make scrollable regions focusable on their own; Safari does not, so a strip with a hidden scrollbar and no focusable children is unreachable there. Declaring it makes the behaviour a property of the component, not of the reader's browser. Pass `label` to name it — an unnamed focusable region announces as a bare group.
- On a horizontal Scroller, a vertical mouse wheel scrolls it sideways, because most mice have no horizontal wheel and the content past the fold is otherwise unreachable on them. The strip releases the wheel at both ends so it never traps the page, and leaves trackpad `deltaX` gestures and `shift+wheel` to the browser.
- Cross-axis arrow keys are deliberately not captured, and a consumer can take the arrows entirely by calling `preventDefault()` in their own `onKeyDown` — a strip of interactive chips usually wants them for roving focus.

## Related

- Components: Carousel, Marquee

## Examples

### Vertical with overflow

```tsx
import { Scroller } from "@sableui/react"

<Scroller label="Editions" className="h-64"><ul className="space-y-2 p-4">{items.map((item) => (<li key={item.id} className="text-body-sm">{item.title}</li>))}</ul></Scroller>
```

### Capped, scrolls past the cap

```tsx
import { Scroller } from "@sableui/react"

<Scroller label="Versions" className="max-h-80 rounded-md border border-border"><ul className="divide-y divide-border">{versions.map((v) => (<li key={v.id} className="px-3 py-2 text-body-sm">{v.label}</li>))}</ul></Scroller>
```

### Horizontal

```tsx
import { Scroller } from "@sableui/react"

<Scroller orientation="horizontal" label="Recent covers" className="w-full"><div className="flex gap-3 p-4">{covers.map((src) => (<img key={src} src={src} alt="" className="h-32 w-32 rounded-lg object-cover" />))}</div></Scroller>
```

### Snap points on the scrolling box

```tsx
import { Scroller } from "@sableui/react"

<Scroller orientation="horizontal" label="Covers" className="w-full rounded-lg border border-border" viewportClassName="snap-x snap-mandatory scroll-smooth"><div className="flex gap-3 p-4">{covers.map((src) => (<img key={src} src={src} alt="" className="h-32 w-32 snap-start rounded-lg object-cover" />))}</div></Scroller>
```

# ScrubField

**Status:** stable

The compact numeric field a property grid is built from: a leading glyph inside the field that doubles as a drag-to-scrub handle, the value, and an optional unit.

**Keywords:** scrub, numeric, number, field, property, inspector, drag, workspace, tool, unit

## Usage

Use ScrubField for numeric properties in tool chrome — an inspector, a property grid, a panel. The leading icon or letter says what the number is and is also the thing you drag, which is why a value like opacity needs no slider. Reach for NumberField instead in page-register forms: it has steppers and locale formatting, and it renders at page-register height. Those two steppers put a ~112px floor on a control that needs to be about 44px in a property grid, which is why ScrubField exists rather than a NumberField size variant. The input is sized in ch, so each field is as wide as its longest value and a grid of them lines up without per-field tuning.

### Best practices

- Do: Give the field an icon or prefix when it stands alone, so the row has a drag affordance and the value has an identity.
- Do: Pass the unit as `suffix` rather than baking it into the label — it renders against the number the way reference tools show 100%.
- Do: Bracket undo with onGestureStart/onGestureEnd. A scrub fires per frame, so without it one undo rewinds a single pixel of the drag.
- Do: Set `step` to the real precision (0.01 for a normalised threshold). Display precision follows it, so a seed shows 1234 and never 1,234.
- Don't: Add a separate drag gripper beside the glyph. The icon or prefix already is the scrub handle; a second one is the same affordance twice and costs width a 240px panel does not have.
- Don't: Pair it with a Slider AND give it a glyph. The slider is already the drag affordance; two on one row is the same gesture twice. Omit icon/prefix when there's a slider.
- Don't: Use it in a page form. It is chrome-sized and has no label, description, or error slots — that's Field plus Input or NumberField.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number | — | The current value (controlled). |
| onValueChange | (next: number) => void | — | Fires on commit, arrow-key step, and every frame of a scrub. |
| min | number | — | Lower clamp, applied to typing and scrubbing. |
| max | number | — | Upper clamp, applied to typing and scrubbing. |
| step | number | 1 | Arrow-key and scrub increment, and the source of display precision. Shift multiplies arrows by 10 and divides scrubbing by 10. |
| label | string | — | Accessible name for the input. Required — the visible glyph is decorative. |
| icon | string | — | Semantic icon name rendered inside the field; doubles as the scrub handle. Any name the app's IconProvider resolves works — image tools typically supply their own checkerboard glyph for opacity, which is a domain icon rather than one Sable's contract carries. |
| prefix | ReactNode | — | Short text used instead of an icon (e.g. "X" / "Y"), with the same scrub role. |
| suffix | ReactNode | — | Unit rendered after the value inside the field (e.g. "%", "px"). |
| onGestureStart | () => void | — | Fires once when a scrub drag begins — open an undo transaction here, and drop expensive downstream work (e.g. a GPU renderer) to a cheap preview quality; without it a pipeline re-renders at full quality on every pointer move and the drag stutters. |
| onGestureEnd | () => void | — | Fires when a scrub drag ends — close the undo transaction here and restore full render quality. |
| disabled | boolean | — | Disables typing and scrubbing. |
| id | string | — | Input id, for a PropertyRow's htmlFor. |

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`, `canvas`, `panel-raised`

## Accessibility

- The input carries the accessible name via `label`; the glyph is aria-hidden because it is decorative.
- Every scrub gesture is reachable from the keyboard: ArrowUp/ArrowDown step by `step`, Shift+Arrow by ten steps.
- Enter commits, Escape reverts to the last committed value, and blur commits — so a partial edit is never silently kept.

## Related

- Components: NumberField, Slider, PanelSection, Workspace, Input

## Examples

### Opacity with a glyph handle

```tsx
import { ScrubField } from "@sableui/react"

<ScrubField label="Opacity" icon="grid" suffix="%" value={60} min={0} max={100} onValueChange={(v) => setOpacity(v)} />
```

### X/Y offset pair (PropertyPair puts two fields on one scan line)

```tsx
import { PropertyPair, ScrubField } from "@sableui/react"

<PropertyPair labels={["Offset X", "Offset Y"]}>
  <ScrubField label="Offset X" prefix="X" value={x} min={-128} max={128} onValueChange={setX} />
  <ScrubField label="Offset Y" prefix="Y" value={y} min={-128} max={128} onValueChange={setY} />
</PropertyPair>
```

### No glyph — the property name is the handle

```tsx
import { PropertyRow, ScrubField } from "@sableui/react"

<PropertyRow label="Block size" scrub={{ value: size, onValueChange: setSize, min: 2, max: 256 }}>
  <ScrubField label="Block size" value={size} min={2} max={256} suffix="px" onValueChange={setSize} />
</PropertyRow>
```

### Paired with a slider (no glyph — one drag affordance per row)

```tsx
import { PropertyRow, ScrubField, Slider } from "@sableui/react"

<PropertyRow label="Block size" stacked>
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Slider value={32} min={4} max={256} className="min-w-0 flex-1" />
    <ScrubField label="Block size" value={32} min={4} max={256} step={1} suffix="px" className="w-16 shrink-0" onValueChange={(v) => setBlockSize(v)} />
  </div>
</PropertyRow>
```

# SearchInput

**Status:** stable

Styled search field with a leading magnifier and a clearable X. Soft-square (rounded-sm), card surface, 2px focus ring; the clear button appears only when there is a value.

**Keywords:** search, input, filter, query

## Usage

Use SearchInput for text queries that filter or search a known content set.

### Best practices

- Do: Use a clear placeholder that names the content being searched.
- Do: Provide a visible clear affordance when query state persists.
- Do: When a button stands in for search (a header trigger that opens CommandMenu with ⌘K), use CommandMenuTrigger. It wears this field's shell from the same source, so the two cannot drift; a hand-styled button already did once, into a borderless chip that matched neither the field nor a button.
- Don't: Do not use SearchInput as a command palette; use CommandMenu for global commands, opened from the header by CommandMenuTrigger. A SearchInput that opens a dialog on focus is a text box you cannot type in.
- Don't: Do not search on every keystroke against an expensive backend without debouncing. The user sees results flicker and reorder under them, and you send a request per character.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | string | — | Controlled value of the search field. |
| defaultValue | string | — | Uncontrolled initial value. The field tracks its own text, so the clear button still appears and empties it. |
| className | string | — | Sizes and places the whole field — magnifier, input and clear button together (e.g. max-w-80). A width cap here keeps the clear button inside the field. |
| inputClassName | string | — | Classes for the <input> element alone, for the rare input-only override. |
| onValueChange | (value: string) => void | — | Called with the next string on every keystroke. |
| onClear | () => void | — | Called when the clear button is pressed. The component also fires onValueChange('') so a controlled value resets. |
| placeholder | string | "Search" | Placeholder text shown when the field is empty. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Dims the control and blocks pointer interaction. |
| ...props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"input"> | — | All native input attributes (name, autoFocus, ref, aria-invalid, …) pass through to the <input> except value/onChange, which are owned by value/onValueChange, and className, which sizes the whole field. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <input type="search"> — keyboard and form semantics come for free.
- Associate a <label htmlFor> (or wrap) — the magnifier glyph is decorative, not a label.
- The leading search Icon is pointer-events-none and purely decorative.
- The clear button is a real <button> (Sable's ghost icon Button) with aria-label='Clear search' and a focus-visible ring. It is hidden while the field is disabled.
- Focus-visible draws a 2px ring in the --ring token; aria-invalid raises the destructive border and ring.

## Related

- Components: Input, CommandMenu, Combobox

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
import { SearchInput } from "@sableui/react"

const [q, setQ] = useState("")
<SearchInput value={q} onValueChange={setQ} placeholder="Search posts" />
```

### With onClear

```tsx
import { SearchInput } from "@sableui/react"

<SearchInput value={q} onValueChange={setQ} onClear={() => console.log("cleared")} />
```

### Uncontrolled, sized as a whole

```tsx
import { Field, SearchInput } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Search posts"><SearchInput defaultValue="editions" className="max-w-80" /></Field>
```

### Disabled

```tsx
import { SearchInput } from "@sableui/react"

<SearchInput disabled placeholder="Search" />
```

# Select

**Status:** stable

Listbox over Base UI Select — typeahead, roving focus, collision-aware popup, ARIA option wiring, and form integration. Trigger shows the selected value; the popup portals to <body>.

**Keywords:** select, listbox, dropdown, picker, option, choice, typeahead, form

## Usage

Use Select when users choose one value from a known, finite set. Use Combobox for searchable or user-entered values, Combobox `multiple` for several choices, and Radio when all options should remain visible.

### Best practices

- Do: Use clear item labels and pass label explicitly when children are richer than plain text.
- Do: Group long option sets with SelectGroup and SelectGroupLabel when categories improve scanning.
- Do: Wrap in Field when the select belongs to a form so label, helper text, and errors are wired automatically.
- Do: Leave the trigger's type alone on mobile. Below the sm breakpoint the md trigger renders text-body-lg (17px) so it matches the Input and Textarea beside it, which carry that tier because iOS Safari zooms the page when a focused field computes under 16px. A custom field in the same row should follow: a second paired tier under a max-sm: variant, never a hand-set font-size.
- Do: Inside a <Workspace> a Select adapts automatically — trigger and popup both pick up the compact density, including across the portal. Do NOT hand-size it per call site; that was necessary before v0.41 and is now drift.
- Don't: Use Select for very large or fuzzy lists. Use Combobox when typing is the primary way to find an option.
- Don't: Use Select for binary on/off settings. Use Switch or Checkbox instead.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root | yes | Owns value, open state, form integration, and item collection. |
| Trigger | yes | The button that shows the selected value and opens the listbox. |
| Content | yes | The positioned popup containing options and optional groups. |
| Item | yes | A selectable option with selected and highlighted states. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SelectTrigger | Base UI Trigger props + placeholder?: ReactNode + size?: "md" \| "xs" + className | The button. Composes Trigger + Value + a chevron Icon that flips on open (data-[popup-open]). `size="xs"` is the property-grid rung — height, padding, radius AND surface move together, which is why it is a prop and not a className: the xs trigger is an inset `bg-canvas` field with no border, matching ScrubField on the same row. A consumer overriding only the height gets an md-register 8px radius on a 24px box and a raised card sitting among inset fields; one inspector panel had eleven of those, and both tells are visible at a glance. |
| SelectContent | Base UI Popup props + side, align, sideOffset + className | Portal + Positioner + Popup + List. side="bottom", align="start", sideOffset=6 by default; matches trigger width. |
| SelectItem | { value: string; disabled?: boolean; label?: string } + className | An option. Composes Item + ItemText + a check ItemIndicator for the selected row. String children double as the item's `label`, so the closed trigger shows the display text — pass `label` explicitly only when children are richer than a string. |
| SelectGroup | Base UI Group props + className | Optional grouping of related options. |
| SelectGroupLabel | Base UI GroupLabel props + className | The heading associated with a SelectGroup for screen readers. |
| SelectValue | Base UI Value props (children render fn) + placeholder | Renders the selected option's label with a placeholder fallback. Already composed inside SelectTrigger; exported for advanced layouts that render the value outside the default trigger. |
| SelectSeparator | Base UI Separator props + className | A thin themed divider between groups of items. Decorative — Base UI marks it aria-hidden. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | Record<string, ReactNode> \| { value: string; label: ReactNode }[] | — | value → label map (a record, or an array of { value, label }). Derived automatically from literal SelectItem children; pass it explicitly when the items are generated in a loop, or a closed trigger renders the raw value instead of the label. |
| Select (Root) | Base UI Select.Root props (value, defaultValue, onValueChange, open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, disabled, required, name, multiple, items) | — | Controls the selected value and open state. Uncontrolled by default. When `items` isn't passed, it is derived from the SelectItem children so the closed trigger shows display text instead of the raw value; pass `items` explicitly when item children aren't plain strings. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `ring`, `border`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `muted-foreground`

## Motion

- **arrival** · SelectContent · `motion-pop` — The popup's transform-origin follows Base UI's anchor, so it grows out of the trigger it belongs to. On a dense form with several selects in a column, that origin is the only thing identifying which field the open list is for.
- **response** · SelectItem · `motion-interactive` — Highlight follows both pointer and keyboard. Easing it means arrow-keying down a list is continuous motion rather than a background teleporting between rows, which is what makes a long list readable while moving.
- **transition** · SelectContent · `motion-pop` — Closing collapses back toward the trigger, so the reader's eye is returned to the field that now holds the value they just picked.
- **activity** · SelectContent · _no motion_ — Select takes a resident list of options. Anything that has to be fetched or filtered as you type is Combobox, which owns that state.

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides listbox/option roles, aria-expanded, typeahead, roving focus, and a hidden form input.
- Esc and click-outside dismiss; arrow keys and Home/End navigate the list.
- Selected option carries data-[selected]; the highlighted option carries data-[highlighted].
- Animate the popup via data-[starting-style] / data-[ending-style].

## Related

- Components: Combobox, Radio, Field, Input
- Patterns: SettingsPage, AuthPage

## Examples

### Basic (controlled)

```tsx
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Select value={value} onValueChange={setValue}><SelectTrigger placeholder="Choose a font" /><SelectContent><SelectItem value="sans">Sans-serif</SelectItem><SelectItem value="serif">Serif</SelectItem><SelectItem value="mono">Monospace</SelectItem></SelectContent></Select>
```

### Grouped

```tsx
import { SelectContent, SelectGroup, SelectGroupLabel, SelectItem } from "@sableui/react"

<SelectContent><SelectGroup><SelectGroupLabel>Weights</SelectGroupLabel><SelectItem value="regular">Regular</SelectItem><SelectItem value="bold">Bold</SelectItem></SelectGroup></SelectContent>
```

### Inside Field

```tsx
import { Field, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Default visibility" description="Controls how new editions appear."><Select defaultValue="public"><SelectTrigger placeholder="Choose visibility" /><SelectContent><SelectItem value="public">Public</SelectItem><SelectItem value="private">Private</SelectItem><SelectItem value="unlisted">Unlisted</SelectItem></SelectContent></Select></Field>
```

### Rich item labels

```tsx
import { Badge, Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Select defaultValue="edition" items={[{ value: "edition", label: "Edition" }, { value: "collectible", label: "Collectible" }]}><SelectTrigger /><SelectContent><SelectItem value="edition" label="Edition"><span className="flex items-center gap-2"><Badge tone="edition">Edition</Badge><span>Edition drop</span></span></SelectItem><SelectItem value="collectible" label="Collectible"><span className="flex items-center gap-2"><Badge tone="collectible">Collectible</Badge><span>Collectible</span></span></SelectItem></SelectContent></Select>
```

# Separator

**Status:** stable

A hairline divider. Horizontal full-width rule or vertical 1px column, tinted with the border token. Optional centered label (horizontal) for a captioned section divider.

**Keywords:** separator, divider, section break, rule

## Usage

Use Separator to divide related groups where spacing alone does not provide enough structure.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it sparingly between sections, menu groups, or dense rows.
- Do: Choose orientation based on the layout direction it separates.
- Don't: Do not use Separator as decoration when hierarchy, spacing, or headings would explain the layout better.
- Don't: Do not use it where space would do. A page whose every section is divided by a rule reads as a form; the rule should mark a real change of subject.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| orientation | "horizontal" \| "vertical" | "horizontal" | Axis of the rule. Vertical stretches to its flex parent's height. |
| label | ReactNode | — | When set (horizontal only), centers a muted caption between two hairline rules. |
| render | ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement | — | Compose with another element/component through the Base UI render prop. Ignored on the labeled variant. |

## Variants

- **orientation**: horizontal, vertical

## Tokens used

`border`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI sets role=separator and aria-orientation for assistive tech.
- The labeled variant renders a div with explicit role=separator + aria-orientation (the caption is the visible context).
- Purely decorative dividers can carry aria-hidden when adjacent content already conveys the grouping.

## Related

- Components: Menu, ContextMenu, Card

## Examples

### Horizontal

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@sableui/react"

<Separator />
```

### Labeled section divider

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@sableui/react"

<Separator label="Other holdings" />
```

### Vertical (inside a flex row)

```tsx
import { Row, Separator } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={3} className="h-6 items-center"><span>Edit</span><Separator orientation="vertical" /><span>Delete</span></Row>
```

# SettingsMenu

**Status:** stable

A compact trigger that states the current settings, over a menu of rows that change them. Each row shows its own value and opens a submenu.

**Keywords:** settings, model picker, model switcher, options menu, preferences, submenu, quality settings, ai chat

## Usage

For a cluster of related settings that a reader checks often and changes occasionally — the model and effort on an AI composer, quality and format on an export control, density and sort on a table. It encodes one shape: summarise the state on the trigger, then open to a list of name → current value → submenu. It knows nothing about any particular domain; the AI-model case is one instance of it.

### Best practices

- Do: Put the current values in `summary`, not a noun. "5.6 Sol High" tells the reader where they are; a trigger reading "Settings" makes them open it to find out, which is the wrong trade for a control glanced at twenty times a session.
- Do: Give every SettingsRow a `value`. One glance at the open menu should answer every setting at once — a menu of bare names is a menu you have to explore.
- Do: Use `MenuRadioGroup` + `MenuRadioItem` inside a row for single-choice settings, so the current option is checked rather than merely remembered.
- Do: Reach for `variant="subtle"` when the trigger sits on a surface where a ghost control would float unanchored — inside a ChatComposer, for instance.
- Don't: Do not use it for a single setting. One choice is a `Select`; the nesting only earns its cost when there are several related settings to summarise.
- Don't: Do not put actions in it. Rows change state; a menu that mixes "Effort ›" with "Delete conversation" makes destructive commands look like preferences. That is `Menu` or `DotsMenu`.
- Don't: Do not nest more than one level deep. Past that the reader loses the path back, and the thing you have is a settings dialog wearing a menu.
- Don't: Do not override the upward, end-aligned default without reason. Its home is the bottom of a composer or toolbar, where a downward menu opens off-screen.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trigger | yes | The summary control. States the current settings and carries a chevron; quiet at rest, so it does not compete with the primary action beside it. |
| SettingsRow | yes | One setting: its name, its current value, and a submenu of options. Without children it renders flat, for a row that is a statement rather than a choice. |
| Submenu contents | no | Usually a MenuRadioGroup of MenuRadioItems, so the active option is checked. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SettingsRow | { label: ReactNode; value?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; children?: ReactNode } | One setting. With children it opens a submenu; without them it renders as a flat statement row. |
| MenuRadioGroup | { value?: string; defaultValue?: string; onValueChange?: (value: string) => void } | Single-choice group for a row's submenu. Exported from Menu; re-used here rather than duplicated. |
| MenuRadioItem | { value: string; disabled?: boolean } | One option, with a check in a reserved leading column so labels do not shift as the highlight moves. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| summary | ReactNode | — | What the trigger reads when closed. Give it the current values, not a noun — the control should answer before it is opened. |
| label | string | "Change settings" | Accessible name for the trigger, since the visible summary is data rather than a label. |
| variant | "ghost" \| "subtle" | "ghost" | Resting treatment. `ghost` disappears into the surface at rest and shows its affordance on hover — right for a toolbar. `subtle` adds a fill for surfaces where a ghost trigger would float unanchored. |
| size | "xs" \| "sm" | "sm" | Trigger height, read off the density ladder so a compact scope retunes it with every other control. |
| side | "top" \| "bottom" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end" | "top" | Which side the menu opens on. Upward by default — its home is the bottom of a composer. |
| align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" | "end" | Alignment along that side. |
| disabled | boolean | — | Disable the trigger. |
| ...Menu props | Omit<ComponentProps<typeof Menu>, 'children'> | — | `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` and the rest of Base UI's menu root props. |

## Variants

- **variant**: ghost, subtle
- **size**: xs, sm

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Base UI's Menu underneath, so roving focus, typeahead, Esc and outside-dismissal, and the full menu/menuitemradio ARIA wiring come for free — including submenu traversal with the arrow keys.
- The trigger carries an explicit `label`, because its visible text is the current state rather than a name: without it, a screen reader announces "5.6 Sol High" with no indication that it is a control or what it changes.
- Radio rows are `menuitemradio` with a real checked state, so the current choice is conveyed to assistive tech rather than only by a visible tick.
- The check occupies a reserved column instead of appearing on selection, so labels never shift sideways as the highlight moves — a change that reads as motion to anyone tracking position.
- Submenus open on the inline-end side, which flips correctly in RTL rather than always opening right.

## Related

- Components: Menu, DotsMenu, Select, ChatComposer, Popover
- Patterns: ChatPanel

## Examples

### A model switcher in a composer

```tsx
import { ChatComposer, MenuRadioGroup, MenuRadioItem, SettingsMenu, SettingsRow } from "@sableui/react"

<ChatComposer
	onSend={send}
	actions={
		<SettingsMenu variant="subtle" size="xs" summary={<><span className="text-foreground">{model.name}</span>{" "}<span className="text-muted-foreground">{effort}</span></>}>
			<SettingsRow label="Model" value={model.name}>
				<MenuRadioGroup value={model.id} onValueChange={setModelId}>
					<MenuRadioItem value="sol">5.6 Sol</MenuRadioItem>
					<MenuRadioItem value="lite">5.6 Lite</MenuRadioItem>
				</MenuRadioGroup>
			</SettingsRow>
			<SettingsRow label="Effort" value={effort}>
				<MenuRadioGroup value={effort} onValueChange={setEffort}>
					<MenuRadioItem value="Low">Low</MenuRadioItem>
					<MenuRadioItem value="High">High</MenuRadioItem>
				</MenuRadioGroup>
			</SettingsRow>
		</SettingsMenu>
	}
/>
```

### Export options — the same shape, no chat involved

```tsx
import { MenuRadioGroup, MenuRadioItem, SettingsMenu, SettingsRow } from "@sableui/react"

<SettingsMenu summary={`${format} · ${quality}`} side="bottom" align="start">
	<SettingsRow label="Format" value={format}>
		<MenuRadioGroup value={format} onValueChange={setFormat}>
			<MenuRadioItem value="PNG">PNG</MenuRadioItem>
			<MenuRadioItem value="SVG">SVG</MenuRadioItem>
		</MenuRadioGroup>
	</SettingsRow>
	<SettingsRow label="Quality" value={quality}>
		<MenuRadioGroup value={quality} onValueChange={setQuality}>
			<MenuRadioItem value="Draft">Draft</MenuRadioItem>
			<MenuRadioItem value="Final">Final</MenuRadioItem>
		</MenuRadioGroup>
	</SettingsRow>
</SettingsMenu>
```

### A flat row for a setting with nothing to choose

```tsx
import { MenuRadioGroup, MenuRadioItem, MenuSeparator, SettingsMenu, SettingsRow } from "@sableui/react"

<SettingsMenu summary="Standard">
	<SettingsRow label="Speed" value="Standard">
		<MenuRadioGroup value="standard">
			<MenuRadioItem value="standard">Standard</MenuRadioItem>
			<MenuRadioItem value="priority">Priority</MenuRadioItem>
		</MenuRadioGroup>
	</SettingsRow>
	<MenuSeparator />
	<SettingsRow label="Plan" value="Team" />
</SettingsMenu>
```

# Sheet

**Status:** stable

Edge-anchored drawer over Base UI Drawer — focus trap, scroll lock, Esc/outside dismissal, portal backdrop, plus swipe-to-dismiss on touch. Slides in from a viewport edge via side and swipes back out toward the same edge.

**Keywords:** sheet, drawer, side panel, overlay, swipe to dismiss

## Usage

Use Sheet for secondary workflows that slide in while preserving context from the underlying page.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for inspect, edit, filter, or create flows that relate to the current page.
- Do: Include clear title, close path, and footer actions for task-oriented sheets.
- Don't: Do not use Sheet for simple confirmations or deeply nested workflows.
- Don't: Do not use it on desktop where a Dialog fits. A sheet's affordance is edge-anchored travel for thumb reach; on a wide viewport it becomes a dialog that arrives from the wrong place.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SheetTrigger | no | The element that opens the sheet. |
| SheetContent | yes | The sliding panel content. |
| SheetClose | no | An explicit close control. |
| SheetHeader | no | The title and description region. |
| SheetTitle | no | The sheet heading. |
| SheetDescription | no | Supporting context for the sheet. |
| SheetFooter | no | Footer actions for the workflow. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SheetContent | Base UI Drawer.Popup props (initialFocus, finalFocus, …) + side: "right" \| "left" \| "top" \| "bottom" + className | Backdrop + edge-anchored popup; portals to <body>. side picks which viewport edge the sheet anchors to and slides in from (defaults to "right"). Left/right are full-height side panels; top/bottom span the width up to 80vh. On touch it swipes closed toward that same edge (right swipes right, left swipes left, top swipes up, bottom swipes down). |
| SheetTrigger | Base UI Drawer.Trigger props (render) | Element that opens the sheet. Compose via render prop. |
| SheetClose | Base UI Drawer.Close props (render) | Element that dismisses the sheet. Compose via render prop. |
| SheetHeader | ComponentProps<"div"> | Top section holding SheetTitle/SheetDescription. |
| SheetTitle | Base UI Drawer.Title props + className | The sheet's accessible name — wires aria-labelledby on the popup. |
| SheetDescription | Base UI Drawer.Description props + className | Muted supporting line; wires aria-describedby. |
| SheetFooter | ComponentProps<"div"> | Bottom row for actions, pinned after the scrollable body. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sheet (Root) | Base UI Drawer.Root props (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, onOpenChangeComplete, modal, disablePointerDismissal, actionsRef, handle) — minus swipeDirection and snap points | — | Controls open state. Uncontrolled by default. The dismiss swipe direction is not a prop: it follows SheetContent's side. onOpenChange reports reason "swipe" when a swipe closed it. |

## Variants

- **side**: right, left, top, bottom

## Tokens used

`popover`, `popover-foreground`, `border`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides focus trapping, scroll lock, aria-modal, and labelled-by wiring (SheetTitle).
- The panel scrolls its own content (thin scrollbar, contained overscroll) when it outgrows its bound — the full height on left/right, 80vh on top/bottom.
- Esc and click-outside dismiss by default; on touch, a swipe toward the sheet's own edge dismisses too. A short or slow drag springs back.
- Swipe is an extra path, never the only one: Esc, click-outside and SheetClose all still work.
- Focus matches Dialog: the first tabbable on mouse/keyboard open, the panel itself on touch (so the virtual keyboard stays down); focus returns to the trigger on close.
- Render a SheetClose inside SheetContent so screen-reader users can escape the popup.
- Slide animation runs via data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] attributes on the motion-duration token; while swiping the panel tracks the finger directly, and a released swipe finishes on the same token (scaled by flick speed), so reduced motion makes it instant.
- A mouse drag that starts on sheet content selects text rather than dragging the panel; mouse dragging only starts from the padding edge.

## Related

- Components: Dialog, Popover, Sidebar

## Examples

### Basic (right)

```tsx
import { Button, Sheet, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetFooter, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Sheet><SheetTrigger render={<Button>Open</Button>} /><SheetContent><SheetHeader><SheetTitle>Filters</SheetTitle><SheetDescription>Narrow the feed.</SheetDescription></SheetHeader><SheetFooter><SheetClose render={<Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>} /><SheetClose render={<Button>Apply</Button>} /></SheetFooter></SheetContent></Sheet>
```

### Left side

```tsx
import { Button, Sheet, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetFooter, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Sheet><SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Menu</Button>} /><SheetContent side="left"><SheetHeader><SheetTitle>Navigation</SheetTitle></SheetHeader><SheetFooter><SheetClose render={<Button variant="secondary">Close</Button>} /></SheetFooter></SheetContent></Sheet>
```

### Bottom side

```tsx
import { Button, Sheet, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetFooter, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Sheet><SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary">Details</Button>} /><SheetContent side="bottom"><SheetHeader><SheetTitle>Edition details</SheetTitle></SheetHeader><SheetFooter><SheetClose render={<Button variant="secondary">Close</Button>} /></SheetFooter></SheetContent></Sheet>
```

# ShowMore

**Status:** stable

Collapsible content region that clips children to a collapsed height, fades the cut edge, and reveals the rest with a toggle.

**Keywords:** show more, disclosure, truncate, expand

## Usage

Use ShowMore to reveal additional content after an intentionally shortened preview.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it when the preview is useful on its own and the rest is optional.
- Do: Make the expanded state reversible when collapsing helps users regain context.
- Don't: Do not place it on a card or tinted surface without checking the fade. The cut-edge gradient fades to the page background color, so on any other surface it reads as a visible band.
- Don't: Do not hide required steps, important warnings, or primary actions behind ShowMore.
- Don't: Do not use it to hide content search engines or screen readers need. Collapsed content is still in the DOM here, but if the user must read it to act, it should not be behind a toggle.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| collapsedHeight | number | 96 | Collapsed height of the content region in px. The inner wrapper clips to this height until expanded. The toggle and fade only appear when the measured content is taller than this; content that already fits shows in full with no control. Expanding animates to the measured height. |
| collapsedLines | number | — | Collapsed height as a count of the content's own lines (measured from its line height). Wins over collapsedHeight, and is the one to prefer: the preview keeps the same number of lines when the type scale or density changes, where a px height shows fewer as type grows. |
| children | ReactNode | — | The content to collapse and reveal. |

## Tokens used

`background`, `foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- The toggle is a real <button> with aria-expanded reflecting the open state.
- The fade overlay is pointer-events-none and decorative; it never traps clicks.
- Collapsed content stays in the DOM, so screen readers can still reach it.

## Related

- Components: Collapsible

## Examples

### Long paragraph

```tsx
import { ShowMore } from "@sableui/react"

<ShowMore><p className="text-body-md text-foreground">A long paragraph that exceeds the collapsed height…</p></ShowMore>
```

### Collapsed to a line count

```tsx
import { ShowMore } from "@sableui/react"

<ShowMore collapsedLines={6}><p className="text-body-md text-foreground">{post.description}</p></ShowMore>
```

# Sidebar

**Status:** stable

Desktop side-navigation rail (in-flow sticky, hidden below lg) with SidebarHeader / SidebarNav / SidebarItem / SidebarFooter parts. Items are router-agnostic via the `render` prop; an optional collapsed icon-rail mode reveals labels in tooltips.

**Keywords:** sidebar, navigation, app chrome, rail

## Usage

Use Sidebar for persistent desktop navigation or application chrome outside the main content region.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for stable app destinations that should remain visible while content changes.
- Do: Keep item labels predictable and active state obvious.
- Don't: Do not use Sidebar for page-local settings, filters, or temporary action groups.
- Don't: Do not put page content in it. It is fixed-width chrome OUTSIDE the content grid, so anything in it is exempt from the page's measure and rhythm.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar | yes | The persistent navigation container. |
| SidebarItem | yes | One navigation destination or action. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SidebarItem | { label: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; active?: boolean; badge?: ReactNode; render?: useRender.RenderProp } + button props | A single nav row. label is the row text (inline when expanded, in a hover tooltip when collapsed); icon is the leading icon node (the consumer swaps fill weight for the active state); active marks the current route (accent fill + aria-current="page"); badge is a trailing node (e.g. a count) pushed to the row end and hidden when collapsed; render composes another element, e.g. render={<Link to="/x" />}. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| collapsed | boolean | false | Collapse the rail to an icon-only width (--sidebar-width-collapsed). Items hide their label + badge and reveal the label in a hover tooltip; the content area reflows. Controlled — wire a toggle from app state. Read the state in custom header/footer content via useSidebar(). |
| icons | boolean | true | Render the leading icon on each SidebarItem. Set false for a text-only rail. Ignored while collapsed (icon-only by definition). |
| variant | "app" \| "inline" | "app" | Where the rail lives. "app" is the page's chrome column — sticky, full viewport height, hidden below lg where AppHeader + BottomNav take over. "inline" is always visible and fills its parent's height, for a rail inside a bounded frame (a nested shell, an embedded preview). Use it instead of overriding the layout with !important classes. |

## Variants

- **variant**: app, inline

## Tokens used

`sidebar`, `sidebar-foreground`, `sidebar-border`, `sidebar-accent`, `sidebar-accent-foreground`, `sidebar-ring`

## Accessibility

- SidebarNav renders a <nav> landmark.
- Active item carries aria-current="page".
- Items expose a focus-visible ring (sidebar-ring).
- Collapsed: items take their accessible name from a string label (or aria-label) and reveal the visible label via the tooltip, so the rail stays usable by keyboard and screen readers.

## Related

- Components: SideNav, BottomNav, AppShell

## Examples

### Rail with nav

```tsx
import { Icon, NotificationBadge, Sidebar, SidebarFooter, SidebarHeader, SidebarItem, SidebarNav } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<Sidebar><SidebarHeader>{brand}</SidebarHeader><SidebarNav><SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Notifications" badge={<NotificationBadge count={3} />} render={<Link to="/notifications" />} /></SidebarNav><SidebarFooter>{wallet}</SidebarFooter></Sidebar>
```

### Collapsible (icon rail)

```tsx
import { Button, Icon, Sidebar, SidebarFooter, SidebarItem, SidebarNav } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

const [collapsed, setCollapsed] = useState(false)
<Sidebar collapsed={collapsed}><SidebarNav><SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="home" />} label="Home" active render={<Link to="/" />} /></SidebarNav><SidebarFooter><Button variant="ghost" size="icon" onClick={() => setCollapsed((c) => !c)} aria-label="Toggle sidebar"><Icon name="chevron-left" /></Button></SidebarFooter></Sidebar>
```

### Inline (inside a bounded frame)

```tsx
import { Icon, Sidebar, SidebarItem, SidebarNav } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="flex h-80 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-border"><Sidebar variant="inline"><SidebarNav><SidebarItem icon={<Icon name="home" />} label="Home" active /></SidebarNav></Sidebar><div className="flex-1 p-6">Content</div></div>
```

# SideNav

**Status:** stable

A lightweight in-content vertical navigation list - the settings / docs sub-nav, distinct from the app-chrome Sidebar. Router-agnostic items, optional SideNavGroup sections, and an explicit active-state vocabulary for content rails or sidebar chrome.

**Keywords:** side nav, navigation, settings nav, sidebar, rail, docs nav, active item, group

## Usage

Use SideNav for vertical navigation inside a settings page, documentation area, dashboard rail, or sidebar chrome. It is router-agnostic: compose items with render={<Link />} and choose activeVariant based on whether the nav sits in content or app chrome.

### Best practices

- Do: Use aria-label on SideNav when a page contains more than one nav landmark.
- Do: Group related items with SideNavGroup when the rail has more than one conceptual area.
- Do: Use size='lg' and activeVariant='sidebar' when the nav is part of persistent app chrome.
- Do: Inside a rounded, padded frame, give each item rounded-concentric-<outer>/<inset> (e.g. rounded-concentric-lg/2 in a rounded-lg p-2 box). The rows' own radius is fixed per size, and a same-radius row inset into a frame reads as a second system.
- Don't: Use SideNav for bottom mobile navigation; use BottomNav in AppShell's bottomNav slot.
- Don't: Mix content and sidebar active variants in the same rail unless individual items intentionally override the group.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nav | yes | The landmark container for the vertical navigation list. |
| Group | no | Optional labelled cluster of related navigation items. |
| Item | yes | Interactive row with label, optional icon, optional badge, and active state. |
| Badge | no | Trailing count or state indicator aligned to the row end. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SideNavItem | { label: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; active?: boolean; badge?: ReactNode; size?: "md" \| "lg"; activeVariant?: "content" \| "sidebar"; render?: useRender.RenderProp } + button props | A single row. label is the row text; icon is an optional leading icon; active marks the current sub-section (active fill + aria-current="page"); badge is a trailing node (e.g. a count) pushed to the row end; size and activeVariant override the enclosing SideNav per item; render composes another element, e.g. render={<Link to="/x" />}. |
| SideNavGroup | { label?: ReactNode } + div props | A labelled section within a SideNav - groups settings into areas. label renders an optional sentence-case caption heading above the group's items. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size | "md" \| "lg" | — | Density shared by all items. "md" (default) = the lightweight in-content sub-nav; "lg" = chrome-weight (larger label + icon, roomier rows) for a rail that pairs with the app Sidebar. |
| activeVariant | "content" \| "sidebar" | "content" | Active-state token vocabulary shared by all items. "content" uses bg-accent/text-accent-foreground for local rails inside the content area; "sidebar" uses bg-sidebar-accent/text-sidebar-accent-foreground for SideNavs rendered inside app chrome. |

## Tokens used

`muted`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `ring`, `sidebar-foreground`, `sidebar-accent`, `sidebar-accent-foreground`, `sidebar-ring`

## Accessibility

- SideNav renders a <nav> landmark; pair multiple navs with aria-label to distinguish them.
- The active item carries aria-current="page".
- Items expose a focus-visible ring; the active state is reinforced by weight + fill, not colour alone.
- Use activeVariant="content" for local in-page rails and activeVariant="sidebar" when a SideNav is placed on Sidebar chrome.

## Related

- Components: Sidebar, AppShell, BottomNav, Badge, Icon
- Patterns: SettingsPage, DashboardPage

## Examples

### Settings sub-nav

```tsx
import { SideNav, SideNavItem } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<SideNav><SideNavItem label="Profile" active render={<Link to="/settings/profile" />} /><SideNavItem label="Account" render={<Link to="/settings/account" />} /><SideNavItem label="Notifications" render={<Link to="/settings/notifications" />} /></SideNav>
```

### Grouped

```tsx
import { SideNav, SideNavGroup, SideNavItem } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<SideNav><SideNavGroup label="Account"><SideNavItem label="Profile" active render={<Link to="/settings/profile" />} /><SideNavItem label="Security" render={<Link to="/settings/security" />} /></SideNavGroup><SideNavGroup label="Workspace"><SideNavItem label="Members" render={<Link to="/settings/members" />} /></SideNavGroup></SideNav>
```

### Chrome-weight rail (size=lg)

```tsx
import { SideNav, SideNavItem } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<SideNav size="lg"><SideNavItem label="Profile" active render={<Link to="/settings/profile" />} /><SideNavItem label="Wallets" render={<Link to="/settings/wallets" />} /><SideNavItem label="Security" render={<Link to="/settings/security" />} /></SideNav>
```

### Inside Sidebar chrome

```tsx
import { SideNav, SideNavItem } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<SideNav size="lg" activeVariant="sidebar"><SideNavItem label="Overview" active render={<Link to="/" />} /><SideNavItem label="Reports" render={<Link to="/reports" />} /><SideNavItem label="Settings" render={<Link to="/settings" />} /></SideNav>
```

### Grouped with icons and badges

```tsx
import { Badge, Icon, SideNav, SideNavGroup, SideNavItem } from "@sableui/react"
// <Link> = your router's link (react-router, next/link, @tanstack/router, …)

<SideNav aria-label="Settings sections"><SideNavGroup label="Account"><SideNavItem icon={<Icon name="user" />} label="Profile" active render={<Link to="/settings/profile" />} /><SideNavItem icon={<Icon name="lock" />} label="Security" badge={<Badge tone="warning" size="sm">2</Badge>} render={<Link to="/settings/security" />} /></SideNavGroup><SideNavGroup label="Workspace"><SideNavItem icon={<Icon name="bell" />} label="Notifications" render={<Link to="/settings/notifications" />} /></SideNavGroup></SideNav>
```
