# Skeleton

**Status:** stable

Loading placeholder — a muted, shimmering block (rounded-md bg-muted motion-shimmer). Shape it with utility classes; rounded-full for circles.

**Keywords:** skeleton, loading, placeholder, pending

## Usage

Use Skeleton to reserve space and hint at the shape of content while data is loading.

### Best practices

- Do: Match the approximate size and rhythm of the eventual content.
- Do: Use it for content regions where layout stability matters during loading.
- Don't: Do not leave Skeleton visible after an error or empty state; switch to EmptyState (tone='destructive' for an error).
- Don't: Do not use a skeleton whose shape differs from the content that replaces it. A mismatched placeholder causes a visible jump, which is worse than a brief spinner.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ...props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"div"> | — | All native div props plus className. Size and shape the placeholder with utilities (h-*, w-*, size-*, rounded-full). |

## Tokens used

`muted`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — A skeleton stands in for content that has not arrived; fading the placeholder in adds a wait before the wait.
- **response** · Root · _no motion_ — Nothing here is interactive. A skeleton that reacted to the pointer would invite a click on a thing that cannot be clicked.
- **transition** · Root · _no motion_ — The skeleton has one state. Swapping it for real content is the parent's job, and the parent decides whether that swap is animated.
- **activity** · Root · `motion-shimmer` — The sweep is the entire point of the component: it is what separates 'still loading' from 'loaded, and empty'. A static grey block is indistinguishable from a broken layout, which is why users reload the page.

## Accessibility

- Purely presentational; the shimmer sweep is decorative, and it stops under reduced motion because motion-shimmer follows --motion-scale.
- Mark the loading region with aria-busy="true" on a parent, and swap in real content (with the same layout) once loaded to avoid shift.

## Related

- Components: Spinner, PageLoader

## Examples

### Shapes

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@sableui/react"

<Skeleton className="h-4 w-40" /><Skeleton className="size-10 rounded-full" /><Skeleton className="h-40 w-full" />
```

### Post-card composition

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="flex items-center gap-3"><Skeleton className="size-10 rounded-full" /><div className="space-y-2"><Skeleton className="h-3 w-32" /><Skeleton className="h-3 w-20" /></div></div>
```

# Slider

**Status:** stable

Slider over Base UI Slider — pointer + keyboard control, ARIA slider wiring, and range support via multiple thumbs. The default export composes Root + Control + Track + Indicator + Thumb; pass an array value for a range.

**Keywords:** slider, range, value, input

## Usage

Use Slider for bounded numeric choices where approximate adjustment is faster than typing.

### Best practices

- Do: Use visible labels, min/max context, and value output when precision matters.
- Do: Choose steps that match the real granularity of the setting.
- Don't: Do not use Slider when users must enter an exact arbitrary number; use NumberField.
- Don't: Do not use it without showing the value. A slider with no numeric readout makes any precise choice guesswork — pair it with a ScrubField or a NumberField.
- Don't: Do not resize the thumb's box on hover, focus, or drag. The thumb is a fixed-size hit target wrapping a decorative dot; only the dot scales. A target that grows under the cursor is a target nobody can learn, and WCAG 2.5.8 measures target size at rest. Restyle the dot, not the box.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SliderRoot | yes | The controlled slider wrapper. |
| SliderControl | yes | The interactive slider control region. |
| SliderTrack | yes | The visible value range. |
| SliderIndicator | no | The filled portion of the track. |
| SliderThumb | yes | The draggable handle. |
| SliderValue | no | A readable value display. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SliderRoot | Base UI Slider.Root props | The unstyled Base UI Root for custom composition — owns the value state and forwards value / defaultValue / onValueChange / min / max / step. Drag state surfaces via data-[dragging]. The default Slider export wires all the parts for you. |
| SliderControl | Base UI Control props + className | The interactive track lane — the positioning context the indicator and thumbs sit in; dims when disabled. |
| SliderTrack | Base UI Track props + className | The full-range rail beneath the indicator. |
| SliderIndicator | Base UI Indicator props + className | The filled portion from min (or the lower thumb) to the current value. |
| SliderThumb | Base UI Thumb props + className | A draggable handle: a fixed-size hit target wrapping a decorative dot. The dot rests small and scales to full size on hover, keyboard focus, and drag; the box never changes, so row metrics and the tap target hold. Range sliders render one per value; pass index for SSR. Interaction state surfaces via data-[dragging]. |
| SliderValue | Base UI Value props | Formatted value readout for custom compositions (e.g. a live number beside the control). |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number \| number[] | — | Controlled value. An array renders a range slider with one thumb per entry. |
| defaultValue | number \| number[] | — | Uncontrolled initial value. An array renders a range slider. |
| onValueChange | (value, eventDetails) => void | — | Fires on every value change. value is a number (or number[] for a range). |
| min | number | 0 | Minimum allowed value. |
| max | number | 100 | Maximum allowed value. |
| step | number | 1 | Granularity the slider steps through. Snaps to multiples. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Ignore user interaction and dim the control. |
| orientation | 'horizontal' \| 'vertical' | horizontal | Axis the slider tracks along. A vertical slider has no intrinsic length — give it a height (h-40, or flex-1 in a column). |

## Tokens used

`secondary`, `primary`, `background`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides role=slider, aria-valuemin/max/now, and arrow-key / Page Up-Down / Home-End control.
- Each thumb is a focusable input[type=range] nested in the thumb element; keyboard focus raises a 2px ring on the thumb via has-[:focus-visible] (a bare focus-visible: on the thumb never fires, since the div itself is not focusable).
- The thumb's hit area is a fixed 16px box at every state. Only the decorative inner dot resizes — rest 12px, full 16px on hover, keyboard focus, and drag — so the target a pointer or finger must land on never moves or changes size. Keyboard users, who never hover, get the enlarged dot from focus-visible.
- The rest-to-full transition uses the motion duration/easing tokens, so it collapses to an instant state change under prefers-reduced-motion or MotionProvider off. The size change itself still happens: it reports interaction state, it is not decoration.
- Range sliders get one thumb per value with minStepsBetweenValues honored.
- Pass an aria-label (or getAriaLabel on a thumb) so each handle has an accessible name.

## Related

- Components: NumberField, Progress

## Examples

### Single value

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@sableui/react"

<Slider defaultValue={50} aria-label="Volume" />
```

### Range

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@sableui/react"

const [range, setRange] = useState([20, 60])
<Slider value={range} onValueChange={setRange} aria-label="Price range" />
```

### Stepped

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@sableui/react"

<Slider defaultValue={40} min={0} max={100} step={10} />
```

### Vertical

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@sableui/react"

<div className="h-40"><Slider orientation="vertical" defaultValue={40} aria-label="Level" /></div>
```

### Composed with a value readout

```tsx
import { Field, SliderControl, SliderIndicator, SliderRoot, SliderThumb, SliderTrack, SliderValue } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Volume"><SliderRoot defaultValue={40} className="flex items-center gap-3"><SliderControl><SliderTrack><SliderIndicator /><SliderThumb /></SliderTrack></SliderControl><SliderValue className="text-mono-sm" /></SliderRoot></Field>
```

---

# Spinner

**Status:** stable

Pure SVG activity indicator. No Base UI, no icon dependency — a role=status ring (faint track + rounded-cap arc) that inherits the current text color. Size with the size prop (sm / md / lg), color with text-*.

**Keywords:** spinner, loading, pending, indeterminate

## Usage

Use Spinner for short indeterminate waits where the user cannot know exact progress.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it in compact panels or places where layout is already stable. In a button, use Button's loading prop rather than placing a Spinner by hand — it disables the button, sets aria-busy and sizes the spinner to the button's icon.
- Do: Pair it with accessible loading text when the surrounding label is not enough.
- Don't: Do not use Spinner as the only content for long waits or full page loading.
- Don't: Do not use it without an accessible name or a nearby status message. A spinning icon is invisible to a screen reader, so the wait is announced as nothing at all.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string | "Loading" | Accessible label announced by screen readers while visible (sets aria-label on the role=status element). |
| appearance | "ring" \| "dots" | "ring" | ring is the default indicator; dots are three bouncing dots, softer, for chat and inline text. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | One scale for both appearances: ring 14 / 16 / 24px, dots 4 / 6 / 8px. |
| className | string | — | Color (text-*); the ring's strokes use currentColor, so it follows the text color. Size with the size prop — a size-* class still overrides the ring for an off-scale context (Button sizes its own spinner this way), but is not the way to pick a size. |

## Variants

- **appearance**: ring, dots
- **size**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `primary-foreground`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — A spinner already signals a wait. Fading it in delays the signal for exactly as long as the user most needs it.
- **response** · Root · _no motion_ — It is a status indicator, not a control.
- **transition** · Root · _no motion_ — One state. Whatever replaces it on completion owns that change.
- **activity** · Root · `motion-spin` — The rotation is the whole component — it is the only thing distinguishing 'working' from 'frozen'. motion-spin rather than Tailwind's animate-spin because the built-in ignores --motion-scale, so the reduced-motion policy cannot freeze it.

## Accessibility

- Wrapped in role=status, a polite live region, with an aria-label (default 'Loading').
- Color comes from currentColor; pair with a text-* token for adequate contrast.
- Spins with the motion-spin utility, which follows --motion-scale, so it slows and stops with the motion setting and reduced-motion.

## Related

- Components: Skeleton, Progress

## Examples

### Dots

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@sableui/react"

<Spinner appearance="dots" label="Assistant is typing" className="text-muted-foreground" />
```

### Default

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@sableui/react"

<Spinner />
```

### Sized + tinted

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@sableui/react"

<Spinner size="lg" className="text-muted-foreground" />
```

### Inside a button (Button owns it — use loading)

```tsx
import { Button } from "@sableui/react"

<Button loading>Collecting</Button>
```

# StatusBar

**Status:** stable

The bottom chrome strip of a Workspace: ambient document facts — dimensions, counts, sync state — in the micro type tier.

**Keywords:** status bar, status, footer, chrome, workspace, tool, ambient, counts, document

## Usage

Use StatusBar for the persistent facts about a document that otherwise have nowhere to live: size, counts, selection state, sync or connection status. Everything in it is ambient — it reports, it does not command. Pair it with Workspace's statusBar slot.

### Best practices

- Do: Put document-scoped facts here — dimensions, layer or record counts, saved/sync state — so panels stop competing for that space.
- Do: Use StatusBarGroup with align="end" for the trailing cluster, and StatusBarSeparator between related facts.
- Do: Render numeric facts in the UI num tier so a changing value doesn't shift the strip's layout.
- Don't: Make it the only route to an action. It's ambient chrome at the micro tier — anything essential needs a real control elsewhere too.
- Don't: Put zoom here. Anchor zoom to the canvas it acts on, which is where every reference tool puts it.
- Don't: Use it for transient feedback like a save confirmation — that's Toast. A status bar states what is true, not what just happened.
- Don't: Derive a fact here separately from the surface that shows it, or from something expensive to recompute. The strip re-renders with the document, so read the same value the canvas or panel uses: a status bar that reports max(asset sizes) while the canvas reports something else is a bug types cannot catch, because both are numbers.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| StatusBarGroup | no | A cluster of items; align="end" pins it to the trailing edge. |
| StatusBarSeparator | no | A decorative dot between related facts; aria-hidden. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| StatusBarGroup | { align?: 'start' \| 'end' } | A cluster of status items; `end` pushes it to the trailing edge. |
| StatusBarSeparator | ComponentProps<'span'> | A decorative middle dot between facts. aria-hidden, since order conveys grouping. |

## Tokens used

`muted-foreground`, `panel`, `hairline`, `hairline-strong`

## Accessibility

- Renders a <footer>, so the strip is a discoverable region rather than an anonymous row of text.
- Separators are aria-hidden — a screen reader announcing 'middle dot' between every fact is noise.
- Micro-tier text is small by design; never put information here that exists nowhere else.

## Related

- Components: Workspace, PanelGroup, InlineStatus, Toast, Banner

## Examples

### Document facts with a trailing cluster

```tsx
import { StatusBar, StatusBarGroup, StatusBarSeparator } from "@sableui/react"

<StatusBar>
  <span className="text-ui-num">1024 × 768</span>
  <StatusBarSeparator />
  <span>3 layers</span>
  <StatusBarGroup align="end">
    <span>Saved</span>
  </StatusBarGroup>
</StatusBar>
```

### With a warning tone

```tsx
import { StatusBar, StatusBarGroup } from "@sableui/react"

<StatusBar>
  <span>Offline — edits are queued</span>
  <StatusBarGroup align="end">
    <span className="text-tone-warning">2 unsynced</span>
  </StatusBarGroup>
</StatusBar>
```

### In a Workspace

```tsx
import { PanelGroup, StatusBar, Workspace, WorkspaceCanvas } from "@sableui/react"

<Workspace statusBar={<StatusBar><span>Connected</span></StatusBar>}>
  <PanelGroup>
    <WorkspaceCanvas />
  </PanelGroup>
</Workspace>
```

# StatusDot

**Status:** stable

A small colored status dot. Tone variants encode state via semantic tone tokens; sizes scale the diameter. Decorative (aria-hidden) — pair with text. Optional pulse adds a live ping ring.

**Keywords:** status, dot, presence, health, state, online, live, indicator

## Usage

Use StatusDot as a compact visual state cue next to text, avatars, rows, or labels. It is decorative by design, so pair it with visible text or use `<Badge appearance="plain" dot>` when the label and dot should travel together — that is the labelled status line, not a hand-built row.

### Best practices

- Do: Place StatusDot beside a readable state label, person name, or row title.
- Do: Use pulse only for live or in-progress states that are actively changing.
- Don't: Use the dot as the only status indicator; it is aria-hidden and color alone is not enough.
- Don't: Mix many dot sizes in the same list. Keep row indicators visually consistent.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dot | yes | The small tone-colored circle. It is decorative and hidden from assistive tech. |
| Pulse ring | no | Optional motion ring for in-progress or live states. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tone | "neutral" \| "standard" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "info" \| "edition" \| "collectible" \| "destructive" | "neutral" | Semantic color of the dot. |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Dot diameter. |
| pulse | boolean | false | Wrap the dot in an animated ping ring to signal a live state. |

## Variants

- **tone**: neutral, standard, success, warning, info, edition, collectible, destructive
- **size**: sm, md, lg

## Tokens used

`muted-foreground`, `tone-standard`, `success`, `tone-warning`, `tone-info`, `tone-edition`, `tone-collectible`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Rendered aria-hidden — purely decorative. Convey status in adjacent text, not color alone.
- A dot conveys state through colour alone, which fails for colour-blind users and announces as nothing. It must always sit beside text that states the same thing, or carry its own accessible name.

## Related

- Components: Badge, Avatar, InlineStatus
- Patterns: DashboardPage, ListDetailPage

## Examples

### Tones

```tsx
import { Row, StatusDot } from "@sableui/react"

<Row gap={2}><StatusDot tone="standard" /><StatusDot tone="info" /><StatusDot tone="warning" /><StatusDot tone="destructive" /></Row>
```

### With label — use Badge

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@sableui/react"

<Badge appearance="plain" tone="success" dot pulse>Live</Badge>
```

# Stepper

**Status:** stable

Where the user is in a multi-step flow — an ordered list of numbered steps, horizontal or vertical, each complete, current, upcoming or in error, with aria-current="step" on the current one. `indicator="dot"` turns it into a timeline of events (an order's delivery) with dots instead of numbers.

**Keywords:** stepper, steps, wizard, multi-step form, checkout steps, onboarding progress, progress steps, timeline

## Usage

Use Stepper above or beside a flow that is split into a known, small number of named steps — checkout, onboarding, an import wizard — so the user can see how far they have come and what is left. It reports position; the flow's own Back and Continue buttons move it.

### Best practices

- Do: Drive it from one number (`current`) and override a single step's `status` only for what a number cannot say — a completed step that now needs attention is `status="error"`.
- Do: Name steps with a word or two ("Shipping", "Payment"). Go vertical when steps need a description or there are more than five; horizontal titles truncate first.
- Do: Give completed steps `onSelect` only when going back to edit them actually works, and keep the user's later answers when they do.
- Don't: Do not use Stepper for a task with unknown length or for a percentage. That is Progress; a stepper promises a fixed set of named stops.
- Don't: Do not use it as navigation between independent sections. Sections the user can visit in any order are Tabs; a stepper implies each step depends on the one before.
- Don't: Do not make upcoming steps pressable to skip ahead. A step that looks reachable but is not is worse than one that is plainly locked.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stepper | yes | The ordered list. Takes `current` and `orientation`, and an aria-label naming the flow. |
| StepperItem | yes | One step: a numbered disc (a check when complete, a warning mark on error) — or, with `indicator="dot"`, a dot centred on the title's first line — a title, and an optional description. |
| Connector | no | The line to the next step, filled once this step is complete. Drawn automatically between items. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| StepperItem | { title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; status?: StepStatus; onSelect?: () => void } + li props | One step. `status` overrides the derived state; `onSelect` makes the disc and title a button for returning to the step. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| current | number | 0 | Zero-based index of the current step. Earlier steps derive complete, later ones upcoming. |
| orientation | "horizontal" \| "vertical" | "horizontal" | Horizontal for a short flow across the top of a form; vertical for long flows, narrow columns or steps with descriptions. |
| indicator | "number" \| "dot" | "number" | `number` for a flow the user moves through; `dot` for a timeline of events (delivery tracking, a document's history) where the position number adds nothing. The dot centres on the title's first line and scales with its type at every density. |
| statusLabels | Partial<Record<StepStatus, string>> | — | Screen-reader status words appended to each title (Completed, Current step, Not started, Needs attention). Override to localize. |
| aria-label | string | — | Names the flow ("Checkout progress"). Every Stepper needs one. |

## Variants

- **orientation**: horizontal, vertical
- **indicator**: number, dot
- **status**: complete, current, upcoming, error

## Tokens used

`primary`, `primary-foreground`, `background`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `border-strong`, `destructive`, `destructive-foreground`, `ring`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Stepper · _no motion_ — The stepper frames the flow and is on screen before any step is. Animating it in would compete with the step content, which is what changed.
- **response** · StepperItem · `motion-interactive` — Only steps with onSelect respond, and the eased underline is what tells a returning user that this completed step can be reopened while the upcoming ones cannot.
- **transition** · Indicator · `motion-interactive` — When the user continues, the disc they leave fills and its connector darkens. Easing the colour makes that read as one step completing rather than the whole bar re-rendering.
- **activity** · Stepper · _no motion_ — A step is a place, not a process. Saving or validating between steps belongs on the Continue button's loading state; a pulsing disc would suggest the step itself is busy.

## Accessibility

- Renders an ordered list, so assistive tech announces the step count and each step's position.
- The current step carries aria-current="step"; every title also gets a visually hidden status word (Completed, Not started, Needs attention), so state never depends on colour or the disc glyph.
- Discs and connectors are aria-hidden — the number is already the list position.
- Steps with onSelect render as native buttons with a visible focus ring; steps without it are not focusable.

## Related

- Components: Progress, Tabs, Form, Button

## Examples

### Checkout

```tsx
import { Stepper, StepperItem } from "@sableui/react"

<Stepper current={1} aria-label="Checkout progress">
	<StepperItem title="Cart" />
	<StepperItem title="Shipping" />
	<StepperItem title="Payment" />
	<StepperItem title="Review" />
</Stepper>
```

### Vertical with descriptions

```tsx
import { Stepper, StepperItem } from "@sableui/react"

<Stepper orientation="vertical" current={2} aria-label="Workspace setup">
	<StepperItem title="Create account" description="Email verified" />
	<StepperItem title="Invite team" description="3 people invited" />
	<StepperItem title="Connect data" description="Choose a source to import from" />
	<StepperItem title="Launch" />
</Stepper>
```

### Delivery timeline (dots)

```tsx
import { Stepper, StepperItem } from "@sableui/react"

<Stepper orientation="vertical" indicator="dot" current={2} aria-label="Delivery status">
	<StepperItem title="Order placed" description="Oct 9, 10:14 AM" />
	<StepperItem title="Printed and packed" description="Oct 10, 4:02 PM" />
	<StepperItem title="Out for delivery" description="Arriving today by 6 PM" />
	<StepperItem title="Delivered" />
</Stepper>
```

### A completed step with an error

```tsx
import { Stepper, StepperItem } from "@sableui/react"

<Stepper current={2} aria-label="Checkout progress">
	<StepperItem title="Cart" onSelect={() => console.log("cart")} />
	<StepperItem title="Shipping" status="error" description="Address needs a postcode" onSelect={() => console.log("shipping")} />
	<StepperItem title="Payment" />
</Stepper>
```

# StreamingText

**Status:** stable

Prose arriving from a live source, a token at a time. Each token resolves out of blur, the trailing edge stays soft while more is coming, and a steady caret marks the write head.

**Keywords:** streaming, stream, tokens, typewriter, generation, assistant, llm, caret, incremental

## Usage

Use StreamingText for text whose final length is unknown while it renders — a model's answer, a live transcript, a log line being written. It is the counterpart to ThinkingOrb and Spinner: those cover the wait BEFORE the first token, this covers the arrival of the tokens themselves.

### Best practices

- Do: Grow `text` and let the component do the rest. It assumes an append-only string and keys units by index, so React mounts only the new spans — re-rendering a longer string animates what was added and leaves what the reader has already read alone.
- Do: Drop `streaming` to false the moment the source closes. That is what removes the caret and the softened tail, and their disappearance is the only signal the reader gets that the answer is complete.
- Do: Turn `caret` off when something adjacent already reports the wait — a spinner in the message header, a status row beneath. Two indicators for one wait read as two things happening.
- Don't: Do not use it for text that is already complete. Staging known text on scroll is TextReveal (a `motion` export, not a component folder), which computes a stagger from the full string; StreamingText cannot, because nothing here knows the length. Using it for static prose animates the whole paragraph on every mount and says 'still generating' about something that finished.
- Don't: Do not wrap it in an aria-live region. Every token would be announced, which is unusable; the component sets `aria-busy` instead. Announce once when the turn settles, from whatever owns the turn.
- Don't: Do not pass `split="char"` for paragraph-length text. It is one element per character — thousands of nodes for an answer, each with its own animation — and word-splitting is indistinguishable at prose reading speed. Reserve it for a headline-length string.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container | yes | The paragraph (or `as` element). Carries `aria-busy` while output is incomplete. |
| Unit | yes | One word or character. Animates once on mount and never again; the newest one carries the softened tail while streaming. |
| Caret | no | The write head, shown while streaming. Steady rather than blinking — see `motion-caret`. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | string | — | The text received so far. Assumed append-only: the component keys units by index precisely so a grown string mounts only its new spans. |
| streaming | boolean | false | Whether more is still coming. Drives the caret, the softened trailing edge, and `aria-busy`. |
| as | ElementType | "p" | Render container element. |
| split | "word" \| "char" | "word" | Split granularity. `char` is one element per character — short strings only. |
| caret | boolean | true | Show the caret while streaming. Turn it off when something adjacent already reports the wait. |

## Tokens used

`foreground`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Unit · `motion-stream-in` — Each token resolves out of blur rather than fading. A fade makes every word a separate event; blur reads as the word coming into focus, so a paragraph arrives as one sentence being written instead of a queue of arrivals.
- **response** · Container · _no motion_ — It is prose, not a control. Selecting and copying it is the only interaction, and both are native.
- **transition** · Container · _no motion_ — There is no state to move between — streaming to complete is marked by the caret and tail leaving, not by the text changing. Animating the whole paragraph on completion would re-stage text the reader already read.
- **activity** · Caret · `motion-caret` — The caret is the write head, and it is deliberately STEADY (`data-streaming="true"` suppresses the blink). A blink during arrival puts two rhythms on screen — text advancing at one rate, a caret flashing at another — and the flashing one carries no information the moving text has not already given.

## Accessibility

- The text is real text in the accessibility tree: units are ordinary spans, not aria-hidden fragments, so a screen reader concatenates them into the sentence.
- `aria-busy` is set on the container while `streaming` is true, marking the output incomplete without announcing each token.
- The caret is `aria-hidden` — it is a rendering of the write head, and a screen reader has no use for it.
- Under reduced motion or with MotionProvider off, no unit animates and no tail is softened; text simply appears as it arrives.

## Related

- Components: ThinkingOrb, Message, Bubble

## Examples

### Streaming an answer

```tsx
import { StreamingText } from "@sableui/react"

<StreamingText text={answer} streaming={pending} />
```

### Inside a message, with the wait reported elsewhere

```tsx
import { Message, StreamingText } from "@sableui/react"

<Message role="assistant"><StreamingText text={answer} streaming={pending} caret={false} /></Message>
```

### A headline resolving character by character

```tsx
import { StreamingText } from "@sableui/react"

<StreamingText as="h2" split="char" className="text-heading-2" text={headline} streaming={pending} />
```

---

# Switch

**Status:** stable

Binary on/off toggle for immediate-effect settings. Track fills with the primary tone when checked; the thumb slides on a spring-eased transform (mirrored in RTL).

**Keywords:** switch, toggle setting, on off, form control

## Usage

Use Switch for immediate on/off settings that take effect as a persistent preference or mode.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it for binary settings where the label describes the enabled state.
- Do: Make the current state obvious through both position and accessible text.
- Don't: Do not phrase the label as a negative, such as "Don't send read receipts". Turning off a negative is a double negative, and the user has to solve it before they can act.
- Don't: Do not use Switch for one-time agreement, multi-select choices, or submit-only booleans.
- Don't: Do not use a Switch whose effect is not immediately visible somewhere. A toggle flipped with no observable consequence gives no confirmation it worked, so the user flips it again to check.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| checked | boolean | — | Controlled on/off state. Pair with onCheckedChange. Omit for an uncontrolled switch. |
| defaultChecked | boolean | false | Initial state for an uncontrolled switch. |
| onCheckedChange | (checked: boolean, eventDetails) => void | — | Fired when the switch is toggled. Note: Base UI passes a second eventDetails arg — not the common (checked) => void, so a single-arg handler must widen its signature. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Dims the control and ignores user interaction. |
| readOnly | boolean | false | Prevents toggling while keeping the control fully visible. |
| required | boolean | false | Marks the switch as required when inside a form. |
| name | string | — | Identifies the field when the enclosing form is submitted. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `ring`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — Switches arrive as part of a settings list. Animating each one in turns a form into a title sequence.
- **response** · Root · `motion-interactive` — The track is small and its hover change is subtle; without the ease the colour shift reads as a rendering glitch rather than a reaction.
- **transition** · Thumb · `motion-interactive` — The thumb sliding IS the affordance — it shows the control has two ends and which one you are now at. Teleporting the thumb makes on and off two unrelated pictures, and users re-read the label to work out which they are looking at. motion-interactive is the right recipe because it declares `translate`, so the thumb transform and the track colour ease on one timeline instead of two.
- **activity** · Root · _no motion_ — A switch commits instantly. If the write is slow enough to need a pending state, the surrounding form owns that, not the control.

## Accessibility

- Renders Base UI's Switch with a hidden native <input> — role, ARIA, and keyboard (Space/Enter) toggling come for free.
- Focus-visible draws a 2px ring in the --ring token.
- Disabled state sets cursor-not-allowed and 50% opacity; readOnly keeps full contrast but blocks changes.
- Give it an accessible name: wrap it in <Field label=… orientation="horizontal">, which wires the label for you.

## Related

- Components: Checkbox, Toggle, ThemeSwitcher

## Examples

### Default (uncontrolled)

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@sableui/react"

<Switch defaultChecked />
```

### Controlled

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@sableui/react"

<Switch checked={on} onCheckedChange={setOn} />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@sableui/react"

<Switch disabled defaultChecked />
```

### With a label

```tsx
import { Field, Switch } from "@sableui/react"

<Field label="Reduce motion" orientation="horizontal"><Switch defaultChecked /></Field>
```

# Table

**Status:** stable

Styled native table subcomponents (Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableCaption). Horizontally scrollable frame, hairline row borders, hover-lift, and selectable rows via data-selected.

**Keywords:** table, data table, rows, columns, grid, caption, header, cell, tabular

## Usage

Use Table for structured data with consistent columns and rows. Use DataTable when the table should be data-driven with sorting or empty state behavior, and use lists or cards when each item has a different shape.

### Best practices

- Do: Use TableCaption and TableHead so the table has a clear purpose and column semantics.
- Do: Keep cells concise and scannable; compose Badge, StatusDot, Avatar, or Button only when they clarify the row.
- Do: Use the built-in horizontal frame for overflow instead of squeezing columns until content becomes unreadable.
- Do: Put a table in a card with `<CardContent flush>`. The first and last columns then take the card's own padding (`--table-edge-px`), so they line up with the CardHeader at any density. Never hand-set `pl-6`/`pr-6` on edge cells.
- Don't: Use Table for heterogeneous items with no stable columns. Use Card, Entity, or a list composition instead.
- Don't: Put every possible action in every row. Use one primary row action, a DotsMenu, or row detail navigation.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Caption | no | Accessible summary of what the table contains. |
| Header | yes | Column labels rendered with TableHead cells. |
| Body | yes | Rows and cells containing the tabular data. |
| Footer | no | Optional totals or summary row group. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TableHeader | ComponentPropsWithRef<"thead"> | The header row group (thead). |
| TableBody | ComponentPropsWithRef<"tbody"> | The data row group (tbody). |
| TableFooter | ComponentPropsWithRef<"tfoot"> | Summary row group (tfoot) with a muted fill. |
| TableRow | ComponentPropsWithRef<"tr"> | A row (tr) — hairline bottom border, hover lift, and a selected state via the data-selected attribute. |
| TableHead | ComponentPropsWithRef<"th"> | A column header cell (th) in muted label styling. |
| TableCell | ComponentPropsWithRef<"td"> | A data cell (td). |
| TableCaption | ComponentPropsWithRef<"caption"> | Accessible description of the table (caption), muted. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| className | string | — | The root renders a horizontally scrollable frame around a native <table>; forwards all native table attributes plus className. Each subcomponent likewise forwards its element's native attributes + className. |

## Tokens used

`border`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

- Renders semantic native table elements (thead/tbody/tfoot/th/td/caption) preserving built-in table semantics.
- Use TableHead (th) for column headers and TableCaption for an accessible description.
- Mark the active row with the data-selected attribute for a visible selected state.

## Related

- Components: DataTable, Pagination, Badge, StatusDot, Avatar
- Patterns: DashboardPage, ListDetailPage

## Examples

### Collectors

```tsx
import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@sableui/react"

<Table>
	<TableCaption>Recent collectors</TableCaption>
	<TableHeader>
		<TableRow>
			<TableHead>Collector</TableHead>
			<TableHead>Edition</TableHead>
			<TableHead>Paid</TableHead>
		</TableRow>
	</TableHeader>
	<TableBody>
		<TableRow>
			<TableCell>@nova</TableCell>
			<TableCell>#012</TableCell>
			<TableCell>0.5 SOL</TableCell>
		</TableRow>
	</TableBody>
</Table>
```

### Rich status cells

```tsx
import { Avatar, Badge, Button, Row, Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@sableui/react"

<Table><TableCaption>Deployments</TableCaption><TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Name</TableHead><TableHead>Status</TableHead><TableHead>Owner</TableHead><TableHead className="text-end">Actions</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader><TableBody><TableRow data-selected><TableCell>Catalog API</TableCell><TableCell><Badge appearance="plain" tone="warning" dot pulse>Building</Badge></TableCell><TableCell><Row gap={1}><Avatar fallback="NR" alt="Nova Reed" size="sm" /><span>Nova</span></Row></TableCell><TableCell className="text-end"><Button size="sm" variant="ghost">View</Button></TableCell></TableRow></TableBody></Table>
```

### Flush in a card

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@sableui/react"

<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Collectors</CardTitle></CardHeader><CardContent flush><Table><TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Collector</TableHead><TableHead>Paid</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader><TableBody><TableRow><TableCell>@nova</TableCell><TableCell>0.5 SOL</TableCell></TableRow></TableBody></Table></CardContent></Card>
```

### Summary footer

```tsx
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableFooter, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@sableui/react"

<Table><TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Item</TableHead><TableHead className="text-end">Amount</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader><TableBody><TableRow><TableCell>Primary sale</TableCell><TableCell className="text-end">42 SOL</TableCell></TableRow></TableBody><TableFooter><TableRow><TableCell>Total</TableCell><TableCell className="text-end">42 SOL</TableCell></TableRow></TableFooter></Table>
```

# Tabs

**Status:** stable

Tabs over Base UI Tabs (roving focus, arrow-key nav, ARIA tablist wiring) in two styles: underline (page sections) or pill (compact switchers). Tabs (Root) + TabsList + TabsTrigger + TabsPanel.

**Keywords:** tabs, tablist, panels, segmented content

## Usage

Use Tabs to switch between related panels within the same page context.

### Best practices

- Do: Use tabs when each panel is peer content and users may compare or switch often.
- Do: Keep tab labels short and make the active tab unmistakable.
- Do: Use variant="pill" for a short switcher inside a card or toolbar (Preview / Code, List / Grid); keep the default underline for sections of a page.
- Don't: Do not use Tabs for unrelated pages or primary navigation that needs distinct URLs.
- Don't: Do not use tabs for sequential steps. Tabs are peer views the user returns to in any order; a process with an order needs a stepper, or the user will skip ahead.

### Anatomy

| Part | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TabsList | yes | The list of tab triggers. |
| TabsTrigger | yes | One selectable tab. |
| TabsPanel | yes | The content associated with a trigger. |
| TabsContent | no | Compatibility alias for panel content. |

## Subcomponents

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TabsList | Base UI Tabs.List props (activateOnFocus, loopFocus) + variant?: "underline" \| "pill" + className | The tablist row. variant="underline" (default) draws a divider rule beneath the triggers; variant="pill" drops the rule and fills the active trigger. Triggers inherit the variant. |
| TabsTrigger | Base UI Tabs.Tab props (value, disabled) + className | A single tab button. value pairs it with the panel of the same value. |
| TabsPanel | Base UI Tabs.Panel props (value, keepMounted) + className | The content shown when the matching trigger is active. |
| TabsContent | Alias of TabsPanel | Re-export of TabsPanel for consumers that prefer this name. |

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tabs (Root) | Base UI Tabs.Root props (value, defaultValue, onValueChange, orientation) | defaultValue: 0 | Controls the active tab. Uncontrolled via defaultValue; controlled via value + onValueChange. |

## Tokens used

`border`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides the tablist/tab/tabpanel roles, aria-selected, and roving tabindex.
- Arrow keys move between tabs; Home/End jump to first/last; panels are linked via aria-controls.
- Active tab styling reads from the data-active attribute; disabled tabs from data-disabled. Disabled tabs are skipped by arrow-key navigation.
- Keyboard focus shows a ring on the focused trigger in both variants; the panel remains focusable.

## Related

- Components: Accordion, BottomNav, SideNav

## Examples

### Basic

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsPanel, TabsTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Tabs defaultValue="overview"><TabsList><TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger><TabsTrigger value="activity">Activity</TabsTrigger></TabsList><TabsPanel value="overview">Overview content</TabsPanel><TabsPanel value="activity">Activity content</TabsPanel></Tabs>
```

### Pill switcher

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsPanel, TabsTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Tabs defaultValue="preview"><TabsList variant="pill"><TabsTrigger value="preview">Preview</TabsTrigger><TabsTrigger value="code">Code</TabsTrigger></TabsList><TabsPanel value="preview">Rendered example</TabsPanel><TabsPanel value="code">Source</TabsPanel></Tabs>
```

### With a disabled tab

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsPanel, TabsTrigger } from "@sableui/react"

<Tabs defaultValue="overview"><TabsList><TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger><TabsTrigger value="holders" disabled>Holders</TabsTrigger></TabsList><TabsPanel value="overview">Overview content</TabsPanel></Tabs>
```

# Textarea

**Status:** stable

Styled native multi-line text control. Soft-square, card surface, --ring focus, and an aria-invalid destructive error state.

**Keywords:** textarea, multi line input, form, text

## Usage

Use Textarea for multi-line freeform text entry such as notes, descriptions, or messages.

### Best practices

- Do: Use labels, helper text, and character limits when expectations are specific.
- Do: Size it to the expected amount of input without making the page feel blocked.
- Do: Keep a focusable field at 16px or larger on mobile. iOS Safari zooms the whole page when a focused textarea computes under 16px and never zooms back out. Textarea handles this itself — below the sm breakpoint it renders text-body-lg (17px) and returns to text-body-md at sm and up. Build a custom field the same way: a second paired tier under a max-sm: variant, never a hand-set font-size.
- Don't: Do not override the type with a page tier below 16px (text-body-md, text-body-sm) without a >=16px mobile arm — that reintroduces the iOS focus zoom.
- Don't: Do not use Textarea for short single-line values; use Input.
- Don't: Do not leave it at the default height for long-form input. A two-row textarea for a paragraph forces the user to write through a letterbox.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aria-invalid | boolean | — | When true, swaps the input border to the destructive token to signal a validation error. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Dims the control to 50% and blocks pointer interaction. |
| rows | number | — | Native textarea row count. The floor is min-h-20 on the spacing scale, so it moves with density. |
| autoResize | boolean | false | Grows to fit content via CSS field-sizing: content (no JS). The min-height stays the floor; browsers without field-sizing fall back to the fixed min-height. |
| ...props | ComponentPropsWithRef<"textarea"> | — | All native textarea attributes (value, placeholder, onChange, name, ref, …). |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`, `destructive`

## Accessibility

- Renders a native <textarea> — label association, keyboard, and screen-reader semantics come for free.
- Renders through Base UI's Field.Control: inside a Field it picks up the label, description, error and validity wiring from context.
- Pair with a <label htmlFor> (or aria-label) for an accessible name.
- Set aria-invalid and reference an error message via aria-describedby to announce validation failures.
- Focus-visible draws a 2px ring in the --ring token.

## Related

- Components: Input, Form, Label

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

<Textarea placeholder="Write a caption…" />
```

### With rows

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

<Textarea rows={6} placeholder="Tell the story behind this edition…" />
```

### Auto-resize

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

<Textarea autoResize placeholder="Grows as you type…" />
```

### Invalid

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

<Textarea aria-invalid defaultValue="Too long" />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@sableui/react"

<Textarea disabled defaultValue="Captions lock once the edition is minted." />
```

# ThemeSelector

**Status:** stable

A presentational radiogroup for choosing a Sable design theme from theme manifests — swatch-strip cards for a settings page, or compact rows for tool chrome. Pair it with useSableTheme().themeId and setThemeId when the app uses SableThemeProvider.

**Keywords:** theme selector, theme, appearance, skin, design theme, preset

## Usage

Use ThemeSelector wherever a person picks a theme. The default `cards` layout is page-register furniture: a swatch strip, a name, and a caption only where one distinguishes the card (the default theme, or a single-mode theme), at ~144px tall. Use `layout="list"` in tool chrome, a popover, or any docked panel — five cards is the wrong object for a 256px surface, however it is sized. For colour mode (light/dark/system) use ThemeSwitcher, which is a segmented control and belongs in chrome as-is.

### Best practices

- Do: Use layout="list" in a popover, a menu, or a docked panel. Rows sit on the --control-sm ladder and still show each theme's swatch strip, so the choice stays visible rather than described. Rows take `sable-frame-inner`, so host the list in a sable-frame (a Popover, or `sable-frame sable-surface sable-surface-popover sable-frame-popover`) and their corners nest concentrically.
- Do: Pass mode={useSableTheme().mode} so every preview renders in the colour mode actually in use, rather than in each theme's manifest default.
- Do: Load each theme's fonts in the host app. Every card carries a type specimen in that theme's own face so people can compare typography as well as color. A theme whose fonts are not loaded falls back to system-ui, and its specimen stops telling the truth.
- Don't: Add a viewport breakpoint to force a column count — `className="sm:grid-cols-1"` or similar. `sm:` keys off the VIEWPORT, not this component's container, so on a wide screen it does nothing for a narrow parent. The cards grid already reflows on its own width via auto-fit.
- Don't: Put the cards layout in workspace chrome. It was built for a settings page; in a 256px popover the cards clip their labels to a single character and grow to roughly twice their intended height.
- Don't: Use ThemeSelector for light / dark / system colour mode. That is ThemeSwitcher — a segmented control. This picks the design theme, which is a different axis entirely, and the two are frequently confused.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | ThemeId | — | The currently selected Sable design theme id. |
| onValueChange | (themeId: ThemeId) => void | — | Called with the next design theme id when an option is chosen. |
| themes | readonly ThemeManifest[] | themeManifests | Theme manifests to render. Defaults to Sable's built-in themes. |
| mode | "light" \| "dark" | — | Preview mode for each card's swatch strip. Pass useSableTheme().mode to match the current color mode; omitted cards use their manifest defaultMode. |
| label | string | "Design theme" | Accessible label for the radiogroup. |
| layout | "cards" \| "list" | "cards" | Presentation. "cards" is the page-register picker (~144px per card); "list" is one compact --control-sm row per theme, for chrome and popovers. A presentation variant, not a size — "list" is not "cards, smaller" — which is why it is a prop rather than a density scope. |
| className | string | — | Merged onto the outer radiogroup grid. |

## Tokens used

`input`, `card`, `border`, `background`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `accent`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- The container is role="radiogroup" with an aria-label; each card is a role="radio" button with aria-checked reflecting the selected theme.
- Focus-visible draws a 2px ring on the focused card.
- The selected card wears the shared selection-card checked ring (the same as RadioCard and CheckboxCard), a muted fill and a check icon, so selection does not rely on colour alone.
- Presentational only: it does not change the document theme; pass useSableTheme().setThemeId or apply the change in onValueChange.

## Related

- Components: ThemeSwitcher, Popover, RadioCard

## Examples

### With SableThemeProvider

```tsx
import { ThemeSelector, useSableTheme } from "@sableui/react"

const { themeId, setThemeId, themes, mode } = useSableTheme()
<ThemeSelector value={themeId} onValueChange={setThemeId} themes={themes} mode={mode} />
```

### Controlled

```tsx
import { ThemeSelector, type ThemeId } from "@sableui/react"

const [themeId, setThemeId] = useState<ThemeId>("base")
<ThemeSelector value={themeId} onValueChange={setThemeId} />
```

### In chrome — a popover or a docked panel

```tsx
import { PopoverContent, ThemeSelector, ThemeSwitcher } from "@sableui/react"

// Five 144px cards is the wrong object for a 256px surface. Rows are.
<PopoverContent align="end" className="w-64 p-3">
  <ThemeSwitcher value={preference} onValueChange={setPreference} />
  <ThemeSelector layout="list" value={themeId} onValueChange={setThemeId} mode={mode} />
</PopoverContent>
```

### Do not reach for a viewport breakpoint

```tsx
import { ThemeSelector } from "@sableui/react"

// ✗ `sm:` keys off the VIEWPORT, not this component's container. On a wide
//   screen it does nothing at all for a narrow parent — and this exact
//   workaround, once documented here, is how the cards layout ended up in a
//   256px popover clipping "Default" to "D".
<ThemeSelector className="sm:grid-cols-1" value={themeId} onValueChange={setThemeId} />

// ✓ The cards grid already reflows on its own width (auto-fit, 9rem tracks).
//   For a genuinely narrow surface, change the presentation instead.
<ThemeSelector layout="list" value={themeId} onValueChange={setThemeId} />
```

# ThemeSwitcher

**Status:** stable

A segmented light / dark / system switch. Presentational: it renders the selected color preference and reports changes via onValueChange; pair it with useSableTheme() when the app uses SableThemeProvider. A radiogroup of three icon buttons (sun / moon / desktop).

**Keywords:** theme switcher, color mode, dark mode, appearance

## Usage

Use ThemeSwitcher for light, dark, and system color mode preference.

### Best practices

- Do: Use it where users expect appearance controls, such as app chrome or settings.
- Do: Respect persisted system or user preference when initializing the control.
- Don't: Do not use ThemeSwitcher to choose brand themes or component style presets.
- Don't: Do not hand-build another segmented capsule for a different choice. ThemeSwitcher wears the shared segmented look (lib/segmented); for any other single-select switch use ToggleGroup appearance="segmented".
- Don't: Do not omit the `system` option or default to a hardcoded mode. Overriding the OS preference is the single most common accessibility complaint about theme controls.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | "light" \| "dark" \| "system" | — | The currently selected color preference. |
| onValueChange | (value: ThemeMode) => void | — | Called with the next color preference when an option is chosen. |
| label | string | "Theme" | Accessible label for the radiogroup. |
| className | string | — | Merged onto the outer radiogroup container. |

## Tokens used

`border`, `card`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

- The container is role="radiogroup" with an aria-label; each option is role="radio" with aria-checked reflecting the selected value.
- Each icon button carries an aria-label (Light / Dark / System) plus a title tooltip, since the visual is icon-only.
- Focus-visible draws a 2px ring on the focused option; selection styling reads from aria-checked.
- Presentational only: it does not change the document theme; pass useSableTheme().setPreference or apply the change in onValueChange.

## Related

- Components: ThemeSelector, Switch, Toggle

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
import { ThemeSwitcher, type ThemeMode } from "@sableui/react"

const [theme, setTheme] = useState<ThemeMode>("system")
<ThemeSwitcher value={theme} onValueChange={setTheme} />
```

### With SableThemeProvider

```tsx
import { ThemeSwitcher, useSableTheme } from "@sableui/react"

const { preference, setPreference } = useSableTheme()
<ThemeSwitcher value={preference} onValueChange={setPreference} />
```

### Light selected

```tsx
import { ThemeSwitcher } from "@sableui/react"

<ThemeSwitcher value="light" onValueChange={setTheme} />
```

# ThinkingOrb

**Status:** stable

Canvas dot-cloud 'agent is thinking' indicator. Three generated modes (orbit / globe / mesh) drawn from pure math — no icon dependency, no animation library. Ink follows currentColor; size steps are separately tuned.

**Keywords:** thinking, orb, agent, ai, chat, loading, streaming, indeterminate, canvas

## Usage

Use ThinkingOrb while an AI agent is working and there is nothing specific to report yet — before the first token streams, or between tool calls. It is a richer, more characterful sibling of Spinner for the one place in a product where the wait is the experience.

### Best practices

- Do: Reserve it for the single active agent state — the composer, the streaming message header, a standalone thinking screen. One orb on screen reads as intent; several read as decoration.
- Do: Switch mode to say what kind of work is happening: orbit for generic thinking, globe while searching or retrieving, mesh while relating sources or running tools. Pair it with a text status so the phase is legible without decoding the animation.
- Do: Use size="sm" inline in a message row or composer and size="lg" only when the orb is the main thing on screen. The size steps are separately tuned, not scaled, so the small one stays legible.
- Don't: Do not put one on every row of a list or in a repeated skeleton. Each orb runs its own animation frame loop painting hundreds of arcs; use Skeleton for content-shaped waits and Spinner inside buttons.
- Don't: Do not use it for a determinate wait. It carries no sense of how far along anything is — reach for Progress when a percentage exists.
- Don't: Do not rely on the animation alone to announce the wait. Give the label a short constant phrase (it is the role=status announcement) or place a status message next to it.
- Don't: Do not pass a label that changes while the orb is up. It is the accessible name of a live region, so every change re-announces the whole thing — feed it a per-token phase and a screen reader interrupts on each delta: "Chromatic drift" → "Chromatic drift · rgb-shift" → "Chromatic drift · rgb-shift → grain", which is unusable. The label names the wait ("Thinking"); the phase belongs in adjacent text, as in the "Inline with a status line" example. If the phase must be announced, announce it once when the turn settles from a separate live region — not per update.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode | "orbit" \| "globe" \| "mesh" | "orbit" | Which cloud to draw. orbit = generic working, globe = searching/retrieving (a scan band sweeps pole to pole), mesh = relating things (nodes wire to near neighbours and signals run the edges). |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "md" | Rendered box on the spacing scale: sm 5 units (20px at the default spacing; inline in a composer or message row), md 8 (32px; beside a status line), lg 16 (64px; standalone). The box moves with density like the text beside it, and the canvas re-measures it. Each step has its own dot density, dot size and speed. |
| speed | number | 1 | Multiplier on top of the per-size tuned speed. Below ~0.5 the orb reads as stalled. |
| paused | boolean | false | Freeze on a representative still frame without unmounting. |
| label | string | "Thinking" | Accessible label announced by screen readers while visible (sets aria-label on the role=status element). Must stay constant for as long as the orb is mounted — it names the wait, it does not report progress. |
| className | string | — | Set the ink with a semantic text-* token (the dots are drawn from the element's computed color). The box is sized by the size prop, not by className. |

## Tokens used

`foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `primary`

## Motion

- **arrival** · Root · _no motion_ — The orb appears when work starts, and the point cloud is already in motion on its first painted frame. There is nothing to stage.
- **response** · Root · _no motion_ — It reports state; it is not a control. A hover reaction would suggest the wait is something you can click your way out of.
- **transition** · Root · _no motion_ — Changing `mode` swaps the renderer on the next frame: the cloud is redrawn as the new shape, not morphed into it. The phase change is carried by the status text beside the orb, which is what a reader actually reads; a per-particle morph would be decoration on top of it.
- **activity** · Root · _custom (outside the recipe layer)_ — The cloud is drawn per frame on a canvas by a single requestAnimationFrame loop — no CSS animation exists to name here. The loop reads the motion policy itself, which is the part worth checking when auditing: `custom` means the kill-switch is honoured in JS rather than by --motion-scale.

## Accessibility

- Wrapped in role=status, a polite live region, with an aria-label (default 'Thinking'); the canvas itself is aria-hidden.
- Because that label is the live region's accessible name, it must not change while the orb is mounted — a name that churns re-announces on every change, so a phase recomputed per streamed delta becomes an interruption per delta. Keep the label constant and let the phase live in adjacent text; announce an outcome once when the work settles, from a separate region.
- Ink is the element's computed color, so contrast is the consumer's token choice — pair with foreground or muted-foreground rather than a decorative tint.
- Honours the motion policy: under prefers-reduced-motion or <MotionProvider> off, it paints one still frame and never starts an animation loop.
- The loop also stops when the orb scrolls out of view or the tab is backgrounded, so a forgotten orb cannot burn a CPU core.

## Related

- Components: Spinner, Skeleton, Progress, InlineStatus, ChatComposer, Message

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { ThinkingOrb } from "@sableui/react"

<ThinkingOrb />
```

### Modes

```tsx
import { ThinkingOrb } from "@sableui/react"

<ThinkingOrb mode="orbit" size="lg" />
<ThinkingOrb mode="globe" size="lg" />
<ThinkingOrb mode="mesh" size="lg" />
```

### Inline with a status line (the label stays constant, the phase moves)

```tsx
import { InlineStatus, ThinkingOrb } from "@sableui/react"

<InlineStatus icon={<ThinkingOrb mode="globe" size="sm" label="Searching" />}>Searching your workspace…</InlineStatus>
```

### Tinted and paused

```tsx
import { ThinkingOrb } from "@sableui/react"

<ThinkingOrb size="lg" className="text-primary" paused />
```
